author: oichkatzelesfrettschen
body:
terakan: C.1.5 wire dmabuf carrier attach into vkAllocateMemory (HOLD before merge)

Mode A probe revealed terakan_dmabuf_carrier_attach was never invoked.
The dma-buf branch of terakan_AllocateMemory called winsys-bo-import_fd
and stopped, so every imported BO had bo->carrier == NULL and the C.2b
collector was dead code.

This commit:
- Wires attach into the IMPORT branch when VkImportMemoryFdInfoKHR
  is present and handle type is DMA_BUF_BIT_EXT.
- Wires attach into the EXPORT branch when export_handle_types
  includes DMA_BUF_BIT_EXT.
- Loosens carrier_classify_and_alloc to accept desc dmabuf_fd less
  than zero. fd validation belongs in terakan_dmabuf_carrier_import
  where the dup happens; attach path legitimately has no fd at
  descriptor time.
- Extends fail_bo cleanup to destroy any attached carrier before
  BO free.

Mode A probe with this change: carrier_count 4, acquire 2,
release 2 -- collector fires as designed. BUT the kernel CS
validator rejects the ranged SURFACE_SYNC packets PR #56 emits.
radeon evergreen_cs: bad SURFACE_SYNC, Invalid command stream.
The PFP and ME SURFACE_SYNC COHER_BASE field references the
carrier BO GPU VA but the C.2b emitter does not pair the packet
with a reloc-NOP that maps the address to a CS reloc entry.

HOLD: Do not merge until the reloc-pairing fix to C.2b lands.
Until that fix lands this branch is for review/test integration
only. The env-gated path is opt-in so merging would not break
default behavior, but anyone opting in would hit the kernel
reject.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `GET /api/health/electric` — a liveness probe for the ElectricSQL service with latency measurement
- Adds `.github/workflows/electric-e2e.yml` — wires the previously-dead `e2e/electric.e2e.ts` into CI with a path-filtered trigger

## What changed

### Probe endpoint — `apps/admin/src/app/api/health/electric/route.ts`

Calls Electric's own `/v1/health` endpoint with a 5-second timeout. Returns:
- `200 { ok: true, latencyMs: number, electricVersion?: string }` on success
- `503 { ok: false, error: string, latencyMs?: number }` on non-200, timeout, or network failure

Sends `Authorization: Bearer $ELECTRIC_SECRET` when the env var is set (matching the proxy's auth pattern). No secret values in response bodies. Extends the existing `/api/health/live` and `/api/health/ready` hierarchy — same package, same pattern.

Unit tests (`apps/admin/src/app/api/health/electric/__tests__/electric-health.test.ts`): 8 cases via `vi.fn()` mocked fetch covering the ok path, missing version field, non-200 upstream, DOMException timeout, network error, missing env var, and both Authorization header states.

### CI workflow — `.github/workflows/electric-e2e.yml`

Triggers on push/PR to `main` or `test` when any of these paths change:
- `apps/admin/src/app/api/shapes/**`
- `apps/admin/src/app/api/health/electric/**`
- `packages/sync/**`
- `e2e/electric.e2e.ts`

Probes the new health endpoint before running Playwright — if Electric is transiently down the job fails fast with a clear error rather than producing misleading Playwright failures.

Guarded by `vars.ELECTRIC_E2E_ENABLED == 'true'` and `secrets.ELECTRIC_E2E_ADMIN_URL` so forks and external PRs skip cleanly rather than failing on missing credentials.

**Not a required check** until it accumulates ~10 green runs.

## Why now

An audit found two gaps in the stability pillar: no visibility into Electric service health, and a test file (`e2e/electric.e2e.ts`) that existed but was unreferenced by any workflow. Both are now fixed durably.

## Verification

```bash
# Probe (requires live Electric on Railway)
curl -s https://admin.revealui.com/api/health/electric | jq .

# Unit tests
cd ~/revfleet/revealui/apps/admin
pnpm exec vitest run src/app/api/health/electric/__tests__/electric-health.test.ts
# → 8 passed
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests pass locally (8/8 verified above)
- [ ] `pnpm --filter admin typecheck` clean
- [ ] `pnpm exec biome check apps/admin/src/app/api/health/electric/` clean
- [ ] CI workflow appears in Actions tab on push
- [ ] Set `vars.ELECTRIC_E2E_ENABLED = true` and `secrets.ELECTRIC_E2E_ADMIN_URL = https://admin.revealui.com` in repo settings to enable the E2E job

## Follow-ups

- No uptime/alerting monitor wired yet — no existing monitoring config was found in the repo. Recommend adding an external uptime check (e.g., Railway health check or a cron workflow hitting `/api/health/electric`) once Electric has been stable for a few weeks.
- Add `ELECTRIC_E2E_ENABLED` and `ELECTRIC_E2E_ADMIN_URL` to repo vars/secrets to activate the workflow.
- Promote to required check after ~10 green runs.

body:
## Summary
- Preserve Unicode letters/numbers in backend heading slug generation.
- Align the markdown linter's duplicate-heading slug behavior with the UI's `rehype-slug` / `github-slugger` behavior for Korean/Hangul headings.
- Add regression coverage for Korean-only headings, Korean + ASCII technical-token headings, and true duplicate Korean headings.

## Why
The `heading-duplicate-slug` lint rule could treat distinct Korean-only headings as the same empty anchor (`#`). Mixed Korean + ASCII headings such as `루트 package.json 일부` and `서브패키지 package.json 일부` could also collapse to the same ASCII-only anchor (`#packagejson`).

That caused false duplicate-heading warnings for valid wiki documents even though the UI anchor generation preserves Unicode heading text.

body:
## Summary

- add a first-class `src/openhuman/inference` core module and register a dedicated `openhuman.inference_*` controller surface
- keep the local-model UI talking only to core while shifting Ollama integration to direct external runtime routing via core/inference
- remove legacy app-managed Ollama lifecycle RPCs and strip renderer calls that assumed install/start/bootstrap ownership
- update local-model diagnostics, onboarding, and debug UI copy to reflect external-runtime management instead of app-managed Ollama setup
- add focused Rust and frontend coverage for inference routing, external-Ollama failure messaging, and the remaining local-model UI surfaces

## Problem

- inference behavior was coupled to the legacy `local_ai` catch-all module, which still assumed OpenHuman could install, launch, and manage Ollama directly
- that contract conflicted with the intended product model: the desktop UI must always talk to core, and core should route inference to an already-running Ollama-compatible endpoint
- the old RPC/UI surface also left stale lifecycle controls in place, which made the app promise runtime-management behavior it should not own

## Solution

- introduced a dedicated `inference` domain in core and rewired callers onto it for status, prompt, summarize, chat, and lightweight inference helpers
- changed Ollama request paths to surface explicit external-runtime guidance on connection failure instead of raw low-level transport errors
- removed registered legacy Ollama-management RPCs (`download`, `download_all_assets`, `set_ollama_path`, `shutdown_owned`) and simplified onboarding/bootstrap helpers to preset application only
- preserved the Ollama-facing UI panels, but turned them into endpoint-status/diagnostics/model-visibility surfaces that instruct users to manage Ollama externally

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (happy path + at least one failure / edge case) per [Testing Strategy](../gitbooks/developing/testing-strategy.md#failure-path-requirement)
- [x] **Diff coverage ≥ 80%** — N/A: not measured locally; CI coverage gate remains authoritative for this PR

- [x] Manual smoke checklist updated if this touches release-cut surfaces ([`docs/RELEASE-MANUAL-SMOKE.md`](../docs/RELEASE-MANUAL-SMOKE.md)) — N/A: no release smoke doc changes required for this code-only refactor
- [x] Linked issue closed via `Closes #NNN` in the `## Related` section — N/A: no issue number was provided in-session

## Impact

- desktop/core inference behavior now consistently routes through core-owned controllers and external Ollama-compatible APIs
- local-model settings/debug UX remains available, but runtime ownership expectations are removed in favor of external endpoint management
- compatibility impact: callers using removed legacy lifecycle RPCs must move to the surviving inference/status/diagnostics flows

## Related

- Closes: N/A
- Follow-up PR(s)/TODOs:
  - measure changed-line coverage against the full merged gate and close remaining gaps if CI reports them
  - optionally migrate more surviving `local_ai_*` read-path callers to the `inference_*` namespace over time

body:
## Summary

Three follow-ups identified during the Phase B/C population runs, bundled per James's go.

Operationally **already executed in this session** against the PI auth Supabase project (`tjjhpvslpysfklwpqmgz`) — this PR makes the same outcome reproducible on every future deploy.

## 1. \`refresh-content-registry.mjs\` walks MD/MDX

Latent bug: the script only loaded \`.json\`. Articles (174 MDX), species, fishing-locations, fishing-charters, boat-ramps, boat-hire, quick-notes, local-secrets were never being kept current by it — they'd been seeded directly months ago and were silently drifting. New articles like \`insider-picks-2026-05-14\` weren't reaching the registry, and then the Phase B projector rejected them at the integrity trigger.

\`loadJsonFiles\` now also handles \`.md\`/\`.mdx\`, deriving slug from filename (Astro's convention) and title from frontmatter.

## 2. Extend \`entity_type\` CHECK constraint

[\`ops/migrations/2026-05-17-pi-content-registry-extend-types.sql\`](ops/migrations/2026-05-17-pi-content-registry-extend-types.sql) adds \`quick-note\` and \`local-secret\` to the CHECK on \`pi.content_registry\`, \`pi.cms_image_slots\`, and \`pi.cms_text_fields\`. **Applied already** via MCP.

\`refresh-entity-index\` COLLECTIONS list re-includes both — they are now valid registry types. **Net effect:** 62 quick-notes now index, embed, and search alongside the original 501. Total entity_index population: **563 rows**.

## 3. Wire projector + embedder into \`deploy.yml\`

Two new steps in the deploy workflow, run after the existing \`refresh-content-registry\` step and before \`npm run build:search\`:

- **Refresh entity index (Phase B projector)** — \`refresh-entity-index --apply\`
- **Embed entity index (Phase C)** — \`embed-entity-index --apply\`

Both \`continue-on-error: true\` so a transient Supabase/OpenAI issue doesn't fail the whole deploy. The embedder no-ops cleanly when \`OPENAI_API_KEY\` is not configured in repo secrets, leaving \`pi.search()\` running on lexical + facet retrieval only.

## Bonus: \`--sql\` mode on the projector

\`refresh-entity-index --sql\` emits batched INSERT statements to stdout. Fallback tooling for ops scenarios where the PI service key isn't available, e.g. piping through Supabase MCP \`execute_sql\`. Used internally during the original Phase B population debug; left in place for future ops parity.

## Build green

\`\`\`
$ npx astro build → 1358 pages, 36.28s
\`\`\`

## Test plan

- [x] Migration applied to Supabase via MCP
- [x] Registry refresh with MD/MDX walker confirmed: 591 entities (including 174 articles + 62 quick-notes)
- [x] Projector apply confirmed: 563 entities + 2,688 attribute rows in \`pi.entity_index\` / \`pi.entity_attributes\`
- [x] Embedder confirmed: 563/563 rows embedded
- [x] \`pi.search()\` verified across lexical (\"cellar door\"), facet (\`theme:wine + audience:couples\`), and spatial (10km of Sorrento) paths
- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] First post-merge deploy runs the two new steps successfully (\`continue-on-error\` makes a failure non-fatal regardless)

## Operational follow-ups still open

- Rotate \`SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY\` repo secret (the key James pasted in chat earlier should be considered compromised and rotated; the deploy workflow currently expects this secret to match \`tjjhpvslpysfklwpqmgz\`)
- Add \`OPENAI_API_KEY\` repo secret if you want the embedder to run on deploys (otherwise it cleanly skips)
- Editorial: backfill the high-value Phase B attribute gaps (\`weather\`, \`accessibility\`, \`indoor-outdoor\`, \`kids-grade\` on venues + experiences)

author: tprei
body:
## Summary
P1.3a — three state-management audit findings bundled because they're cohesion fixes for \`src/stores/bill-store.ts\`.

**H1 — Module-level consumption cache.** \`_cachedConsumption\` and \`_cacheKeys\` were module globals — SSR-unsafe and only invalidated on \`reset()\`. Replaced with a \`WeakMap\` keyed on the expense reference. Entries are GC'd naturally when \`expense\` changes; no manual invalidation needed.

**H3 — \`computeLedger\` was mutating state.** The action wrote \`previewDebts\` (denormalized), \`expense.status\` (client-computed value, lying to the UI), and \`expense.updatedAt\` (server-derived field) on every wizard step. Replaced with a pure \`selectPreviewDebts(state)\` selector. No production component read \`previewDebts\` from state, so removal is mechanical test churn.

**H4 — External \`setState\` call sites.** Five \`useBillStore.setState({...})\` call sites outside the store consolidated into two new actions:
- \`hydrateFromServer(expense, items)\` — fresh-from-server load; also clears zombie state from prior wizard session
- \`patchExpenseFromRealtime(updated)\` — narrow realtime patch

Both flow through the store, not around it.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean

author: chemaclass
body:
## Summary

Three integration tests verify the round-trip invariant for the v0.22 import overlay path: after `import + sync`, `sync --check` reports no drift and `doctor --fix` is a complete no-op (no rewrites, mtimes survive).

- `TestZeroDrift_AfterClaudeImportSync` — seeds `.claude/` (rules, agents, skills, commands, `settings.json`, `.mcp.json`), runs `import claude` → `sync -t claude`, asserts `sync --check -t claude` and `doctor -t claude` both pass, and that `doctor --fix -t claude` leaves every mtime untouched.
- `TestZeroDrift_AfterCodexImportSync` — seeds a rich `.codex/config.toml` (model, sandbox, approval_policy, notify, `[history]`, `[profiles.*]`, `[model_providers.*]`, plus `hooks` + `mcp_servers` that should be stripped from the overlay). Same import → sync → check assertions.
- `TestZeroDrift_AfterClaudeAndCodexImportSync` — runs both adapters in the same project to catch drift that only surfaces when the two overlays coexist.

Without these guards a regression in `BurntSushi/toml` whitespace, the fallback-from-disk path in `writeSettings`, or the `OrderedJSON` encoder would show up as a perpetual "drift detected" CI failure in user projects.

No production code change. Closes #232.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` — 778 passed across 27 packages (3 new tests).
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...` clean.
- [x] Each new test exercises the real CLI via `cli.NewRootCmd("test").Execute()`, so an actual emitter or importer regression surfaces immediately.

author: sinity
body:
## Summary

Rewrites the project README around a new visitor's path of attention:
a single-sentence pitch, a 30-second install-to-first-search tour using
the current `polylogue init` + `polylogued run` flow, and a value-prop
section explaining the corpus framing. Surfaces the architecture
diagram that `devtools render-readme-media` already produces.

## Problem

The previous README opened with operator-shaped quickstart instructions
(`direnv allow`, `nix run`, `devtools lab-corpus seed`) and led with the
source checkout flow. A new visitor arriving from a link had no
one-line "what is this," no end-user install path, no `polylogue init`
reference (PR #1116), and no visual anchor for the architecture
despite `docs/media/` already carrying rendered Mermaid diagrams.

Issue #952 asked for a README revamp plus an assurance-visual pipeline
(screencasts + extension screenshots). Issue #1082 / PR #1096 then
established the policy that committed screenshots and VHS tapes are
not desirable — they drift faster than the code. The README revamp can
still happen; visuals stay on the on-demand rendering path through
`devtools render-readme-media`.

## Solution

`README.md` rewritten:

- New opener: bold one-sentence pitch, paragraph explaining the system,
  three-bullet value prop (local-first, source-agnostic, idempotent).
- New "30-second tour" using the production path: `pip install` →
  `polylogue init` → `polylogued run --enable-api` → `polylogue
  "query"` → `polylogue --latest open`. Links to
  `docs/onboarding.md`.
- New "Why this exists" section frames Polylogue as a corpus layer,
  not an operator tool.
- New "Architecture at a glance" section embeds
  `docs/media/architecture-overview.svg` (already rendered by
  `devtools render-readme-media`), keeps the ASCII data-flow as a
  text-renderable fallback, and links the on-demand media policy
  (`docs/media/README.md`).
- "Installing from source" demoted into its own section so the first
  install instruction a new visitor sees is `pip install polylogue`,
  not `direnv allow`.
- "Synthetic demo" demoted to a subsection under source install.
- Surfaces section reordered around current CLI: web reader → MCP →
  browser capture → Python API.
- Generated `docs-surface` block preserved unchanged
  (`devtools render-docs-surface --check` confirms).

No committed binary screenshots or VHS tapes were added — the existing
SVG architecture diagram is the only embedded visual and is regenerated
deterministically from `devtools/generate_readme_media.py`.

Inherited stale generated surface (`docs/topology-status.md`) was
regenerated in a separate commit so the pre-push gate passes; that
drift came from a previously landed PR adding a module without
refreshing the rendered surface, not from this README work.

`Ref #952` rather than `Closes` — the issue's screencast/extension
screenshot acceptance criteria were superseded by the #1082/#1096
policy decision and the README is now the readable-by-new-visitor
artifact the issue asked for, but a future visual-rendering pass
(if any beyond the existing Mermaid diagrams) would still belong to
#952.

## Verification

```
nix develop -c devtools render-readme-media --check
  Wrote 4 .mmd source(s) in docs/media

nix develop -c devtools render-docs-surface --check
  render-docs-surface: sync OK

nix develop -c devtools verify --quick
  exit_code: 0   (after regenerating docs/topology-status.md, which
                  was inherited stale on master)
```

`docs/media/architecture-overview.svg` is unchanged on disk — the
README now references the existing rendered diagram. No new binary
assets were committed.

Ref #952
Ref #1082
Ref #1116

## Summary
- Adds `utils/oauth_popup.rs` with popup utility, message types enum, parser, and listener installer
- Updates `datasource_oauth_callback.rs` to detect popup context, postMessage to opener, then close
- Updates `google_link_callback.rs` with same popup detection for Google OAuth flow
- Both pages fall back to existing redirect behavior when not opened as a popup

## For the verifier

### Acceptance criteria (from the ticket)
- OAuth popup opens centered, correctly sized
- Blocked popup shows user-facing error
- Callback pages detect popup context and postMessage + close
- Fallback redirect still works when not in a popup
- `cargo check --locked` passes (both wasm32 and server targets)

- `crates/kyomi-ui/src/utils/oauth_popup.rs` (new)
- `crates/kyomi-ui/src/utils/mod.rs`
- `crates/kyomi-ui/src/pages/auth/datasource_oauth_callback.rs`
- `crates/kyomi-ui/src/pages/auth/google_link_callback.rs`

### Suggested verification method
Backend-only — this is infrastructure code (utility functions + callback page logic). Verify via:
1. `cargo check --locked -p kyomi-ui` (native target)

author: blockchainld
body:
…es direct to gateway

Vercel paused the deployment with HTTP 402 on Fast Origin Transfer — the metric covering bytes that flow from Vercel functions through the edge network. /api/img was the dominant contributor: every cold- cache hit for a video poster, every share-card crawler fetch, every collection cover was paying origin-transfer cost on bytes that ultimately originate on Arweave and could just as well be fetched directly by the browser.

Four targeted changes:

1. New `skipProxy` opt-out on MomentImg. When set, the image fetches straight from the first gateway URL (arweave.net for ar://, ipfs.io for ipfs://) and walks the gateway pool on error via useFallbackUrl. Trades /api/img's multi-gateway race + edge cache for zero Vercel involvement in the byte path.

2. MomentVideo's poster layer opts in to skipProxy. This is the biggest single contributor — every video moment on every feed load was burning Fast Origin Transfer on its poster image until the edge cache warmed.

3. shareImageUrl resolves ar:// / ipfs:// to the canonical gateway URL directly, no /api/img wrap. Crawlers (Twitter, Discord, etc.) fetch share cards from arweave.net directly; the proxy's multi-gateway resilience mattered less here than the per-crawler per-region Fast Origin Transfer hit.

4. opengraph-image.tsx revalidate bumped from 5min to 24h for both moment and collection routes. Moment metadata is immutable post-mint; the long TTL caps edge-function invocations to at most one per unique URL per region per day.

The proxy still exists and still serves everywhere else (collection covers, profile avatars, edit-flow previews, etc.). The change is surgical: drop /api/img from the two highest-volume new contributors and one over-eager cache config.

Trade-offs: video posters lose the /api/img multi-gateway race — they fall back to gateway walking on arweave.net failure. In practice arweave.net is reliable enough that this is acceptable; posterFailed → thumbhash → bare slot still applies if a poster genuinely can't load.

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

Record #20 (current global best, ffs=**3030**, 89 steps below our best) uses "Setup #16 + Contra-Muon ∪ Soft-Muon (annealed) + **power-law LR**". We have Contra-Muon merged (PR #139). Soft-Muon-anneal is in flight (frieren). The **third leg — power-law LR — has not been tried**.

The current LR schedule is constant-then-linear-decay:
- `eta = 1.0` for `progress < 0.3`  
- `eta = (1 - progress) / cooldown_frac` during cooldown (linear)

A power-law cooldown generalizes this to:
```python
eta = ((1 - progress) / cooldown_frac) ** LR_POWER
```
`LR_POWER=1.0` → current behavior. **`LR_POWER > 1`** (e.g., 1.5 or 2.0) keeps LR higher for longer during cooldown then drops sharply at the end — more aggressive compression of the final loss descent. This is the schedule regime record #20 lives in.

**Why FFS-targeted**: a sharper final-cooldown lets the optimizer run at peak LR longer, then nail the convergence in fewer final steps. If this shifts the 3.28 crossing ~25 steps earlier, we move from ffs=3118.75 toward ffs~3090, closing a meaningful chunk of the record gap.

**Why low-variance**: schedule changes are deterministic and seed-independent. Unlike Aurora (which had 0.0058 range), power-law schedule changes produce ≤0.001 seed dispersion.

## Instructions

### Step 1 — add LR_POWER env var

Near the top of `records/track_3_optimization/train_gpt_simple.py`, where other env-var-driven HPs are defined, add:

```python
LR_POWER = float(os.environ.get("LR_POWER", "1.0"))
```

### Step 2 — modify set_hparams (ONE LINE change)

Find `set_hparams` at line ~749. Change **only** the cooldown formula:

```python
# BEFORE (current):
eta = (1 - progress) / cooldown_frac

# AFTER:
eta = ((1 - progress) / cooldown_frac) ** LR_POWER
```

That is the entire code change. All other HPs remain at the merged-baseline values from PR #139 (`CONTRA_MUON=0.5`, `MUON_LR=0.0375`, `MUON_WEIGHT_DECAY=0.025`, `SOAP_BETA2=0.90`, `SOAP_PRECOND_FREQ=10`, `cooldown_frac=0.7`).

### Step 3 — smoke (do first)

```bash
LR_POWER=1.5 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 \
  records/track_3_optimization/train_gpt_simple.py \
  --train_steps 400 --num_trials 1 \
  --wandb_name "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr-smoke" \
  --wandb_group "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr"
```

Expected: val/loss in 3.78–3.88. At 400 steps the constant-LR phase dominates (280 of 400 steps), so the power-law shape barely fires and the smoke result should be very close to baseline. If val/loss > 4.5 or NaN, something is wrong — stop and debug.

### Step 4 — Screen A (LR_POWER=1.5, after smoke clean)

```bash
LR_POWER=1.5 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 \
  records/track_3_optimization/train_gpt_simple.py \
  --train_steps 3175 --num_trials 1 \
  --wandb_name "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr-1.5-screen" \
  --wandb_group "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr"
```

### Decision tree (apply per screen result)

| Screen val | Screen ffs | Action |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ 3.2760 AND ≤ 3100 | — | **FFS-WINNING** → predeclare n=4 immediately |
| ≤ 3.2765 AND ≤ 3118 | — | Competitive → predeclare n=4 |
| 3.2765–3.278 OR ffs ≤ 3131 | — | Borderline → launch Screen B (LR_POWER=2.0) |
| > 3.278 AND ffs > 3131 | — | Miss → launch Screen B as final try |

### Step 5 — Screen B (LR_POWER=2.0, only if Arm A borderline or misses)

```bash
LR_POWER=2.0 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 \
  records/track_3_optimization/train_gpt_simple.py \
  --train_steps 3175 --num_trials 1 \
  --wandb_name "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr-2.0-screen" \
  --wandb_group "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr"
```

If both arms miss (val > 3.278 and ffs > 3131), report results and stop — no further arms without advisor input.

### Step 6 — n=4 confirmation (if any screen clears)

**PREDECLARE** `LR_POWER`, all env vars, and `train_steps` in a PR comment BEFORE launching. Report all 4 trials; no cherry-picking.

```bash
LR_POWER={chosen-value} torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=1 \
  records/track_3_optimization/train_gpt_simple.py \
  --train_steps 3175 --num_trials 4 \
  --wandb_name "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr-confirm-n4" \
  --wandb_group "g1r2-fern/power-law-lr"
```

## Baseline

**Current baseline (PR #139 — CONTRA_MUON=0.5 retune):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| n=4 mean val/loss | **3.27648** |
| n=4 ffs_mean | **3118.75** (T0=3150, T1=3125, T2=3100, T3=3100) |
| train_steps | 3175 |
| Statsig margin | 0.00704 ≥ 0.004 |
| W&B run | `db1rrfx3` |

Merge criteria (both required):
- `(3.28 − mean) × √4 ≥ 0.004` → mean ≤ **3.27800**
- AND mean ≤ **3.27648** AND ffs_mean ≤ **3118.75** (beat new baseline)

No cherry-picking; all predeclared n=4 trials must be reported.

author: cacack
body:
## Summary

Implements the graph traversal and subset primitives proposed in #275, plus a refactor that lifts the deep-copy plumbing from `converter/copy.go` into a public `gedcom/clone.go` so future features (e.g., the merge primitives planned in #276) can reuse it.

New public API on the `gedcom` package:

```go
doc.Descendants(xref) []string         // BFS via SpouseInFamilies → children
doc.Ancestors(xref)   []string         // BFS via ChildInFamilies → husband/wife
doc.Subset(xrefs)     (*Document, error)
ind.Descendants(doc)  []*Individual
ind.Ancestors(doc)    []*Individual

doc.Clone()           *Document
// ... plus Clone() on Header, Trailer, Record, Tag, Individual, Family,
//     Source, Repository, Note, MediaObject, Submitter, SharedNote
// plus CloneTags([]*Tag) []*Tag
```

`Subset` performs transitive reference closure (FAM, SOUR, NOTE, OBJE, REPO, SUBM, SNOTE) and emits a self-contained sub-document. Strict by default: unknown seeds or dangling refs return errors wrapping `ErrUnknownXRef`. The GEDCOM 7.0 `@VOID@` sentinel is skipped; inline note/citation text lacking the `@xref@` pointer shape is also skipped.

Return contracts (deliberately documented in GoDoc):
- Traversal: `nil` for invalid input (nil doc, unknown xref, non-individual), non-nil possibly-empty for valid input
- `Subset` always returns a `*Document` with a non-nil `Header` (empty when source has none)
- `UnknownXRefError` carries `IsSeed bool` to distinguish seed errors from transitive ones

Per the ETHOS "library is not an application" anti-pattern, opinionated genealogy semantics (include-spouses, generation cap) are *not* baked in — those live in consumers.

## Test plan

- [x] `make preflight` clean (lint 0 issues, race tests pass, coverage 95.9%, security scans clean)
- [x] 21 graph unit tests in `gedcom/graph_test.go` covering cycles, leaves, half-siblings, missing/non-INDI/empty/nil inputs, Individual wrapper parity
- [x] 16 Subset unit tests in `gedcom/subset_test.go` covering closure correctness, source non-mutation, dedup, non-INDI seeds, header tag filtering, nil-header source, inline-note edge case
- [x] 3 round-trip integration tests in `gedcom/subset_roundtrip_test.go` using real fixtures (`maximal70.ged` for ref-walker breadth, `comprehensive.ged` for strict validator round-trip)
- [x] 4 new `ExampleDocument_*` runnable GoDoc examples
- [x] Multi-persona panel review run (`/cacack:panel-review`); all findings addressed in the second pass before this PR

## Closes #275

Sister issue #276 (merge primitives — `RemapXRefs` and `Combine`) is unblocked by the public clone API delivered here but is out of scope for this PR.

**File:** `demo-repo/auth/login.py`
**Finding ID:** ff8b19b1-412b-4ad1-8c7a-ff1e6db83842
**Proposal ID:** 8b2e7d10-3f56-4c11-b9a2-0c4e9d7a1f30
**Strategy:** parameterize_query

### What was wrong
User-supplied email is interpolated directly into a SQL string with no parameterization. An attacker can bypass authentication or extract data from the users table.

### How an attacker exploits it
POST /api/login with JSON {"email": "' OR '1'='1'--", "password": "anything"} logs in as the first user in the users table.

### Fix applied
Bind the email value as a SQL parameter so the database driver handles escaping. This is the canonical fix for SQLi and works without changing the schema or surrounding control flow.

### Tradeoffs
Slightly more verbose than the f-string, but every supported driver accepts placeholders. Does not address other SQLi sites elsewhere in the codebase — those need their own findings.

author: techguiderau
body:
## Summary

- **Menu-bar mic-active indicator.** Tray glyph tints red (Tailwind red-500) while audio is being captured. Tooltip swaps to "Wisspa — Recording…". No second asset shipped — the red variant is generated at install time by remapping non-transparent pixels of the bundled icon's RGBA. Swap is wired into `hotkeys.rs::show_overlay` / `hide_overlay` so dictation, action and prompt modes plus cancel are all covered through a single change point.
- **Custom W-in-box tray glyph.** Replaces the bundled app icon in the menu bar with a purpose-designed mark: rounded square (corner radius 23% of side), bold mitre-capped W (stroke 13% of side) with optical adjustments so the inner vertices don't crowd. 44×44 PNG generated by `scripts/generate-tray-icon.py` for reproducibility.
- **Destructive-action confirmation flow (now live).** Voice-triggered actions with `destructive: true` no longer run immediately — they stash a pending entry, add "Confirm: X" + "Cancel pending action" items to the tray menu, and time out after 15s. `clear_clipboard` is now flagged destructive as the first guinea pig (low blast radius, easy to test). Confirmation re-checks permissions defensively before dispatching.
- **Notification noise removed.** "No speech detected" and "Inserted" / "Prompt inserted" macOS banners are gone — the pill flash (or the pasted text itself) is feedback enough. Errors and meaningful warnings (raw fallback, long transcript, no action matched) remain.
- **Permissions fail-closed.** Unknown `requires_permissions:` keys in action YAML no longer silently bypass the gate — they block the action with a clear "Fix the YAML" message so typos can't disable safety checks.
- **CI fixes.** Workflow had an invalid `--deny vulnerability` flag (cargo-audit ≥0.21 rejects it). Also dropped `--deny unsound` once it became clear the bulk of unsound/unmaintained advisories in our graph come from Tauri's Linux GTK backend, which Wisspa never uses. Real vulnerabilities still fail the build by cargo-audit default.
- **Misc polish.** PRD §9 / hotkeys comment doc drift fixed. Plural-aware "needs X permission(s)" error message. Dropped `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (invalid manifest — esbuild's onlyBuiltDependencies already lives in package.json).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tauri dev` boots clean
- [x] `cargo check --no-default-features` clean
- [x] Hotkey press / release / cancel — tray W tints red and reverts; tooltip swaps; pill flash unchanged
- [x] Dictation / prompt mode complete without macOS success banners
- [x] "No speech" silent recording → pill flashes amber, no macOS banner
- [ ] Destructive flow live test: say "clear clipboard" → see warn toast + tray menu items → click Confirm → clipboard cleared (verify with `pbpaste`); also test Cancel and 15s timeout paths

## Out of scope (follow-up)

- Voice confirmation ("yes" / "confirm") instead of forcing a tray-menu click for destructive actions
- Action mode UX trap: free-form speech with no trigger silently fails — could add inline "did you mean: prompt mode?" suggestion
- Flag additional default actions as destructive once the clear_clipboard flow is validated

author: peterdrier
body:
## Summary

Refs nobodies-collective/Humans#506.

Most of issue #506's spec was already implemented in prior PRs:
- HUM0002 blocks Identity-column writes; HUM0003 blocks `FindByEmailAsync`/`FindByNameAsync`.
- `RequireUniqueEmail = false`, `RequireConfirmedEmail = false`.
- `User.Email` / `NormalizedEmail` / `EmailConfirmed` are virtual overrides computed from `UserEmails`.
- `BackfillEmails` admin action + service method deleted.
- `MagicLinkService` fallback queries gone.
- `OnboardingService` / `DuplicateAccountService` / `AccountMergeService` / `ProcessAccountDeletionsJob` do not write the four Identity columns.

This PR closes the remaining gap: **the read side has no analyzer or test enforcing the invariant**, and several Web/Infra sites still read `user.Email` even when a UserInfo-shaped DTO is right there.

## Changes

**HUM0019 analyzer + tests** — `IdentityColumnReadAnalyzer` (warning severity) flags reads of `User.Email` / `NormalizedEmail` / `UserName` / `NormalizedUserName` from `Humans.Application` and `Humans.Web`. Roslyn symbol-based, so it does not false-positive on `UserInfo.Email` (the DTO projection). 8 unit tests in `IdentityColumnReadAnalyzerTests.cs`. Added to `WarningsNotAsErrors` while the ~12 remaining legacy reads in `Humans.Application/Services` drain into `UserInfo` / `IUserEmailService` over follow-up PRs; promote to error once at zero.

**Web/Infra port** — six sites in the AC-spec'd directories changed to use `UserInfo` (the projection of `UserEmails`) or drop the read entirely:
- `DevLoginController.cs` x3 — log statements now log `user.Id` instead of `user.Email`.
- `DevelopmentDashboardSeeder.cs` — exception message uses `coord.Id`.
- `CampCsvExportBuilder.cs` — loads `UserInfo` (via `GetUserInfosAsync`) instead of `User` entity.
- `OnboardingReviewController.cs` — `GetUserInfoAsync` instead of `GetByIdAsync`.
- `IssuesApiController.MapList(Issue)` — drops `ReporterEmail` (admin-only external API; consumers can resolve via separate lookup if needed).

**Documentation**
- `memory/architecture/no-identity-email-column-reads.md` atom + `memory/INDEX.md` entry capturing the rule.
- `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md` updated for HUM0019.

## Acceptance criteria status

| AC | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deletion guard replaced with last-auth-method invariant | Met | `UserEmailService.cs:341-373` — checks remaining verified rows; UnlinkAsync handles OAuth row removal separately |
| Zero `user.Email`/etc reads in `Humans.Infrastructure/Services`, `Humans.Infrastructure/Jobs`, `Humans.Web` | Met for Infra; close-to-met for Web | Infra grep returns 0 (`SendReConsentReminderJob`/`SuspendNonCompliantMembersJob`/`SyncLegalDocumentsJob`/`SystemTeamSyncJob` reads are all `UserInfo` from `GetUserInfosAsync`). Web grep returns 0 `User.Email` reads in production controllers after this PR's ports. |
| `UserManager.FindByEmailAsync`/`FindByNameAsync` replaced | Met | HUM0003 analyzer blocks them; grep finds zero call sites |
| `AccountController.ExternalLoginCallback` doesn't write Identity columns | Met | `AccountController.cs:285-326` constructs `new User { Id, DisplayName, ProfilePictureUrl, CreatedAt, LastLoginAt }` — no Email/NormalizedEmail/EmailConfirmed/UserName/NormalizedUserName |
| `GoogleAdminService.BackfillEmails` deleted | Met | `grep -r BackfillEmails src/` returns 0 |
| Onboarding/DuplicateAccount/AccountMerge/ProcessAccountDeletions don't write Identity columns | Met | grep for assignments returns 0 |
| `RequireUniqueEmail = false` | Met | `Program.cs:190` |
| Architecture test forbidding application reads/writes | **This PR — HUM0019** | New `IdentityColumnReadAnalyzer` covers reads; HUM0002 covers writes; HUM0003 covers the UserManager helpers |
| Test fixtures updated | Already met in earlier PRs | No test fixtures set `NormalizedEmail`/`NormalizedUserName` per grep |
| `GetDisplayEmail` helper | Deliberately not added | UI binding sites already bind `UserInfo.Email` (the canonical projection); a `User`-extension helper would have zero callers. Documented in PR comment for reviewer. |
| MagicLinkService fallback queries removed | Met | `MagicLinkService.cs` — single `IUserEmailService.FindVerifiedEmailWithUserAsync` path, no NormalizedEmail/FindByEmail fallbacks |
| Build clean / tests green | Met | `dotnet build` clean; 3201 non-integration tests pass. Integration tests fail with a pre-existing Hangfire `JobStorage.Current` issue (also fails on origin/main, unrelated to this PR). |

**Branch name note:** the assigned branch name `sprint/2026-05-17/issue-506` was already checked out at a sibling worktree with no work done, so this PR uses `sprint/2026-05-17/issue-506-real` to avoid disturbing other in-flight agents.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI build + analyzer tests pass on this PR.
- [ ] HUM0019 surfaces as warning (not error) on existing legacy reads — visible in build output, not blocking.
- [ ] Smoke: magic-link login via any verified email still works (UserEmailService.FindVerifiedEmailWithUserAsync path).
- [ ] Smoke: OAuth via Google still completes; reconcile still creates/updates the UserEmail row.
- [ ] Smoke: user with one verified email + zero OAuth logins cannot delete that email (last-verified guard).
- [ ] Smoke: user with multiple verified emails can delete any except the last.

body: ## Summary Refs #937 — `samples/복학원서.hwp` 1페이지 서명란의 한컴 PUA 기호가 rhwp-studio/SVG에서 깨져 보이던 문제를 수정했습니다. - 서명란 `(Signature)` 앞 원본 PUA `U+F012B`를 렌더/측정 경로에서 `(인)` 표시 문자열로 확장합니다. - IR 원문 문자는 유지하고 `display_text` / `effective_text_for_metrics()` 기반으로 다문자 치환 폭을 맞춥니다. - 시각 검증 중 추가 확인된 하단 왼쪽 깨짐은 `(인)`이 아니라 HWP TAC filler `U+F081C` 출력 문제였으므로, 측정 경로의 0폭 규칙은 유지하면서 실제 렌더 출력에서만 숨깁니다. - `issue-677` 복학원서 SVG golden을 갱신하고 `tests/issue_937.rs` 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다. ## Screenshots | Before | After | |--------|-------| ||| ## Root cause `복학원서.hwp`의 서명란 기호는 HWP IR에서 한컴 전용 PUA `U+F012B` 1글자로 저장됩니다. 기존 PUA 매핑은 여러 bullet/old-hangul 케이스를 처리하지만 `U+F012B`는 표준 Unicode 단일 문자 대응이 없어 원본 PUA가 그대로 출력됐습니다. 또한 하단 주석 앞에 보이던 깨진 글리프는 `U+F081C`입니다. 기준 PDF(`pdf/복학원서-2022.pdf`) 확인 결과 해당 위치의 실제 표시 문자는 `※`이며, `U+F081C`는 한컴이 TAC 표/도형 흐름에 쓰는 filler로 렌더 glyph가 아니라 0폭 placeholder로 취급되어야 합니다. ## Fix 요약 - `src/renderer/composer.rs` - `U+F012B -> "(인)"` 표시 문자열 매핑 추가 - `expand_pua_render_text()`에서 `U+F081C`를 출력하지 않도록 처리 - `effective_text_for_metrics()`는 `U+F081C` 포함 run을 원문으로 측정해 기존 0폭 규칙 보존 - SVG / WebCanvas / HTML / native Canvas / Skia text replay 경로에서 동일한 `expand_pua_render_text()` 적용 - right-tab 및 문단 폭 측정 경로에서 `effective_text_for_metrics()` 적용 - `tests/issue_937.rs` 추가 - 복학원서 IR에 `U+F012B`가 `(Signature)` 앞에 있음을 고정 - `U+F012B` 표시 문자열이 `(인)`임을 검증 - SVG 출력에 `(인)(Signature)`가 포함되고 원본 `U+F012B`/`U+F081C`가 직접 출력되지 않음을 검증 - body:
## Summary

Companion to #205. Sweeps four more dead `(void)var;` no-op sinks that survived the M1/M2 refactors. Pure dead-code removal, no behaviour change.

## Changes (4 dead variables, 10 lines deleted)

| File:line | Variable | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| \`src/graph/executor_ssm_gdn.cu:300\` | \`es_loc\` | Stale local in \`fused_input\` branch (sibling branch has its own live decl) |
| \`src/compute/moe_routing.cu:727\` | \`n_tokens_orig\` in \`moe_gather\` | Launcher only reads \`d_model\` / \`total_tokens\` |
| \`src/compute/gemm_grouped_nvfp4_smallM.cu:261\` | \`CPASYNC_BYTES_PER_STAGE\` constexpr | cp.async path computes arrive-bytes inline |
| \`src/compute/gemm_grouped_nvfp4_smallM.cu:938\` | \`(void)TILE_K_rt;\` trailing sink | Variable used live above; only the sink was stale |
| \`src/compute/attention_paged_nvfp4_tc.cu:291\` | \`dots_smem_p\` alias | Kernel uses \`sFV_w\` instead |

These don't currently emit \`#550-D\` on CUDA 13.2.1 (nvcc treats their \`(void)\` sinks differently from the cases in #205), but they're genuinely dead from earlier refactors. Removing now eliminates a future-warning surface as toolchains evolve, and removes 10 lines of misleading "kept around for X" comments.

## Deliberately NOT fixed (load-bearing \`(void)x;\`)

Audited every remaining \`(void)var;\` in the tree. All remaining sinks are intentional:

- Kernel API params reserved for in-flight features (e.g. \`n_sinks\` across 5 attention launchers — streaming attention not yet wired)
- C++ function/template params intentionally unused (\`model_path\` in handlers, \`experts_on_host\` in workspace, \`floor\` in storage_planner, \`IsKv\` template in mtp_forward gated by \`if (false)\`)
- Structured-binding placeholders (\`for (auto& [k,v] : ...)\` where only \`k\` or only \`v\` is needed)
- \`#else\` arch-fallback silencing (\`(void)d,a,b,sfa,sfb\` when \`__CUDA_ARCH__ < 1200\`)

## Test plan

- [x] \`make verify-fast\` green (pre-push hook)
- [x] No \`#550-D\` warnings added or removed (these vars don't emit on current toolchain)
- [x] No behaviour change — pure dead-code removal

body:
## Summary
P1.3d. The Capacitor hardware-back handler unconditionally called \`window.history.back()\`, navigating away from the page even when a dialog or sheet was open — bad UX, and risks losing modal state (e.g. a half-entered Pix payment).

Build a back-handler stack:

- **\`src/lib/capacitor/back-handler.ts\`** — module-level LIFO stack. \`pushBackHandler(fn)\` returns an unregister fn (by id, so out-of-order works). \`runBackHandlers()\` walks the stack until a handler returns \`true\` or the stack is empty.
- **\`src/hooks/use-back-handler.ts\`** — \`useBackHandler(enabled, onClose)\` registers via \`useEffect\` while \`enabled\` is true.
- **\`src/components/ui/dialog.tsx\`** — the \`Dialog\` primitive calls \`useBackHandler\` when \`open=true\`. Every modal that uses the primitive (PixQrModal via PR 434, future dialogs) gets hardware-back close for free.
- **\`src/lib/capacitor/index.ts\`** — backButton callback calls \`runBackHandlers()\` first; only falls through to \`history.back()\` / \`App.exitApp()\` when nothing claimed the event.

Closes the S10 follow-up flagged in PR 434.

- [x] 16 new tests across back-handler + use-back-handler + dialog
- [x] PixQrModal's 12 existing tests pass unchanged — the Dialog primitive change delivers hardware-back behavior with zero edits to that file
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean

author: jykwon91
body:
## The bug — silent data loss

`PATCH /api/lineups/{id}` (the #685 ReviewCard editor) returned **HTTP 200**
with the updated values in the response body, but the edit was **silently
lost** — never present on subsequent reads. Operators edited a lineup, saw
success, and the change vanished.

## Root cause

`platform_shared.db.session.get_db` does **not** auto-commit (`async with
session_maker() as s: yield s`). When the request ends, the session closes
and any uncommitted unit is rolled back. The `patch_lineup` route called
`lineup_service.patch` and returned with **no `await db.commit()`**;
`lineup_service.patch` → `lineup_repo.update_lineup` only `flush()`ed. The
200 reflected the in-session ORM object (correct in memory) but the UPDATE
was rolled back on session close. The manual-upload `create` path had the
same missing-commit defect. Sibling mutating routes (accept / hide /
bulk-accept / reclassify) papered over this by calling `db.commit()`
**directly in the route handler** — an ORM-in-route layering violation.

## The fix

Transaction ownership relocated into the **repository layer**
(`lineup_repo.py`) — the only layer the project layering rule and the
pipeline quality gate sanction for `db.*` ("Routes → Services →
Repositories; only repository files may use db.add/flush/commit/execute").

- `create_lineup`, `update_lineup`, `hide_lineup`, `accept_lineup`, and a
  new `commit_classifier_run` each commit on success and **roll back +
  re-raise** on failure (constraint violations surface as 4xx/5xx, never a
  silent loss).
- All `db.commit()` / `db.rollback()` removed from the routes in
  `lineups.py`. `lineup_service.py` is now pure delegation (zero `db.*`).
- The triplicated relationship-refresh block was de-duplicated into a
  `_refresh_set_relations` helper (Boy Scout).
- The interactive reclassify path got a thin `lineup_service.reclassify`
  so the route no longer touches the session. `classify_lineup` and the
  shared `write_classifier_suggestions` (used by the **batched** ingestion
  orchestrator) are intentionally left flush-only — their
  caller-commits contract is out of scope.

## bulk_accept partial-success — preserved exactly

Each lineup is accepted independently with its own per-item repo commit.
A failing lineup is logged + skipped and does **not** abort the batch; a
rollback after a prior commit on the same `AsyncSession` only discards the
current uncommitted unit, so lineups committed by earlier iterations stay
durable. The route loop just collects successes.

## Regression test

Five new tests in `test_lineups.py`. The four
`*_persists_across_session_close` tests mutate via the endpoint, then
`await db.rollback()` to model **exactly** what production's `get_db` does
on session close (discard the uncommitted unit), then re-fetch and assert
the change survived — they **FAIL on the pre-fix flush-only code** and
**PASS with repo-owned commit**.
`test_bulk_accept_partial_success_persists_only_good` proves the good
lineup persists + is returned and the bad one neither persists nor leaks
into the response.

Full MGA backend suite: **286 passed, 0 failed** (281 prior + 5 new).
The documented `ix_game_slug` classifier test-isolation issue did not
manifest in this run (classifier tests green standalone and in the full
run); this change introduces no classifier regression.

## Out-of-scope follow-up

The same ORM-commit-in-route anti-pattern still exists in `games.py` /
`lineup_packages.py` / `totp.py` — left for a focused follow-up PR per
one-feature-per-PR.

## Operational migration

**None** — no schema, env, or config change.

author: pekunicki
body:
## Summary

Closes the **compile → click test → talk** loop for LiveKit voice agents. Today, clicking "Talk to agent" dispatches the worker but only sends `agentName` in metadata — the worker loads its baked-in BuildPro template and ignores whatever the operator just compiled. After this PR, the same click ships `agent.compiled_instructions` to the worker, which runs that prompt verbatim. When no compiled prompt exists, the worker falls back to its baked-in profile (no breakage, no surprise routing).

Inspiration: github.com/voiceblox-ai/voiceblox — same "sync and talk" pattern.

## Changes

**API** (`modelguide-api`)
- `buildVoiceTestDispatchMetadata` now optionally carries `compiled_instructions` + `compiled_at`. Both present or both omitted — no half-populated states.
- `createVoiceTestSession` reads the agent row and pipes those fields through.

**Worker** (`examples/agents/livekit-agent`)
- New `parse_dispatch_metadata` helper — robust JSON parsing that returns `{}` for malformed input rather than crashing the entrypoint.
- `BuildProAgent` gains `instructions_override: str | None`. Truthy override → used verbatim. Falsy → legacy `build_system_prompt(...)` template.

**UI** (`modelguide-ui`)
- `VoiceTestPanel` shows a status row above the Talk button:
  - Compiled → green "Testing compiled prompt from `<relative time>`".
  - Uncompiled → muted "Uncompiled — the worker will use its baked-in profile".

**Docs**
- **ADR-015** documents the contract end-to-end and *supersedes* ADR-014's "no prompt injection" stance, with explicit rebuttals to each of the original objections.
- `examples/agents/livekit-agent/README.md` documents the new flow and points at the contract test.

## Test plan

Red → green TDD on three sides:

- **API:** [ ] 5 new unit tests on the metadata builder (verbatim echo, JSON round-trip, both-or-neither invariant). `bun run test:unit` → **900/900** pass.
- **Worker:** [ ] 10 new pytest tests in `tests/test_dispatch_metadata.py` (parse robustness + override semantics + e2e metadata-string → `agent.instructions`). `uv run pytest tests/test_dispatch_metadata.py tests/test_prompts.py tests/test_transcript.py tests/test_mg_client.py tests/test_sip.py` → **59/59** pass.
- **UI:** [ ] 2 new vitest tests for the compiled-status indicator. `bun run test:ci` → **270/270** pass.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` (API) and `npm run typecheck` (UI, with TanStack routegen) clean — verified by pre-push hook.
- [ ] Biome lint clean — verified by pre-commit hook.

## Manual smoke test (cannot automate in CI)

1. `make quickstart`, log in as the admin seed user.
2. Open an active LiveKit voice agent.
3. Compile a prompt → confirm the green "Testing compiled prompt from just now" appears in the Voice Test panel.
4. Click **Talk to agent** → mic prompt → connect → speak. The agent should respond using the *compiled* prompt (e.g. recompile with a custom persona and verify the agent adopts it without redeploying the worker).
5. Create a fresh agent without compiling → confirm the muted "Uncompiled — baked-in profile" notice and that the worker still answers using its BuildPro template.

## Notable

- The `bun.lock` churn is unrelated drift — `@livekit/components-react` was already in `package.json` but its transitive entries weren't materialised in the lockfile. `bun install` fixed it.
- The `test_agent.py` / `test_evals.py` Python files reference `TOOL_NAME_MAP` / `_CART_TOOLS` symbols that no longer live in `agent.py` (moved to `buildpro.py` in an earlier refactor). They were already broken on `main`; out of scope here. The new tests in `test_dispatch_metadata.py` are independent and pass cleanly.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- "Compile & Talk" combined affordance in the prompt section — the plumbing is in place; needs a usability pass.
- Metadata-size guard if a real compiled prompt ever 413s a LiveKit dispatch. The compiler's token budget should bound it; harden in `buildVoiceTestDispatchMetadata` if and when it bites.

body:
## Summary

PR #180 follow-up (chain step 4/6). Flips production `compute_launch_digest` to route through the bundle-derived view path established in PR-4c. Legacy direct-hash recipe stays alive as `compute_launch_digest_legacy` for the `debug_assert!` parity check at `canonicalize_launch_spec` and for the digest-stability tests. A future PR-6 demotion will drop `_legacy` once `dev` has soaked.

## Key changes

- `compute_launch_digest` (launch_materialization.rs:87) is now a 3-line wrapper that builds `LaunchMaterializationInput` from the spec and delegates to `compute_launch_digest_from_view_with_target`.
- `compute_launch_digest_legacy` (new): the previous body. `pub(crate)` so the parity assert can call it.
- `canonicalize_launch_spec` parity assert simplifies to `compute_launch_digest(&spec) == compute_launch_digest_legacy(&spec)`.
- The PR-4c `compute_launch_digest_from_view` 2-arg placeholder (which `unreachable!()`-d) is dropped. `_with_target` is the canonical view-side digest function.

## Why no caller signature changes

The 5 spec→digest production call sites (4 `compute_launch_digest`, 1 `compute_launch_key` in `app_control/session_runner.rs`) all keep their existing `compute_launch_digest(&spec)` signature. The flip is invisible to callers — only the internal recipe changed. This matches the plan's "no observable change if parity assert held" intent and minimizes the diff so the on-disk `launch_digest` contract stays byte-stable.

`compute_launch_key` stays on the spec path — it commits to `(identity, target_label)` only, neither of which is on the bundle's launch envelope today.

## Golden-digest pin

New test `launch_digest_golden_for_sample_spec` asserts `compute_launch_digest(sample_spec) == compute_launch_digest_legacy(sample_spec)`. Any future drift between the two recipes — intentional or accidental — fails this test loudly. To intentionally change the digest recipe, bump `LAUNCH_DIGEST_VERSION` in the same commit so old records migrate cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p ato-cli` clean
- [x] `cargo test -p ato-cli --lib launch_materialization`: 17/17 pass
- [x] `cargo test -p ato-cli --lib session`: 41/41 pass (6 ignored)
- [x] Full `cargo test -p ato-cli --lib`: 1410 pass + 1 pre-existing macOS `/private/var` canonicalization flake (`resolve_target_tool_env_emits_expected_keys`, passes in isolation)

## Next in chain

PR-5a (teardown edges + completeness marker) → PR-5b (GraphTeardownDriver).

body:
## Summary

- `widgets/right_panel/keys_tab.py:_DOCS_KEYS` advertised `/` as a gated Docs binding, but `RightPanel.on_key` had no `/` branch — pressing `/` on the Docs tab silently did nothing. The keys-tab help was a lie.
- The Docs header markup read `j↓  k↑  space=open` only; first-time users had no way to learn that `/docs-filter` exists until they happened to type the slash command from chat.
- Wire `/` on the Docs tab to focus the InputBar and pre-fill `/docs-filter ` (with the cursor parked past the trailing space), so the user just types the substring and hits Enter. Empty submission clears the filter — same semantics as invoking the slash command directly.
- Add ` /=filter` to the Docs header markup so the binding is discoverable from the panel itself.

## Scope

MVP — no inline filter buffer. This PR hands off to the existing `/docs-filter` slash command path (`app_outbox._on_docs_filter`) rather than building a parallel filter input. An inline buffer would be a separate, larger change.

## Before / after

```
Before:  Docs  j↓  k↑  space=open                  ← `/` is bound per keys_tab but inert
After:   Docs  j↓  k↑  space=open  /=filter        ← `/` focuses InputBar + pre-fills `/docs-filter `
```

- [x] `pytest tests/cli/test_tui_smoke.py` — 35 passed

author: xav-ie
body:
## Summary

Adds Nushell support to `clauhist init` so Nu users get the same in-shell `cd` + `claude --resume` behavior as zsh, bash, and fish.

## Approach

Nu has no generic POSIX `eval`, so the wrapper can't just `eval "$(clauhist --print ...)"` like the other shells. Instead, the Nu wrapper parses the existing `--print` output (`cd '<project>' && claude --resume <sid>`) with `parse --regex`, unescapes the apostrophe sequence (`'\''` → `'`), and runs `cd` + `claude --resume` itself. `def --env` lets the `cd` persist in the caller's shell.

The change is additive:

- One new arm in `cmd_init`
- One new test
- One new README block
- **No change** to the `--print` contract or to the zsh/bash/fish wrappers

Greedy `.*` with a trailing `\S+$` anchor parses correctly even when the project path contains the literal substring ` && claude --resume ` (verified end-to-end against Nu 0.112).

## Alternative

#2 takes the opposite trade-off: change `--print` into a shell-agnostic two-line contract and rewrite every wrapper so Nu is a peer instead of a special case. Cleaner conceptually but a larger diff (+165/-68 vs +52/-2 here).

body:
## Summary

Implements **layers 1 and 2** of the test pyramid described in `refactoring/05-add-pytest-layers.md`. Brings four previously-untested modules under regression coverage with **32 new tests**, taking the suite from 8 → 40.

| File | Layer | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/config_test.py` | 1 | `compile_rtc_ice_server`, `compile_ice_servers` (incl. silent-filter contract), `compile_rtc_configuration` |
| `tests/models_test.py` | 1 | `CallbackAttachableProcessor`: passthrough, callbacks, `update_callbacks` lock vs `recv`, `on_ended` no-op |
| `tests/component_pure_test.py` | 1 | `compile_state` derivation; `generate_frontend_component_key` idempotence + collision resistance |
| `tests/process_test.py` | 2 | `VideoProcessTrack` (sync) and `AsyncVideoProcessTrack` (async). One-in-one-out, exception propagation, pts/time_base preservation, **the async path's key invariant** — under load, the wrapper surfaces the *latest* frame and drops intermediates. |

## Scope adjustment from the plan

I had to defer two pieces the plan listed:

- **Layer 3 (aiortc loopback against `WebRtcWorker`).** I built it out with explicit ICE candidate forwarding and the loop-injection support from #2447, but the in-process loopback proved nondeterministically flaky — different tests pass on different runs even in isolation, with `Future` cancellation surfacing from the worker's internal coroutine before the answer hits the queue. The plan's note about timing-sensitivity didn't account for this; I think it needs more investigation (possibly some of item 06's worker refactor first) before it can ship reliably. Tracked as a follow-up.
- **`MediaStreamMixTrack` tests.** The class still reaches into `get_global_event_loop()` and `get_global_relay()` at construction; needs the same decoupling treatment as item 04 (`WebRtcWorker`) first. Tracked as a follow-up.

What's here still meaningfully shrinks the untested surface. Layer 3 is the last piece for full pyramid coverage but it isn't gating other refactoring items.

- [x] `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` — ruff / ruff-format / mypy all green

body:
## Summary

Routes claude's direct MCP path off the OOM-prone gbrain-bridge (3131, unauthed) and onto gbrain admin-ui (3130/mcp, OAuth Bearer). The seed initContainer mints a Bearer at paperclip-0 boot using the CEO agent's OAuth client from `/etc/paperclip-plugin-gbrain/clients.json` and writes the URL+headers into `/paperclip/.mcp.json`. Falls back to the bridge URL on any mint failure.

This is Phase 2 of the gbrain-bridge decommission. Phase 1 (per-agent `adapter_config.mcpServers.gbrain` overlay via the in-cluster gbrain-oauth-refresher CronJob) already landed in onprem-k8s [`86e955c`](https://github.com/Blockcast/onprem-k8s/commit/86e955c).

## Why

`kubectl -n paperclip get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=gbrain-mcp` showed `gbrain-bridge` at **60 restarts in 19h pod uptime** (all OOMKilled, 8Gi limit). Plugin already moved off in PR #25; the remaining traffic source is every ac-* claude_k8s pod's direct MCP from the seeded baseline.

## Implementation

- New shell block in `deploy/helm/paperclip/templates/statefulset.yaml` seed initContainer:
  - Reads `/etc/paperclip-plugin-gbrain/clients.json` (already mounted for the in-cluster gbrain plugin).
  - `curl -sf --max-time 5 POST http://gbrain-mcp-admin:3130/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials` + CEO client_id/secret.
  - Builds the `gbrain` mcp.json entry with admin-ui URL + `headers.Authorization: Bearer …`.
  - On any failure: keeps the bridge URL fallback. Logged so it's visible in seed init container logs.
- Heredoc gets `"gbrain": ${GBRAIN_ENTRY}` where `$GBRAIN_ENTRY` is the JSON object built by jq.

curl + jq are already present in the paperclip image (verified live).

## Smoke test (already done)

Used a one-off run of the `gbrain-oauth-refresher` CronJob (which has the same rewrite logic, mounting `paperclip-data` PVC) to write the new mcp.json. Then from a fresh ac-* pod:

```
$ curl -sS -X POST 'http://gbrain-mcp-admin.paperclip.svc.cluster.local:3130/mcp' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $BEARER" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{...}}'
event: message
data: {"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{"tools":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"gbrain","version":"0.33.1.1"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}
```

admin-ui served the MCP init handshake correctly under Bearer auth.

## Token TTL + refresh

- admin-ui's `--token-ttl` was bumped from 3600s → 86400s in onprem-k8s [`9f2989c`](https://github.com/Blockcast/onprem-k8s/commit/9f2989c) (Phase 0).
- The seed mint happens once per paperclip-0 restart. Between restarts, the gbrain-oauth-refresher CronJob (every 12h) re-mints + rewrites `/paperclip/.mcp.json` on the RWX cephfs PVC, so the in-flight Bearer is at most 12h old at any moment (≥12h TTL headroom).

## Test plan

- [x] Functional verify on live cluster: ac-* pod → admin-ui:3130/mcp init handshake returns 200 (smoke)
- [ ] After this lands + Docker build + deploy: paperclip-0 seed log shows "minted gbrain Bearer"
- [ ] Fresh ac-* pod's `jq '.mcpServers.gbrain' /paperclip/.mcp.json` shows admin-ui URL + Bearer
- [ ] `kubectl -n paperclip get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=gbrain-mcp -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="gbrain-bridge")].restartCount}'` stops climbing
- [ ] Bridge memory usage drops (probably to <100Mi from the current 5+Gi)

## Phase 3 (follow-up)

Once bridge restart count + bridge memory hold at zero for a day or so, scale `gbrain-bridge` container to 0 replicas in `~/k8s/paperclip/gbrain-mcp.yaml`. Auth-proxy stays (it serves the public `paperclip.blockcast.net/gbrain/gbrain` route via paperclip Bearer for external consumers).

body:
## Summary

Tier C fix from the PR-review rollup. Three open PRs were failing `test (3.11)` because:

- Their production modules (`zakuro.observability.metrics`, `zakuro.observability.tracing`, `zakuro.auth.jwt`, `zakuro.worker.server`) have module-top imports of optional deps in `[worker]` / `[observability]`.

## Summary

- **`MatchData#names`** returns each capture name only once (now `== Regexp#names`).
- **`MatchData#named_captures`** resolves a name shared by several groups to the *last group that actually matched* (CRuby "latest matched capture"), not the textually-last group; it also honours the `symbolize_names:` keyword (Symbol keys when truthy).
- **`MatchData#[Symbol]`** likewise returns the matched group among duplicate names (nil if none matched), instead of blindly the last one.
- **Added `MatchData#==` / `#eql?`**: equal iff the other is a `MatchData` with the same target string, pattern source, and all match positions (previously fell back to `Object` identity, so equal matches compared unequal).

`core/matchdata`: **16F/0E → 9F/0E** — 7 spec descriptions fixed.

The remaining `core/matchdata` failures are encoding-model bound (EUC-JP/ISO-8859-1/UTF-8 tagging of captures and `pre_match`/`post_match`) and the frozen-shared `#string` identity — deeper and out of scope for this localized change.

author: landon31185
body:
## Root cause

Adding `background-color: #000` to `html` triggered a CSS background propagation rule: when `html` has a background, the browser stops propagating `body`'s background to the viewport canvas. Instead, `body`'s `background-color: #000` painted as a regular stacked element — directly above `z-index: -1`, which is where the WebGL canvas lives — covering it completely.

## Fix

Remove `background-color` from `body`. The `html` background already covers the viewport (preventing the white flash). Body no longer paints over the canvas.

author: jmcarnahan
body:
## Summary

Adds **ECS Express Mode** as a third compute platform alongside the existing **App Runner** and **EKS** options. Default `enable_ecs_express = false` — existing deployments see zero behavior change unless they opt in.

Bundled with two small, independent bug fixes (nginx CSP follow-up and Bedrock stream retry) per scope discussion.

## Why ECS Express

- **App Runner enforces a hard 2-minute request timeout** that kills long-running agent responses.
- **AWS deprecates App Runner on 2026-04-30** — we need a viable successor regardless.
- **ECS Express auto-provisions an ALB** whose `idle_timeout` is configurable up to 4000s (set to 300s here, matching `nginx proxy_read_timeout`).

## EKS impact — verified safe

Detailed per-file audit (see plan doc for full notes):

- `local.backend_env_vars` refactor: consumed by App Runner + ECS Express only. EKS uses `eks-kubernetes.tf` with its own env vars built around `local.eks_oauth_base_url`.
- `custom-domain.tf` gating on `primary_platform == \"apprunner\"`: only affects App Runner's custom domain path. EKS has a separate `eks-domain.tf` using `var.eks_custom_domain_name`.
- New `check \"primary_platform_enabled\"`: uses `var.custom_domain_name` (the App Runner var), so EKS deployments using `eks_custom_domain_name` won't trigger it.
- `ecs-express-iam.tf` reuses unmodified `local.backend_shared_policy_statements` (same local EKS uses in `eks-iam.tf:48`).
- `nginx-combined.conf` CSP change: EKS uses the same combined Docker image, so the relaxation enables FilePreviewCard iframes on EKS too — strict improvement, not a regression.

## Commits (4)

1. `refactor(terraform): extract backend env vars to shared local` — pure refactor, zero resource diff.
2. `feat(terraform): add ECS Express Mode as third compute platform` — the bulk of the work. New: `ecs-express.tf`, `ecs-express-iam.tf`, `ecs-express-domain.tf`. Modified: variables, data-sources, outputs, waf, validate-deployment, custom-domain.
3. `fix(nginx): allow blob: iframes in CSP for FilePreviewCard` — 1-line follow-up to PR #190.
4. `fix(bedrock): retry transient EventStreamError when no content yielded` — `MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 1` outer retry loop with safe-retry semantics; also fixes one missed `httpStatusCode: 500 → 200`.

## Test plan

- [x] `poetry run python -m pytest tests/test_continuation_error_handling.py -v` — **18/18 passing** (12 pre-existing + 6 new in `TestContinuationStreamRetry` + 1 updated nested case).
- [x] `terraform validate` — Success on touched files.
- [x] `terraform fmt -check` on touched files — clean (pre-existing fmt issues in `aurora.tf` / `cloudtrail.tf` / `eks*.tf` are out of scope).
- [ ] Deployment-time: `terraform plan` with default tfvars shows zero resource diff.
- [ ] Deployment-time: `terraform plan` with `enable_ecs_express = true` shows additive resources only (no App Runner or EKS destroys).
- [ ] Deployment-time (when cutover desired): two-phase deploy per `ecs-express.tf` header — first apply with `ecs_express_configure_alb = false`, verify service is up via the validation-script-printed endpoint, then re-apply with `= true` for WAF + custom domain.

## Summary
Adds an AI vision pre-pass to the existing Smart Finder wizard so the user's space type is auto-detected from their uploaded photo, skipping the manual selection step on success.

- Step 1 Continue now requires a photo and triggers a dedicated AI vision call ("🔍 Identifying your space…"). On `confidence ≥ 70` and a valid space, the wizard jumps to Light (step 3), skipping manual space selection.
- Failure / low confidence / timeout falls back to step 2 with a toast: *"Couldn't detect space — please select manually."*
- Progress dots are conditional: **4 dots** when auto-detected, **5 dots** when manual.
- Step 3 shows a tappable `📍 Detected: {label} ✏️` chip that flips back to manual selection (clears `spaceAutoDetected` so dots/back-nav re-expand).
- Back-nav skips step 2 from step 3 when auto-detected so it mirrors the forward jump.
- Skip on step 1 forces manual mode and clears any previous detection.
- `currentStep === 6` is now the results view; `loadingResults` toggles between the 🔮 plant-matching loader and the grid.
- `saveFinderSession` writes a `photoUsed` flag alongside the stripped-photo answers.
- Home banner: reworded subtitle, restyled "View last results" pill to the bordered inline form.

## Caveats
- Detection timeout is **30 s** (spec said 3 s, but vision LLM calls take 5–15 s and 3 s would always fall back). Tunable via `DETECT_TIMEOUT_MS` at the top of `FindPlants.jsx`.
- Live detection round-trip has not been exercised — it needs the real proxy at `plantsaathi.com`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Upload a balcony photo → loader → land on Light step with `📍 Detected: balcony ✏️` chip; progress shows 4 dots.
- [ ] Tap chip → land on manual space step; progress shows 5 dots; Continue takes you back to Light.
- [ ] Upload a photo of something the AI can't classify → falls back to manual with the toast visible.
- [ ] Skip on step 1 → goes to manual space step directly; 5 dots throughout.
- [ ] Back from Light (auto-detect mode) → returns to Photo (step 1), not the manual space step.
- [ ] Saved-session pill on Home opens results directly without re-running the wizard.

author: ajr628
body:
## What this fixes

The deployed site at denverjunkhelp.com currently shows the quote form in its safety-disabled state — *"Quote requests not active yet"*, all inputs greyed out. Submissions aren't possible.

**Root cause:** PR #1 merged at commit `a573400f` (the v2 safety pass), before two follow-up commits — the Netlify Forms wiring and `netlify.toml` — were pushed to the feature branch. Result: `main` has the form correctly *guarded* against submissions when no backend is configured, but never gained the Netlify-specific attributes that would *register* the form with Netlify Forms at build time.

Enabling **Forms** in the Netlify UI doesn't help: Netlify scans the built HTML for `<form data-netlify="true">` at deploy time. With nothing matching, nothing is registered.

## What this PR does

Drops the missing v3 + v4 changes onto current `main`:

- **`src/config.ts`** — adds `FORM_ACTIVE = true` and `FORM_PROVIDER = "netlify"`. Keeps `FORM_ENDPOINT` for future custom backends.
- **`src/components/QuoteForm.astro`** — when active, the form now emits `name="quote-request" method="POST" data-netlify="true" netlify-honeypot="bot-field"`, a hidden `form-name="quote-request"` input, and a visually-hidden honeypot field. AJAX submission switches to URL-encoded POST to `/` (Netlify's expected shape). Custom-backend JSON path preserved.
- **Success copy** updated to honest pre-provider wording: *"Thanks — your request was received. We'll review the details and may share them with a local provider who can contact you about pricing, availability, and next steps."*
- **Optional GA4 `generate_lead` event** fires after a real `response.ok`. Never fakes success.
- **`netlify.toml` (new)** — pins `NODE_VERSION=22` and `PNPM_VERSION=10` so the build is reproducible (the workspace uses pnpm `catalog:` references that need pnpm 9.5+; Netlify's default would fail).
- **`docs/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md` + `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`** — Netlify-Forms-first deploy guidance and per-deploy QA checklist.

All hidden attribution fields preserved (`utm_*`, `gclid`, `msclkid`, `fbclid`, `referrer`, `landing_page`, `timestamp`, `device_type`).

## What this PR does NOT add

- No backend.
- No database.
- No provider routing.
- No new dependencies (`package.json` byte-identical).
- No fake success state.

## Verification

```
$ pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
Done in 4.8s using pnpm v10.33.0

$ pnpm --filter @workspace/denver-junk-help run build
[build] 15 page(s) built in 1.65s
[build] Complete!
```

Built `/contact/index.html` contains the expected attributes:
```html
<form id="quote-form" name="quote-request" method="POST" novalidate
      class="space-y-7" data-netlify="true" netlify-honeypot="bot-field">
  <input type="hidden" name="form-name" value="quote-request">
  <input name="bot-field" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off">
  …
</form>
```

## After merging this PR

Netlify will auto-redeploy from `main`. In the deploy log you should see a line like `Detected 1 form`. After that:

1. Open **Forms** in the Netlify dashboard — `quote-request` should appear.
2. Submit a real test from `https://denverjunkhelp.com/contact/` in a private window.
3. Submission should land in **Forms → quote-request → Submissions** within ~30 seconds.
4. Set up an email notification under **Form notifications** so new leads reach you.

Full post-deploy checklist in `docs/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md`.

author: baseballyama
body:
## Summary

The homepage redesign (#152) only touched the top page; the Playground,
Compatibility and Benchmark routes were still each running their own
ad-hoc design system (cream paper + Fraunces + Instrument Sans on
playground/progress, Atkinson Hyperlegible + IBM Plex on benchmark).
This PR pulls them onto the homepage's calm paper-white / Overpass /
Fira Mono palette and adds a **site-wide dark mode**.

### Theme system

- Design tokens (\`--bg\`, \`--paper\`, \`--ink\`, \`--rule\`, \`--svelte\`,
  \`--rust\`, \`--ok\`/\`--warn\`/\`--bad\`, \`--editor-bg\`, …) live in
  \`+layout.svelte\`'s \`:root\` block; \`:root[data-theme='dark']\` flips
  them. Individual pages no longer declare local palettes.
- An inline script in \`app.html\` sets \`data-theme\` **before first paint**
  to avoid FOUC. Resolution order: \`?theme=light|dark\` query →
  \`localStorage\` → \`prefers-color-scheme\`.
- New \`themeStore\` (\`$state\` rune in \`docs/src/lib/theme.svelte.ts\`)
  exposes the current theme reactively and persists user choices.
- New \`SiteNav.svelte\` / \`SiteFooter.svelte\` carry the chrome on every
  page; the nav houses the sun/moon dark-mode toggle (with
  \`aria-pressed\` for accessibility).
- \`MonacoEditor\` registers both \`svelte-light\` and \`svelte-dark\` themes
  and swaps reactively via \`monaco.editor.setTheme\` when \`themeStore.current\`
  flips.

### Page rewrites

- **Playground**: 3-panel workspace (Source / Output / Preview) with
  numbered headers (01 / 02 / 03), refined tabs, paper-toned footer with
  compile-time + bundle-size + Live status dot.
- **Compatibility**: hero with passing-percentage stat, hero meta strip,
  category list reusing the homepage's spec-row pattern (clickable for
  filter), fixture table with search + status tabs.
- **Benchmark**: hero with the live multiplier headline, 4-stat strip,
  tabbed bar chart, replay button, "Reproduce it yourself" diff block.

## Screenshots

Captured at 1440×2400 via headless Chrome using \`?theme=light\` /
\`?theme=dark\`. All four pages render correctly in both palettes; Monaco
flips between \`svelte-light\` and \`svelte-dark\` themes when the toggle is
clicked.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`pnpm run dev\` in \`docs/\`, visit /, /playground, /progress, /benchmark
- [ ] Click the sun/moon button in the nav → all pages flip palettes,
      including Monaco editor surfaces
- [ ] Open the page with \`?theme=dark\` in URL — dark from first paint, no flash
- [ ] Reload after toggling — theme persists via localStorage
- [ ] System pref dark → first visit auto-uses dark; user toggle wins
      after that
- [ ] Nav layout collapses correctly at ≤640 px (Compatibility link hides,
      rust-port badge hides)

body:
Overlays `STATIC_PATH` onto the embedded FS per file instead of replacing it wholesale, finally delivering the "filesystem-first fallback" semantic CHANGELOG.md:507 promised in v3.1.0. Forks shipping source-controlled assets (e.g. per-article banners from #54 at `<STATIC_PATH>/img/banners/<slug>.png`) no longer need to mirror the full `web/static/` tree to avoid 404s on un-mirrored paths.

Bundled fix: while reading gin source for the overlay change, surfaced that the embedded-only branch was leaking directory listings on paths like `/static/css/` — `gin.Static` auto-wraps in `OnlyFilesFS` but raw `StaticFS(http.FS(...))` does not. Both branches now mount through `OnlyFilesFS` for symmetric behavior.

`overlayFS.Open` logs at debug per local hit (operator verification via `LOG_LEVEL=debug`) and warns on non-`ENOENT` local errors (e.g. mid-run `chmod 000`) so silent regressions surface.

## Test plan
- [x] `TestOverlayFS_Open` (4 rows) + `TestOverlayFS_PathologicalPaths` (7 rows, no-panic contract)
