author: arthur742ramos
body:
Completes the **discovery half of recommendation #6** from [docs/sledgehammer_lsp_research.md](https://github.com/Arthur742Ramos/Isabelle-VSCode/blob/main/docs/sledgehammer_lsp_research.md#implications-for-the-extension) (Milestone 7 plumbing). The settings landed in PR #33 supply `isabelle.sledgehammer.{provers,isar,try0}` overrides; this PR adds the always-on subscriber that lets the rest of the extension consult the LSP-discovered prover list synchronously without each caller having to round-trip the language server.

## What

New file `src/sledgehammer/PideSledgehammerProversCache.ts`:

- Subscribes once to `PIDE/sledgehammer_provers_response` via the notification registry shipped in PR #31, so the handler persists across language-client restart cycles.
- Listens to `IsabelleLanguageClient.onStatusChange`.
- Dispatches `PIDE/sledgehammer_provers_request` on the `disabled -> running` transition (and on construction if the language client was already running, for the late-wiring case).
- Caches the response (trimmed + whitespace-normalized) and exposes it synchronously via `getProvers()` / `hasCachedProvers()` / `getLastUpdatedAt()`.
- Drops the cache when the client stops, fails, or disables so callers never surface stale data; re-fires on the next running transition.
- Is **`vscode`-free**: takes injectable `ProversCacheClient`, `ProversCacheLogger`, and clock interfaces. The production `IsabelleLanguageClient` and `vscode.OutputChannel` satisfy the client and logger contracts structurally without any adapter.

`extension.ts` is updated to instantiate the cache alongside `languageClient` and `languageServerStatusBar`, register it on `context.subscriptions`, and dispose it early in `deactivate()` so its notification + status subscriptions release cleanly before the language client shuts down.

## Validation

15 vitest cases in `test/sledgehammer/PideSledgehammerProversCache.test.ts` against an in-memory `FakeClient` covering:

| # | What | Why |
|---|------|-----|
| 1 | Initial empty state | Default contract |
| 2 | No request when client is initially disabled | Don't spam an inert LSP |
| 3 | Request on disabled -> running transition | The core trigger |
| 4 | Fire on construction when client already running | Late-wiring safety net |
| 5 | Cache normalizes the response and stamps `lastUpdatedAt` | Happy path |
| 6 | Ragged whitespace in payload is normalized | Defensive normalization |
| 7 | Malformed payloads (non-string, null, undefined) ignored + logged | Hostile input |
| 8 | Empty-but-well-formed response logs without "malformed" | Avoid false alarms |
| 9 | Cache drops on stopping/failed/disabled transitions | No stale data |
| 10 | Re-fires request on restart cycle | Restart resilience |
| 11 | Doesn't double-fire on running -> running | Defensive dedup |
| 12 | `sendNotification` failure is logged but doesn't throw | Transport robustness |
| 13 | Post-dispose response is safely ignored | Lifecycle safety |
| 14 | `dispose()` is idempotent | Lifecycle safety |
| 15 | Subscriptions released on dispose | No leaks |

Total suite: **213 tests, all green** (baseline 198 from PR #33 + 15 new). `npm run check` passes.

## What this PR does NOT do

- It does **not** consume the cache anywhere yet. The consumer is the LSP-mode branch of `SledgehammerPanel.run()` (research recommendation #2), which depends on:
  - this cache (PR adds it);
  - the settings reader from PR #33;
  - the parser from PR #32;
  - the quiescence gate (recommendation #7) — still to land in a separate PR.
- It does **not** change any existing behavior for users with `isabelle.languageServer.enabled = false`. The cache is constructed but its `onStatusChange` listener only acts on transitions and `dispatchRequest` is a no-op until the client enters `running`.

author: viniciuscffreitas
body:
#### Context

QA video pipeline had 4 bugs discovered via deep code analysis. All silent — no runtime crash, just wrong evidence reaching Linear.

#### TL;DR

- `session.webm` was always the setup-parents auth video, not the feature being tested
- Video uploads >~3MB silently timed out (Req `receive_timeout` defaulted to 15s)
- `File.read` was loading the entire WebM into memory just to compute byte size
- `shots`/`screenshots` field in checks was dead code — never read by `_write_report` or the Elixir uploader

#### Summary

- `qa_publish.py`: added `_is_setup_suite()` that filters top-level Playwright suites with `.setup.` in the file path before iterating. `setup-parents` ran first (as a dependency), so its video always won the "first video wins" race — the PM was watching account provisioning, not the ticket.
- `file_upload.ex`: added `receive_timeout: 120_000` to `Req.put`. S3 presigned PUT only responds after the full body is received, so any video larger than ~3MB silently failed at the 15s default.
- `file_upload.ex`: `upload/1` now uses `File.stat` for the GraphQL `size` field — file is only read once, just before the PUT.
- `qa_publish.py`: removed dead `shots` list and `screenshots` key from checks dict.

#### Alternatives

Filtering by project name instead of file path — rejected because Playwright JSON organizes suites by file, not by project name at the suite level.

#### Test Plan

- [x] `test_setup_suite_video_does_not_win` — RED before fix, GREEN after
- [x] `test_setup_suite_excluded_from_checks` — RED before fix, GREEN after
- [x] All 4 existing `QaPublishTest` tests green (no regression)
- [x] 617/617 Elixir tests green
- [x] Dialyzer 0 errors

author: djdanielsson
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the full web UI, FastAPI backend, migration planner, and supporting infrastructure that was developed on the `surgery` branch and refined on `fixes`.

### Web UI (React + PatternFly)
- Full single-page app with Dashboard, Connections, Object Browser, Dependency Analysis, Migration, Planner, Sizing, and Jobs pages
- Real-time job log streaming via WebSocket with REST fallback
- Migration progress visualization with expandable phase groups, resource-level detail, and live status bars
- Analysis results viewer with org dependency graphs, migration wave breakdown, and quality scores

### FastAPI Backend
- Connection management with encrypted token storage
- Dependency analysis engine that computes org migration waves and cross-org resource dependencies
- Migration execution engine (export -> transform -> import pipeline) with org-scoped filtering
- Cleanup operations with concurrent batch deletion
- Job service with DB persistence, WebSocket broadcast, cancellation support, and startup recovery

### Migration Planner
- Multi-source, multi-phase migration plans with analysis-driven wave auto-population
- One phase per analysis wave (simple, clean)
- Org dependency warnings in the phase editor (cross-org resource refs, ordering issues)
- Phase execution with per-phase job tracking and status

### Credential Pause
- After all credentials and credential_input_sources are migrated across all sources, the job automatically pauses with `waiting_for_input` status
- Queries source AAP to build a list of critical credentials that are actually referenced by projects, EEs, inventory sources, instance groups, credential input sources, and org galaxy credential associations
- New **Credentials** tab in job detail shows the credential review table with type, org, and what uses each credential
- CSV download of the credential list for offline review
- **Continue Migration** button calls `POST /api/jobs/{id}/resume` to resume after secrets are updated on the target
- Survives container restarts (paused jobs marked failed with re-execute message on startup)

### CaC Org-Update Pass
- After all resource types finish, organizations are PATCHed to assign `default_environment` (execution environment) and galaxy credential associations that were created after the initial org shell

### Bug Fixes
- **inventory_groups cleanup/update 404s**: `delete_resource` and `update_resource` in `AAPTargetClient` now use `get_endpoint()` to map internal resource type names to API endpoints (e.g., `inventory_groups` -> `groups/`)
- **name_prefix not applied**: Resources now get `name_prefix` prepended to their name before import, not just in log messages
- **projects migrated as manual**: `defer_project_sync=False` passed to transformer so SCM type is preserved
- **Phase status column too short**: Widened to `String(30)` to fit `completed_with_errors`
- **Job status inconsistency**: Jobs stuck in `running` on restart are marked `failed`
- **Resource type ordering**: Sources processed per-resource-type (all sources' creds together) instead of per-source (all types for source 1 then source 2)
- **Mypy and lint fixes**: All ruff, bandit, mypy, and TypeScript checks pass

### Container Setup
- `Containerfile.api` and `Containerfile.ui` for engine and UI containers
- `docker-compose.yml` with PostgreSQL, engine, UI, and CLI containers
- nginx reverse proxy config for API/WebSocket proxying

### Dependency Updates
- Merged all open Dependabot PRs (pydantic, click, aiofiles, mkdocs-material, types-requests, types-pyyaml, isort, python-dateutil, setup-python action)

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify `populate_plan` generates one phase per analysis wave
- [ ] Run a migration and verify credential pause triggers after creds finish
- [ ] Verify credential review table shows in job detail with CSV download
- [ ] Click "Continue Migration" and verify job resumes
- [ ] Run cleanup and verify inventory_groups delete without 404s
- [ ] Verify CaC org-update pass assigns default_environment and galaxy credentials
- [ ] Restart engine container and verify waiting_for_input jobs are marked failed

Closes Section 11 of openspec/changes/add-application-control/tasks.md items 11.1 (host_groups + assignments schema), 11.2 (CDHASH/SIGNINGID/ TEAMID rule types end-to-end), and 11.3 (cdhash on every exec event).

Server schema (server/rules/bootstrap/schema.go):
- Add host_groups (id, name UNIQUE, description, criteria JSON, timestamps).
- Add app_control_assignments (policy_id, host_group_id, priority, created_at) with PK (policy_id, host_group_id) and intra-context CASCADE FKs.

Seed (server/rules/internal/appcontrol/store.go):
- EnsureDefaultPolicy now runs the Default policy + the all-hosts host group + the Default->all-hosts assignment in a single transaction. INSERT IGNORE keeps each row idempotent; assignment lookup goes via SELECT BY NAME because LAST_INSERT_ID() is unreliable on suppressed inserts.
- ListHostGroupsForPolicy(policyID) inner-joins host_groups with app_control_assignments and returns rows ordered by (priority DESC, name ASC).

Public types (server/rules/api/types.go):
- DefaultHostGroupName='all-hosts', HostGroupCriteriaTypeAll='all'.
- HostGroup + Assignment struct types.
- ApplicationControlStore gains ListHostGroupsForPolicy.

Fan-out (server/rules/internal/appcontrol/service.go):
- fanout(ctx, policyID, payload) walks the assignment layer: resolves the policy's host groups, walks each group's criteria via resolveHostGroup, unions the host ids, dedups, and enqueues one command per unique host. Phase A's only criteria shape is {type:'all'} which delegates to the existing HostLister, so observable behavior matches the demo cut. Phase B grows the resolver with tag/hostname/OS predicates without touching this loop.
- New fanoutSkipReason values: assignment_list_error, no_assignments.

Validators (server/rules/internal/appcontrol/validate.go):
- ValidateRuleType accepts CDHASH, SIGNINGID, TEAMID alongside BINARY. CERTIFICATE + PATH stay gated until Phase B (leaf-cert cache + Launch Services indirection).
- ValidateIdentifier returns nil for well-formed CDHASH (40 hex), TEAMID (10 uppercase alnum), SIGNINGID (TeamID|platform:bundle.id) rather than the prior unsupported error.

Extension (extension/edr/extension/ESFSubscriber.swift):
- handleAuthExec is rewritten around the precedence walker. Extracts the AuthTuple (cdhash if hardened-runtime via CS_RUNTIME=0x10000 gate, file_sha256 from FileHashCache, prefixed signing_id, team_id) via the new buildAuthTuple helper; walkPrecedence walks CDHASH -> BINARY -> SIGNINGID -> TEAMID returning the first match.
- isHardenedRuntime(flags:) and cdhashHexString(from:) helpers. The hex encoder treats an all-zero cdhash as nil (unsigned binaries).

Extension exec event (extension/edr/extension/EventSerializer.swift):
- ExecPayload gains optional cdhash field. Encoder uses encodeIfPresent so the wire shape stays compact for non-hardened binaries; decoder uses decodeIfPresent for backwards-tolerance.

UI (ui/src/components/ApplicationControl/AddRuleModal.tsx):
- RULE_TYPES flips available:true for CDHASH, SIGNINGID, TEAMID.
- validateIdentifier(ruleType, value) dispatches to per-type regexes mirroring the server validator shapes. Length constants extracted so the no-magic-numbers lint stays clean.
- normalizeIdentifier lowercases BINARY/CDHASH only; TEAMID/SIGNINGID stay untouched. PLACEHOLDERS is a Map<string,string> so the lookup never trips the object-injection lint.

UI tests (AddRuleModal.test.tsx): 6 new cases covering CDHASH happy path + case normalization, TEAMID happy path + lowercase rejection, SIGNINGID TeamID:bundle.id form, SIGNINGID platform: prefix, and SIGNINGID missing-colon rejection. All 41 UI tests pass.

## Summary

Closes #48

이 PR은 `fix: address security issues #48 #49 (PII in logs, input length validation)`에 포함된 변경을 현재 PR 본문 계약에 맞게 정리합니다.

## Background

닫힌 PR #54의 기존 기록을 보존하면서 표준 섹션과 마지막 `## DoD Status` 구조로 정리했습니다.

## What This Solves

- PR 제목과 기존 본문에 기록된 문제·변경 목적을 표준 형식으로 읽을 수 있게 합니다.
- 기존 사실과 검증 기록을 보존하고 형식 해석의 모호성을 제거합니다.

## Work Done

- 기존 PR 본문을 표준 섹션으로 재배치했습니다.

<details>
<summary>기존 본문 기록</summary>

### Summary

Fixes two MEDIUM-severity security issues.

### #48 — Remove PII from exception messages (OWASP A09)

Exception messages and log lines in blockword processors embedded the full
user-supplied text, risking PII disclosure in log aggregators or 500 responses.

**Fix**: replace `text=[$text]` / `request=$request` with
`textLength=${text.length}` — structural metadata only, no content.

**Locations**:
- `KoreanBlockwordProcessor` — `findBlockwords` and `maskBlockwords` catch blocks
- `JapaneseBlockwordProcessor` — `maskBlockwords` catch block

### #49 — Input length validation (OWASP A04)

No public API enforced a maximum input length. Combined with O(n²) tokenizer
complexity, arbitrarily large inputs could exhaust CPU/memory in HTTP services.

**Fix**:
- Added `MAX_TOKENIZE_TEXT_LENGTH = 100_000` constant
- Added `MAX_BLOCKWORD_TEXT_LENGTH = 100_000` constant
- `tokenizeRequestOf()` and `blockwordRequestOf()` factory functions now throw
  `IllegalArgumentException` when `text.length > limit`
- Callers needing a higher limit can construct the request data class directly

### Test Results

```
./gradlew :tokenizer-core:test :tokenizer-korean:test :tokenizer-japanese:test
BUILD SUCCESSFUL — all tests passing
```

Closes #48, #49

</details>

author: laceyp99
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a final-pass Ollama post-processor to murmur's transcription pipeline.

After Whisper finishes the final document text, murmur can now send that cleaned transcript through a local Ollama model for punctuation, capitalization, and light semantic correction. The Ollama pass runs once at finalization, not during live chunk transcription.

This PR also adds a repo-local `user_vocab.json` flow for preferred spellings and names, startup model warmup, and a small acceptance gate so obviously invalid LLM responses fall back to the pre-LLM transcript instead of replacing it.

## What changed

- Added Ollama configuration fields:
  - `ollama_enabled`
  - `ollama_endpoint`
  - `ollama_model_name`
  - `ollama_timeout_seconds`
  - `ollama_preload_model`
- Added `OllamaClient` and `LLMPostProcessor`
- Wired final-pass LLM cleanup into `Transcriber.finalize_text()`
- Added startup warmup through `MurmurApp`
- Added repo-local `user_vocab.json` loading and saving
- Added conservative output acceptance rules for final LLM text
- Updated README to document current Ollama behavior and local vocab usage
- Added/updated focused unit tests for config, post-processing, transcription, startup warmup, and vocab loading

## Behavior

- Ollama cleanup is enabled by default
- The LLM runs only once per completed recording
- Warmup does not pull missing models automatically
- If Ollama is unavailable, times out, or returns suspicious output, murmur falls back to the non-LLM cleaned transcript
- Preferred vocabulary can be supplied locally through `user_vocab.json`

## Validation

Ran:

```powershell
pytest -q test_config.py test_llm_postprocess.py test_transcription.py test_main.py test_user_vocab.py
```

## Notes

- This PR uses the Ollama Python package rather than a custom HTTP client
- The prompt flow now uses chat history with a few-shot example for more stable cleanup behavior
- The acceptance gate currently rejects empty output, obvious assistant preambles, length explosions, and chat/list-shaped responses

author: eyalm321
body:
## Summary

Every tool is registered with an `outputSchema` (`{ data }`, `{ message }`, …). `toMcpError` attaches `structuredContent: { error: { code } }` to failure results. The server SDK skips output validation when `isError` is set, **but MCP clients validate a result's `structuredContent` against the advertised output schema regardless of `isError`**, and the error shape conforms to none of the declared schemas.

Net effect: every failed tool call surfaces the opaque **`structured content does not match the tool's output schema`**, and the real error is hidden. Reads appear fine; all write tools (`manage_acl`, `manage_policy_file`, `manage_keys`, `manage_dns`, …) look silently broken — e.g. the `requireRisk` gate's `Tool requires write/admin risk level`, or a genuine Tailscale API error, never reaches the caller.

## Fix

Error results omit `structuredContent`. Per MCP semantics, error results aren't expected to satisfy `outputSchema`; the actionable message is carried in the text `content` as before. No change to success results.

## Test plan

- [x] New `src/__test__/observability/errors.test.ts` asserting `toMcpError` returns `isError: true`, no `structuredContent`, and the real message in text content (AppError / Error / non-Error).
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] `biome check` clean on changed files
- [x] Repro: with default `TAILSCALE_ALLOWED_TOOL_RISK=read`, `manage_policy_file update` returned the schema error; after the fix it returns `Tool requires write risk level`.

author: tya5
body:
## Summary

The router's tool descriptions and system prompt used `skill__code_review` as the canonical example of a qualified action name. There is no such skill in stdlib — none of the 15 stdlib skill directories ship with that name. The LLM ingested the example from tool descriptions (`plan`, `list_actions`, `describe_action`, `invoke_action`) and the router SP, treated it as canonical reference data, and **reproduced it verbatim in capability-question replies**.

A fresh-install user asking *"what can you do?"* / 「何ができる?」 was told the agent could run `skill__code_review` — a hallucinated capability with no implementation behind it. The fix replaces the hallucinated example with a real stdlib skill name so LLM echoes refer to a real capability.

## Trace evidence

Captured the failing path with `REYN_LLM_TRACE_DUMP` while running `reyn chat --cui` against `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` and prompt 「教えて、reyn で何ができる?」:

- `dogfood_trace.py --mode llm-tools-schema`: `skill__code_review` appears **4 times** in tools= description bytes (`plan` once, `list_actions` once, `describe_action` once, `invoke_action` once).
- LLM reply: enumerates `skill__code_review` alongside real stdlib skills (`skill__skill_builder`, `skill__index_docs`, …) as if it were a real capability.

`dogfood_trace.py` confirmed the hallucination root: the LLM is not making up a name; it is echoing what the descriptions told it to expect.

## Fix

Replace `skill__code_review` → `skill__index_docs` everywhere it appears as a canonical example. `index_docs` is chosen because it:

- is a real stdlib skill (file exists, schema is valid, postprocessor pipeline is documented)
- is the README's flagship RAG-demo
- is not a wrapper-skill (= unlike `read_local_files`, which is redundant with `invoke_action(file__read, …)` post-FP-0034)
- is concrete enough to make example contexts read naturally

Touch points (LLM-facing first, user-doc parity after):

- `src/reyn/tools/plan.py` — `steps_json` description's concrete example
- `src/reyn/tools/universal_catalog.py` — 5 places: `list_actions` / `describe_action` / `invoke_action` descriptions + `parse_qualified_name` docstring example
- `src/reyn/chat/router_system_prompt.py` — Action categories section + ROUTING RULE ABSOLUTE example
- `docs/concepts/universal-catalog{,.ja}.md` — reader-facing
- `docs/reference/config/reyn-yaml{,.ja}.md` — reader-facing
- `tests/test_plan_unified.py` — byte-identity description pin
- `tests/fixtures/llm/router/*.jsonl` — 7 LLMReplay fixtures re-recorded with `REYN_LLM_RECORD=1` (the router SP + tools= description change shifts the `args_hash` key)

Diff: 15 files, +32 / -17 (mostly fixture re-records; production source change is ~10 lines across 3 files).

## Measurement (weak gemini-2.5-flash-lite, N=5)

| Axis | Pre-fix | Post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| JA: `skill__code_review` hallucination | mentioned in description-driven reply path | **0/5** ✓ |
| JA: load-bearing meta-tool leak (`invoke_action` / `list_actions` etc) | ~40% (2/5) | ~40% (2/5) — unchanged, as expected |
| JA: prefix qualified-name leak (other `skill__X`, real ones) | ~60% (3/5) | ~60% (3/5) — unchanged, as expected |
| EN regression: hallucination present? | n/a | **0/5** ✓ |

The structural cleanse closes the hallucination axis cleanly. The load-bearing-name leak (`invoke_action` is mentioned 27 times across tool descriptions because the LLM needs the name to call the function-calling API) is unchanged — this is the structural ceiling. Going below would require either an SP rule forbidding function-name enumeration in reply text (= prompt-level workaround, deferred and gated on numerical justification per the team's weak-model thesis) or a stronger router model.

## Test plan

- [x] **Targeted tests** — `pytest tests/test_plan_unified.py tests/test_universal_catalog.py tests/test_universal_dispatch.py tests/test_universal_handlers.py tests/test_router_tools_universal_wrappers.py tests/test_router_invoke_skill_enum.py tests/test_replay_skill_router.py` → 223 passed
- [x] **LLMReplay re-record** — `REYN_LLM_RECORD=1 OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy LITELLM_API_BASE=http://localhost:4000 pytest tests/test_replay_skill_router.py` → 14 passed (recording mode)
- [x] **Replay after re-record** — same tests without `REYN_LLM_RECORD` → 14 passed (replay mode)
- [x] `ruff check src/reyn tests/test_plan_unified.py`
- [x] **Manual e2e (hallucination eliminated)** — `printf '教えて、reyn で何ができる?\n/quit\n' | reyn chat --cui` × 5 — `skill__code_review` appears 0 times across N=5
- [x] **Manual e2e (no EN regression for hallucination)** — `printf 'What can you do?\n/quit\n' | reyn chat --cui` × 5 — `skill__code_review` appears 0 times

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- `src/reyn/tools/action_usage_tracker.py:13` (module docstring example) and `src/reyn/events/event_schema.py:36` (comment) still reference `skill__code_review`. These are not LLM-facing — left as a separate doc-consistency sweep.
- Historical dogfood batch journals (`docs/deep-dives/journal/dogfood/2026-05-16-batch-23-fp-0034-practice/`) reference `skill__code_review` because that batch's test prompts literally used the name. Not touched — historical record.
- `scripts/dogfood_b23_driver.py` is a historical driver — not touched.
- **Patch C** (SP rule forbidding function-name enumeration in reply text) — deferred pending leader judgement on the thesis tension (= prompt-level workaround vs structural constraint).

## Summary

PR #93 / #94 マージ後の staging frontend E2E で発生していた 2 件の偽 fail を修正。release/v3.3.0 取込前のブロッカー解消。

## 原因と修正

### 1. `image-selection.spec.ts:49` shape regression (PR #92 由来)
**原因**:
- filter が `request().method() === 'GET'` を期待していたが、`App.vue:380` は `axios.post(endpoint, compositeParams, ...)` で送信。
- `waitForResponse(20s)` がマッチせずタイムアウト（3 retry 全失敗）。
- 元の PR #92 では ARM Pi で chromium が動かず実環境検証なしでマージしてしまい、UI 経路で実行された最初の機会で顕在化。

**修正**:
- filter を POST に変更（`resp.request().method() === 'POST'`）
- 検証対象を URL `searchParams` から **POST body** `response.request().postDataJSON().image2` に変更
- これで「フロントが正しい s3:// パスを組み立てて合成 API が 200 を返す」という本来のテスト目的を実際に検証できる

### 2. `settings.spec.ts:73 AC 9.4 デフォルトルールには削除ボタンが表示されない`
**原因**:
- `page.locator('div', { hasText: PRESET_RULE_NAME }).first()` が外側のリストコンテナ全体にヒット。
- その内部に含まれる **他カードの削除ボタンもカウント対象**になり、E2E 蓄積で user rules が増えると顕在化（DDB 6 件中 5 件が `e2e-*` rule に成長していた）。

**修正**:
- `RuleListItem.vue` の card root クラス `rounded-lg` で narrowing:
  - 旧: `page.locator('div', { hasText: PRESET_RULE_NAME }).first()`
  - 新: `page.locator('div.rounded-lg', { hasText: PRESET_RULE_NAME }).first()`

### 補助対応（コード外）
staging DDB の蓄積 `e2e-ui-*` / `e2e-nav-*` rules 5 件を DELETE API で削除済み（即時アンブロック）。preset 1 件のみ残存。

- [ ] CI 4/4 pass
- [ ] マージ後、staging frontend E2E 手動 dispatch で 2 件とも pass を確認

## 進め方
1. 本 PR を dev にマージ
2. staging frontend E2E 確認 → 全 pass
3. release/v3.3.0 に dev 取込
4. PR #81 CI 再走 → main マージ

author: aapeliv
body:
The recent UMS moderation PRs for thread comments/replies (#8510) and discussions (#8511) introduced `where_moderated_content_visible()`, which only checks an item's moderation *state* — not whether its author is a deleted, banned, blocked, or shadowed user.

In `threads.py` the moderation PR **replaced** `where_users_column_visible()` with `where_moderated_content_visible()` instead of applying both. The two are orthogonal checks and are used together everywhere else in the codebase (`references.py`, `api.py`, `requests.py`, etc.). The regression: comments and replies authored by invisible users were no longer hidden from other users.

This PR:
- Restores `where_users_column_visible()` alongside `where_moderated_content_visible()` in all `GetThread` queries (comment list, reply list, parent-comment existence check) and in `total_num_responses()`.
- Fixes a pre-existing inconsistency where the per-comment `num_replies` count included replies regardless of moderation state or author visibility — it now uses a correlated subquery with both filters, matching the depth-1 reply list.

Discussions are cluster-owned community content and were never filtered by creator visibility (before or after the moderation PR), so they are intentionally left unchanged.

## Testing
- Added `test_comment_by_invisible_user_hidden` and `test_reply_by_invisible_user_hidden` to `test_threads.py`. Both approve the moderation state so they isolate the author-visibility check; the reply test also asserts the parent comment's `num_replies` count drops when the replier is deleted.
- `uv run pytest src/tests/test_threads.py src/tests/test_discussions.py src/tests/test_events.py` — all pass.
- `make format` and `make mypy` clean for the changed files.

author: nmorabowen
body:
Follow-up to the Tunel-by-label thread. Building the tunnel in the natural orientation (x horizontal, z vertical — the **XZ plane**) and applying a convergence pressure with `line(normal=True, away_from=centre)` produced forces pointing purely **out-of-plane in ±Y** — it resolved without error but was physically meaningless.

## Root cause

`_edge_normal_q` in `LoadsComposite.py` hardcoded the in-plane normal to the **XY plane** — both branches computed `(Ty, -Tx, 0)`. For any model not in XY (tunnel cross-sections are almost always XZ), the edge normal collapsed to the global Y axis. Same silent-wrong-result class as the `add_wire` / `select` footguns.

## Change

Generalise the pressure normal to **any plane**:

- **`away_from` path:** fit the plane of the loaded curves (SVD over the edge endpoints), compute the edge normal as `T × P` in that plane, then sign-flip per edge to point away from `away_from`. `P`'s sign is irrelevant (disambiguated by `away_from`).
- **Surface path (no `away_from`):** use the adjacent face's **Gmsh-oriented normal** (`getParametrizationBounds` + `getNormal`), keeping the existing boundary-loop `sign` mechanism — now plane-general instead of XY-only.
- For an XY model (`P = +z`) the formula reduces **exactly** to the historical `(Ty, -Tx, 0)` (verified algebraically and empirically), so existing behaviour is unchanged.
- **Fail loud** when the in-plane normal is genuinely undefined: collinear curves (single straight segment) raise unless an off-line `away_from` breaks the degeneracy; a non-planar 3-D space curve raises and points the user to `q_xyz=`.

Helpers: `_fit_plane_normal`, `_surface_unit_normal`, `_curve_inplane_frame` (replaces `_curve_inplane_sign`; all private, single internal caller). `line()` docstrings de-XY-fied.

## Sign convention (unchanged, now verified across planes)

| `magnitude` with `away_from` = cavity centre | direction | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `−q` | inward (toward centre) | **convergence** (ground load) |
| `+q` | outward | internal pressure |

## Tests

New `tests/test_loads_line_normal_plane.py` (7 tests): XZ **and** XY convergence vs internal pressure with **zero out-of-plane leakage**, surface path on a non-XY plane, non-planar fail-loud, collinear recovery via `away_from`. The `loads.line(normal=True)` path had **zero prior test coverage**.

Loads / geometry / queries regression sweep green (**135 passed**, no regressions). Rebased onto current `main` (no conflicts).

author: mjbommar
body:
## Summary
Adds two new ``SpanSubject`` values — ``JUDGE`` and ``ROUTE`` — and wires emission so SSE consumers can finally see what the LLM judge was asked / how it scored, and what the Route primitive decided based on it.

Wishlist items #7 + #8, paired because both serve the same observability gap (plan-execute decisions invisible in the event stream).

## Why
Pre-0.1.0a9, when ``matched=False`` killed a plan there was no way to ask "what did the judge see?" or "what triggered REPLAN here?" without reading VFS-persisted ``SessionMemory``. The R1-REAL v2 matrix Test 7 re-verify against 0.1.0a8 hit exactly this — the SPA's run inspector showed plan steps and tool calls but the Route decision flow was opaque.

## What ships
- ``SpanSubject.JUDGE`` and ``SpanSubject.ROUTE`` enum values.
- ``Span`` docstring's attribute-conventions table extended with the keys both new subjects carry.
- ``evaluate_semantic`` accepts optional ``emitter`` + ``step_id`` kwargs:
  - START span with ``{step_id, expected, result_preview}`` (200-char truncation).
  - COMPLETE span on success with ``{matched, confidence, reasoning, mode}``.
  - ERROR span on Call.invoke failure with ``error_type`` / ``error_message``.
  - ``emitter=None`` is a no-op (backwards compat for direct unit-test callers).
- ``compose`` accepts optional ``emitter`` kwarg; emits ROUTE START + COMPLETE pair after every Route decision with ``{step_id, decision, reason, judgment_matched, judgment_confidence, replan_count}``.
- ``execute_decompose`` / ``execute_adaptive`` / ``execute_direct`` thread ``emitter`` through.
- ``PlanExecuteAgent._handle_plan_streaming`` passes its turn emitter into ``execute_adaptive``.

## What's NOT in this PR
- Span emission from the Direct strategy's structural-evaluate path (no LLM judge there → no useful JUDGE span). ``execute_direct`` accepts ``emitter`` for signature parity only.
- Backwards-incompatible changes to the ``Decision`` enum or ``RouteResult`` shape — the existing ``PrimitiveTrace`` flow is preserved.
- An SPA-side run-inspector change to render the new spans — covered by a follow-up kaos-ui PR.

## Test plan
- [x] ``uv run pytest tests/unit/events/test_judge_route_spans.py -v`` — 8/8 pass (enum extension, emitter-None backwards compat, START+COMPLETE pair, START+ERROR pair, input truncation cap, compose signature gain)
- [x] ``uv run pytest tests/unit/events/ tests/unit/planning/ tests/unit/test_route.py tests/unit/test_plan_response_formatter.py`` — 165 pass, no regressions
- [x] ``uv run ruff format --check`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run ruff check`` — clean
- [x] ``uv run ty check`` — clean

One of several wishlist PRs bundled into 0.1.0a9. Conflicts expected at merge time with #34 (DEEPEN drop) — resolution will keep DEEPEN-removed compose.py signature + the new emitter kwarg.

author: lmorchard
body:
## Summary

Salvaged from #518 (parked pending WASM-based replacement — see linked issue). Adds structured `.data` shapes alongside the existing `.text` rendering on the read-heavy tool families: vault, workspace, notes, and tabstack.

`ToolResult.data` is auto-rendered as a fenced JSON block in the tool result the LLM sees, giving downstream consumers parseable structure without hallucinating shape from prose. This benefits **every LLM-direct caller** — no `code_execution` sandbox required.

## Design rule

`.data` carries STRUCTURE; `.text` carries PROSE/PAYLOAD. They do not duplicate large content — body/content stays in `.text` only so the auto-rendered JSON block doesn't double the tool-result token cost.

## Per-tool shapes

| Tool | `.data` |
|------|---------|
| `vault_read` | `{"path", "frontmatter", "body_size", "body_lines"}` (body is in `.text`) |
| `vault_search` | `{"query", "mode": "semantic"\|"substring", "results": [...]}` |
| `vault_write` | `{"path", "created", "bytes_written"}` |
| `vault_journal_append` | `{"path", "tags", "entry_size"}` |
| `workspace_read` | `{"path", "size", "lines", "range", "truncated"}` (content is in `.text`) |
| `workspace_list` | `{"path", "entries": [{"name", "is_dir", "size"}]}` |
| `workspace_glob` | `{"pattern", "path", "matches": [...], "truncated"}` |
| `workspace_search` | `{"pattern", "path", "total_matches", "truncated", "files": [{"path", "match_lines"}]}` |
| `notes_read` | `{"count", "notes": [{"timestamp", "text"}]}` |
| `notes_append` | `{"timestamp", "chars"}` |
| `tabstack_extract_markdown` | `{"url", "size"}` |
| `tabstack_extract_json` | `{"url", "result": <parsed object>}` |
| `tabstack_research` | `{"query", "mode", "size"}` |

## Signature changes

Two function signatures changed from `-> str` to `-> ToolResult`:
- `vault_journal_append`
- `tabstack_extract_markdown`, `tabstack_extract_json`, `tabstack_research`

The `execute_tool` layer already normalizes `str → ToolResult` via `_to_tool_result`, so this is purely additive at every call site.

## Why salvaged separately

PR #518 (always-loaded `code_execution` sandbox) was parked after Copilot's second review surfaced a framing-vs-reality issue: the subprocess runner doesn't actually restrict stdlib (`subprocess`, `socket`, `urllib`, filesystem) — only the advertised `dc.*` API. Real isolation needs a WASM-based runtime (or similar capability boundary).

The `.data` work in this PR is **completely orthogonal** to the sandbox. It benefits direct LLM tool use today; whatever code-execution primitive eventually lands will also benefit. Splitting it out lets it ship now without waiting on the larger architectural redesign.

See #538 for the WASM-based code_execution follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `make check` (lint + pyright + tsc) — all green
- [x] `make test` — 2554 passed
- [x] New `tests/test_tool_data_shapes.py` — 12 cases pinning down the `.data` contract per tool, so future edits surface regressions
- [x] Existing tests updated where return type changed (3 in `test_vault_tools.py` + assertion helper switches in `test_workspace_tools.py`)

## Summary

- Extends the #838 prototype-method recogniser to fire when the receiver
  is a function declaration (or function-valued local), not just a `class`
  block. dayjs's minified bundle uses `function M(t){}; var m =
  M.prototype; m.format = function(){…}` — pre-fix `lookup_class("M")`
  returned None and every method registration was a silent PropertySet.

  `js_register_function_prototype_method` and `js_new_function_construct`.
  Both go through a shared `synthetic_class_id_for_function` keyed by the
  closure's NaN-boxed bits (reuses the `FUNCTION_CLASS_IDS` side-table
  from #711) so the register site and the matching `new <FuncRef>(args)`
  site stamp the same id on the instance.
- Closes four collateral Perry gaps that surface together in dayjs's
  outer IIFE: FnDecl hoist-pre-pass reusing outer-scope locals, missing
  `Expr::NewDynamic` arm in `referenced_from_fn` pre-scan, `Expr::New {
  class_name }` routing for function-valued locals, and the
  `keys_array == null` early-return in `js_object_get_field_by_name`
  that skipped `CLASS_PROTOTYPE_METHODS` lookup. Also adds shallow

author: yuechen-li-dev
body:
### Motivation
- Provide the M64 seed for tag-only enums and expression-level `match` so SDSL‑V can represent enum declarations and match arms in the AST and parser as a first step toward full exhaustiveness/type lowering.
- Wire minimal validator/emitter/runner handling to avoid regressions while leaving full lowering/type-checking and HLSL emission for follow-up work.
- Keep the changes conservative: parsing + AST + baseline validation first, with explicit unsupported fallbacks in execution/emission paths.

### Description
- Added AST nodes for enums and match: `SdslvDecl::Enum`, `SdslvEnumDecl`, `SdslvEnumVariant`, `SdslvExpression::Match`, and `SdslvMatchArm`.
- Added lexer/token entries for `enum` and `match` and extended the parser to parse top-level `enum Name { Variant; ... }` and expression-level `match subject { Enum.Variant => expr }` with both `=>` and `->` arm arrows.
- Implemented baseline validation hooks: enums participate in top-level name uniqueness and a `ValidateEnum` check enforces non-empty enums and rejects duplicate variant names.
- Wired the new nodes through validator/emitter/runner with conservative fallbacks: `Match` currently resolves to `Unknown` in type-resolution, the emitter emits an explicit unsupported placeholder in unsupported expression contexts, and the test runner rejects executing `match` expressions to avoid runtime regressions.
- Left full M64 responsibilities (variant resolution against subject type, exhaustive-match checking, HLSL lowering to integer constants and if/else chains, and match result type unification) as the next concrete follow-up.

### Testing
- Ran unit and integration test suite with `cargo test -q --lib` and `cargo test -q`, which passed (271 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored in this run).
- Ran style check with `cargo run --bin wyrmfmt -- check --lang rust src tests examples`, which completed successfully aside from existing deprecation/warning notes.
- The change is a seed pass (Outcome B — meaningful progression): parser/AST and baseline validation landed and tests pass, while full exhaustive-match validation and HLSL lowering remain to be implemented.

author: gfargo
body:
## Summary

Final PR for the recursive submodule navigation epic (#931). Two changes:

### Cache-aware boot-load pop

The runtime's per-frame `RepoFrameRuntime` already preserved `context` / `contextStatus` across drill-out cycles (#983 shipped the slice-don't-clear pop semantics). But the boot-load effect in `LogInkApp` was happily re-firing for the parent's git on every pop and overwriting the cached context with a fresh fetch. Functionally correct, but the network round-trip + brief loading flicker made drill-out feel laggier than it had to.

**Fix:** gate each per-key load on the active frame's `contextStatus[key]` — skip when it's already `'ready'`. The frame's seed status is all `'loading'` (`createInitialContextStatus()`), so first mount and freshly-pushed frames still fetch as before; only pops back to a cached frame skip the work.

The status read goes through a ref so we don't have to include `contextStatus` in the effect's dep array — including it would re-fire the effect on every per-key `'ready'` write the effect itself produces, causing duplicate in-flight fetches for not-yet-completed keys. The ref pattern gives us "read latest" semantics with the effect still gated on git swaps only.

### Workstation README docs

New **"Nested-repo navigation (#931)"** section in [src/workstation/README.md](src/workstation/README.md) documenting:

- The two parallel structures (view-model `repoStack` vs. runtime `RepoStackRuntimes`)
- The active-frame projection model
- The two drill-in entry points (commit-diff + submodules view)
- Esc / `<` / palette `navigateBack` exit semantics
- A recipe for adding another entry point (write a pure resolver, plumb the output, dispatch `pushRepoFrame`)

## Closes the epic

#931 asked for:

| Requirement | Shipped in |
|---|---|
| `Enter` on a submodule row drills into its history | #986 (commit-diff) + #992 (submodules view) |
| Navigate the submodule's commits / files / branches as if `coco ui` were launched from the submodule directory | #985 (per-frame `SimpleGit` swap) |
| `Esc` / `<` pops back to the parent repo | #984 |
| `SubmoduleStack` state on the root view model | #941 |
| Rebound `SimpleGit` instance for every loader | #985 |
| Title-bar breadcrumb | #984 |
| Context-load invalidation / scoping per frame | #983 + #985 + this PR's cache-aware pop |

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npm run test:jest` — 173 suites, **2032 passed** (no regressions; this PR adds no new tests since the boot-load gating is a one-line guard inside a React effect that isn't tested directly — the existing scenario fixture `submodule-with-history` exercises the round trip)
- [x] `npm run build` (no schema regen)
- [x] `npm run test:cli` — 10/10
- [x] `npm run release:dry-run`

## Known follow-ups

Each small enough for a focused follow-up issue if they ever bite:

- **In-flight refresh-during-push race.** A user `r` refresh that's mid-await when a push fires writes its result to the new active frame. Rare, non-destructive (stale data briefly). Closing the race needs a frame-by-git tag on the writes.
- **Per-frame sidebar tab / sort mode persistence.** Today these carry over root → submodule; users may want frame-scoped state. The persistence keys would need to incorporate the frame's workdir.

Closes #931.

author: hagevvashi
body:
## Goal
Enforce mandatory git-expert agent delegation for all write operations, preventing unvetted commits and ensuring proper testing, verification, and conflict resolution before changes are applied.

## Strategy
Add RULE 4 to the check-deprecated-git.sh hook to block direct execution of write-related git commands (commit, push, switch, restore, rebase, merge, reset, revert, tag, stash) and require delegation to the git-expert agent instead. Continue allowing read-only operations (status, log, diff, show, remote, branch -v) to unblock developer workflows.

## Why

| 比較項目 | 重み | 直接実行許可 | git-expert 強制 | hybrid（一部許可） |
|---------|------|-----------|----------------|-----------------|
| a. コミットメッセージ品質 | 高 | △ | ◎ | △ |
| b. テスト実行保証 | 高 | × | ◎ | △ |
| c. ブランチ状態確認 | 高 | △ | ◎ | △ |
| d. コンフリクト解決 | 高 | × | ◎ | × |
| e. 開発効率（読み取り操作） | 中 | ◎ | ○ | ◎ |
| f. アクシデント防止 | 中 | × | ◎ | △ |
| **採用** | | | **✅** | |

git-expert 強制により、全ての書き込み操作が適切なレビュー・検証を通るため、品質と安全性を最大化できます。読み取り専用操作は許可することで、開発効率も保ちます。

## What
- **check-deprecated-git.sh**: RULE 4 追加（行 44-69）
  - 読み取り専用操作の許可: git status, log, diff, show, remote, branch -v
  - 書き込み操作の禁止: commit, push, switch, restore, rebase, merge, reset, revert, tag, stash
  - git-expert 委譲の強制と、利用可能な読み取り操作の明示

- **settings.json**: hook パス簡潔化

## Summary

Two greenfield phase-agent skills shipped as **Initiative 1 Phase 5** of the phase-agent architecture (parent: CTL-443, plan: `thoughts/shared/plans/2026-05-16-catalyst-phase-agent-architecture.md`). Both consume the broker's `phase_lifecycle` interest (CTL-447, shipped) by emitting canonical `phase.<name>.<status>.<TICKET>` events, and are wired into the orchestrator state machine in CTL-452.

### Skills

- **`phase-triage`** (Opus) — reads a Linear ticket via `linearis`, classifies (`feature` | `bug` | `docs` | `refactor` | `chore`), expands acronyms (PR / CLI / API / OTel / …), identifies cross-ticket dependencies, estimates scope (`small` | `medium` | `large` | `epic`), writes `triage.json`, posts a triage comment to Linear, applies the `triaged` label (tolerant of absence).
- **`phase-monitor-deploy`** (Haiku) — reads merge SHA from `phase-pr.json`, blocks on a `deployment_status` event via `catalyst-events wait-for`, delegates to the gstack `/canary` skill on deploy `success`, writes `phase-monitor-deploy.json`. Emits `.skipped` when no deploy event arrives before the per-skill timeout (env-configurable).

### Architecture decisions

- **No scaffold dependency.** CTL-448's planned helpers (`phase-agent-dispatch`, `phase-agent-emit-complete`, `_phase-agent-template/SKILL.md`) are not on `main` yet despite the Linear state. These two skills are self-contained: each sources a small new helper at `plugins/dev/scripts/lib/phase-emit-complete.sh` that builds the canonical OTel event through the existing `lib/canonical-event.sh`. When CTL-448 lands, its richer dispatcher can absorb this helper mechanically — the call sites do not change.
- **Skipped is success.** When the deploy pipeline does not emit a `deployment_status` event for the merge SHA, `phase-monitor-deploy` writes `phase.monitor-deploy.skipped.<TICKET>` and exits 0. The orchestrator treats `.skipped` as a forward step, not a failure — the PR is already merged.

### Files added

```
plugins/dev/scripts/lib/phase-emit-complete.sh         (helper)
plugins/dev/skills/phase-triage/SKILL.md
plugins/dev/skills/phase-monitor-deploy/SKILL.md

## Summary

PR #1114 already shipped half of this fix — Teller **connect** in v2. The other half (Teller **reauth** in v2) was left as a TODO in #1114's PR body. This is that follow-up.

Symptom: clicking *Reconnect* on a Teller connection that's `pending_reauth` does nothing — the Teller Connect popup never opens. `reauth-sheet.tsx` was reading `window.__TELLER_APP_ID__`, a global nobody sets, exactly the same dead-global bug PR #1114 fixed for the connect path.

Why the reauth path can't just reuse #1114's fix: for connect, `link_token` IS the Teller app id (Teller has no server-issued session token). For reauth, `link_token` is the existing enrollment id (it pins Teller Connect to the broken connection so the user re-enters credentials for *that* enrollment). Teller Connect's `setup({applicationId, enrollmentId})` needs **both**, so the reauth response has to carry the app id as a second field.

Changes:
- `internal/provider/provider.go`: add optional `ApplicationID` to `LinkSession`.
- `internal/provider/teller/reauth.go`: populate `ApplicationID: p.appID` (Plaid leaves it empty).
- `internal/api/connections_reauth.go`: add `application_id` (omitempty) to the response.
- `web/src/api/types.ts`: add `application_id?: string` to `LinkSession`.
- `web/src/features/connections/reauth-sheet.tsx`: drop the `__TELLER_APP_ID__` global; read `session.application_id` and surface an error toast if the server isn't configured.
- Integration test asserting Teller reauth returns `application_id` (and a regression-pin asserting Plaid still doesn't).

#1112 is superseded — its connect-flow half is already in main via #1114, and its CI was failing on an older base. Closing it.

author: copilot
body:
This PR bootstraps the first demonstrable CRIS-GVIE MVP as a standalone local voice interaction runtime (not a chatbot platform). It implements the end-to-end local loop: mic capture → local STT → Ollama response → local TTS playback → persisted session transcript.

- **MVP runtime architecture (modular, replaceable components)**
  - Added a clean `gvie/` package split by responsibility:
    - `runtime.py` orchestrator loop
    - `recorder.py` microphone capture
    - `stt.py` local transcription via `faster-whisper`
    - `llm.py` Ollama local REST client
    - `tts.py` Piper synthesis + local playback
    - `session.py` isolated persistence layer
    - `models.py` transcript schema
    - `config.py` typed runtime configuration
  - Exported runtime entrypoints via `gvie/__init__.py`.

- **Local interaction loop implementation**
  - Added interactive flow in `VoiceRuntime.run()`:
    - start recording on Enter
    - stop recording on Enter
    - transcribe audio
    - generate response with Ollama (`qwen2.5:14b` default)
    - synthesize and play response audio
    - persist user/assistant turns
    - repeat until quit.

- **Session persistence contract**
  - Implemented session storage under:
    - `sessions/session_<timestamp>/metadata.json`
    - `sessions/session_<timestamp>/transcript.jsonl`
  - Transcript rows follow a stable schema with timestamp, speaker, and text.

- **Bootstrap and docs**
  - Added runnable example: `examples/local_interviewer.py`.
  - Added `requirements.txt` with lightweight MVP dependencies.
  - Replaced README with architecture, setup (Python/Ollama/Piper), run instructions, MVP limits, and roadmap.
  - Added `sessions/.gitignore` and `docs/.gitkeep` scaffolding.

Example orchestrator usage:

```python
from gvie import RuntimeConfig, VoiceRuntime

runtime = VoiceRuntime(config=RuntimeConfig())
runtime.run()
```

→ Speak response using Piper

author: choiceoh
body:
## Summary

`mirjson.fromInstr` encodes `IntrinsicInstr.Kind` as `int(x.Kind)` — the raw `iota` value. The LIR Proto subprocess decodes via `toolchain/mir_json.osty::mirJsonIntrinsic` which expects the **toolchain's** `MirIntrinsicKind` declaration order. Go's enum had `IntrinsicBytesConcat` at position 86; toolchain has `MirIntrinsicBytesConcat = 7`. Result: every intrinsic from position 7 onward was silently miscompiled — `strings.indexOf` produced `osty_rt_strings_HasSuffix` calls (off-by-one wrong intrinsic).

### Changes

- **[internal/mir/mir.go](internal/mir/mir.go)**: move `IntrinsicBytesConcat` from position 86 → position 7 to align with toolchain wire format.
- **[toolchain/lir_proto.osty](toolchain/lir_proto.osty)**: `lirLowerMirIndexOf` now recognizes `Int?` sugar form (not just explicit `Option<Int>`) so it routes through `lirWrapOptionFromI64Sentinel` instead of falling through to PR #1891's auto-wrap (which would `Some(-1)` for not-found, semantically wrong).
- **[internal/mirjson/intrinsic_wire_test.go](internal/mirjson/intrinsic_wire_test.go)** (new): regression test pinning all 67 intrinsic kind wire values. New intrinsic added on one side without the other → immediate fail.

### Before / after IR for `strings.indexOf("hello", "ll")`

**Before** (off-by-one decode):
```llvm
call i1 @osty_rt_strings_HasSuffix(ptr @.str.0, ptr @.str.1)
zext i1 %t1 to i64
insertvalue %Option.Int undef, i64 0, 0    ; Some()
insertvalue %Option.Int %t3, i64 %t2, 1    ; payload = HasSuffix's i1 zext
```
Semantics: `Some(0)` or `Some(1)` — but `endsWith != indexOf`.

**After**:
```llvm
call i64 @osty_rt_strings_IndexOf(ptr @.str.0, ptr @.str.1)
icmp ne i64 %0, -1                          ; sentinel-aware
select i1 %1, i64 0, i64 1                  ; disc: Some=0/None=1
; ... Option<Int> aggregate ...
```

## Test plan

- [x] `osty install-self` 클린 빌드 통과 (osty-self regen)
- [x] `osty build --backend llvm <indexOf smoke>`: IndexOf intrinsic correctly emitted
- [x] `go test ./internal/mir/... ./internal/mirjson/...` 통과
- [x] `just osty-tests` 33 tests passed
- [x] `just prepush` 통과
- [ ] CI 그린 확인

## 영향 범위

Wire-format 이 -1 shift 되어 `IntrinsicChanMake` (7→8) 이후 모든 intrinsic 의 정수 인코딩이 변경. 캐시된 osty-self 자동 무효화 → 다음 build 시 재생성. 사용자 수동 작업 불필요.

body:
Closes part of #375 (MVP — see Followups for what was intentionally deferred).

## Summary

Pursuit is the on-demand answer to "track this for me" — a markdown file
under \`~/.loom/pursuits/<id>.md\` that 絲絲 reads, refreshes with fresh
data, and rewrites when the user asks about it.

Aligned with the design comment on #375 (https://github.com/Dakai666/Loom/issues/375#issuecomment-4469519048):
- **Task axis, not memory axis** — pursuit lives in the filesystem, never touches \`memory.db\`. \`memory.db\` stays as 絲絲's cognition; pursuit stays as user-directed task artifacts that die with the task.
- **On-demand, not daemon** — no background poller, no Hook D dependency, no race conditions. The agent calls \`pursuit_read\` + web tools + \`pursuit_write\` herself when prompted.
- **Edit-style, not verb soup** — single \`pursuit_write\` overwrites the whole markdown (per #205/#206 lesson).

## Surface

| Tool | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| \`pursuit_list\` | Returns active pursuit ids (filesystem listing) |
| \`pursuit_read\` | Returns full markdown for a given id |
| \`pursuit_write\` | Atomic overwrite of the whole markdown by id |

Recommended markdown shape (suggested in tool description, not enforced):

\`\`\`markdown
# OpenAI 世紀審判
status: active
created: 2026-05-17
last_pulled: 2026-05-17

## 維度
- 陪審團裁決
- 估值變化（±20%）
- 監管動向

## 累積快照
### 2026-05-17（初建）
- 估值 last known: \$300B
- 監管: SEC 8 月有非正式 inquiry
\`\`\`

## Architecture decisions

- **Placement**: \`loom/core/tasks/pursuit.py\` (logic) + \`loom/platform/cli/tools.py\` (tool factories) + \`loom/core/session.py\` (registration), mirroring TaskListManager's split. Did not open a new top-level module (no \`loom/extensibility/\`, no \`loom/pursuit/\`) — YAGNI and tasks/ is the natural home per CLAUDE.md's Tasks layer.
- **PursuitStore is filesystem-rooted, session-agnostic** — one instance per session is fine (no per-session state).
- **Path traversal**: id validated against \`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$\` before any FS touch. Paths outside \`~/.loom/pursuits/\` are unreachable.
- **Atomic writes**: tmp + rename, so a crashed write never leaves a half-file.

## Pre-flight checks (per CLAUDE.md)

- \`gitnexus_impact(TaskListManager, upstream)\` → **risk LOW** (only \`tasks/__init__.py\` imports it; we add a sibling file, don't modify TaskListManager).
- \`gitnexus_detect_changes(all)\` → **risk_level: low**, 0 affected processes. The "touched" jobs/_fmt_job/_jobs_* entries are line-shift artifacts (insertion above them), not real edits.
- New imports respect the layer rules (no Tasks → Autonomy/Memory leakage).

## Tests

41 new tests in \`tests/test_pursuit.py\`:
- PursuitStore id validation (parametrized: 6 valid / 10 invalid including path traversal, uppercase, dots, underscores, length overflow)
- list / read / write / delete / exists semantics
- atomic write leaves no .tmp leftover
- Tool executors: success, missing arg, invalid arg, not-found, overwrite, path traversal rejection

Run: \`pytest tests/test_pursuit.py\` → 41 passed in 0.41s. Combined with \`test_tasklist.py\`: 69 passed.

## Intentionally NOT in this PR (Followups)

- **\`pursuit_pull\` composite tool** — original design proposed this; cut after realizing the agent can orchestrate \`pursuit_read\` + \`web_search\` + \`pursuit_write\` more flexibly. Reconsider if real usage shows the chaining is awkward.
- **\`pursuit_delete\` tool** — \`PursuitStore.delete()\` exists but is unexposed. Users can \`rm\` the markdown for now; add the tool when retiring trackers becomes a frequent verb.
- **Schema enforcement** — markdown shape is a suggestion in the tool description, not validated. Let real usage pressure the shape before locking it.

## Test plan

- [ ] In a fresh \`loom chat\` session, say "幫我追蹤 OpenAI 世紀審判" and verify 絲絲 creates \`~/.loom/pursuits/openai-trial.md\` via \`pursuit_write\`
- [ ] Ask "OpenAI 案最近怎樣" later, verify she calls \`pursuit_read\` then runs searches
- [ ] Say "我目前在追什麼" and verify \`pursuit_list\` is invoked
- [ ] Edit the markdown by hand, then have 絲絲 read it — verify she sees the edit

author: jeremylongshore
body:
## Summary

Closes #660 item 4 (Freshie compliance snapshot design).

The `*_compliance` tables had `<entity>_path TEXT UNIQUE`. `INSERT OR REPLACE` therefore collided on path alone, silently overwriting prior validation runs even though every row had a `run_id` column. Running the validator twice in one day kept only the latest, losing the before/after history the `run_id` column was meant to enable.

## Fix

- Drop single-column UNIQUE on `skill_compliance.skill_path` / `agent_compliance.agent_path` / `plugin_compliance.plugin_path`
- Add composite `UNIQUE (<path>, run_id)` so `INSERT OR REPLACE` only collides within the same run
- Idempotent in-process migration in `populate_compliance_db()`: PRAGMA-introspects each table at startup, detects the legacy single-column autoindex, renames old table → `<table>__migrate_tmp`, lets `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` build the new schema, copies rows across the column intersection, drops temp
- Only acts when legacy constraint is present — fresh DBs and already-migrated DBs both no-op

## Verified locally

Ran the migration against a copy of `freshie/inventory.sqlite`:

```
BEFORE:
  skill_compliance:   sqlite_autoindex... cols=[skill_path]  (3563 rows)
  agent_compliance:   sqlite_autoindex... cols=[agent_path]  (213 rows)
  plugin_compliance:  sqlite_autoindex... cols=[plugin_path] (380 rows)

AFTER:
  skill_compliance:   sqlite_autoindex... cols=[skill_path, run_id]  (3563 rows preserved)
  agent_compliance:   sqlite_autoindex... cols=[agent_path, run_id]  (213 rows preserved)
  plugin_compliance:  sqlite_autoindex... cols=[plugin_path, run_id] (380 rows preserved)
```

Then inserted the same `skill_path` with a different `run_id`:
```
Rows for plugins/saas-packs/guidewire-pack/skills/guidewire-performance-tuning:
  [(99, 'A', 1), (74, 'C', 6)]
```

Both snapshots coexist — was 1 row before, now 2.

## Not in this commit

`freshie/inventory.sqlite` itself is untouched. The next discovery run that calls `populate_compliance_db` will trigger the migration in place. From that run onward the snapshot history accumulates correctly.

## Test plan
- [x] Migration round-trip preserves row counts
- [x] Composite-UNIQUE allows same-path-different-run coexistence
- [x] No-op on already-migrated DB
- [ ] CI green on this PR (no production DB touch)

## Closes
Closes #660 item 4. Items 1b / 2 / 3 still open in #660.

- Jeremy Longshore

author: ryanclark2
body:
## Summary

Fixes an `invalid input syntax for type uuid` crash in the heartbeat dispatcher when a skill mention link in issue markdown uses a slug (e.g. ``skill://my-skill-slug``) rather than the company-skill UUID. The crash blocks Paperclip auto-recovery from resuming any issue whose description/comments reference a skill by slug.

## Root cause

`resolveRunScopedMentionedSkillKeys` (`server/src/services/heartbeat.ts`) was querying `company_skills.id` (UUID column) with the raw output of `extractSkillMentionIds`, which returns the *host* portion of every ``skill://X`` link. For code-built mentions that host is the company-skill UUID, but for human-authored markdown it is the skill slug. The query then trips Postgres' UUID parser.

author: reasonofmoon
body:
💡 **What:** Optimized the `AnalyzedContent` component by caching the regex generation and text splitting in a `useMemo` hook, wrapping the component in `React.memo`, and substituting an O(N) array lookup with an O(1) mathematical index parity check (`index % 2 === 1`).

🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation reconstructed an expensive regex and ran `.split` on potentially large texts upon every re-render. Additionally, finding if a split string was a highlighted word required traversing the entire vocabulary list array (`.some`), leading to sluggish mapping over the split array chunks for larger texts and vocabs. 

📊 **Impact:** Re-renders of the large body of text are prevented on unrelated parent state changes (like selecting a word). Iterating over the parsed string pieces is computationally cheaper as finding if a substring should be rendered as a highlighted button is now O(1) instead of O(N).

🔬 **Measurement:** Profile the render time of the `AnalyzedContent` component via React DevTools when clicking words to define them, or unchecking them from the vocabulary list. The component should not re-render, and the initial render parsing string segments should execute measurably faster.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [4216401763475266183](https://jules.google.com/task/4216401763475266183) started by @Reasonofmoon*

## Summary by Sourcery

Optimize the AnalyzedContent component’s rendering performance and document a regex-based index parity optimization.

Enhancements:
- Memoize regex construction and text splitting in AnalyzedContent and wrap the component with React.memo to reduce unnecessary re-renders.
- Replace array-based highlight detection with an O(1) index parity check when iterating over split text segments.

body:
## Summary

- **Fix "always Spoiled" detection bug** — `brownDark` was a catch-all `else` bucket that absorbed all background/ambiguous pixels, inflating the brownDark ratio on every image and forcing a Spoiled result. Now only genuinely dark (v < 42) or brownish pixels count; teal/magenta/neutral pixels are skipped entirely. `total` counts classified fruit pixels only so background never skews the ratios.
- **Fix "always Apple" bug** — HSV circular mean was polluted by low-saturation background pixels slipping through the old `s<12` filter. Raised to `s<20`, increased centre-region weight from 2× to 3×, so the fruit dominates the hue average.
- **Recalibrated ripeness profiles** — each of the 5 fruits now has well-separated per-stage colour vectors matched to the new bucketing logic (e.g. Banana Ripe: yellow 0.87, Spoiled: dark 0.88).
- **Fix phone camera on iOS Safari** — replaced `onClick → element.click()` (blocked by iOS Safari) with the `<label htmlFor>` → `<input id>` HTML pattern. Split into two buttons: **TAKE PHOTO** (rear camera) and **UPLOAD FROM GALLERY**.
- **Presentation Mode** — narrowed to 5 supported fruits only in a 5-column grid.
- **Code quality** — fixed unused imports in Chatbot/Hero, moved `CustomTooltip` outside Timeline render, excluded legacy nested directory from ESLint. Lint: 0 errors · Build: success.

author: x812033727
body:
## Summary

User's wrapper `AVBT/系列/回胴錄/DAM-046/` had two main videos: `DAM-046.mp4` (972 MB) and `DAM-046 (3).mp4` (610 MB). Cleanup refused to flatten because the existing logic required **exactly one** main video. The wrapper just sat there.

Per the user's rule:
- 「如果遇到兩個檔案一樣只是解析度不一樣而已就搬最大的」 — same content, different resolution → keep largest
- 「如果是有分集都搬」 — multi-part (CD1/CD2/...) → keep all

## Implementation

`_canonical_video_name(name)` strips PikPak's `(N)` auto-dedupe suffix and quality tags (`HD` / `720p` / `1080p` / `4K` / `高清` / `超清` …) but leaves part markers (`CD1`/`CD2`, `-1`/`-2`, variant letters `A`/`B`/`C`) intact.

| Name | Canonical | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `DAM-046.mp4` | `DAM-046` | (same canonical = dup) |
| `DAM-046 (3).mp4` | `DAM-046` | dropped (smaller) |
| `DAM-046 HD.mp4` | `DAM-046` | dropped (smaller) |
| `DAM-046-CD1.mp4` | `DAM-046-CD1` | kept (distinct part) |
| `DAM-046-CD2.mp4` | `DAM-046-CD2` | kept (distinct part) |
| `DAM-046A.mp4` / `DAM-046B.mp4` | `DAM-046A` / `DAM-046B` | both kept |

The flatten branch now triggers whenever `main_videos ≥ 1`. It groups them by canonical, keeps the largest per group, and flattens every keeper to the parent. The wrapper is then trashed (taking the smaller dups, junk mp4s, gifs, apks, etc. with it).

- **1 keeper** → name after the wrapper code (`code_full`), preserving existing behaviour.
- **2+ keepers** → name each after its canonical so CD1/CD2 don't collide.

NDJSON event's `reason` now reports `分集 N 部・丟掉 M 個低解析重複` so the UI surfaces what happened.

## For user's case

`DAM-046/` flattens cleanly:
- `DAM-046.mp4` (972 MB) → moved to `回胴錄/`
- `DAM-046 (3).mp4` (610 MB), 7 junk mp4s/gifs, BT-spam apk/rar → trashed with the wrapper

## Test plan

- [ ] Run 「整理此資料夾」 on `回胴錄/` — `DAM-046/` should disappear, `DAM-046.mp4` appears next to the other DAM-* files.
- [ ] Manually create a CD1/CD2 wrapper → both files survive the flatten.
- [ ] Pre-existing 1-keeper wrappers still flatten exactly as before.

author: shiyucheng2018
body:
## Summary

Two-commit PR aligning polily-plugin with Claude Code's documented plugin conventions, plus a CI gate so we don't slip on CHANGELOG discipline going forward.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin manifest location | `plugin.json` at repo root | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` ✓ canonical |
| Marketplace index | _(none — couldn't `/plugin marketplace add` this repo)_ | `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` ✓ |
| Plugin install identifier | `polily-plugin` (awkward) | `polily` ✓ (repo stays `polily-plugin`) |
| Manifest fields | name/version/desc/homepage/repo | + author / license / keywords |
| README install command | legacy `claude plugin add ...` | modern `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install` |
| CHANGELOG | absent | added, with 0.1.0 / 0.1.1 / 0.1.2 backfill |
| CI | none (no `.github/` dir) | `changelog-check` job mirrors sister polily repo |

## Why this matters

The root-level `plugin.json` was being silently ignored by Claude Code — the plugin manager only reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Auto-discovery picked up `skills/polily/SKILL.md` and the install mostly worked, but `/plugin list` / `/plugin details` displayed no metadata. And without `marketplace.json`, users couldn't do the two-step `add marketplace` → `install plugin` flow that gives them `/plugin update` afterward.

Verified against the [obra/superpowers reference layout](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) and the [official Claude Code plugin docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference).

## Commits

1. **`f0467ac feat(packaging): align to canonical Claude Code plugin layout (v0.1.2)`**
   The substantive refactor. Manifest moves, marketplace index gets added, name normalises, README + CLAUDE.md get the new flow.

2. **`a338baf ci: add CHANGELOG release-discipline gate`**
   `scripts/check_changelog.py` (pure-stdlib, no install step) + `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Validates the topmost section is `[X.Y.Z]` not `[Unreleased]`, footer link uses `releases/tag/` format, and the `[Unreleased]` link compares against the current top release. Locally verified passes on this PR's CHANGELOG and fails on injected bad states (Rule 1 + Rule 4).

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m json.tool` clean on both `.claude-plugin/*.json`
- [x] `plugin.json.version` (0.1.2) matches `marketplace.json.plugins[0].version` (0.1.2)
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_changelog.py CHANGELOG.md` passes locally
- [x] Negative tests: gate catches `[Unreleased]` at top with no release below (Rule 1), and stale `[Unreleased]` footer link (Rule 4)
- [ ] CI `changelog-check` job passes on this PR (self-test — the new gate runs against this PR's own CHANGELOG)

author: amals367
body:
💡 What:
Replaced the `detail_exists` function, which queried the database for each item individually, with `get_all_existing_ids`. This new function queries the database once to load all existing identifier values into a Python set before the batch processing loop begins. The item check inside the loop is now a fast `O(1)` set membership check.

🎯 Why:
The original approach suffered from the N+1 query problem, causing significant latency and database load that grew linearly with the number of items being processed. This was particularly impactful during long-running collection jobs.

📊 Measured Improvement:
A benchmark processing 1000 items showed the N+1 query approach taking ~0.2901 seconds while the single set lookup took ~0.0019 seconds, resulting in an ~155x speedup for the check phase.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Fixes YouTube downloads failing with "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" errors by auto-detecting the user's browser and passing its cookies to yt-dlp. Also strips playlist parameters (`list`, `index`, `start_radio`) from URLs so pasting a link from a playlist/mix correctly downloads only the single video.

**Changes:**
- `detect_browser()` / `get_cookie_opts()` — iterates Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Opera/Brave/Chromium to find an available browser for cookie extraction, then passes `cookiesfrombrowser` to yt-dlp
- `clean_url()` — regex-strips playlist query params from the URL
- `noplaylist: True` added to all yt-dlp option dicts
- Error messages for auth failures and unavailable videos now show user-friendly Vietnamese text instead of raw tracebacks

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **`detect_browser()` calls `yt_dlp.cookies.extract_cookies_from_browser()` on every request** for up to 6 browsers just to detect availability. This is potentially slow and wasteful. Consider caching the result or using a lighter check.
- [ ] **`clean_url()` regex edge cases** — if `list=` is the first query param (after `?`), stripping it may leave a malformed URL (e.g., `https://youtube.com/watch?&v=...`). Test with various URL formats.
- [ ] **Privacy/permissions** — `cookiesfrombrowser` reads cookies from the user's browser profile. On some OSes the browser must be closed, and users should be aware their cookies are being accessed. Verify this works on Windows (the user's platform).
- [ ] **`yt_dlp.cookies` API stability** — `yt_dlp.cookies.extract_cookies_from_browser` may not be a stable public API. Confirm it works with the yt-dlp version in requirements.txt.

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Open Chrome/Edge, log into YouTube
2. Run `python app.py`, open `http://localhost:5000`
3. Paste a playlist URL (e.g., `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XXX&list=YYY&index=2`) and verify only the single video info loads
4. Download as MP3 and MP4 — verify both complete without auth errors
5. Try with browser closed to see if cookie extraction still works or fails gracefully

### Notes
- This was triggered by a user report that `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UbhxtQybTFo&list=RDW4P8gl4dnrg&index=2` could not be downloaded. The root cause was YouTube's bot detection requiring authentication cookies.
- End-to-end testing was not performed during development due to the same bot-detection issue on the dev machine (no logged-in browser).

author: eltonaguiar
body:
## Problem

Verification run 25983068148: both scanners generated 8 picks via the Tiingo failover, but only **Bond's 8 picks persisted** to `active_picks.json` — ETF's were lost (`etf_scanner: 0` on main, `bond_scanner: 8`).

`etf-scan` and `bond-scan` run **in parallel**. Both merge into `active_picks.json` and commit it. Bond committed first (`fe07d19e6cf`); the ETF job's `git pull --rebase` then conflicted on `active_picks.json`, the 5× rebase-retry loop failed every attempt, and the ETF commit was silently dropped (the step still exits 0).

## Fix

`bond-scan` gains `needs: etf-scan` (+ `if: always()` so Bond still runs if ETF fails). The jobs now run sequentially — Bond checks out a main that already has ETF's commit, so its `git pull --rebase` is clean. No shared-file commit race.

# Pull Request

<!-- Thanks for contributing to ros2_medkit_web_ui! -->

## Summary

Fix incorrect namespace rendering in the node Overview page.

Previously, the node details view could show `/` as the namespace even when the node was actually running under a custom namespace. This happened because the app selection path was only using `appData.namespace` and `appData.fqn` when they were already populated, and the host data loaded from the backend was not always enriched with ROS 2 node namespace information.

This PR fixes the root cause in two places:

- In `handleAppSelection()`, the namespace is now derived from the FQN when `namespace` is missing.
- In `loadChildren()` for component hosts, the host data is now enriched with `x-medkit.ros2.node`, and the app node stores derived `fqn`, `namespace`, and `node_name` values.

As a result, the Overview page now displays the actual ROS 2 node namespace instead of always rendering `/`, and the node details view stays consistent with the namespace grouping shown in the sidebar/entity tree.

Ex: - the main session https://langfuse.cofacts.tw/project/cmm0emerr0001qi07eugd0760/sessions/6498b3f2-860c-494f-a955-5461688c06d6 - a trace with correct session_id but somehow created wrong Langfuse session https://langfuse.cofacts.tw/project/cmm0emerr0001qi07eugd0760/sessions/5eaedb9e-12b9-4664-93e6-41352bedf39d ## Summary - Adds `RootSessionSpanProcessor` to ensure all spans in a trace land in the correct Langfuse session - `openinference-instrumentation-google-adk` incorrectly stamps sub-agent spans with ADK-internal session UUIDs instead of the user-facing `session_id` (upstream bug: https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/issues/3117) - Fixes this by reading the parent span's session at `on_start` time and writing it as `langfuse.session.id`, which Langfuse gives precedence over `session.id` in OTLP ingestion - Stateless implementation — no dicts, no cleanup logic, no edge cases ## Test plan Subagent spans are now assigned with parent session ID - [x] Trigger an invocation that calls a sub-agent (investigator or verifier) - [x] Confirm the Langfuse trace `sessionId` matches the user-facing ADK session shown in the chat URL - [x] Confirm all observations (including `call_llm` spans under sub-agents) carry `langfuse.session.id` equal to the root session 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jessekauppila
body:
## Summary

Custom Pi cameras now appear/disappear on the map by the **exact same ring/radius predicate** as Windy webcams — plus a 90-minute snapshot-freshness window so stale/offline cams fall off cleanly. This collapses two visibility code paths into one.

The fix: a new `customClassification` module fetches `source='custom'` cams with fresh snapshots, shapes them through the same `classifyWebcamsByPhase` math against the same ring coords used for Windy, and returns DB-id rows. Those rows union with Windy results (Windy first, dedupe by `webcamId`) before upsert and deactivate.

Along the way, two `dbOperations.ts` functions that the spec called "unchanged" turned out to be Windy-coupled — `upsertTerminatorState` did internal external_id translation and `deactivateMissingTerminatorState` hardcoded `source='windy'`. Both are now source-agnostic. The cron route lifts external_id resolution into its own scope and unions all sources before any DB write.

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-custom-cam-visibility-single-source-of-truth-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-16-custom-cam-visibility-single-source-of-truth.md`
- 244 tests pass on this branch (2 pre-existing failures on main: `useSetMarker.test.ts`, `terminatorRing.test.ts`, unrelated).

## Behavioral notes

- **Existing custom rows that were incorrectly `active=true` (i.e., visible at wrong times relative to the terminator) will flip to `active=false` on the first cron tick after deploy.** That's the bug fix this PR delivers — not a regression.
- Tick latency: the new SQL hits `idx_webcam_snapshots_webcam_captured_desc` from migration `20260514_webcam_snapshots_latest_idx.sql`. No new index required.
- Rollback: revert commit `0edb060bb` (the wiring); the helper modules and refactors (`11e392e5c`, `7d6cff07a`, `9cc532ef2`, `49a712cba`, `a5c477b9c`) leave Windy behavior identical and are independently safe to keep.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx vitest run --exclude '.claude/**' --exclude 'node_modules/**'` — green (or only the 2 known pre-existing failures).
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors in `app/api/cron/**`, `app/lib/**`.
- [ ] **Manual smoke against deployed cron:** hit `/api/cron/update-cameras` with `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET` (or `?secret=$CRON_SECRET`); verify response is 200.
- [ ] Inspect `terminator_webcam_state` for the live test camera:
  ```sql
  select s.webcam_id, s.phase, s.rank, s.active, s.last_seen_at,
         w.source, w.lat, w.lng
  from terminator_webcam_state s
  join webcams w on w.id = s.webcam_id
  where w.source = 'custom'
  order by s.updated_at desc;
  ```
  Confirm test cam is `active=true` only when geometrically near the terminator AND has a snapshot within the last 90 minutes.
- [ ] Map UI sanity-check: test-cam dot only renders during its actual sun window.

## Follow-up items (deferred)

These are low-risk improvements flagged in code review but not blocking:

- Hoist `unionByWebcamId` (and possibly `toWindyDbRows`) to module scope so they can be unit-tested independently. Adding a `<T extends {webcamId: number}>` generic would future-proof the union helper.
- Doc comment on `unionByWebcamId` explaining the Windy-wins-on-collision policy.
- Rename `route.test.ts`'s "skips upsert/deactivate for empty buckets gracefully" — the body actually asserts upsert/deactivate are CALLED with empty arrays (the right contract), not skipped.
