## Summary

Opens B3 (construction-class) block. Per user "no deferrals on 9.O — pull any newly-possible items in" directive, scope iteratively expanded across 4 commits to cover the foundational TR/INTR design plus 3 follow-on construction classes that became achievable from it.

**Cumulative audit-corpus impact**: full-corpus 666/5186 (12.84%) → **688/5186 (13.27%)**, **+22 abs / +0.43pp**. Seeded-sample xwave: 337/2327 (14.48%) → 353/2327 (15.18%), +16 abs / +0.70pp.

## Commits

### 1. Foundational (B3.A + B3.B + 2 newly-possible bonuses) — `fef8baf`

- **B3.A — TR/INTR polysemy via `AV_ABSOL` feat**. `_synthesize_verb_entry` → multi-return `_synthesize_verb_entries`. New `AV_ABSOL: true` root-level feat in `data/tgl/verbs.yaml` — when set on a TR root, the synth path emits BOTH the canonical TR `<SUBJ, OBJ>` and an absolutive `<SUBJ>`-only entry for the AV voice. Parser picks whichever produces a complete parse. Applied to 7 V roots: `alala` (8.I) / `pasok` (8.O) / `laro` / `regalo` / `sakit` / `tanong` / `tingin` (9.D).
- **B3.B — `ma_an` paradigm cell**. 4 new cells: PFV (`na+root+an` → `nalimutan`), IPFV (`na+redup+an` → `nalilimutan`), CTPL with redup (`ma+redup+an` → `malilimutan`), bare CTPL without redup (`ma+root+an` → `malimutan`). `limot` affix_class extended.
- **Bonus 1**: `mang_retain` bare CTPL cell — produces `mangyari` (closes 9.E `mangyari` IMP/INF deferral).
- **Bonus 2**: bare ADJ `kilala` in adjectives.yaml — closes `Kilala si Maria.` predicative.
- **Pin flips**: 8.I (`nag-aalala` + `malimutan`), 8.Q (`kilala` → `kumbidado`), 9.D `TestVRootNoRegression` parametrize 1 → 6 cases.
- **Yield**: +13 abs / +0.25pp.

### 2. 9.O.3 — Bare-ADJ with GEN-actor (STATIVE_PRED) — `8696cc6`

- New `STATIVE_PRED` feat in `BINARY_FEATS` (55 → 56). Count test updated.
- New CFG rule: `S → ADJ[STATIVE_PRED] NP[CASE=GEN] NP[CASE=NOM]` with PRED `<SUBJ, OBJ-AGENT>`. The ADJ acts as a stative-passive participle; GEN-NP is the implicit AGENT, NOM-NP is the patient pivot/SUBJ.
- `¬ (↓ STATIVE_PRED)` constraint on ADJ-MOD rules in `cfg/nominal.py` — prevents the new analysis from competing with the V/PSYCH control-XCOMP path on linker-bound contexts (resolves Phase 6 LDD `test_psych_av_inner` conflict with `gusto`-as-ADJ).
- 5 STATIVE_PRED ADJ entries: `kilala`, `mahal` (polysemous: "expensive" 1-arg / "love" 2-arg), `ayaw`, `gusto`, `kailangan`. The last 3 coexist with their existing VERB[CTRL_CLASS=PSYCH/MODAL] entries in particles.yaml (linker-introduced XCOMP path unchanged).
- Closes `test_kilala_with_gen_actor_still_fails` (pin flipped).
- **Yield**: +8 abs / +0.16pp.

### 3. 9.O.4 — AV-NVOL absolutive (`Naalala ko`) — `6ba7540`

- `AV_ABSOL` registered in `BINARY_FEATS` (56 → 57) — was already used in YAML/synth since 9.O B3.A but lacked formal registration.
- New CFG rule: `S → V[VOICE=AV, MOOD=NVOL, AV_ABSOL=true] NP[CASE=GEN]` binds the GEN-clitic actor to SUBJ in NVOL-with-implicit-pivot context. Restricted to AV_ABSOL + NVOL to avoid loosening canonical AV case-marking globally.
- `AV_ABSOL: true` added to `kita` so `Nakita ko.` also closes.
- Closes `test_naalala_av_absolutive_still_fails` (pin flipped).
- **Yield**: +1 abs / +0.02pp (small audit-corpus footprint; closure value is construction-class hygiene).

### 4. 9.O.5 — mangyari polite-imperative wrap — `87d1395`

- New `POLITE_MARKER` feat in `BINARY_FEATS` (57 → 58).
- `feats: {POLITE_MARKER: true}` set per-cell on the bare-CTPL `mang_retain` cell (only `mangyari`; PFV `nangyari` "happened" and other yari forms unaffected).
- New CFG rule: `S → V[POLITE_MARKER=true] PART[LINK=NG] S` with full-lift `(↑) = ↓3` and `(↑ POLITE_MARKER) = true`. Structurally a politeness-marker wrap, not a control verb.
- Closes `test_mangyaring_polite_imperative_still_fails` (pin flipped).
- **Yield**: 0 audit hits (construction class itself unblocked).

| Stage | Parses | Rate | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Post-9.N (pre-9.O baseline) | 666/5186 | 12.84% | — |
| Post-9.O foundational | 679/5186 | 13.09% | +13 / +0.25pp |
| Post-9.O.3 STATIVE_PRED | 687/5186 | 13.25% | +8 / +0.16pp |
| Post-9.O.4 AV-NVOL absol | 688/5186 | 13.27% | +1 / +0.02pp |
| Post-9.O.5 mangyari | 688/5186 | 13.27% | 0 |
| **9.O cumulative** | **688/5186** | **13.27%** | **+22 / +0.43pp** |

- 8.I `test_nag_aalala_intransitive_use` → `_closed_in_9o`
- 8.I `test_malimutan_lf_nvol_form` → `_closed_in_9o`
- 8.Q `test_real_oov_still_reported` repinned: kilala → kumbidado (anti-deferral chain)

body:
## Status: Ready for review (post-audit amendment landed)

Implements `@nekostack/schema` v0.3 per the merged plan in [#9](https://github.com/cmclicker/NekoStack/pull/9) ([`packages/schema/docs/PHASE_PLAN_v0.3.md`](packages/schema/docs/PHASE_PLAN_v0.3.md)). Audit pre-mapped to [`checklists/package/implementation-acceptance.md`](checklists/package/implementation-acceptance.md); walked clean before promote.

## Audit amendment (post-review)

Two blockers + two cleanups landed in commit [`ec2f239`](https://github.com/cmclicker/NekoStack/commit/ec2f239):

**Blockers**
1. **`INVARIANTS.md` contradicted the v0.3 contract.** The corollary still said runtime refinements MUST emit `x-nekostack-runtime-refinement: true`, but `JSON_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md` and the generator both say they throw. Rewrote the corollary to match the throw contract and explain the meta-vs-throw rule: metadata = "JSON Schema validates the same input, downstream needs to know more"; throw = "emitting would change what the schema validates."
2. **`GENERATOR_VERSION` bumped from `@0.2.0` → `@0.3.0`.** The provenance on every v0.3 JSON Schema artifact previously claimed `@nekostack/schema@0.2.0` — bad provenance. Bumping now invalidated every v0.2 snapshot's header (50 snapshots + 7 committed example artifacts), which is expected snapshot churn, not a reason to defer to a post-merge patch. Two doc example snippets (`USAGE.md`, `EXAMPLES.md`) also updated to show the new version.

**Cleanups**
3. **`UnsupportedNodeKindError` message** previously pointed at `PHASE_PLAN_v0.2.md`. Made phase-neutral: now references `packages/schema/docs/` for the active generator contracts.
4. **`src/generators/json-schema-meta.ts` added** — the file the v0.3 plan promised. Codifies the three `x-nekostack-*` extension keys (`provenance`, `defaultAppliedBy`, `strip`) as constants, refactored `json-schema.ts` to import + use them. Spelling and meaning are now grep-able; any new extension key has to land in this file first.

## What ships

- **`generateJsonSchema(node, options?)`** — emits canonical draft 2020-12 JSON (sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline). Models accepted input only — no `mode` option in v0.3.
- **Identity** — URN `$id` by default (`urn:nekostack:schema:<id>:<version>`); URL form via `options.idBase`; anonymous schemas omit `$id`; never emits `$defs` in v0.3 (inline schemas only).
- **Absence semantics** mapped per Decisions #6–#9 — see [`docs/JSON_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md`](packages/schema/docs/JSON_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md) for the full table.
- **`stripUnknown` corrected** per Decision #12 — `additionalProperties: true` + `x-nekostack-strip: true`, not `false`. JSON Schema models accepted input; the runtime is responsible for stripping.
- **Refinement mapping** per Decision #10, plus regex-with-non-empty-flags **throws** per Decision #11a.
- **Provenance** in an `x-nekostack` extension block (JSON has no comment syntax).
- **Ajv2020 test harness** — uses `ajv/dist/2020.js` (the draft-2020-12 class), not the default draft-07 import.

## What does NOT ship

OpenAPI 3.1 (v0.4), composition operators (v0.5), runtime `parse`/`validate` (v0.6), CLI handlers (v0.7), `sourceHash` (v0.7), `$defs` extraction and cross-package `$ref` (v0.7), output-shape JSON Schema (deferred indefinitely — no concrete consumer needs it), opt-in lossy regex-with-flags mode (deferred). Generators for unsupported IR kinds (`date`, `union`, `recursiveRef`, `transform`, runtime refinements, regex-with-flags) throw `UnsupportedNodeKindError` with the stable `code`/`kind`/`generator` shape from v0.2.

## Implementation-acceptance checklist walkthrough

### Scope (blocking)

- [x] PR names the phase — "v0.3 candidate" — and links the plan + ROADMAP v0.3 entry.
- [x] Every shipped feature maps to a plan-scope item.
- [x] No out-of-scope features.
- [x] Explicit non-scope in PR body (above).

### Public API (blocking)

- [x] Every new export justified:
  - `generateJsonSchema` — the headline new function; Decisions #1–#12.
  - `JsonSchemaGeneratorOptions` — type-only; carries `idBase`.
- [x] No future-only capability re-exported. `DateNode`, `UnionNode`, `RecursiveRefNode`, `TransformNode` remain internal.
- [x] `UnsupportedNodeKindError`'s `generator` field extended to include `"jsonSchema"`; no other public type changed.
- [x] No `@internal`-tagged item exported.

### Boundary (blocking)

- [x] No `@nekostack/*` imports in source: `grep -r "from.*@nekostack/" packages/schema/src` → empty.
- [x] `npm ls --workspace=@nekostack/schema`:
  ```
  +-- @types/node@22.19.19
  +-- ajv-formats@3.0.1
  +-- ajv@8.20.0
  +-- typescript@5.9.3
  +-- vitest@2.1.9
  `-- zod@3.25.76
  ```
  Zero `@nekostack/*` deps. Two new devDeps (`ajv`, `ajv-formats`) — both used by the JSON Schema test harness only.
- [x] `docs/SCOPE.md` lists non-owned capabilities consistent with `BOUNDARIES.md`.

### Contracts (blocking)

- [x] All 8 invariants in `docs/INVARIANTS.md` upheld. New v0.3 corollary added: "Non-runtime generators surface semantic loss via `x-nekostack-*` extensions; throw when emitting would change validation semantics."
- [x] Contract-defining tests reference contracts by name:
  - `describe("Ajv2020 exec — absence semantics parity with v0.1")` — references v0.1 contract
  - `describe("generateJsonSchema — absence semantics (Decisions #6-#9)")` — references the v0.3 contract
  - `describe("generateJsonSchema — object policy (Decision #12)")` — references the corrected mapping
  - `describe("generateJsonSchema — identity ($id) per Decision #2")` — references the URN/URL rule
- [x] Semantic loss explicit:
  - **Metadata** (`x-nekostack-*` extensions): `default()` → `x-nekostack-default-applied-by: "runtime"`; `stripUnknown` → `x-nekostack-strip: true`.
  - **Throw** (would change validation): runtime refinements → `kind: "runtimeRefinement"`; regex with flags → `kind: "regexFlags"`.
- [x] New contract doc [`docs/JSON_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md`](packages/schema/docs/JSON_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md) codifies the v0.3 contract.

### Immutability + determinism (blocking)

- [x] Generator is a pure function of IR. Output is canonical JSON.
- [x] Explicit determinism test: `same IR + same options → byte-identical output`.
- [x] Trailing-newline guarantee: `output ends with exactly one newline`.

### Tests (blocking)

- [x] Runtime tests cover every new public surface. Breakdown:
  - 39 from `json-schema.test.ts` (snapshots, identity, absence semantics, object policy, throw cases, determinism, root structure)
  - 6 from `json-schema-ajv2020-self.test.ts` (every generated schema loads via Ajv2020)
  - 17 from `json-schema-ajv2020-exec.test.ts` (compile + run against the absence-semantics matrix)
  - 3 from `tests/examples/regenerate.test.ts` (one JSON Schema example per existing example schema)
- [x] `describe` strings name contracts/behavior — examples above.
- [x] No `.only` or `.skip` committed.

### Validation commands (blocking)

```
$ npm test --workspace=@nekostack/schema
Test Files  14 passed (14)
Tests       219 passed (219)
Type Errors no errors

$ npm run typecheck --workspace=@nekostack/schema
(clean)

$ npm run build --workspace=@nekostack/schema

$ npm pack --workspace=@nekostack/schema --dry-run

package size: 85.7 kB
unpacked size: 303.6 kB
total files: 103

$ npm ls --workspace=@nekostack/schema
@nekostack/schema@0.0.0 -> .\packages\schema
  +-- @types/node@22.19.19
  +-- ajv-formats@3.0.1
  +-- ajv@8.20.0
  +-- typescript@5.9.3
  +-- vitest@2.1.9
  `-- zod@3.25.76
```

### Local artifacts (blocking)

- [x] `README.md` — unchanged.
- [x] `docs/SCOPE.md` — unchanged.
- [x] `docs/INVARIANTS.md` — extended with v0.3 corollary.
- [x] `docs/ROADMAP.md` — v0.3 marked candidate with full feature list.
- [x] Contract docs:
  - `docs/IR_CONTRACT.md` — unchanged.

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the inline `.filter().length` call for category counts inside the mapping over categories with a precomputed dictionary.
🎯 **Why:** Inside the render loop over categories, `componentMetadata.filter((c) => c.category === category).length` was being called to get counts. This is an O(N*M) operation on every render. Precomputing the category counts in a single pass O(N) into a dictionary using `useMemo` is much more efficient.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** We wrote a local benchmark script using `renderToString` for 500 iterations. Before optimization, rendering time for 500 iterations took roughly ~2704ms. After optimization, it decreased. Importantly, it reduced the Big O time complexity from O(N*M) down to O(M) component iterations for building the count record plus an O(1) loop iteration lookup, saving CPU cycles on repeated re-renders.

author: kottlerg
body:
## Summary

Replaces the last Unix-only mechanisms in xtask's toolchain-mirror
assembly with portable Rust-native equivalents. After this PR every
piece of xtask compiles cleanly on Unix, macOS, BSD, and Windows
without shell scripts, `chmod`, or `std::os::unix::*` outside narrow
\`cfg(unix)\`-gated implementation modules.

| Layer | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Mirror assembly symlinks | \`std::os::unix::fs::symlink\` at 4 call sites in \`rust_src.rs\` | \`fs_compat::link_or_copy\` — symlink → hard link → copy fallback chain, returns the kind that succeeded |
| Wrapper scripts | \`#!/bin/sh\` heredocs written + \`chmod +x\` | \`seraph-wrapper-shim\` native binary (new workspace member, zero deps), installed as both \`rustc\` and \`ws-clippy\`, dispatches by argv[0] basename |
| Env wiring | piecewise \`cmd.env(\"RUSTC\", ...)\` at 2 call sites | \`SeraphToolchain::apply_env(&mut Command)\` — sets RUSTC, RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER, SERAPH_SHIM_*, RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP in one call |
| Missing-tool errors | \`Command::spawn\` opaque \"No such file or directory\" | \`util::require_tool\` (via \`which\` crate) — names the tool and lists install commands per platform |

## Why

This was the third and final PR of the xtask portability refactor.
The previous two PRs (#80 terminal I/O, #81 firmware/accel) made
everything except the toolchain mirror portable. The mirror still
relied on:

- Unix-specific \`std::os::unix::fs::symlink\` for the directory tree
  that mirrors the real rustup toolchain.
- \`#!/bin/sh\` shebang-interpreted wrapper scripts at \`bin/rustc\` and
  \`bin/ws-clippy\` — no equivalent on Windows.
- Unix-only \`set_mode(0o755)\` to make the scripts executable —
  Windows doesn't have a separate execute bit.

After this PR, mirror assembly works on every host. On Windows
without developer mode, dir-symlink falls back to recursive copy
(slower but functionally identical). The shim binary is a normal
native executable that needs no special privileges to run.

## The shim binary

Lives in \`xtask/wrapper-shim/\`. Zero external dependencies. Reads
configuration from three env vars at startup:

- \`SERAPH_SHIM_REAL_RUSTC\` — absolute path to rustup's rustc
- \`SERAPH_SHIM_REAL_CLIPPY\` — absolute path to rustup's clippy-driver
- \`SERAPH_SHIM_MIRROR_SYSROOT\` — absolute path to the seraph mirror

Dispatches on argv[0] basename:

- **rustc**: exec real rustc with \`--sysroot=<mirror>\` prepended,
  unless caller already supplied \`--sysroot\`.
- **ws-clippy**: cargo invokes \`<wrapper> <rustc_path> <args...>\`;
  drop the rustc_path, set \`SYSROOT\` env, re-drive clippy-driver
  with \`<mirror>/bin/rustc\` and \`--sysroot=<mirror>\`.

On Unix uses \`exec(3)\` to replace the current process; on Windows
spawns and mirrors the exit code. xtask is always the root of the
process tree, so env vars set on xtask's cargo invocation propagate
to the shim child.

## Dependency changes

Added: \`which = \"8\"\`. Wraps the cross-platform PATH lookup so missing
host tools surface clear errors.

The shim crate is dep-less: a normal release build of
\`seraph-wrapper-shim\` produces a ~400 KiB binary with no transitive
crates beyond \`std\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo xtask test\` — 61 xtask tests pass (4 new \`fs_compat\`).
      Coverage: file copy, recursive directory copy, missing-source
      error, deep nested copy.
- [x] \`cargo xtask clean --all && cargo xtask build && cargo xtask
      run --headless\` on x86_64 — full from-scratch build exercises
      shim crate build, mirror assembly via link_or_copy, shim
      install, SERAPH_SHIM_* env wiring, end-to-end \`ALL TESTS
      PASSED\`.
- [x] Same flow on riscv64.
- [x] \`cargo xtask run-parallel --parallel 2 --runs 2\` — 2/2 PASS
      with the require_tool resolution at startup.
- [x] \`PATH=/tmp /path/to/xtask run\` — confirms the
      \`require_tool\` clean error path: \"qemu-system-x86_64 not
      found on PATH ... Install with: dnf install qemu-system-x86
      ...\".

## By-design unverified

- macOS / Windows / BSD link_or_copy fallback chain (works in
  principle; CI is Linux only).
- The shim's Windows code path (CommandExt::spawn-and-mirror vs the
  Unix exec(3) replacement).
- Windows-without-developer-mode dir-symlink → recursive copy fallback.

The cfg-gated code paths compile cleanly on a Linux host; runtime
behavior on the other hosts is on the next person who runs xtask
there to confirm.

## Summary

- Adds a thin observability layer underneath the MCP server: every tool call (and lifecycle event) is appended as one JSON line to `~/.schemabrain/events.jsonl`.
- New `schemabrain tail` CLI follows the file in real time with pretty colored rendering or raw `--json` for jq.
- `schemabrain serve` gains `--events-path` / `--no-events` and emits `server_start` / `server_stop` events.
- A 4-rule `EventRedactor` strips connection URLs, long blobs, `get_metric` filter values, and email-shape strings BEFORE write.

## Commits

- `9f2e27f` — event bus substrate (`Event` dataclass + `EventRedactor` + `JsonlEventBus` + per-tool result extractors)
- `e2d2135` — `@instrument` decorator wired into all 9 MCP tool closures in `mcp/server.py::build_server`
- `731a118` — `schemabrain tail` CLI subcommand (poll-based reader, inode-tracking rotation, pretty + `--json` modes)
- `cec6dc5` — `--events-path` flag + env var + `server_start`/`server_stop` lifecycle emissions on `serve`
- `ceed595` — README "Watch what the agent does" section + `docs/observability.md` deep-dive
- `dd2ebcb` — fix: fold pre-merge findings (6 HIGH + 3 MEDIUM)
- `6979b26` — chore: docstring + docs scrub
- `8ed7d79` — chore: rewording in docs

## Test plan

- [x] CI: lint + unit (Py 3.11, 3.12), integration / docker+postgres, security (bandit + pip-audit + semgrep) — all 4 jobs green on `8ed7d79`
- [x] Manual smoke against a throwaway Postgres-16: brought up `schemabrain serve` with events file in a tmp path, exercised 4 tool calls (describe_table, find_relevant_tables, an error path, list_entities), confirmed events file appears with mode 0600 and contains every call
- [x] `serve` stdin EOF → `server_stop` event emits via the `finally` block (same path SIGINT takes)
- [x] Confirmed `server_session_id` propagates consistently across every event in one serve run, and a new UUID is generated on the next serve start
- [x] Triggered an error envelope (`describe_table` on `public.nope`) → pretty render shows `→ ERROR unknown_name` and the JSON event carries `status="error"`, `error_kind="unknown_name"`
- [x] Passed `"show me postgresql://u:p@h/d details"` as the `query` arg to `find_relevant_tables` → events file shows `"query": "<redacted-connection-url>"`, the raw URL never reaches disk
- [x] Forced rotation by emitting 30k events with `max_bytes=10 MiB` → `events.jsonl.1` appeared at exactly the rotation threshold; a separate live-tail run during a tight-loop rotation confirmed tail jumped to the new active file via inode tracking and kept yielding post-rotation events

## Out of scope

- OpenTelemetry exporter (`schemabrain[otel]` extra) — separate PR
- A durable-store consumer for higher-trust events — roadmap item
- `schemabrain tail --histogram` aggregations — user can pipe `--json` to `jq` or `awk`
- Multi-session filtering (`--session-id UUID`) on tail — future when multi-process serve becomes common
- Web UI for events — out of platform direction (terminal-first)

author: kenansun-dev-bot[bot]
body:
Two follow-up bugs in PR #50 caught by Kenan VM Claw smoke run minutes after merge.

## Why a new PR same day?

PR #50 was merged 14:09 GMT+8; VM caught the race at 14:19, 10 minutes later. MEMORY daily-PR rule normally says "commit to today's open PR" — but #50 is already closed/merged and branch deleted. Re-opening a stack on the merged branch is messier than a fixup PR. Flagging here so owner can decide if a different batching is preferred.

## 1. `setMyCommands` race — `/chatid` + `/ping` disappeared

PR #50 added a `COMMANDS.map(...)` registration call inside `src/channels/telegram.ts` on bot `onStart`. But `src/index.ts` was already calling `registerTelegramCommands(botToken)` from `src/slash-commands.ts` for the same purpose — and that path used only `COMMANDS` (no `/chatid` or `/ping`).

Two registrations race; whichever finishes last wins. On VM the index.ts path won and `/chatid` + `/ping` vanished from the menu. On rpi5 the channels/telegram.ts path won and they were present. Pure timing luck.

**Fix**: single source of truth in `registerTelegramCommands()` — it now includes the tg-only utility commands (`/chatid`, `/ping`) on top of `COMMANDS`. The duplicate `setMyCommands` call in `channels/telegram.ts` is removed and replaced with a load-bearing comment. Test asserts both surfaces (tg-only + COMMANDS) in the rendered menu so future drift fails CI.

## 2. symlink-aware direct-run guard

When systemd / `npm link` launches `node` against the symlinked `~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/<pkg>/dist/index.js`, the `isDirectRun` check compared `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` (Node resolves through symlinks → realpath in `~/gitrepos/`) against `path.resolve(process.argv[1])` (literal symlink path). They didn't match → `main()` never ran → event loop empty → silent `exit(0)`.

**Repro on rpi5 today**: `systemctl --user start nanoclaw` exited 0 with no log output. Workaround was rewriting the unit to use the realpath; this PR fixes the check itself with `fs.realpathSync` on both sides (wrapped in try/catch so a Windows or ephemeral path failure falls back to the previous behavior, not regression).

## Verify

- `npx vitest run`: **1452 passed** (updated existing `registerTelegramCommands` test to assert `chatid`/`ping` presence)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npm run build`: clean
- Prettier: clean
- Manual: rpi5 daemon already running with realpath workaround unit; this PR makes the workaround unnecessary.

cc @Kenan-VM-Claw for review.

## Summary

Failing-first Playwright E2E spec for the `sub-to-20` content tier per `design/math/sub-to-20-content.md` §6.8 acceptance criteria. Spec lives at `e2e/sub-to-20.spec.ts` (4 tests, all wrapped in `test.fixme()` per Option B).

**Paired implementation work:**
- Devon — ticket **86c9utcf7** (`distractorClass: 'decade-anchor'` union widening + `decadeAnchorDistractors` algorithm + Math.tsx dispatch wiring)
- Kevin — planner directive + canon re-bake (the `MATH_TRACK_GUIDE` `sub-to-20` directive block + 22-fact no-borrow pool + `public/canon/math/level-1/sub-to-20.json` re-bake)

## Option choice — Option B (`test.fixme`)

Mirrors the well-established PR #202 / #206 / #226 / #239 / #265 precedent. Reasons:

- Devon's PR is not yet authored; the `'decade-anchor'` member of `PickDistractorsOpts.distractorClass` union does **not** exist on `origin/main` (`distractors.ts:159` still reads `'off-by-one' | 'wrong-op'`).
- Kevin's PR (planner + canon) is also pending. Current `public/canon/math/level-1/sub-to-20.json` carries a pre-spec one-shot bake from the legacy 1-line `_planner.ts:1022` skeleton and openly violates the §1.1 no-borrow constraint (P5=`15-5=10`, P6=`14-7=7` ← BORROW, P7=`18-9=9` ← BORROW, P8=`19-3=16`). The current canon is the empirical RED state.
- Option A (un-fixme'd, RED on base) would block this PR from merging until both paired impls land, and impls can't merge cleanly behind this PR. Classic stacked-PR dependency.
- With `test.fixme()`, this PR is CI-green and mergeable immediately. A tiny follow-up PR (≤10-line diff) flips `test.fixme(` → `test(` after the paired PRs merge.

## Coverage table — 4 tests mapped to spec §2 + §3 conditions

| Test | AC | Spec section | RED-on-base classification | Covers |
|------|-----|---|---|---|
| 1 | AC1 | §1.1 pool + §2.1 P1 | RED-on-base post-Kevin-merge | Trigger: seeded `sub-to-20` focus produces P1 with minuend ∈ {11..19} + ones-digit(a) ≥ subtrahend (no-borrow). Survives any §1.1 pool re-curation that keeps the teen-minuend constraint. |
| 2 | AC2 | §3.3 Class B + §2.2 ≥2/5 | RED-on-base post-Devon-merge | Class B fires at P4 when fact is CLEAN-eligible: chip row contains DEC=10 trap (count exactly 1). Includes a pre-condition `test.skip` guard for vacuous canon plays (the §2.2 ≥2/5 rule is pool-side; this is the cheap 1-of-5 render-side gate). |
| 3 | AC3 | §1.1 NO-BORROW SELF-CHECK | RED-on-base post-Kevin-merge | Across all 8 session problems, NO read-line contains a forbidden borrow operand pair (computed at module-load from the strict `ones-digit(a) < b` definition; 36 forbidden pairs total). Asserts `violations.toEqual([])` for full diagnostic on failure. |
| 4 | AC4 | §3.5 sub-to-20-only scope | Trivially-green today; regression-guard post-Devon-merge | Sub-to-10 focus does NOT produce sub-to-20 minuends, and chip row does NOT contain DEC=10 trap (with branch for off-by-one's legitimate `correct + 1 === 10` case when correct = 9). |

## Structural-vs-literal assertion choices

Applied `[[testing-and-ci.md §6 "Canon-content-coupled E2E spec drift"]]` lessons (PR #266 broke a sibling spec on a commutative-equivalent re-bake). This spec **avoids literal canon-content pins**:

- **Test 1** — does NOT assert `addend-a === "17"` literally. Asserts `SUB_TO_20_MINUEND_SET.has(addendA)` against the structural set `{11..19}` + `ones-digit(minuend) ≥ subtrahend`. Survives any pool re-bake that keeps the no-borrow constraint.
- **Test 2** — does NOT assert "P4 is `16-4=12`". Reads whatever `correct` is currently rendered, validates Class-B-CLEAN preconditions (DEC=10 in range, not aliasing correct, not aliasing off-by-one), THEN asserts the chip row contains DEC=10 exactly once. Survives any canon re-bake that lands a §1.1 CLEAN fact at P4. Vacuously skipped if canon places a non-CLEAN fact at P4 (per §2.2 the ≥2/5 rule is enforced pool-side; the 1-of-5 sample is the cheapest render-side gate — future polish could walk all 5 P4-P8 slots).
- **Test 3** — derives the BORROW pair set at module-load from the §1.1 structural rule, NOT from a literal canon scan. The forbidden-substring filter is the structural assertion; works against any canon shape.
- **Test 4** — pure structural — sub-to-10 minuend NOT in sub-to-20 teen set + chip-value count assertion conditional on the rendered `correct` value.

Chip-walk uses `data-problem-index` 0-based DOM gate per `testing-and-ci.md §4.1.3` rule 5 (not `waitForTimeout`).

Count assertions per `[[feedback_count_assertions_on_regression_tests]]`: `.filter(...).length === N` and `.toEqual([...])`, never `.toContain` on regression behaviour.

## Testid contract with Devon (ticket 86c9utcf7)

**No new testid required.** Spec uses existing selectors:
- `[data-testid="math"]` (root, with `data-problem-index` 0-based advance gate)
- `[data-testid="math-addend-a"]` / `[data-testid="math-addend-b"]` (operands as text)
- `[data-testid="math-chip"]` with `data-value` (chip value) + `data-correct="true"` (correct-chip selector)
- `[data-testid="math-caption"]` (read-line caption surface — `renderCaption(captionText, captionRevealed)` at `Math.tsx:2265`; consumed by Test 3's `readAllProblemReadLines` helper)
- `[data-testid="math-symbolic"]` (visibility gate)
- `[data-testid="hub-tree-node"][data-tree="number-garden"]` (Hub → Math navigation)

If Devon decides to add a diagnostic `data-distractor-class="decade-anchor"` attribute on `math-chip`, this spec does NOT depend on it (chip values are checked directly). Flag in the flip-PR if a future spec wants that attribute.

## Local verification

```
npx playwright test e2e/sub-to-20.spec.ts --project=chromium --reporter=list
```

Result: **4 skipped on chromium** (Option B contract confirmed). Typecheck (`yarn typecheck`) passes.

## Non-obvious findings

1. **Current sub-to-20 canon is the empirical RED state.** `public/canon/math/level-1/sub-to-20.json` was baked from the 1-line directive skeleton at `_planner.ts:1022` and OPENLY contains BORROW facts (`Fourteen minus seven`, `Eighteen minus nine`). When Kevin's re-bake lands, those will disappear by construction. This means Test 3 has a particularly strong pre-merge RED signal — the violation is visible in the committed canon JSON today.

2. **Structural BORROW-set construction.** The `FORBIDDEN_BORROW_READ_SUBSTRINGS` constant is built at module-load by enumerating `(a, b)` with `minuend ∈ [11, 19], subtrahend ∈ [1, 9], ones-digit(a) < b`. 36 forbidden pairs total (8+7+6+5+4+3+2+1 = 36 per `buildForbiddenBorrowReadSubstrings`; the earlier "35" figure was a count slip — code is correct). This is the structural-vs-literal pattern in its purest form — derived from a §1.1 rule, never from a literal canon scan. Survives any future canon shape and any pool widening/curation.

3. **Class B pre-condition gate in Test 2.** The spec §2.2 contract is "≥2 of P4-P8 carry CLEAN Class B"; the E2E gate is the cheaper 1-of-5 P4 sample. If the canon's P4 lands a non-CLEAN fact (e.g. `15-5=10` ALIAS or `12-1=11` BOUNDARY), the test skips vacuously via `test.skip(!isCleanEligible)`. The §2.2 rule is enforced pool-side + directive-side; the render-side delivery is what the spec exercises. Future polish: walk all P4-P8 and assert `cleanWithTen.length >= 2` matching the §2.2 contract directly.

4. **GREEN-side mock posture deferred to flip-PR.** Per `testing-and-ci.md §6` corollary: a canon-content-pinning test can't use `failNetwork: true` because `pickStaticMathPlan()` produces hardcoded fallback problems. THIS spec's structural assertions tolerate `failNetwork` for Tests 1, 3, 4 (no borrow fact would ever appear in any static plan; the minuend-range guard is structural). Test 2 is the exception — it requires the new canon to land at P4 with a CLEAN-eligible fact, which the static fallback can't satisfy. When the flip-PR un-fixmes Test 2, consider switching to a sub-to-20-canon-serving mock following the `installCvcWordsClaudeMock` pattern at `mockClaude.ts §4.2`. This is flagged inl

Tainan TG 5248–5253 (2026-05-17): flagged that chart, table, image template previews were visibly off after PR #23 — content pushed to a corner, right edge cropped.

## Root cause

Drift signal #1 from PR #23 body. `scripts/preview-gen.ts` viewport was 960×540 / 540×960 but every template `.tpl-root` rule declares `width: 1280px; height: 720px` (or 720×1280). Fixed-width slides rendered past the viewport edge, and Playwright `fullPage: false` truncated the screenshot to the viewport → right 33% of every fixed-canvas template was cut off.

Pre-bump fonts left enough whitespace that the cropped region still *looked* centered. The +30% font bump pushed content into the cropped strip → visible breakage.

## Fix

One-line change: viewport `1280×720` / `720×1280` to match every CSS canvas. Regenerated all 28 PNGs.

## Verified

- chart/landscape: title + full-width chart placeholder rendered correctly
- table/portrait: title + table rendered in upper canvas (intentional layout for 720×1280)
- image/landscape: image + caption fully visible
- 11 already-correct templates (responsive widths) unchanged

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run preview` completes for all 14 templates
- [ ] After merge: Dokploy `template-studio-xxf7um` rebuild picks up new previews
- [ ] Visual diff via `git diff --stat` shows 26 PNGs touched

## Summary

- `testMode`, `assemblyNames` (`run_unity_tests`), `assemblyName`, `typeName`, `methodName` (`run_method_in_unity`), `action` (`unity_play_control`) were validated as required at runtime but were typed as `String? = null`, so `KParameter.isOptional()` returned `true` and they were excluded from the JSON Schema `required` array
- Changed all 6 parameters to non-nullable with no default value — `KParameter.isOptional()` now returns `false`, placing them in `required`
- Removed the now-redundant `"REQUIRED."` text prefix from `@McpDescription` on `testMode` and `assemblyNames`
- Simplified unreachable `if (param == null)` error message branches in `RunUnityTestsTool` and `PlayControlTool`

## Background

The JetBrains MCP Server (`mcpserver.jar`, Rider 2025.3.3) generates JSON Schema by iterating `KCallable.parameters` and checking `KParameter.isOptional()` — **not** `isMarkedNullable`. Parameters with `= null` defaults are excluded from `required` regardless of nullability. Verified by decompiling `Schema_utilKt.parametersSchema` with `javap`.

## Test plan

- [x] All unit tests pass (`./gradlew --no-configuration-cache test`)

author: fernandezc
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces the first production-ready version of the SpectroChemPy plugin architecture.

The goal is to keep the core package lightweight for regular users while moving optional, domain-specific, or heavier functionality into separately installable plugins. Official plugins still feel integrated once installed: users import `spectrochempy as scp`, then use stable namespaces such as `scp.nmr`, `scp.iris`, `scp.hyper`, and `scp.carroucell`.

This is a pragmatic first plugin-system milestone. The core provides discovery, registration, lazy namespaces, missing-plugin hints, handler dispatch, unit-context hooks, class-based accessors, and compatibility shims without automatically importing plugin implementations at `import spectrochempy` time.

## Official Plugins

This PR adds four official plugin packages under `plugins/`:

- `spectrochempy-nmr`
- `spectrochempy-iris`
- `spectrochempy-hypercomplex`
- `spectrochempy-carroucell`

`Cantera` is no longer part of the official plugin set installed by `spectrochempy[plugins]`. It remains available separately as an experimental plugin, with its own experimental environment and release path.

## Core Plugin Infrastructure

- Adds a plugin manager with discovery, registration, lifecycle tracking, and failure isolation.
- Adds a central registry for plugin contributions: readers, writers, processors, visualizers, analyses, simulations, metadata, dataset accessors, unit contexts, and named handlers.
- Adds pluggy hook specifications and public hook markers.
- Adds public plugin API entry points under `spectrochempy.api.plugins`.
- Adds testing support through `spectrochempy.testing.plugins.PluginTestHarness`.
- Adds a plugin template for future plugin packages.
- Adds handler dispatch for core extension points, including FFT encodings/post-processing, numeric method overrides, coordinate reversal, importer inference/directory resolution, remote download handling, and concatenation metadata hooks.
- Adds class-based dataset accessors so plugins can expose namespace-style extensions such as `dataset.hyper.RR`.
- Adds unit-context hooks so plugins can register Pint conversion contexts tied to dataset metadata.

## Core Decoupling

The core no longer contains NMR-, quaternion/hypercomplex-, or Carroucell-specific runtime logic:

- NMR TopSpin reading, FFT metadata handling, 2D encodings, ppm conversion, and NMR unit contexts live in `spectrochempy-nmr`.
- Quaternion and hypercomplex behavior lives in `spectrochempy-hypercomplex` through dataset accessors and numeric handlers.
- IRIS analysis and plotting workflows live in `spectrochempy-iris`.
- The Carroucell reader lives in `spectrochempy-carroucell`.
- Generic importer utilities now delegate format-specific directory/file inference through plugin handlers.
- Missing official plugin symbols raise actionable `AttributeError` messages with installation guidance, without scanning or importing plugins dynamically.

## Dependency Trimming

Several dependencies have been removed from the core and moved to plugin or documentation extras:

- `osqp` moved to `spectrochempy-iris`.
- `xlrd` moved to `spectrochempy-carroucell`.
- `numpy-quaternion` moved to `spectrochempy-hypercomplex`.
- `numpydoc` is no longer a runtime core dependency.

## User-Facing API Shape

Recommended new usage is namespaced:

```python
scp.nmr.read_topspin(...)
scp.iris.IRIS(...)
scp.hyper.set_quaternion(...)
scp.carroucell.read_carroucell(...)
dataset.iris.kernel_matrix(...)
dataset.hyper.component("RI")
```

Compatibility aliases remain where practical, for example `scp.read_topspin(...)` and `scp.read_carroucell(...)`, but new documentation and examples prefer plugin namespaces.

## Documentation And Examples

- Separates user-facing plugin documentation from developer/plugin-author documentation.
- Adds developer documentation for plugin architecture, accessors, handlers, numeric backends, unit contexts, and authoring new plugins.
- Clarifies why hypercomplex support is separate from core, and how it relates to ordinary complex data and 2D NMR.
- Separates core and plugin examples in the gallery structure.
- Keeps PR documentation previews fast by building PR docs without notebook execution, while full branch previews still execute the documentation.
- Parallelizes full documentation builds.

## CI And Release Infrastructure

- Adds plugin package metadata, editable install paths, and release workflows for official plugins.
- Adds `spectrochempy[plugins]` to install the official plugins: NMR, IRIS, Hypercomplex, and Carroucell.
- Keeps Cantera outside the official extra as an experimental plugin.
- Skips coverage collection on pull-request test jobs.
- Runs pull-request package tests with `pytest-xdist`, while tests marked `serial` run separately.
- Keeps coverage/reporting behavior for non-PR jobs.

## Reviewer Focus

Useful review areas:

- lazy plugin discovery and registration behavior;
- absence of heavy plugin imports during `import spectrochempy`;
- consistency of `scp.<plugin>.*` namespaces and dataset accessors;
- handler dispatch boundaries between generic core and domain-specific plugins;
- official plugin packaging metadata and entry points;
- documentation clarity for user vs developer/plugin-author material;
- CI workflow changes for docs, PR tests, package builds, and plugin releases.

## Validation

Representative checks run during integration included:

```bash
pytest tests/test_plugins -q -ra
pytest plugins/spectrochempy-nmr/tests -q -ra
pytest plugins/spectrochempy-iris/tests -q -ra
pytest plugins/spectrochempy-hypercomplex/tests -q -ra
pytest plugins/spectrochempy-carroucell/tests -q -ra
pytest tests/test_docs/test_py_in_docs.py -q -ra
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Recent CI updates also validated:

- PR docs preview in about three minutes without notebook execution;
- full branch docs preview with parallel Sphinx builds;
- PR package tests using xdist;
- pre-commit regeneration of requirements/environment files after adding `pytest-xdist`.

body:
## Summary

Implementa **exportação LGPD/portabilidade de dados** para MVP-2: endpoint autenticado `GET /user/me/export` que retorna pacote JSON completo do usuário, organizado por entidade, usando o registry LGPD do #1255 como fonte de cobertura.

Foundation depende de #1255 (registry) ✅ + #1259 (consents — automaticamente exportados via REGISTRY) ✅. Próximas: #1257 (delete integral), #1258 (AI min).

## Mudanças por commit (6)

1. **`f306146` feat(lgpd): export service** — `app/application/services/lgpd_export_service.py` com `build_user_export(user_id) → dict`. Itera REGISTRY filtrando `export_included=True`, serializa rows preservando UUIDs/datetimes/enums/Decimal. Auto-coverage: nova entity entra automaticamente.
2. **`16e3da2` feat(lgpd): controller** — `MeExportResource` em `/user/me/export` (alinhado com `DELETE /user/me`), `@jwt_required`, `@doc` OpenAPI completa
3. **`c18e6e8` test(lgpd): 18 testes iniciais** — 7 classes cobrindo auth, metadata, entity coverage, isolation, retentions, excluded entities, serializer primitives
4. **`ea3c660` test(lgpd): date/None branches** — coverage 100% nos novos arquivos
5. **`b37fdd5` chore(openapi+postman): regen + ENRICHMENT** — schema atualizado; Postman test_lines validam status 200 + metadata.scope + retentions array
6. **`fb56f9c` fix(lgpd): exclude credential columns** — blocklist `(table, column)` filtra password hash + JTIs + reset tokens do User row. **+2 testes garantindo que credenciais nunca vazam mesmo para o próprio usuário**

## Estrutura do pacote exportado

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "generated_at": "2026-05-17T06:00:00+00:00",
    "user_id": "uuid",
    "registry_version": "1.0",
    "scope": "lgpd_full_export"
  },
  "users": [{ "id": "...", "name": "...", "email": "...", ... }],
  "consents": [...],
  "transactions": [...],
  "goals": [...],
  ...,
  "retentions": [
    {
      "entity": "fiscal_documents",
      "reason": "fiscal",
      "retention_days": 1825,
      "explanation": "Fiscal documents — Brazilian tax retention"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Segurança — credenciais filtradas

Colunas NUNCA exportadas (blocklist em `_SENSITIVE_COLUMNS`):
- `users.password` (bcrypt hash)
- `users.current_jti`, `users.refresh_token_jti`
- `users.password_reset_token_hash` + `_expires_at` + `_requested_at`
- `users.email_verification_token_hash` + `_expires_at`

Razão: zero upside LGPD em exportar essas; cria superfície de ataque (offline brute force, replay de JTI roubado).

## Acceptance Criteria (#1256)

- ✅ Usuário autenticado baixa pacote de dados completo (`GET /user/me/export`)
- ✅ Pacote inclui metadados de geração, versão e escopo
- ✅ Campos retidos por obrigação legal explicados (seção `retentions` com reason + days + explanation)
- ✅ Registry como fonte de cobertura (auto-detect de novas entidades)
- ✅ Testes com usuário rico (consents, transactions) validam presença
- ✅ Endpoint documentado no OpenAPI
- ✅ Isolamento entre usuários testado

- ✅ `ruff format --check .` — 12615 files clean
- ✅ `ruff check app tests` — clean
- ✅ `mypy app` — 0 issues (437 source files)
- ✅ `pytest tests/test_lgpd_export.py` — **22/22 passed**
- ✅ Coverage **87.81%** (gate 85%); novos arquivos a **100%**
- ✅ Full canonical CI gate (`bash scripts/run_ci_quality_local.sh --local`) PASS em 11min35s
- ✅ Pre-commit hooks: Sonar local, repo-hygiene, alembic single head, GraphQL auth, etc — all PASS

Closes #1256

Próximas: #1257 (delete integral), #1258 (AI minimization)

author: apollozhangongithub
body:
## Summary

Closes #223. Dispatcher now nudges the **lead** session when it's idle, with copy that matches lead's actual job (dispatch work) instead of the employee OKR prompt.

### Why

The right organizational model is:
- **Employees idle is normal** — they wait for orders. Nudging them with "继续工作 OKR" creates make-work and noise (this very session has been spammed by that nudge for ~30 min while waiting on CI for in-flight PRs).
- **Lead idle stalls the team** — nobody is dispatching. Lead is exactly who *should* be nudged.

Previously `NudgeCoordinator` excluded lead from `get_dev_sessions`'s protected set and never processed it.

### Changes

- `helpers.get_lead_session(cfg)` returns `"lead"` if `{prefix}-lead` exists in tmux, else `None`.
- `NudgeCoordinator._process_lead_session(now)` mirrors `_process_session` but routes the lead through inbox → flush → `_try_lead_idle`. Same cooldown, effectiveness tracking, and backoff as employees.
- `_try_lead_idle` text: `检查团队状态：跑 cnb board --as lead view 看谁空、谁卡住；处理你的 inbox；扫一遍 open PR 看需要谁 review 或 rebase；主动分派下一批活给空闲同学。不要等。`
- `tick()` calls `_process_lead_session` after iterating `dev_sessions` (which still excludes lead — minimal blast radius).

### Tests

- `TestGetLeadSession` (2): session exists → returns "lead"; missing → None
- `TestLeadKeepAlive` (5): idle lead nudged with lead copy (no "OKR" in text); active lead not nudged; missing lead session is no-op; inbox unread takes priority over lead-idle; idle skipped when already at prompt (#226-style stacking guard)

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_concern_helpers.py tests/test_nudge_coordinator.py` (61 passed, was 53 before this PR)
- [x] Full suite: 1713 passed
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean

author: trick77
body:
## Summary
- Bridge stdlib loggers (uvicorn, httpx, openai, sqlalchemy) through structlog so every container log line is one JSON object with the same schema. Stamps `service`/`env` on every record; new `NOERGLER_ENV` setting (default `dev`).
- Strip Splunk-reserved field names (`source`, `host`, `index`, `event`, ...) via a safety-net processor; rename `event`→`msg`, `level`→`log_level`.
- HTTP middleware emits one `msg=http_request` per request with `request_id` (from `X-Request-Id` or UUID), `method`, `path`, `status_code`, `duration_ms`. Bound to contextvars so handler logs inherit it. `/health` silenced; `uvicorn.access` set to WARNING.
- Reviewer binds `pr_tag`/`repo`/`pr_id` to contextvars for the lifetime of `review_pull_request` — Splunk can filter all logs for one PR with a single query.
- `riptide_client` migrated to structlog kwargs (`riptide_reachable team=...` → structured fields). Other modules keep `%`-format for now; the stdlib bridge still renders them as JSON, just without per-key indexing.

**Hard cutover:** Splunk searches against old plain-text uvicorn lines or `asctime`/`levelname` fields must update to the new schema (`msg`, `log_level`, plus `request_id`/`pr_tag` correlation fields).

author: carlheinmostert
body:
## What changed

Service worker now routes `_thumb.jpg`, `_thumb_line.jpg`, `_thumb_color.jpg`, and `_thumb_bw.jpg` URLs through network-first (with cache fallback for offline) instead of cache-first. mp4s + non-thumb JPGs stay cache-first — they really are immutable.

## Why

Carl's device QA reproduced the bug: move the Hero star on a video → Republish → cloud `_thumb.jpg` updated correctly (verified via direct curl + DB `storage.objects.updated_at`) → reload Safari lobby → **stale frame still showing**.

PR #372 made the SW cache-first for media on the assumption that media URLs are content-addressable and immutable. PR #376 then introduced `thumbnailsDirty` to re-upload thumbnails on Hero regeneration — but the file PATH stays the same. Cache-first + identical URL = Safari serves first-publish bytes forever.

## How to test

1. Hard-clear Safari cache once (Settings → Privacy → Manage Website Data → remove homefit-related entries → reload).
2. Move the Hero star on a video in Studio → republish.
3. Reload the lobby — new Hero frame shows. No data clear needed for subsequent edits.

After this lands, every future Hero edit propagates on the next normal reload.

## Risk

~50-200ms cold-load per thumb when online (same penalty PR #372 accepted for the app shell). Acceptable vs. permanent visual staleness after Hero edits. Offline still works (cache fallback).

## R-10 parity

`diff -q web-player/sw.js app/assets/web-player/sw.js` → 0 differences.

- All 71 `font-size: Npx` literals (CSS + inline JS) swapped to brand tokens (`var(--text-xs/sm/base/md)`). The page now scales with viewport like the rest of the suite.

author: cataggar
body:
Under \`-Drpmzig-verify-pure-zig=true\`, libtdnf now uses ONLY the pure-Zig
OpenPGP verifier added in PRs #1–#9. The gpgme path (\`verify.c\`,
\`libgpgme.so.11\`, \`libgpg-error.so.0\`, \`libassuan.so.0\`) is excluded
from the build under this flag. \`client/gpgcheck_zig.c\` routes straight
to \`tdnf_rpmzig_verify_pure\`; the cross-check block added in PR #7 and
strictened in PR #10 is removed — both are now obsolete under this flag.

## Acceptance

Plan acceptance criterion #3 (plan-pure-zig-pgp.md §6) — \`ldd
libtdnf.so\` under \`-Drpmzig-verify-pure-zig=true\` lists no
\`libgpgme*\`, \`libgpg-error*\`, or \`libassuan*\`:

\`\`\`
$ ldd ./out-pure/lib/libtdnf.so | grep -E 'gpgme|gpg-error|assuan'
(no matches)
\`\`\`

The two other build modes are unchanged on the link surface:

\`\`\`
$ ldd ./out/lib/libtdnf.so       | grep gpgme   # default: no match
$ ldd ./out-x/lib/libtdnf.so     | grep gpgme   # libgpgme.so.11 (expected)
\`\`\`

## Build matrix after this PR

| Flag                              | Verifier                  | Links gpgme? |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------|--------------|
| (default)                         | librpm primary            | no           |
| \`-Drpmzig-verify=true\`            | rpmzig + gpgme primary    | yes          |
| \`-Drpmzig-verify-pure-zig=true\`   | rpmzig + pure-Zig primary | **no**       |

## Smoke tool

\`tdnf-rpm-verify\` under the pure-Zig flag only exposes the \`--pure\`
verification path; \`--homedir\` and the gpgme backend are excluded
(they would link \`verify.c\` and \`libgpgme\`, which are gone in this
build). The default and \`-Drpmzig-verify=true\` builds still show the
full usage line with \`--homedir\`.

## Tests

\`zig build test\`, \`zig build -Drpmzig-verify=true test\`, and \`zig build
-Drpmzig-verify-pure-zig=true test\` all pass.

## Notes

- The \`rpmzig_verify\` flag's auto-imply behaviour for
  \`rpmzig_verify_pure_zig\` is replaced with two explicit derived
  bools, \`rpmzig_verify_any\` (compile the rpmzig glue) and
  \`rpmzig_verify_gpgme\` (compile \`verify.c\` + link \`libgpgme\`). This
  keeps the \`TDNF_RPMZIG_VERIFY\` macro defined under both flags
  (so \`client/gpgcheck.c\` keeps routing through \`TDNFRpmzigVerify\`)
  while only the gpgme-build adds the libgpgme dependency.
- \`rpmzig/verify.h\` is unchanged — both gpgme and pure-Zig entry
  points remain declared. PR #11 doesn't remove symbols, it just
  makes the gpgme ones unreachable under the pure-Zig build.

Closes plan-pure-zig-pgp.md.

author: gauravs11112003
body:
**BEFORE YOU START**: please make sure your pull request is against the `dev` branch.
We cannot accept pull requests against the `main` branch.
See our [contributing guide](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/stanza/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for details.

## Description
Adds an optional binary "begins a known fixed multi-word expression" input feature to the POS / morphological tagger so the model can learn the `ExtPos` UFeat despite the extreme class imbalance discussed in #1575.

- A new `FixedExpressionVocab` (in `stanza/models/pos/vocab.py`) holds a lowercased set of n-gram tuples.
- `Dataset.build_fixed_expressions` (in `stanza/models/pos/data.py`) auto-builds the lexicon from training data by collecting every span rooted at a token whose children carry `deprel=fixed`, with an optional `--fixed_expression_min_count` filter and an optional `--fixed_expression_file` external whitespace-tokenized list to union in.
- Each token's flag (`0`=pad, `1`=no, `2`=yes) is mapped through a small `nn.Embedding(3, fixed_expression_emb_dim, padding_idx=PAD_ID)` and concatenated alongside the existing word / pretrain / char / BERT inputs in `Tagger.forward`, so the BiLSTM and every head (UPOS / XPOS / UFeats — including the `ExtPos` slot) get the cue. This matches @nschneid's suggestion on the issue: "appended to the embedding for the word and fed into the morphological feature predictor."
- New CLI flags (all off / no-op by default):
  - `--use_fixed_expressions` (store_true, default `False`)
  - `--fixed_expression_emb_dim` (int, default `5`)
  - `--fixed_expression_min_count` (int, default `1`)
  - `--fixed_expression_file` (optional path)

## Fixes Issues
- Closes #1575 (the input-feature variant proposed by @nschneid and endorsed by @AngledLuffa in the issue thread).

## Unit test coverage
Yes — new tests live in [`stanza/tests/pos/test_fixed_expressions.py`](stanza/tests/pos/test_fixed_expressions.py) covering:
- `FixedExpressionVocab`: empty lookup, case-insensitive lookup, max-window clamping, case-sensitive mode, singleton skipping, `state_dict` / `load_state_dict` roundtrip.
- `Dataset.build_fixed_expressions`: end-to-end extraction of `de hecho` (ES) and `in case of` (EN) from synthetic CoNLL-U; `min_count` filtering; merging with an external file.
- `Dataset` integration: default-off run produces `batch.fixed_flags is None` (i.e. legacy behaviour preserved); enabling `--use_fixed_expressions` threads the flags through `preprocess` / `__getitem__` / `__collate_fn` and yields the expected per-token labels.
- `MultiVocab` serialisation roundtrip including the new vocab.

Existing tagger / data tests (`stanza/tests/pos/test_tagger.py`, `stanza/tests/pos/test_data.py`) continue to pass unchanged — the new feature only activates when `--use_fixed_expressions` is set.

## Known breaking changes/behaviors
None expected. The feature is opt-in and fully backward compatible:
- Old checkpoints have no `'fixed'` vocab and no `fixed_expression_emb_dim` in `args` → the model ctor skips the new `fixed_emb` module, `Dataset.preprocess` skips the slot, `__collate_fn` yields `fixed_flags=None`, the trainer passes `None` through, and `Tagger.forward` skips the branch.
- `MultiVocab.load_state_dict` registers the new `FixedExpressionVocab` class so new checkpoints round-trip cleanly.
- `Tagger.forward`'s new `fixed_flags` argument is a keyword-only-defaulted parameter, so any external callers using the existing positional signature are unaffected.
- `POSProcessor` requires no code changes; it picks up the new vocab automatically from the loaded model.

author: sferadev
body:
## Summary

Completes the unified platform service (`@sferadev/platform`) and migrates
the photocall app to use it as the single source of truth for identity,
billing, organizations, and entitlements.

### Platform service additions
- **Org-based billing**: `organizations.stripeCustomerId` column with an
  `afterCreateOrganization` hook that auto-provisions a Stripe customer.
- **`getStripeCustomerId`** is now org-aware — looks up the org first, then
  the user, so products that bill at the org level (like photocall) just
  pass the org id as `accountId`.
- **New endpoints**:
  - `POST /api/billing/checkout` — hosted Stripe Checkout for plan/price.
  - `GET /api/billing/subscription` — current subscription per org+product.
  - `GET /api/organizations/:idOrSlug` — service-token org resolver for
    anonymous routes (kiosk pages).
- **Webhook handler rewritten** to resolve accountId from the metadata or
  by looking up the `stripeCustomerId` (handles both legacy user-keyed and
  new org-keyed customers).
- Generated initial Drizzle migration; added `apps/platform/README.md` with
  setup, env vars, and product-registration recipes.

### SDK additions (`@sferadev/platform-sdk`)
- `createCheckoutSession()`, `getSubscription()` for billing.
- Full **organization plugin wrappers**:
  `listOrganizations`, `getOrganization`, `createOrganization`,
  `updateOrganization`, `deleteOrganization`, `setActiveOrganization`,
  `listMembers`, `removeMember`, `updateMemberRole`,
  `listInvitations`, `inviteMember`, `getInvitation`,
  `acceptInvitation`, `rejectInvitation`, `cancelInvitation`.
- `lookupOrganization()` (service-token) for anonymous routes.
- Distinct service-token vs user-credentialed request paths in the SDK
  client: org wrappers forward the user's cookies, billing/entitlement
  calls use the platform service token.
- 21 unit tests covering all new methods.

### Photocall migration — zero custom auth/billing code
- Dropped `better-auth`, `stripe`, and Resend deps entirely.
- Removed tables: `user`, `session`, `account`, `verification`,
  `organizations`, `organizationMembers`, `invitations`, `stripeEvents`,
  `userProfiles`, plus all subscription/limit columns. The remaining
  photocall schema is just `events`, `kiosk_sessions`, `photos`,
  `templates`, `usage_logs`, and a tiny `org_settings` table for the
  photocall-specific org logo.
- Added a `middleware.ts` **reverse proxy**: `/api/auth/*` →
  platform `/auth/*`, preserving cookies as first-party on the photocall
  domain. Works for local dev and production with separate domains.
- Rewrote `lib/auth-helpers.ts`, `actions/organizations.ts`,
  `actions/billing.ts` (new), the billing/team/invite dashboards, and the
  sign-in flow to use the SDK exclusively.
- Replaced local plan-limit checks in `actions/events.ts` /
  `actions/photos.ts` with `platform.can()`.
- Generated photocall Drizzle migration for the slimmed schema.

### Verification
- `grep "better-auth\|from 'stripe'" apps/photocall` → empty.
- `pnpm --filter @sferadev/platform tsc` ✓
- `pnpm --filter @sferadev/platform-sdk tsc` ✓ + 21 tests pass.
- `pnpm --filter @sferadev/photocall tsc` ✓
- `pnpm --filter @sferadev/photocall test` → 20 tests pass.
- `pnpm --filter @sferadev/photocall build` ✓
- `pnpm biome check` ✓ across all changed files.
- `pnpm knip` ✓

## Test plan

- [ ] End-to-end: sign up via photocall sign-in form → Stripe customer
      created on platform → create org → invite member → start checkout
      → upgrade plan → reach paid entitlements.
- [ ] Webhook delivery: trigger `checkout.session.completed` and verify
      subscription is created/updated for the right org.
- [ ] Anonymous kiosk loads via `lookupOrganization` (no session).

author: arkstack-dev
body:
## Summary

Closes the two user-visible data-loss bugs flagged in #45's review and documented inline in the test suite ever since as \"pre-existing limitation\" comments. Both were caused by drift between the SDK annotation surface and the processor's read-side assumptions; both silently dropped every user-supplied value.

| Bug | What broke | Where | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | \`@Field.computedFrom\` array values dropped | \`extractFieldMetadata\` used \`instanceof String[]\` on javac's \`List<AnnotationValue>\` form | Flatten array attributes once at \`extractAnnotationValues\` |
| 2 | \`@EventSourced.streamPrefix\` + \`.snapshotThreshold\` ignored | \`extractEventSourcedMetadata\` read attribute names from the SDK *model* (\`aggregateType\`, \`snapshotEvery\`) — neither exists on the *annotation* | Read the SDK annotation attribute names and translate to model field names |

## Bug 1 — \`@Field.computedFrom\` silent data loss

\`\`\`java
// Before: instanceof never matches javac's List<AnnotationValue> form
if (computedFromValue instanceof String[] array) {
    builder.computedFrom(Arrays.asList(array));
}
\`\`\`

A user writing \`@Field(computed = true, computedFrom = {\"firstName\", \"lastName\"})\` got \`\"computedFrom\": []\` in the emitted metadata.

**Fix at the seam** (\`extractAnnotationValues\`): when the raw annotation value is a \`List<?>\`, walk it and unwrap each \`AnnotationValue\`'s inner value once. After this:
- \`String[]\` attributes come through as \`List<String>\`
- \`Class[]\` as \`List<TypeMirror>\`
- nested \`@Annotation[]\` as \`List<AnnotationMirror>\` — preserving the existing \`extractEventsMetadata\` container-walk semantics that already used \`instanceof AnnotationMirror\` on elements.

The \`computedFrom\` call site simplifies to \`instanceof List<?>\` + element-level \`String\` filter. Generalising at the seam (rather than only the one call site) removes the same class of silent-cast-failure bug for any future array-typed attribute. Audited: \`computedFrom\` was the only array-value consumer before the fix.

## Bug 2 — \`@EventSourced\` SDK drift

\`\`\`java
// Before: aggregateType / snapshotEvery are NOT attributes on @EventSourced.
String aggregateType = values.containsKey(\"aggregateType\")
        ? (String) values.get(\"aggregateType\")
        : element.getSimpleName().toString();
return EventSourcedMetadata.builder(aggregateType)
        .snapshotEvery(getInt(values, \"snapshotEvery\", 100))
        .build();
\`\`\`

The SDK annotation exposes \`streamPrefix\` (default \`\"\"\`) and \`snapshotThreshold\` (default \`50\`). The SDK metadata-model record exposes \`aggregateType\` and \`snapshotEvery\`. The processor was reading the *model* names from the *annotation* values map — neither was ever present, so every user value silently became a default. Class-name fallback for \`aggregateType\` happened to mask the bug for the prefix; the snapshot threshold was always wrong.

**Fix**: read \`streamPrefix\`/\`snapshotThreshold\` from the annotation values map, then translate to \`aggregateType\`/\`snapshotEvery\` when populating \`EventSourcedMetadata.builder\`. Class-name fallback preserved for empty \`streamPrefix\` (matches the SDK Javadoc). Default for \`snapshotThreshold\` is now **50** to match the SDK annotation default (was 100 — didn't match anything).

## Test changes

**New (in \`ExerisDomainProcessorGapsTest.BugfixRoundTripTests\` — 4 tests):**
- \`computedFromArrayPropagates\` — \`{\"firstName\", \"lastName\"}\` round-trips as a populated JSON array.
- \`emptyComputedFromList\` — \`computedFrom = {}\` doesn't crash.
- \`eventSourcedUserValuesPropagate\` — \`streamPrefix = \"Billing\", snapshotThreshold = 25\` flows into emitted \`aggregateType = \"Billing\", snapshotEvery = 25\`.
- \`eventSourcedEmptyStreamPrefixDefaultsToClassName\` — bare \`@EventSourced\` → class-name fallback + threshold default 50.

**Updated (existing tests that had \"pre-existing limitation\" comments documenting the bugs):**
- \`ExerisDomainProcessorBranchTest.everyFieldAttributeFlowsThrough\` — now asserts \`computedFrom\` array actually propagates (was previously documenting silent drop).
- \`ExerisDomainProcessorBranchTest.eventSourcedDefaults\` — now asserts \`aggregateType\` + \`snapshotEvery\` reflect user-supplied annotation values (was previously asserting only \`enabled : true\`, sidestepping the broken translation).

## Results (\`mvn verify -o\`)

| | Before | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| processor L | 94.4% | **94.9%** | +0.5pp |
| processor B | 87.3% | **87.6%** | +0.3pp |
| processor M | 97.7% | 97.8% | unchanged |
| processor test count | 41 | 45 | +4 |

All four module gates still pass. Full reactor (incl. e2e-tests) builds cleanly — no downstream consumer broke on the \`snapshotEvery\` default change (was 100, now 50; only emitted JSON differs, no API touch).

## Test plan

- [x] \`mvn verify -o\`: BUILD SUCCESS across all 8 modules.
- [x] All four JaCoCo gates still pass.
- [x] 45/45 processor tests green; 4 new bugfix round-trips + 2 updated tests asserting the FIXED behaviour.
- [x] Branch protection (added today) will require the \`mvn verify (JDK 26)\` check before merge.

body:
## Summary
Enhanced the project validation system to support granular step-by-step verification across all 10 wizard steps, with the ability to flag specific steps as needing rectification and attach notes. This replaces the simple binary validation model with a more detailed review workflow.

## Key Changes

**Frontend Components:**
- Added `VerificationDialog` component that presents all 10 wizard steps in a modal, allowing each party (Sales, Projects, Operations) to mark steps as verified, needs rectification, or pending
- Added `RectificationPanel` component to display flagged issues inline on the validation card
- Enhanced `ValidationCircle` to show overall status (verified/needs_rectification/pending) with issue counts and expandable rectification details
- Added `StatusIcon` utility component for consistent status visualization across the UI
- Updated `ProjectValidationPanel` to manage dialog state and handle step-level note submission
- Added helper functions `partyStatus()` and `partyStepNotes()` to extract party-specific validation data

**Projects List View:**
- Updated `ValidationDots` component to display status indicators (verified/needs_rectification/pending) instead of just binary validated state
- Added "Resolve" link in validation column when any party has flagged rectification needs
- Added inline alert banner in project details when rectification is flagged

**API & Database:**
- Extended `ProjectValidation` model with step-level tracking:
  - `salesStepNotes`, `projectsStepNotes`, `operationsStepNotes` (JSON fields storing step status and notes)
  - `salesStatus`, `projectsStatus`, `operationsStatus` (overall status per party)
- Updated `/api/projects/[id]/validate` endpoint to accept and process `stepNotes` payload
- Added `computeStatus()` function to derive overall party status from step notes (verified only if all steps verified, needs_rectification if any step flagged, otherwise pending)
- Only sets `validatedById` and `validatedAt` when status is "verified"; otherwise clears them

**Database Migration:**
- Added `v27_0_validation_step_notes.sql` with conditional column additions for all new fields using stored procedure pattern (no `IF NOT EXISTS`)

**Type Updates:**
- Extended `ValidationData` type to include step notes and status fields for all three parties
- Added `StepNote` and `StepNotes` types for type-safe step tracking
- Updated `ValidationStatus` type in projects list to include status fields

## Implementation Details

- The wizard defines 10 fixed steps (Project Info, Buildings, Scope Definition, Activities, Duration, Coating System, Payment Terms, Project Checklist, Technical Specs, Parts Upload)
- Each step can be marked as: `verified`, `needs_rectification`, or `pending`
- Optional notes can be attached to any step, required when marking as needs_rectification
- "Verify All" button allows quick marking of all steps as verified
- Overall party status is computed deterministically from step statuses
- Validation is only considered complete when all three parties have status "verified"
- Projects with any "needs_rectification" status are highlighted with amber indicators and "Resolve" links throughout the UI

**[e2e-coder]**

## Summary

- **Defect (N5 probe, 2026-05-17)**: `build_system_prompt` hardcoded "4 universal wrappers: list_actions / search_actions / describe_action / invoke_action" unconditionally, even when `search_actions` was excluded from `tools[]` by the D14 gate (= `action_retrieval.embedding_class` not configured, the default in most environments).
- **Empirical failure case**: `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` read the SP, hallucinated a call to `search_actions(query="...")`, received an `unknown_tool` dispatcher error, and gave up without recovering via `list_actions` or a hot-list alias. Concrete reproducible failure.
- **Fix**: add `search_actions_enabled: bool = True` kwarg to `build_system_prompt`. RouterLoop passes `_search_visible` (already computed from the D14 gate) as `search_actions_enabled` when universal wrappers are enabled. When `False`, SP says "3 universal wrappers" and all `search_actions` Behaviour guidance is suppressed.

## Diff scope

- `src/reyn/chat/router_system_prompt.py` — new `search_actions_enabled` kwarg + conditional wrapper-line + conditional Behaviour guidance
- `src/reyn/chat/router_loop.py` — pass `_search_visible` to `build_system_prompt` (uses existing `_search_visible` variable already computed for `build_tools`)
- `tests/test_router_system_prompt_wrapper_visibility.py` — 9 new Tier 2 tests

Default is `True` (not `False`) to preserve byte-identical SP output for existing LLMReplay fixture keys. Tests recorded before this PR include `search_actions` in the SP; changing the default would invalidate those fixture keys, which contradicts the "do NOT re-record" constraint. The `_univ_enabled=False` guard in `router_loop.py` ensures the non-wrapper path also stays byte-identical.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_router_system_prompt_wrapper_visibility.py` — 9/9 pass (new)
- [x] `pytest tests/test_router_system_prompt.py tests/test_router_sp_universal_categories.py` — 31/31 pass (existing)

author: shaun0927
body:
## Release 0.6.1 — develop → main catch-up + secure-field paste fix

**OpenSafari 0.6.1 is a catch-up release.** `v0.6.0` was tagged on 2026-05-16 but never merged to `main` and never published to npm (`npm view opensafari-mcp versions` confirms `0.5.0` was the latest published until this PR). Rather than ship a separate 0.6.0 → 0.6.1 pair, this PR rolls the entire 0.6.0 body forward together with one targeted pasteboard fix uncovered after the 0.6.0 tag (#761).

This PR contains **356 commits** from `develop` (= the v0.6.0 release body + #761). No breaking changes since 0.5.0.

## Headline

- **Fix #761 / closes #760** — `app_type_element` pasteboard backend now works on `AXSecureTextField` (password) elements. The #639 PR C readback contract was rejecting every successful password paste as `PASTE_NOT_APPLIED` because iOS masks `AXSecureTextField` AXValue with bullet chars (`••••…`) regardless of plaintext. Verifier now skips for secure-field signals (role / trait) and the pasteboard backend honours `verify: false` symmetrically with simhid. Response gains optional `secureField: true` field.
- **Rolled forward from 0.6.0** — `ax-bridge` recursive scored content-root search (#40, follow-up to #4). Closes the silent-empty-content bug on Xcode 26.4 / iOS 26.4 with a typed `DEVICE_CONTENT_ROOT_EMPTY` error instead of falling back to bare `AXWindow`.

## Themes (full per-PR notes in `CHANGELOG.md` `[0.6.1]` section)

| Area | Highlights |
|---|---|
| Reliability batch | Boot / lifecycle / network (#752, #753, #754, #755, #756, #757) |
| Decomposition | WebKit (#706 1/5–5/5), Simulator (#708 1/4–4/4), Input (#707 a/b), Protocol typing (#710 a/b), DOM-input (#709) |
| Performance | CLI lazy-load (#700), WebKit fast paths (#702), native-input batching (#705), proxy readiness split (#701), bootstatus-aware polling (#703), Web Inspector socket cache (#704) |
| Security | HTTP MCP transport hardening (#714 series), auth profile persistence (#716), audit log retention (#711, #717) |
| Bug fixes | DOM input dispatch (#726), ax-bridge coord scaling (#693 WU3 #720), ax-bridge content sizing (#693 WU3-prep #695, #693 WU1 #694), pasteboard secure-field (#761) |
| Features | `feat(tap)` macOS-pt → iOS-pt scaling (#693 WU3), `feat(ax-bridge)` `--debug` machine-readable stderr (#660), `TRANSITIONAL_STATE_TIMEOUT` + `--max-settle-retries` (#46) |
| CI / DX | Separate runtime/dev audits (#712, #718), `no-explicit-any` enforcement on migrated paths (#710 b) |

## Migration notes (since 0.5.0)

- **No tool-name or schema changes.** All `app_*` / `webkit_*` / bridge tools keep parameter shapes and response envelopes.
- **`app_type_element` response shape gains an optional `secureField: true` field** on the pasteboard backend when the focused element is an `AXSecureTextField`. Callers that ignore unknown fields are unaffected.
- **`verify: false` parameter on `app_type_element` is now honoured on both backends** (`auto`/`simhid` and `pasteboard`). Callers relying on the previous silent-no-op on pasteboard should review their flows.
- **HTTP MCP transport** tightens defaults; STDIO transport (default) unaffected.

## Verification

```
$ npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json   # exit 0
$ npx jest --config jest.config.js --testPathPatterns='tests/unit'
Test Suites: 176 passed, 176 total
Tests:       2646 passed, 2646 total
Snapshots:   6 passed, 6 total
Time:        75.6 s
```

## Post-merge release checklist

1. ✅ `release/0.6.1` → `main` PR merged (this PR)
2. ⏳ Tag `v0.6.1` on the merge commit and push:
   ```bash
   git tag -a v0.6.1 -m "Release OpenSafari MCP 0.6.1" <merge-sha>
   git push origin v0.6.1
   ```
3. ⏳ `npm publish` from `main` (handled by user out-of-band)
4. ⏳ Backmerge `main` → `develop` so develop's `[Unreleased]` lines up with main's `[0.6.1]` history

Closes #760 (via #761 already merged to `develop`).

author: thkt
body:
## 概要

#133 (RC-006) の解消。`src/storage/search.rs` の N+1 ホットパス 2 箇所を bulk-fetch にリファクタリング。

- **`vec_search_multi`**: 旧実装は embedding ごとに `vec_search` を呼んでいたため 2N DB round-trip（KNN + metadata）。新実装は全 embedding で共有する 1 回の filtered metadata fetch にまとめ、N+1 round-trip に削減。
- **`get_keyword_doc_frequencies`**: 旧実装は keyword ごとに `COUNT(*)` を発行（N round-trip）。新実装は `UNION ALL` で 1 query にまとめ、明示的な `idx` で順序保証。bulk fail 時は per-keyword fallback。

privateヘルパー (`knn_only`, `build_semantic_results`) を追加して `vec_search` / `vec_search_multi` 間で共有。metadata fetch は既存の `get_chunks_by_ids` を type/path filter 受けに拡張する形で統合。

## ベンチマーク (debug profile, 200-chunk corpus, 20 iters × 3 runs)

| 関数 | 形状 | Before (main) | After | 改善 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vec_search_multi` | 5 embeddings | 15.43 ms/call | **10.40 ms/call** | **33%** |
| `get_keyword_doc_frequencies` | 50 keywords | 1.42 ms/call | **1.28 ms/call** | **9%** |

doc-freq の改善が小さいのは local SQLite で FTS5 MATCH が round-trip overhead を支配しているため。構造的な改善 (N→1 queries) は higher-latency storage や larger N で意味あり。

再検証コマンド:
```
cargo test --release -- --ignored --nocapture bench_search_hot_path_5emb_50kw
```

## /polish レビューで追加した安全策

- **MAX_VEC_CANDIDATES = 30,000**: `vec_search_multi` の共有 IN-clause を SQLite の `SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER` (32766) 以下に bound。これがないと `search_from_file` で 150+ chunks の source file 経由でオーバーフロー可能。
- **MAX_BULK_DOC_FREQ_KEYWORDS = 500**: SQLite の `SQLITE_MAX_COMPOUND_SELECT` デフォルト以下で UNION ALL bulk path を skip、pathological 入力では per-keyword に fallback。

## 挙動同値性

`vec_search_multi` の「merge してから truncate」は、`k = limit * VEC_MAXSIM_OVERSAMPLE` (10×) という前提のもとで旧実装の「emb 毎に truncate してから merge」と同じ top-`limit` ranking を返す。既存 3 つの behavioral test (T-563/T-545/T-008) で確認済み。

## コミット

1. `refactor(search): extract knn_only helper from vec_search`
2. `refactor(search): share metadata fetch across vec_search_multi (#133)`
3. `refactor(search): bulk doc-frequency via UNION ALL (#133)`
4. `test(search): wall-clock bench for #133 bulk-fetch refactor`
5. `refactor(search): polish review fixes for #133 bulk-fetch` (EFF-001 / REUSE-001 / EFF-002 + readability)

## テスト計画

- [x] `cargo test --lib` → 460 pass, 0 fail
- [x] vec_search_multi 既存 3 テスト不変 (T-563/T-545/T-008)
- [x] get_keyword_doc_frequencies regression test 不変
- [x] T-580 bench harness 追加 (`#[ignore]`)
- [ ] CI clippy + tests
- [ ] (follow-up) MAX_VEC_CANDIDATES / MAX_BULK_DOC_FREQ_KEYWORDS cap 分岐の unit test

author: skywills
body:
## Summary

- `planDebaterOp` has a static session role `"debate-plan"`. All three paths in `runPlan` (verifier-pick, stateful, one-shot) were building `debaterCtx` without a `sessionOverride`, so `callOp` used that static role for every debater
- `SessionManager.nameFor()` produced the same session name for all N debaters (e.g. `nax-f22b55d4-<storyId>-debate-plan`), so debaters 2 and 3 immediately hit the single-flight invariant guard and failed
- Fix: inject `sessionOverride: { role: \`debate-plan-${index}\` }` into each debater's `CallContext`, mirroring the pattern already used by `runner-stateful.ts` (`debate-${stage}-${index}`) and `runner-hybrid.ts` (`debate-hybrid-${index}`)

## Root cause trace

```
runner-plan.ts Path B (stateful sessions):
  debaterCtx = { ...ctx.callContext, agentName }   // no sessionOverride
  callOp(debaterCtx, planDebaterOp, ...)
    → sessionRole = ctx.sessionOverride?.role ?? runOp.session.role
                  = undefined               ?? "debate-plan"   // same for all
    → SessionManager.nameFor() → nax-<hash>-<feature>-<storyId>-debate-plan
  Debater 2 opens same session → single-flight guard fires → fails
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing `test/unit/debate/runner-plan.test.ts` — all 26 tests pass (verified locally)
- [ ] Typecheck clean (`bun run typecheck`)
- [ ] Run `nax plan debate` with a multi-debater config and confirm all debaters complete without single-flight errors
