body:
Closes #173. Follow-up to #172 (the view-lens mechanism).

Gates each dashboard panel by the active view lens, so a user sees only the panels relevant to how they work. Deep links and data are untouched — this only filters what renders.

## Per-lens panel sets

| Lens | Panels |
|------|--------|
| Spec writer | Counts, Readiness |
| Spec implementer | Implementation, Schedule health, Capacity, Risks, Anomalies |
| Reviewer | Readiness, Reviews |
| All (default) | Everything — unchanged |

The lens-to-panels mapping lives on `ViewLens` (`panels()` / `revealsPanel()`), alongside the existing lens-to-sections mapping from #172. For the **All** lens every gate evaluates true, so the rendered dashboard is unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php` gains 4 lens tests over a shared fixture that exercises all 8 panels. Panel presence is asserted on panel-unique headings/column headers rather than entity titles — the readiness panel cross-references risks, anomalies, reviews, and work items as finding subjects, and lists an "Implementation" readiness gate, so those strings legitimately surface outside their own panels.

Verified: 19 `DashboardTest|ViewLensTest` pass, 64 other dashboard-touching tests pass, `pint` clean.

## Note

Readiness and schedule share one `lg:grid-cols-2` section, so a lens that shows only one of the two renders it at half-width. Functionally correct; the issue calls the mapping a tunable "starting point", so this is left for a follow-up if the half-width layout is unwanted.

author: lincyaw
body:
## Summary

When the user runs `SELECT * FROM "abnormal_traces" LIMIT 100`, the Trace tab used to dump every span across every TraceId into one `<TraceTree>` — a jumbled multi-root forest on a shared time axis. `<TraceTree>` is a one-trace-per-render primitive; the violation was on the page side.

This PR fixes that and the silent ns/ms unit mismatch.

### UX

- **1 TraceId in result** → render `<TraceTree>` directly, prefixed with a caption: `name · traceId · N spans · 245ms`, error dot if any span errored.
- **N TraceIds** → ribbon of chips (sorted **error-first**, then **duration desc**) above the tree; default selection = first chip. Overflow past 12 collapses into a native `<select>`.
- **Trace truncated by `LIMIT`** (any "root" actually has a parent we just don't have in the result) → caption shows `⚠ truncated by LIMIT`.

### Bug fix: start/duration unit mismatch

OTel parquet's `Timestamp` is ns-since-epoch — Arrow → BigInt → 19-digit string via `arrowToRows.normalizeCell` (BigInts outside safe-int range stringify). `Duration` is ns too. Old code scaled only `Duration / 1_000_000`, leaving `Timestamp` as a raw ns number — bars were rendered with start offsets 1e6× larger than their widths.

New `toMs()` is value-driven: ≥15-digit decimal strings or BigInts scale via BigInt div, normal numbers/strings pass through, and ISO strings fall through to `Date.parse`. Drops the `startDivisor` field.

### Scope

All changes in `apps/console/src/apps/portal/pages/InjectionData/ResultView.tsx` + companion CSS. `packages/ui/` untouched — `<TraceTree>`'s contract was correct.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm lint:css`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm build` all green
- [ ] Verify on byte-cluster after deploy: open `/portal/injections/25/data`, click `abnormal_traces.parquet`, confirm ribbon appears with the multiple traces and clicking each switches the tree below.
- [ ] Single-trace query (`WHERE TraceId = '...'`) → no ribbon, just caption + tree.

Previously the status check called `findWorkspaceProjects`, which validates each project's `engines` and `os`/`cpu`/`libc` and warns about useless fields in non-root manifests — work that the install pipeline already performs. With no `nodeVersion` threaded through, the engine check also fell back to the system Node from `PATH` and emitted spurious "Unsupported engine" warnings before scripts ran. Status-only callers now use `findWorkspaceProjectsNoCheck`; install paths continue to validate.
- Fixed `pnpm add <alias>:@​scope/pkg` for [named registries](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/11324). The local resolver was claiming any specifier containing `/` as a local directory, so `pnpm add bit:@​teambit/bit` (with `bit` configured under `namedRegistries`) installed a bogus link to `bit:@​teambit/bit/` instead of resolving from the configured registry. The local resolver now runs after the named-registry resolver in the resolution chain.
- Updated `@zkochan/cmd-shim` to 9.0.3. The sh shim it writes for `.cmd` / `.bat` targets now escapes the `/C` switch as `//C`, so it survives the path translation Git Bash applies when launching `cmd.exe`. Without this, a bare `/C` was rewritten to `C:\` before reaching cmd.exe — the switch was dropped, cmd started interactively, and the calling script saw the cmd banner instead of the wrapped command's output. Affects any cmd-shim-wrapped batch script invoked from Git Bash / MSYS / Cygwin on Windows. See [pnpm/cmd-shim#55](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/cmd-shim/pull/55).

</details>

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: currentsuspect
body:
## Summary

`bounceRangeToWav` now tracks write errors, returns `false` on failure, and removes partial output files.

## Why

Previously the function returned `true` even after a write error (disk full, permission denied), leaving a partial/corrupt WAV file on disk with no indication of failure.

## Testing performed
- Code review of error path
- Verified partial file cleanup on write error
- Verified playback state restoration on both success and failure

## Docs updated?
No

## Risk/rollback notes
- Low risk: only changes error handling behavior
- Rollback: revert commit if bounce behavior regressions found

Fixes #195

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## What changed

- **bounceRangeToWav now properly tracks and handles write errors**: The function detects when PCM writes fail during the render/export loop and sets a `writeError` flag to mark the operation as failed.

- **Returns correct failure status**: Returns `false` to callers when a write error occurs, preventing truncated or corrupted exports from being treated as successful bounces.

- **Cleans up partial files on failure**: When a write error is detected, the function attempts to delete any partially written output WAV file using `std::remove()`, logging whether the cleanup succeeded and any error codes (`errno`) if the deletion fails.

- **Added test coverage for write error handling**: New test case (`ArsenalExportLiveParityTest.cpp`) forces a bounce write failure via the `AESTRA_TEST_FORCE_BOUNCE_WRITE_ERROR` environment variable and verifies that:
  - The function returns `false` (failure signal)
  - The partial output file is removed from disk

## Why

Fixes issue `#195` — prevents silent data corruption by ensuring that when `bounceRangeToWav` encounters write errors (disk full, permission denied, I/O errors), the operation fails cleanly instead of reporting success and leaving corrupt files on disk. Callers can now reliably detect bounce failures.

author: noahgift
body:
## Summary

PMAT-019 (#50) shipped a *citation gate* proving harnesses **exist**; this PR adds the *verification gate* proving they **discharge**. Converts the Symbolic stratum from claim to fact for any local developer with Kani installed.

## What lands

\`crates/xpile/tests/kani_verify.rs\` (new):

- Walks every \`contracts/kani/*.rs\` file.
- Materialises a one-shot Cargo crate per harness (Cargo.toml + copy of harness as \`lib.rs\`) in a temp dir.
- Runs \`cargo kani\` from the temp dir.
- Asserts exit-0 AND stdout contains \`VERIFICATION:- SUCCESSFUL\`. **The grep guards against Kani's historical \"exit 0 on swallowed solver error\" failure mode** — silent success on a broken installation is the failure case we most want to catch.
- On \`py_int_arith.rs\` (the one harness today): 2 of 2 checks pass in ~4 seconds locally.

## Skip behaviour

| Environment | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Local dev with Kani installed | Gate fires, harness is verified end-to-end |
| Local dev without Kani | Test prints install hint, exits OK |
| Current CI (no Kani) | Test prints install hint, exits OK |
| Future CI with Kani (XPILE-QUORUM-003) | Gate fires on every PR |

Same posture as the python3/rustc skip in \`diff_exec.rs\` — opt-in for environments that have the tool, no false failures elsewhere.

## What still remains under XPILE-QUORUM

| Ticket | Scope |
|---|---|
| QUORUM-003 | Install Kani in GitHub Actions so the gate fires on every PR. Heavy (CBMC + solvers) but one-time. |
| QUORUM-004 | §14.5 F3 pairwise-correlation guard. Defer until ≥3 independent oracles make the matrix meaningful. |
| QUORUM-005 | Extrinsic stratum verdict-recording via pmat work-item notes. |

## Self-test

\`collect_finds_at_least_the_py_int_arith_harness\` pins the expected file so a future move of \`contracts/kani/\` fires loudly rather than silently passing on zero harnesses (the failure mode equivalent of an empty test suite).

(Refs PMAT-020)

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test --workspace\` — 93 tests pass (was 91)
- [x] \`cargo test -p xpile --test kani_verify\` — Kani actually runs, verifies, ~4s
- [x] \`cargo fmt --all -- --check\` clean
- [x] \`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings\` clean
- [x] \`cargo deny check advisories\` clean

author: addulaajay
body:
The Archetype Discovery Quiz runs as part of the pre-signup onboarding flow — the mobile client has no Cognito JWT at that point. The frontend's quiz API calls (src/services/api/quiz.ts on the mobile client) are explicitly ``requiresAuth: false``.

The JWT-authorizer PR (security/cognito-jwt-authorizer) didn't list these two routes as public, so the catch-all was rejecting them with
401. End-user impact: the alert "Unable to load quiz questions. Please check your connection and try again." on the quiz screen, blocking the entire signup funnel for new users.

Adds the two routes to the public list in serverless.yml, alongside the existing auth + health + IAP-webhook exceptions:

  - GET  /api/mirrorgpt/quiz/questions
  - POST /api/mirrorgpt/quiz/submit

Backend endpoints are read-only (questions) / append-only with an optional anonymousId (submit), so there's no per-user authorization to enforce here. The anonymousId gets linked to the real user once they confirm their email.

Validation:
  - YAML parses cleanly.
  - Diff is purely additive — no existing route's auth posture changes.

author: arawn-davies
body:
## Summary

Closes both **slice 8** ([#144](https://github.com/Arawn-Davies/Makar/issues/144) — Linux-style signal subsystem) and **slice 9** ([#145](https://github.com/Arawn-Davies/Makar/issues/145) — preemption hardening), plus the immediate CI flake item from the original handoff (GDB ISO test timeout), plus the htop-style picker app and assorted small kernel + userspace fixes that surfaced along the way.

## What landed

### Slice 8 — Linux i386 signal subsystem

- **Per-task signal infrastructure** (`kernel/signal.{h,c}`): SIG_* numbers, `sig_handler_t` typedef, SIG_DFL/SIG_IGN sentinels, per-task handler table held out-of-band, default-action classifier matching Linux defaults.  SIGKILL bypasses mask + handler; SIGKILL/SIGSTOP can't have their disposition overridden.
- **Syscalls**: `SYS_KILL(37)`, `SYS_SIGNAL(48)`, `SYS_SIGRETURN(119)` — Linux i386 numbers.  Userspace stubs in `src/userspace/syscall.h`.
- **Scheduler-driven default-terminate**: `sig_deliver` runs on both the outgoing and incoming tasks in `schedule()`; default-terminate marks the task DEAD and the existing reaper / slot-reuse path frees its resources (no inline free in `schedule()`, which was the #128 regression vector).
- **Ring-3 trampoline + SYS_SIGRETURN** so user-installed handlers actually run.  `signal_check_user()` is called at the end of `isr_handler` / `irq_handler` / `syscall_dispatch` (the universal "about to iret to ring 3" hook).  Builds a sigframe on the user stack below `regs->useresp` with saved general regs + saved iret frame + an embedded 7-byte trampoline (`movl $SYS_SIGRETURN, %eax; int $0x80`) + a magic guard.  Handler returns into the trampoline; `SYS_SIGRETURN` validates the magic, restores the iret frame, the next iret resumes the interrupted instruction.
- **Ctrl+C → SIGINT migration**: keyboard ISR now does `sig_send(kb_focused, SIGINT)`; shell tasks install `SIG_IGN` for SIGINT at startup; legacy `kb_sigint` + `keyboard_sigint_consume()` removed.
- **`task_t.unkillable`**: idle (in `tasking_init`) and shell tasks (in `shell_run` startup) opt in; `sig_deliver` drops SIGKILL + default-terminate on those targets.

### Slice 9 — Preemption hardening

- **`in_schedule` re-entrancy guard** in `schedule()`, cleared *before* `task_switch` (fresh tasks bypass the schedule epilogue, so post-switch clearing would deadlock the kernel on the first context switch into any new task).
- **`irq_save_disable` / `irq_restore`** wrap the critical section so the caller's IF state is preserved across every exit path.
- **Per-task `kticks`** PIT-tick accounting incremented by `timer_callback`; rendered in `/proc/tasks`.
- **Runtime-tunable `g_sched_quantum`** (default 4 PIT ticks = 40 ms slice) via a new `sched_quantum [n]` shell builtin clamped to `[1..100]`.
- **`test_preempt` ktest** — spawns a no-yield busy-loop victim and asserts its `kticks` counter advances (proves preemption is doing its job under TCG).

### Userspace: maktop.elf

htop-style task viewer.  Resolution-agnostic via `sys_term_cols`/`sys_term_rows`.  Horizontal CPU% + memory meter bars (green → yellow → red); the kernel-rendered tmux-style VT status bar stays present at the bottom.  Auto-refresh every 1 s via the new `O_NONBLOCK` stdin path (POSIX-aligned `fcntl(F_SETFL)` + `read` returning `-EAGAIN`).  ↑↓ navigate, **F9** opens a left-side scrollable signal picker (SIGHUP..SIGTSTP), `s` is a numeric-entry alternate, `r` forces refresh, **F10** / `q` quits.  pid 1 (idle) excluded from the CPU% denominator (otherwise always-100%).  Diff render skips cells whose (ch, clr) didn't change since the last frame.

### Misc kernel polish surfacing alongside the work

- **`/proc/meminfo` rewritten Linux-style**: `MemTotal`, `MemFree`, `MemAvailable`, `MemUsed`, `Buffers` (0), `Cached` (0), heap fields, `PageSize`, `FreeFrames`, `TotalFrames`.  `pmm_init` caches the managed frame count for `MemTotal`.
- **`/proc/tasks` filters `TASK_DEAD`** so the zombies bg-ktest leaves behind (`preempt_victim`, `ktest_noop2`, …) don't appear forever.
- **Exec'd tasks get real names** (basename of the path, minus `.elf`) via `task_t.name_buf[16]` — was always `"exec"` before.
- **`task_t.fb_touched`** — set by `SYS_PUTCH_AT` / `SYS_TTY_CLEAR`.  `shell_exec_elf` only calls `shell_clear_screen()` after the child dies if this is set, so fullscreen apps that exited via SIGKILL get cleaned up while line-mode children (cat, hello, makbox fallback on typos) keep their output on screen.
- **`SYS_FCNTL(55)`** with `F_GETFL` / `F_SETFL` and `O_NONBLOCK` on stdin.

### Test infra

- **Expect-style sync in ui_runner.sh**: `wait_for_serial <regex> <start_bytes> [timeout]` + `it_until` helper.  The shell emits `[shell:ready vt=N]` to serial on every `shell_readline` entry (gated by `g_serial_verbose`).  Tests can now sync on "the prompt is ready" instead of `sleep N` — pexpect / Tcl-Expect style.  Eliminated the timing flake the original `typo-doesnt-clear` scenario hit under TCG.
- **New scenarios**: `ctrlc-kills-child`, `user-sigusr1-handler`, `no-dead-in-proctasks`, `typo-doesnt-clear`.

### CI flake fix (`4123e40`)

Original handoff item: release run 25948150516 was killed at exit 124 by the outer `timeout 120` wrapping the GDB ISO test under TCG on a shared GitHub runner.  Bumped to 300 s (~2.5× headroom on the slowest observed run); on FAIL, `tests/groups/ktest_bg.py` prints the last `ktest_bg_completed/total` it observed so triage doesn't need to download the serial artifact for the basic "which suite stalled" question.

## Test results

- **iso-test**: 269 / 0 across kernel ktest; all 5 GDB groups (Boot Checkpoints, Hardware State, VESA Framebuffer, Background ktest, CD-ROM content) pass.
- **ui-test**: **11 / 11** green across two consecutive runs after the expect-style sync went in.

## Manual smoke tests

CI covers the rest; these are the operator-facing flows that the
automated suites can't reach from inside a sendkey + serial-grep
harness:

- [ ] `./run.sh iso-boot` → `exec /cdrom/apps/maktop.elf` → F9 picker, navigate, send a signal
- [ ] In maktop: F9 → SIGKILL on a `shellN` is dropped (`[signal] SIGKILL dropped on unkillable pid=N` in serial); the VT stays alive
- [ ] In maktop: SIGKILL on maktop itself leaves a clean shell screen afterwards (proves `task_t.fb_touched` cleanup gate)
- [ ] q (or F10) quits maktop cleanly; shell palette restored
- [ ] Ctrl+C at the empty prompt prints `^C` without killing the shell
- [ ] Ctrl+C during `exec /cdrom/apps/calc.elf` returns to the prompt promptly
- [ ] Typing a typo runs the makbox fallback, prints its "unknown applet" error, and the next `pwd` output is visible (no screen wipe)

author: ahuman1684
body:
Fixes #6367

## Problem
When an invalid architecture name is passed to `rz-asm -m`, the tool
silently exits with code 0 instead of showing an error.

## Root Cause
The `case 'm':` block in `librz/main/rz-asm.c` called
`rz_core_cpu_descs_print()` without first validating that the
architecture name is known to the plugin registry.

## Fix
Added a call to `rz_asm_plugin_find()` before proceeding. If the
architecture is not found, `RZ_LOG_ERROR` prints a descriptive message
to stderr and the tool exits with code 1.

## Before
$ rz-asm -m ic
$ echo $?
0

## After
$ rz-asm -m ic
ERROR: rz-asm: unknown architecture 'ic'
Use 'rz-asm -L' to list all available architectures.
$ echo $?
1

## Testing
Added regression test in `test/db/tools/rz_asm`. All 57 existing tests
still pass.

- `dotnet new aspire-servicedefaults` → `src/shared/TemporalEngine.ServiceDefaults`

The AppHost orchestrates:
- **Temporal** dev server as a container resource (`temporalio/admin-tools`, `temporal server start-dev`) with an HTTP health check on the UI endpoint so `WaitFor` actually blocks on readiness
- **Postgres** (one instance, three databases: `temporal_sport`, `temporal_catalog`, `temporal_finance`) via the official `Aspire.Hosting.PostgreSQL`
- **Three per-service workers** (see below)
- **Three per-service APIs**
- **DemoDriver** as explicit-start

Temporal target host is published to workers/APIs via `ReferenceExpression.Create($"{host}:{port}")` — defers resolution to runtime so the DCP-allocated proxy port is what each process actually receives.

### Per-service workers
- `src/sport/TemporalEngine.Sport.Worker`     ← refs only Sport.Workflows + Sport.Data + ServiceDefaults
- `src/catalog/TemporalEngine.Catalog.Worker` ← refs only Catalog.Workflows + Catalog.Data + ServiceDefaults
- `src/finance/TemporalEngine.Finance.Worker` ← refs only Finance.Workflows + Finance.Data + ServiceDefaults

Each is its own Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web project; uses Aspire's `AddNpgsqlDbContext<T>("Sport")` etc. for connection-string + health-check wiring. Each worker registers the engine's custom search attributes at startup (idempotent helper in `TemporalEngine.Shared.Contracts.SearchAttributeRegistration`). The combined `TemporalEngine.Worker` is gone — no more build-time coupling across bounded contexts on the worker side either.

### What stays as-is (intentionally)
The three `*.Api` projects and the `TemporalEngine.DemoDriver` remain plain ASP.NET / console hosts with fixed-port `UseUrls` fallbacks. Aspire still orchestrates them (injects `Temporal__TargetHost`, `SPORT_URL`/`CATALOG_URL`/`FINANCE_URL`), but the projects don't pull in ServiceDefaults or extra retry helpers — keeps the standalone (non-Aspire) run path clean and dependency-light.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build` clean across the solution
- [x] End-to-end under Aspire: `ASPIRE_ALLOW_UNSECURED_TRANSPORT=true dotnet run --project src/hosts/TemporalEngine.AppHost --launch-profile http` brings up Postgres, Temporal, three workers, three APIs; demo-driver triggers the full flow; all 4 workflows reach Completed in the Temporal UI

## macOS dev caveat
The default `https` launch profile fails on macOS because the .NET dev cert can't be exported from Apple Keychain. Use the `http` profile + `ASPIRE_ALLOW_UNSECURED_TRANSPORT=true` for local dev.

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary

Closes #8074.

Worktree PR/issue overlays raced against branch identity in two ways:

1. **Stale overlay attribution** — When a worktree's branch changed mid-flight on a PR or issue lookup, the late-arriving `pr-detected`, `pr-cleared`, or `issue-detected` event landed on the now-different branch and corrupted the row (wrong PR number, wrong CI rollup, wrong issue title). The existing `issue-not-found` handler had the right pattern (guard on identity, drop silently); the other three didn't.

2. **Reconnecting flicker** — The "Reconnecting…" indicator in the Sidebar rendered synchronously on every `onDisconnected`, so routine sub-400ms port replacements flashed a spinner. Violates the Doherty Threshold rule already applied to `showRefreshSpinner` on the same component.

## Fix

The lookup branch is now captured at candidate-build time in `PullRequestService` (before `await batchCheckLinkedPRs`) and threaded through the event chain: `events.ts` payload types → `PRIntegrationCallbacks` → `WorkspaceService.sendEvent` → `WorkspaceEvent` wire format → renderer handlers. Reading `monitor.branch` at `sendEvent` time would defeat the guard because the branch field already reflects the post-switch state by then — Codex caught this during planning.

Three layers of guard, each addressing a distinct injection vector:

- **Host (`WorkspaceService` callbacks)** — drop the host write when `data.branchName !== monitor.branch`. Without this, `monitor.setPRInfo` + `emitUpdate` would bake stale PR data into the `worktree-update` snapshot and bypass the renderer guard entirely. Caught during /work:review.
- **Renderer overlay events** — `branchesMatch(event.branchName, existing.branch)` guard at the start of `pr-detected`, `pr-cleared`, `issue-detected` handlers. `undefined` on either side allows through (detached HEAD + backward compat with older host code).
- **Renderer `pr-cleared`** — also clears `prCiStatus` so an early-startup window (`monitor.hasInitialStatus` false) can't leave a CI rollup hanging without a PR.

The reconnecting indicator now uses `useDeferredLoading(isReconnecting, UI_DOHERTY_THRESHOLD)` — mirroring the existing `showRefreshSpinner` pattern one line above it.

## Files changed

- `electron/services/events.ts` — `branchName?` added to `sys:pr:detected`, `sys:pr:cleared`, `sys:issue:detected`
- `electron/services/PullRequestService.ts` — snapshot lookup-time branch per worktree before each `await batchCheckLinkedPRs`; thread to `handleWorktreeUpdate`, `handleWorktreeRemove`, `checkForPRs`, and `revalidateResolvedPRs` emits
- `electron/workspace-host/PRIntegrationService.ts` — added `branchName?` to `PRIntegrationCallbacks` signatures; threaded through event subscribers
- `electron/workspace-host/WorkspaceService.ts` — host-side branch guard in `onPRDetected`, `onPRCleared`, `onIssueDetected`; forward `branchName` in `sendEvent`
- `shared/types/workspace-host.ts` — added `branchName?` to wire-format event types
- `src/contexts/WorktreeStoreContext.tsx` — `branchesMatch` helper + guards in three handlers; clear `prCiStatus` in `pr-cleared`
- `src/components/Sidebar/SidebarContent.tsx` — `useDeferredLoading` on `isReconnecting`
- `src/contexts/__tests__/WorktreeStoreContext.prDetected.test.tsx` — 13 new tests
- `src/components/Sidebar/__tests__/SidebarContent.reconnecting.test.ts` — new
- `electron/workspace-host/__tests__/WorkspaceService.prBranchGuard.test.ts` — new

## Test plan

- [x] Targeted vitest (60 tests across 5 files) — pass
- [x] `npm run check` (typecheck + lint + format) — pass; lint ratchet dropped 3 warnings
- [x] `npm run build` — pass
- [ ] Manual: switch worktree branches rapidly during PR detection cycle, confirm no row corruption
- [ ] Manual: trigger a fast workspace-host restart, confirm no "Reconnecting…" flash

author: benediktms
body:
## Summary
Relocates the long-lived file-watcher service from cli's `brain watch`
command into the `brain-daemon` binary. The daemon now owns the
`IndexPipeline`, `BrainWatcher`, `IpcServer`, signal handlers, and the
embed/summarize/optimize tick loops. `brain watch` and `brain daemon
start` are thin RPC clients.

This removes the cli's role as a daemon host and completes the
centralized-writer migration on the cli side. The writer-lock
contention fix lands for default users (no `--remote` flag needed).

## Wire protocol (additive — `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays at 1)
- `Request::Watch{Add,Remove,List}` + `Response::Watch{Added,Removed,List}`
- `WatchSummary { brain_name, brain_id, note_dir, watching }`
- Typed methods `DaemonClient::watch_add` / `watch_remove` / `watch_list`
- 17 roundtrip + wire-format-stability tests
- Handlers paired `#[cfg(feature = "embed")]` / `not(embed)` — wire
  stays unconditional, only daemon-side behavior is feature-gated

## Daemon
- `Supervisor::bootstrap_and_run` ports the entire `run_multi` body
  verbatim (Phase 1-5 shutdown preserved)
- Spawned on a dedicated `std::thread` with its own tokio current-thread
  runtime — mirrors the per-request runtime pattern used by memory
  handlers
- New `--no-watcher` flag for lightweight (brain-mcp) use
- Shutdown coordination: supervisor's Phase 1 calls
  `rpc_shutdown.request()`, flipping the main thread's `AtomicBool`;
  reverse direction handled via `recv()-returns-None ->
  ShutdownReason::ChannelClosed`
- Re-binds the legacy `IpcServer` on `~/.brain/brain.sock` from inside
  the supervisor — same socket path, same lifecycle (retirement gated
  on cross-brain writes landing on the wire)

## CLI
- `cli/src/commands/watch.rs` 1429 LOC → 45 LOC thin RPC client; no
  tokio runtime, no `BrainStores`, no `brain_lib::pipeline`
- `brain daemon start` post-fork child execs the brain-daemon binary
  directly (instead of falling through to the cli's dispatcher)
- Binary path resolution: sibling-of-`current_exe()` first, PATH fallback
- Stripped cli deps: `tracing-appender`, `notify-debouncer-full`,
  `tokio-util` (now only used by the relocated supervisor)
- `--log-filter` / `--log-max-files` / `--log-max-size-mb` /
  `--log-format` clap flags kept for backwards compat but marked
  no-op pending forward-to-brain-daemon work

## Architectural ratchet
- `cli/src/commands/watch.rs` no longer carries any daemon-hosting code
- `brain_daemon` gains an `embed` feature; the watcher module is gated
  behind it; the daemon binary stays usable with `--no-watcher` when
  embed is on, or compiled without embed for a pure RPC dispatcher

## Test plan
- [ ] CI: `cargo check --workspace --all-features` green
- [ ] CI: `cargo check --workspace --no-default-features --tests` green
- [ ] CI: clippy clean (`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`)
- [ ] CI: existing `brain_rpc` round-trip tests pass; 17 new
      wire-format-stability tests for Watch* variants pass
- [ ] Manual: `brain daemon start` → `ps aux | grep brain-daemon` shows
      the running daemon; `brain watch /tmp/foo` returns immediately;
      `ctrl-C` in the cli terminal does NOT kill the daemon;
      `brain daemon stop` triggers Phase 1-5 shutdown and process exits
      within ~15s
- [ ] Manual: `brain daemon start --notes-path /some/path` bails with
      the redirect-to-`brain link` error
- [ ] Manual: touching a `.md` file under a registered brain's notes
      produces an index entry within 2s

## Out of scope (follow-ups)
- Retiring the legacy `brain_lib::ipc::IpcServer` — gated on cross-brain
  writes landing on the wire
- Forwarding `--log-filter` etc. from `brain daemon start` to the
  brain-daemon binary
- The `#[ignore]`'d smoke test at `brain_daemon/tests/watcher_supervisor.rs`
  — needs a mockable Embedder/IpcServer; tracked as a follow-up
- 3 CodeRabbit-deferred quality items filed as follow-up comments on
  the closing migration ticket

author: gfargo
body: The codebase is now ~6500 lines and growing. A regression in one of the helper functions (time parser, CCT math, palette normalization, strobe DMX mapping, etc.) would silently break everything downstream. This PR adds a focused unit-test suite + CI that runs on every PR — the highest-leverage \"stop hurting future me\" investment from the recent gaps brainstorm. ## Suite — 178 tests, sub-second | File | What it covers | |------|----------------| | \`test_time_parser.py\` | \`_parse_time_ms\` + \`_format_time_ms\` — every accepted cue-list timestamp form (\`\"0:32.500\"\`, \`\"32s\"\`, \`\"32500ms\"\`, \`\"1:23:45\"\`, int ms), edge cases, roundtrip | | \`test_cct.py\` | \`_cct_to_rgb\` Tanner Helland algorithm anchors (1800/2700/3200/5600/6500/10000K), monotonicity, clamping. \`_wwa_mix\` proportional blend including amber taper below 2700K | | \`test_strobe.py\` | \`_strobe_dmx_value\` rate → DMX 0..255 mapping, \"off\" forms, suffix parsing (\`\"5Hz\"\`), clamping above 20Hz | | \`test_palette.py\` | \`_normalize_palette_value\` across all six accepted input shapes per group (color name, Kelvin number, Kelvin with K suffix, dict forms, short-key) | | \`test_cue_normalizer.py\` | \`_normalize_cue\` — scene / chase / action cue shapes, missing-field errors, precedence ordering | | \`test_misc_helpers.py\` | Direction + run-order enum normalization, fixture ID coercion, \`_parse_level\` (absolute, percentage, relative) | By design the suite **avoids** Flask routes, the QLC+ WebSocket loop, AI provider calls, XML workspace mutations, and cue list playback — those need integration tests, which are out of scope for this PR. ## Infrastructure - \`control-server/pytest.ini\` — config (testpaths, strict markers) - \`control-server/tests/\` — package with \`conftest.py\` adding the parent dir to \`sys.path\` so \`import app\` works from tests/ - \`control-server/requirements-dev.txt\` — adds \`pytest>=7.4\` on top of runtime requirements ## CI — \`.github/workflows/test.yml\` Runs on push + PR to main: | Job | What it does | |-----|--------------| | **python** | pytest on Python 3.11 + 3.12 matrix + \`ast.parse\` on both servers | | **js** | extract inline \`

author: copilot
body:
Club setup was functionally correct but still placeholder-heavy: league assignments could drift, finances were flat, and reputation/squad context was too shallow to feel like a credible management sim. This change introduces deterministic realism across data, schema, and UI while preserving existing Supabase UUID relations and career flow.

- **League assignment correctness + future-proofing**
  - Added normalization utilities (`normalizeClubName`) and strict domestic validation (`validateLeagueCountry`) in app logic.
  - Added DB-level guardrail: trigger-based validation to prevent clubs being assigned to leagues from a different country.
  - Extended seed pipeline with alias/canonical mapping and auto-correction of mismatched club↔league assignments before upsert.

- **Persistent club realism model (schema + seed)**
  - Expanded `clubs` persistence with:
    - `transfer_budget`, `wage_budget`, `board_confidence`
    - `season_expectation`, `board_expectation`, `fan_expectation`
    - `stadium_name`, `club_colors`, `founded_year`, `tactical_style`, `rival_club_id`, `country`
  - Seed now derives realistic financial tiers from reputation/tier/stature and writes consistent metadata per club.
  - Added deterministic rivalry linking for key derby pairs.

- **Granular reputation system (1–100)**
  - Added `getReputationProfile(reputation)` to derive:
    - star rendering
    - media expectation
    - transfer pull
    - sponsorship power
    - board ambition

- **Club selection immersion (FM-style pre-career context)**
  - Upgraded `/solo/club-select` with:
    - richer club cards (rep + budgets)
    - league-themed styling
    - detailed **Club Overview** panel (finances, expected finish, squad quality, strongest player, weakest area, tactical style, stadium, fan expectations)
    - **Board Introduction** briefing prior to career start

- **Squad quality and career context**
  - Added squad analytics from `players` table:
    - average age/overall
    - attack/midfield/defense ratings
    - depth quality
    - strongest player + weakest area
  - Added board/expectation briefing block in `/solo/game` to carry immersion into career start.

```ts
export function getReputationProfile(reputation: number): ClubReputationProfile {
  const clamped = Math.max(1, Math.min(100, Math.round(reputation)));
  if (clamped >= 95) return { label: "World-class giant", ... };
  if (clamped >= 85) return { label: "Champions League contender", ... };
  if (clamped >= 75) return { label: "Strong top-flight club", ... };
  if (clamped >= 65) return { label: "Mid-table side", ... };
  return { label: "Relegation candidate", ... };
}
```

author: bingran-you
body:
## Closing — no real drift; the "fix" was based on a shallow-clone artifact

### What I found after CI failed

CI's `make sync-check` failed because the regenerated catalog on CI **did not match** what I had committed. After digging in:

- My local working copy of `bingran-you/bingran-you` was a **shallow clone** (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → `true`, 51 commits visible).
- The personal-site generator (`scripts/generate-skills-data.mjs`) uses `git log -1 --format=%cI` on each SKILL.md to derive `updatedAt`. With a shallow history, that returns the *shallow boundary commit* (`73cfb18`, 2026-05-10) instead of the actual last-touching commit.
- After `git fetch --unshallow` (full history = 297 commits), regenerating produces `2026-04-30T22:50:16.000Z` for `cli-creator` — which is **exactly what `origin/main` already has**.

### Conclusion

The catalog on `main` is already correct. Merging this PR would have replaced the correct timestamps with shallow-clone artifacts and broken CI on `main`.

### Actual state of skills (verified)

All three managed submodules are at the tip of their tracked branches (0 commits behind):
- `trusted-external-repos/open-design` @ main
- `trusted-external-repos/marketingskills` @ main
- `trusted-external-repos/gstack` @ main

And the catalog matches what `make sync` produces against full history.

Closing without merge. Branch will be deleted.

author: mjbommar
body:
## Summary

The 0.1.0a10 release shipped the dispatch redirect correctly (PLAN/RESEARCH intent on `ChatAgent` redirected through `_handle_tool_use` so real tools fire), but the typed `PatternMismatch` event was **invisible to anyone outside the agent process** — including the React SPA's run inspector, OTel hook, and live integration tests.

## Root cause

`BaseAgent._detect_pattern_mismatch` called `emitter.emit(PatternMismatch, ...)` and discarded the return value. `EventEmitter.emit` instantiates the event and only pushes to an active `collect_events()` collector — it does NOT yield it from the `_dispatch_streaming` async generator. Unit tests opened a collector so they passed. Production consumers iterate the generator and never saw the event.

How I caught it: ran L2 of the A+ test plan (live ChatAgent + Sonnet + real Federal Register tools) and the test asserted `len(mismatches) == 1`; got `0`. The diagnostic event was just lost. The dispatch redirect was working — confirmed by the 3 real tool calls in the same run — but its observable signal was gone.

## Fix

* `BaseAgent._detect_pattern_mismatch` now returns `(redirect_handler, mismatch_event)` instead of just the handler.
* `BaseAgent._dispatch_streaming` yields the `mismatch_event` before invoking the redirect handler, so the event flows through the same `async for` loop as every other `KaosEvent`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit: 11/11 `tests/unit/test_pattern_mismatch.py` pass (updated to assert events appear in the `events` list, not just a collector — closes the original blind spot).
- [x] Full unit suite: 2531 pass, 5 skipped (graph extras), 5 warnings.
- [x] Live L2 — Sonnet `tests/integration/test_plan_intent_dispatches_with_tools.py`: both tests PASS. Pre-fix `PatternMismatch=0`; post-fix `PatternMismatch=1`, `tools=2`, real FR doc cited (Reg S-P), cost $0.11 (vs. pre-bug $0.005 for fabricated answers).
- [x] Live L2 — Haiku 4.5: new `test_dispatch_extended.py::test_haiku_plan_intent_emits_pattern_mismatch_and_uses_tools` PASS — dispatcher is model-agnostic.
- [x] Live L2 — Negative case: `test_trivial_respond_intent_no_pattern_mismatch_sonnet` PASS — gate is selective (no PatternMismatch on `What is 2+2?`).
- [x] Live L2 — Multi-turn: `test_followup_turn_in_same_session_still_dispatches_correctly` PASS — no per-turn state leak.
- [x] L8 regression net: `tests/integration/test_planning_live.py` + `tests/integration/test_router_live.py` — 20/20 live tests PASS. Wishes #2/#4/#5/#7/#8 from 0.1.0a8/a9 are unbroken.

## Notable side-fix

Relaxed `test_plan_pattern_plan_intent_runs_plan_execute_with_tools`'s `Span(JUDGE, COMPLETE) >= 1` assertion — JUDGE is *conditional* (fires only when the planner needs semantic re-eval on a step that returned `matched=False`). A clean-execution plan against Sonnet + Federal Register tools never triggers it. The test now documents the conditional behaviour.

## What this doesn't cover yet

L3-L7 of the A+ plan (CLI smoke, SPA backend curl, Chrome DevTools MCP end-to-end on the React SPA, multi-model coverage beyond Anthropic, persistence + cost reconciliation) will run after this PR merges and ships as 0.1.0a11 — the SPA backend pin and Chrome MCP runs need to test against the *PyPI-published* version, not local source.

author: simonvelucia-afk
body:
## Summary
This migration addresses a Supabase security alert (`rls_disabled_in_public`) by enabling Row-Level Security (RLS) on four tables that were previously created without RLS protection: `dependents`, `lunch_sessions`, `deletion_requests`, and `lunch_queue`.

## Key Changes
- **dependents**: Added RLS with policies allowing parents to manage their own dependents and admins to see all records (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)
- **lunch_sessions**: Added RLS with policies for anonymous kiosk access (time-limited), authenticated user creation, and admin debugging access
- **deletion_requests**: Added RLS with policies allowing users to view/create their own deletion requests and admins to manage all requests
- **lunch_queue**: Added RLS with permissive policies for anonymous access (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)

## Implementation Details
- All changes are **idempotent**: the migration uses `DO` blocks with existence checks to safely re-run without errors
- Uses `IF EXISTS` checks for tables and `IF NOT EXISTS` checks for policies to handle partial deployments
- Preserves existing application behavior while securing data access
- Includes comprehensive rollback instructions (commented at end of file)
- Sends `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'` to refresh PostgREST schema cache
- All policies are role-based, leveraging the `profiles.role` column for admin checks

author: szsz-online-bot[bot]
body:
## Goal
Fix the two reporting bugs on
[2026-05-17-085355 report](https://coolwasmfiles.z6.web.core.windows.net/app-builds/2026-05-17-085355/tests/output/reports/):
- The test-row table shows only 46 of 107 rows (header summary is
  correct but table body is truncated).
- The snapshot-milestones embedded iframe doesn't load.

## The truncated table
PR #98 added a regression-test description containing
`/wasm/<id>?access_token=...`. `run-all-tests-parallel.sh` injected
that string verbatim into a `<td>` cell. The browser HTML parser
treats `<id>` as an unknown start tag and silently consumes content
until it finds something it recognises — eating every subsequent
table row.

Build header showed "Total: 107 · Passed: 99 · Failed: 8" because
those counters are computed in the bash loop *before* the rendered
HTML is parsed. Only the visual table is truncated; the underlying
data is correct.

## The broken snapshot-milestones embed
`run-all-tests-parallel.sh` embedded `<iframe src="/report/snapshot-milestones/">` —
an absolute path. The local viewer (viewer.szebeni.hu) has a
`/report/*` static route that resolves it; the Azure publish at
`coolwasmfiles.z6.web.core.windows.net` does not. The published
iframe always 404'd, even though `test-and-publish.sh` already
mirrors the rich report to `../snapshot-milestones/` (sibling of
the `reports/` dir).

## Changes
- `wasm/run-all-tests-parallel.sh`:
  - Add `html_escape()` helper (sed-based, escapes & < > " ').
    Apply to slug, title, and description before injecting them
    into the table cells.
  - Iframe src + "Open in new tab" link → `../snapshot-milestones/`
    (works on both local viewer and Azure publish).
- `wasm/run-all-tests.sh`:
  - Defensively tidy the cool-html-substitution test description
    to use `[fileId]` instead of `<id>` and pre-encode `&` as
    `&` — defence in depth even though the escape helper
    handles it now.

## Verification
Locally: pass cell text containing `<id>` through `html_escape()`
returns `<id>`, which renders as the literal "<id>" string.
No more parser swallow.

The fix lands on the next dev push's report (and is also reflected
on the local viewer's `/reports/index.html` immediately after a
deploy).

- [x] AC1: tool 呼び出しが toggle として折り畳まれて表示される (`TestRenderBlocks_AssistantWithToolUses`)
- [x] AC2: toggle を開くと tool 名・入力 JSON・出力本文が code block で見える (json + plain text の code block ペア、Spike #2 検証済)

author: gavingolden
body:
## Why

The `/pr-review` Step 12 audit line is constructed inline by the LLM via prose in `skills/pipeline/pr-review/SKILL.md`, which means the exact wording is enforced only by the model re-reading the spec each run. Drift in the format — a missing parenthetical on `Y = 0`, a different separator, a paraphrased rubric category — silently changes the contract the user relies on to spot pipeline misbehavior. The line is small but high-signal; pinning it deserves a test.

## What

- New `bin/flow-classify-step.ts` Bun helper renders the audit line from `--ran`, `--total`, `--prose-promoted`, and zero-or-more `--reason` flags.
- Sibling `bin/flow-classify-step.test.ts` pins the canonical line, the `Y = 0` branch (omit parenthetical), the `M = 0` branch (`no Test Steps to verify`), reason ordering, and rejection of unknown reasons / impossible counts.
- `skills/pipeline/pr-review/SKILL.md` Step 12 calls the helper instead of constructing the line inline; the format spec stays as documentation.

## Key decisions

- **Renderer, not parser.** The helper takes pre-classified counts via CLI flags rather than parsing the rendered Test Steps section. The LLM in Step 8c / 8c.ii is the only component that can decide which manual-test-rubric category applies per unticked item; once that decision exists, rendering is mechanical and belongs in a helper with a test. A parser would duplicate `flow-gate-decide`'s section parse and would still need the LLM to supply reasons separately.
- **Kebab-case slugs for `--reason`.** The five rubric categories are written as human prose in `manual-test-rubric.md` (`subjective UX`, `production-only`, etc.). The helper accepts kebab-case slugs on the CLI and maps them to the human form in output — CLI flags don't accept spaces ergonomically.
- **Validate reasons strictly.** Unknown reason values exit non-zero rather than passing through. Drift in the category vocabulary is the failure mode this helper exists to prevent.
- **No `--json` output mode in v1.** The only consumer is the structured report's stdout line. Adding `--json` is straightforward later if a structured consumer appears; we don't pre-build for it.
- **Out of scope: classification logic.** `/pr-review` Step 8c still does the per-item runnable / not-runnable / promote decision and tracks counts. This helper is a pure renderer.

## User-facing changes

- New helper on PATH after `flow setup`: `flow-classify-step --ran <N> --total <M> --prose-promoted <X> [--reason <slug>...]` emits the audit line on stdout. Useful as a standalone CLI for anyone hand-editing a PR body's audit line.
- The audit line in `/pr-review`'s structured report is now byte-identical across runs (pinned by a unit test) rather than re-derived by the model each invocation.

author: oaustegard
body:
## Summary

Per the issue's acceptance, `Self` should "just work" as a type
identifier with no grammar change needed — verified. The existing
grammar parses all four target forms cleanly; this PR adds corpus
tests to lock the behavior in, plus highlight rules so editors can
distinguish `self` and `Self` from generic identifiers.

## What's verified

- `fn clone(self) -> Self:` — Self as return type
- `fn __init__(self, *, copy: Self):` — Self with keyword-only marker
- `fn __init__(self):` — bare self
- `fn __init__(self, *, copy: Self, take: Self):` — multiple kw-only Self params

All four parse cleanly against current main (post-#5).

## Highlight rules

```scheme
((identifier) @variable.builtin (#eq? @variable.builtin "self"))
((identifier) @type.builtin (#eq? @type.builtin "Self"))
```

Placed **before** the general naming-convention rules so they take
precedence on these specific identifiers. Without this, `Self` would
match the `@constructor` rule via `#match? "^[A-Z]"`, which is wrong
for the Self type — it's a builtin, not a user-defined constructor.

## Note on fusemojo usage

The fusemojo corpus uses `out self` (Mojo's ownership modifier), not
bare `self`. The corpus tests in this PR use bare `self` because this
branch is against main, which doesn't yet have argument conventions
from PR #17. Once #17 lands, the `out self` form will also parse
cleanly — both #17 and this PR are needed for the full fusemojo
constructor surface.

## Test plan

- [x] `tree-sitter test` 23/23 green (4 new tests pass on current main, no grammar change)
- [x] `script/check-errors.sh` unchanged at 42 (no grammar change in this PR)
- [x] No regression in prior corpus tests
- [x] Highlight rules placed before the catch-all naming-convention rules

## What

Three intertwined changes that together make auto-pushed firefly transactions read like the operator's own manual entries.

### 1. Tier-3 prompt enrichment (the headline change)

- **TIME CONTEXT block** — staged.txn_timestamp converted to IST, bucketed into breakfast / lunch / dinner / etc. + weekday-vs-weekend. The LLM can now call a 21:30 restaurant txn "Dinner" without guessing.
- **STYLE SAMPLES block** — top 10 most-recent descriptions the operator has previously written for the SAME merchant. Distinct from the existing HISTORICAL EXAMPLES block (which is for ID evidence). System prompt explicitly tells the model to MIRROR these.
- **Placeholder licence** — model is told to emit \`___\` (three underscores) for missing specifics. \`"Dinner with ___"\` over \`"Mezzaluna dinner"\`.

### 2. Description preservation across structural-confidence rejection

When the LLM returns ok=false (low confidence on ids or missing structural fields), we now plumb its \`description_suggestion\` onto the Tier-1/Tier-2 fallback Decision. Was losing titles for ~160 Tier-1/2 rows previously.

### 3. Narration → notes, merchant → description fallback

- \`push.go\`: firefly's notes field now carries raw fold narration unconditionally (was \`""\`). Bank ground-truth alongside the title.
- \`push.go\`: description fallback chain extended to \`confirmed → proposed → merchant_extracted → narration\`. Tier-1/2 rows get a readable title ("zomato") rather than duplicating the narration.

- \`TestMealContext_Buckets\` — every IST bucket + weekend/weekday distinction

author: copilot
body:
Google sign-in/sign-up was failing due to OAuth redirect mismatches and inconsistent redirect construction across auth flows. This change standardizes redirect generation and ensures Supabase auth continues to rely on environment configuration.

- **Problem summary**
  - Google OAuth callbacks were sensitive to runtime origin differences, causing redirect URL mismatches.
  - Redirect targets were duplicated in multiple components, making behavior drift-prone.

- **Auth configuration updates**
  - Kept Supabase client initialization strictly env-driven via:
    - `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`
    - `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
  - Added optional `VITE_AUTH_REDIRECT_URL` support for explicit callback domains (useful when app origin differs from OAuth-allowed redirect origin).

- **OAuth redirect centralization**
  - Added `getAuthRedirectTo()` in `src/lib/supabaseClient.js`.
  - Default behavior: `${window.location.origin}/auth/callback`.
  - Override behavior: use `VITE_AUTH_REDIRECT_URL` when set.

- **Auth flow integration**
  - Updated Google OAuth calls in:
    - `src/components/Auth/SignInPage.jsx`
    - `src/components/Auth/SignUpPage.jsx`
  - Updated email signup redirect in `SignUpPage.jsx` to use the same shared redirect helper.

- **Developer env docs**
  - Extended `.env.example` with:
    - `VITE_AUTH_REDIRECT_URL=https://your-domain.com/auth/callback`

```js
export const getAuthRedirectTo = () => {
  const configuredRedirectUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_REDIRECT_URL;
  if (configuredRedirectUrl) return configuredRedirectUrl;
  return `${window.location.origin}/auth/callback`;
};
```

author: quantumexplorer
body:
## Why

`ProvableCountTree` and `ProvableCountSumTree` bind their aggregate count into every node hash via `node_hash_with_count`. That committed count IS the answer to an `AggregateCountOnRange` query.

Today, `NonCounted` and `NotCountedOrSummed` children are accepted in those parents (via `is_count_bearing` / `is_count_and_sum_bearing`). They contribute `own_count = 0`, so the cryptographically-committed count silently disagrees with the actual number of stored elements — confusing for callers, and a footgun for proof-driven readers who reasonably assume "if I iterate this range I'll get the same number the proof returned."

This PR makes that shape impossible going forward, while leaving the wrappers fully usable in the non-provable count-bearing parents where the count is plain bookkeeping rather than a cryptographic commitment.

## Rule

| Wrapper | Allowed parent(s) | Newly rejected parent(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `NonCounted` | `CountTree`, `CountSumTree` | `ProvableCountTree`, `ProvableCountSumTree` |
| `NotCountedOrSummed` | `CountSumTree` | `ProvableCountSumTree` |
| `NotSummed` | unchanged (uses `is_sum_bearing`) | — |

`is_count_bearing` and `is_count_and_sum_bearing` are unchanged — they still answer the structural question "does this tree track count/sum?" for the aggregate logic that legitimately needs that. The new wrapper-acceptance rule lives in two new dedicated predicates:

```rust
TreeType::accepts_non_counted_children()          // CountTree | CountSumTree

author: hahabsw
body:
## Summary

Two NexPress projects on the same machine both defaulted to host port 5433 for their compose container. The second \`docker compose up -d db\` would fail to bind, and the failure mode read like a transient docker issue rather than a port collision. From the queued setup-wizard follow-ups — last open item that didn't fit into #795.

Three coordinated changes so operators never have to think about ports when they're running more than one scaffold:

## What lands

### 1. \`create-nexpress\` derives a per-project host port

\`dbPortFromProject(projectName)\` hashes the project name into the 5433–6432 range (1000 buckets, same Java-style \`* 31\` mixing the rest of the CLI uses). Deterministic — same project always gets the same port.

The port gets written into the scaffold's \`.env\` as both:
- \`NEXPRESS_DB_PORT=N\` — read by the compose file's \`\${NEXPRESS_DB_PORT:-5433}\` interpolation
- The \`:N\` segment of \`DATABASE_URL\` — read by the app

So compose and the app land on the same port without operator intervention.

### 2. Setup wizard pre-fills the form from existing \`.env\`

Without this, the wizard's hardcoded \`5433\` default would clobber the scaffolder's derived port the first time the operator submitted the form. \`getFormDefaults\` reads \`.env\` and threads parsed values through:
- \`DATABASE_URL\` → host, port, db name, full URL
- \`NEXPRESS_DB_PORT\` (wins over URL port when set)
- \`TEST_DATABASE_URL\` — when absent, derived from the parsed main URL so it doesn't fall back to \`5433\` while the main URL points elsewhere

\`renderHtml\` becomes parameter-driven; the route handler awaits \`getFormDefaults()\` before rendering.

### 3. \`saveEnv\` mirrors the port back

When the wizard's submitted \`databaseUrl\` points at a non-default port, \`saveEnv\` adds a \`NEXPRESS_DB_PORT=N\` line so compose stays in sync after the wizard rewrites \`.env\`. Default 5433 case skips the line — keeps single-project \`.env\` files visually clean and behavior identical to before.

## Tests

- \`utils.test.ts\` — new file. Covers \`dbPortFromProject\` range (\`[5433, 6432]\`), determinism, distinct outputs for distinct names, plus existing \`formatProjectName\` / \`generateSecret\` coverage that didn't exist before.
- \`templates.test.ts\` — extended \`baseConfig\` with a pinned \`dbPort: 5500\` and added a test that both \`.env\` and \`.env.example\` carry \`NEXPRESS_DB_PORT=5500\` and a \`DATABASE_URL\` whose port matches.

## Backward compat

- Existing scaffolds (pre-this-PR): \`.env\` has no \`NEXPRESS_DB_PORT\` line. Wizard's \`getFormDefaults\` parses \`DATABASE_URL\`'s port (5433 for most) and pre-fills with that. \`saveEnv\` doesn't write \`NEXPRESS_DB_PORT\` when the value is 5433, so the rewritten \`.env\` matches the previous shape. No visible change.
- Setup wizard's HTML form looks the same; the values inside the inputs differ.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm typecheck\` clean (turbo 58/58)
- [x] \`pnpm build\` clean (turbo 31/31)
- [x] \`pnpm test\` — all green
- [ ] Manual smoke: \`pnpm create nexpress site-a\`, \`pnpm create nexpress site-b\` in adjacent dirs → \`docker compose up -d db\` in both succeeds (different ports bound)
- [ ] Manual smoke: \`pnpm setup\` in site-a, submit with defaults → \`.env\` keeps the derived port (not overwritten with 5433)

author: texascoding
body:
## Summary

All 5 currently-open Dependabot PRs (#115, #116, #117, #118, #119) have the same single failing check: `claude-review`. Tests + drift-check pass on every one.

**Root cause:** GitHub does not expose repo secrets — including `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` — to workflow runs triggered by Dependabot-authored PRs. This is a deliberate security default (a malicious dependency could otherwise exfiltrate credentials via a crafted PR). The action lands in the runner with empty credentials and exits 1 before doing anything useful.

Evidence from the log on PR #115's run ([25990801467](https://github.com/TexasCoding/kalshi-python-sdk/actions/runs/25990801467)):

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:
```

**Fix:** add `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'` at the job level. Skips the run entirely rather than firing and failing. Dep-bump diffs are low-signal for AI review anyway (version range changes, not behavior).

Alternative considered: configure Dependabot secrets (a separate secret store GitHub exposes to dependabot-triggered runs). Rejected — extra complexity for an action that doesn't add review value on version bumps.

After this merges, the 5 open Dependabot PRs will need a re-trigger (close/reopen, or push a no-op) for the skip to take effect on a fresh run.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML parses cleanly
- [ ] After merge, retrigger one Dependabot PR and confirm `claude-review` is skipped (not failed)

## Summary

Merges the entire Yandex Games adaptation into `main`. This consolidates ~16 stacked feature branches that were developed incrementally but never merged, resulting in repeated work across sessions. After this merge, `main` contains the full Yandex Games build alongside the existing Telegram Mini App build.

### What's included

**Platform layer** (`src/yandex/`):
- Yandex Games SDK init, cloud save (`player.setData/getData/setStats`), rewarded video ads
- Dual entry point: `index.yandex.html` + `src/main.yandex.ts` (Telegram entry untouched)
- Vite resolve aliases swap `WebSocketClient` for a Yandex-flavoured subclass; `GameSync`/`DiceSync` use the real implementations

**Server auth & DB** (`server/`):
- `validateYandexSignature` (HMAC-SHA256) with `parseYandexPlayerUnsafe` dev fallback
- `findOrCreateYandexUser` upsert by `yandex_id`
- DB migration: adds `users.yandex_id`, `users.platform`, `lobbies.no_bet`, `lobbies.bet_amount`
- Full matchmaking service (queue, timeout, ready confirmation, bet selection)
- Stats service with cloud-save pip sync

**Multiplayer fixes** (shared — affects both Telegram and Yandex):
- Reconnect mid-game: `handleLeaveLobby` differentiates in-game disconnect (30s reconnect window) vs pre-game permanent leave
- `lobby.leaveLobby` returns structured `LeaveLobbyResult`; force-closes lobby when < 2 players remain during active game
- Active throw tracking for reconnect replay (`activeThrows` map in handlers)
- `handleRestartGame` rejects when < 2 players (server-side guard)
- Dice selection: per-instance `EdgesGeometry` outline mesh instead of mutating shared materials
- Dice settle: requires 4 consecutive sub-threshold checks (~400ms) before reading `getTopFace()`
- Mobile/iOS audio unlock: synchronous context creation inside gesture, broader gesture coverage, `interrupted` state handling

**Yandex-only UI** (`src/yandex/`):
- `SoloUI`, `SoloShop`, `SoloInventory` (design keys, custom dice)
- `MultiplayerLobbyUI` (create/join by 8-char code, matchmaking, game mode picker)
- `MultiplayerReconnectDialog`, `MultiplayerLobbyGuard`, `ConnectionErrorBanner`
- Ad-rewarded boosts, ReactionWheel (chat/emoji), settings i18n

**i18n**: ~90 new keys each for `en` and `ru`.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

This is a high-risk merge — 55 files, ~9000 insertions, no CI. Please verify carefully:

- [ ] **DB migration safety**: Review `server/src/db/migrate-yandex.ts`. Statements use `IF NOT EXISTS` / `DO $$ ... pg_constraint`, but they drop `NOT NULL` on `users.telegram_id` and add columns to `users` and `lobbies`. **Run against a staging DB copy first.**
- [ ] **Auth security**: `server/src/services/auth.ts` has a `parseYandexPlayerUnsafe` dev fallback that accepts unsigned data when `YANDEX_APP_SECRET` is empty. Confirm the secret is set on the production server before deploying, otherwise any client can impersonate any player.
- [ ] **Telegram build regression**: Shared files (`Game.ts`, `Dice.ts`, `handlers.ts`, `GameSync.ts`, `DiceSync.ts`, `WebSocketClient.ts`, `AudioManager.ts`, `lobby.ts`) were modified. Run `npm run build` (Telegram) and verify the Telegram Mini App still works end-to-end: lobby creation, multiplayer game, dice editor, shop.
- [ ] **Reconnect/disconnect flow**: Start a 2-player match → one player leaves mid-game → other player should see disconnect notification → leaving player reloads → reconnect dialog should appear within 30s. Also test: leaving *before* game start should permanently remove the player (no reconnect).
- [ ] **Dice selection isolation**: In Palmo's Dice reroll phase, select 1–2 dice. On the other player's screen, only the selected dice should show a gold outline — not all five. Verify no residual glow after deselection or new turn.

### Notes

- Pre-existing `tsc --noEmit` errors (82 in client code) are unchanged; no new errors introduced.
- `dist/` and `server/dist/` build artifacts appear tracked in the repo. These are included as-is from the feature branches.
- The `wsClient` stub's import path (`../../multiplayer/WebSocketClient`) bypasses the Vite alias intentionally to subclass the real client. Do not "simplify" this path.
- Boost cooldowns are client-side only (localStorage). A determined player can reset them — acceptable for a solo/casual build.
- `.gitignore` is added by this PR (was missing from the repo previously).

author: sanity
body:
## Problem

Ivvor reported on Matrix (2026-05-17):

> First attempt to create and share private room failed at sync stage.
> Invites shared using old link method. Two invitees processed invite and
> room opened, but no messages shown. Invitees could see each others
> nicknames, but not nickname of room owner. Only room owner can send
> messages, but they don't show up, even as encrypted, to other members.
> According to room info, owner is on secret #3. The other members are
> on secret #0.

The smoking gun is in `common/src/room_state/message.rs`:
`MessagesV1::apply_delta` enforced two checks that, together, paralysed
the room as soon as the owner's local `current_version` got ahead of any
invitee's.

1. **Strict version mismatch**. Any private message encrypted at v_new
   arriving while the invitee was still at v_old caused `apply_delta` to
   return `Err`. The composable macro short-circuited via `?` and dropped
   the ENTIRE `ChatRoomStateV1Delta` — including the message itself,
   membership updates, and any in-band secrets-delta in the same payload.
   The invitee's UI therefore never even saw the encrypted message, and
   back-fill from a peer later was impossible (nothing to back-fill).

2. **Complete-distribution gate**. `has_complete_distribution(members)`
   had to be true for the current version. A single member missing a
   blob froze the entire room for messages with no recovery path unless
   that member came online and the owner re-issued their blob.

Compounding this, `RoomSecretsV1::apply_delta` mutated `self.versions`
before running later checks. If any later check failed, the
half-mutated state survived as the new baseline and broke CRDT
idempotence: re-applying the same failing delta would now succeed
because the version was already pushed, but `current_version` /
`encrypted_secrets` / pruning never ran.

## Approach

Three minimal changes, all in `common/`:

1. **Relax `MessagesV1::apply_delta` (message.rs)**: accept any
   `secret_version` that has a corresponding owner-signed record in
   `parent_state.secrets.versions`, instead of requiring exact match to
   `current_version`. A message at a fabricated version (no signed
   record) is still rejected as defense in depth. Author safety is
   already enforced by `MessagesV1::verify`'s member-or-owner signature
   check, and `ChatRoomStateV1::post_apply_cleanup` purges DMs from
   banned authors.

2. **Remove the `has_complete_distribution` gate from
   `MessagesV1::apply_delta`**. A single member's missing blob no longer
   freezes the room for everyone.

3. **Make `RoomSecretsV1::apply_delta` transactional (secret.rs)**:
   stage all changes on a `working` clone of `self`, then commit
   (`*self = working`) only if every check passes. The composable
   `apply_delta` is now all-or-nothing for the secrets sub-state.

Also: gate the wasm32-only `behavior` binding in `conversation.rs` so
the file is clippy-clean on native (pre-existing unused-variable
warning, unrelated to Bug #3 but blocks `cargo make clippy`).

## Migration

Adds `legacy_delegates.toml` entry V20 capturing the pre-change chat
delegate key:

- `code_hash =
  05a96a22b12f548d51a9d785c374790f6dcb22986e0d98e9f0dc023ffbaa4ca0`
- `delegate_key =
  49b626c43a0b0bf9a8506a5266c690afdebc1dc6ce8a7d6d9397b8b1f1b21a4d`

`cargo make check-migration` passes. Users' room data migrates to the
new delegate key on next load.

## Testing

Four new regression tests in `common/tests/private_room_test.rs`:

- `message_at_older_or_newer_known_secret_version_is_accepted`:
  invitee at `current_version=0` with v0+v1 signed records accepts a
  message at v1 (Ivvor's exact repro). Defense in depth: a message at
  v99 (no signed record) is still rejected.
- `single_member_missing_blob_does_not_freeze_room`: Alice/Bob
  members, Bob missing v1 blob — Alice's v1 message is still accepted.
- `secrets_apply_delta_is_transactional_on_failure`: a bad delta
  leaves `RoomSecretsV1` byte-identical to its pre-call state. Pre-fix
  this leaks the failed `versions.push`.
- `delta_with_rotation_plus_message_at_new_version_applies_atomically`:
  combined rotation+message delta applies cleanly (regression guard for
  the happy path the composable macro ordering enables).

Verified each test fails on `1d150125` (PR #268 merge, current main)
without the fix and passes with it. All 251 river-core tests, the
`migration_test`, and the full `cargo make test` suite pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p river-core` (251 tests pass)
- [x] `cargo test -p river-core --test migration_test` (4 pass)
- [x] `cargo make test` (full workspace)
- [x] `cargo make check-migration`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p river-core -p room-contract -p chat-delegate --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo check -p river-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features no-sync`
- [x] Each new test verified failing without fix, passing with fix

## Two-PR plan

This is part 1 of 2 for Bug #3.

**PR B** (will follow after this merges):
- UI back-fill path so previously-rejected messages re-sync after the
  contract validation is relaxed (the `get_response.rs` PUT changes).
- `chat-delegate` prune-fix per freenet/river#110.

Filing PR B as a follow-up because it touches different files (UI +
delegate) and benefits from being reviewed separately once the
contract-validation change has landed and migration is in place.

author: f0rrealtho
body:
### Which issue does this PR close?
Closes #253 

### Rationale for this change
The current `HybridCSR_COO::impl_removeVertex` implementation eagerly rewrites
the entire COO buffer, CSR arrays, and vertex index map on every vertex removal.
Each `std::vector::erase()` inside a loop shifts all subsequent elements,
resulting in **O(E²) worst-case** time complexity. The `vertex_to_index` hashmap
is also fully cleared and rebuilt from scratch, causing unnecessary rehashing.

### What changes are included in this PR?
Implemented a **tombstone-based lazy deletion** strategy:

- Added `_tombstoned` set (`std::unordered_set<size_t>`) to track logically
  deleted vertex indices.
- `impl_removeVertex()` is now **O(1)** — it simply inserts the index into
  `_tombstoned` and erases from `vertex_to_index`. No arrays are touched.
- Added `compactTombstones()` private method that performs the deferred cleanup:
  builds an index remap, filters dead edges from COO/CSR, and compacts
  `vertex_order` — all in a single pass.
- `buildStructures()` and `incrementalUpdate()` call `compactTombstones()`
  before proceeding, ensuring stale entries are cleaned up lazily.
- `populateFromAdjList()`, `impl_clearVertices()`, and `exc()` updated for
  tombstone awareness.

### Are these changes tested?
- [x] Yes — all 40/40 existing unit and integration tests pass locally.

### Are there any user-facing changes?
- [x] No — the public API is unchanged. This is a purely internal optimization.

## Summary

PR-A (#58) の上に、パスキー専用ログインモード本体を実装。これで v3.11.0 として完成。

セキュリティを最大化したいユーザーが「パスワードログインを完全に無効化」できるようにし、紛失時のリカバリコード救済をオフライン保管推奨で提供。リカバリログイン後は「**パスキー再登録 + リカバリコード再生成**」を完了するまで他操作をブロックする強制復旧フローを実装。

### 新エンドポイント

- `POST /settings/passkeys/passkey-only/enable` — 前提（パスキー >=1 + 有効リカバリコード）を満たせば有効化
- `POST /settings/passkeys/passkey-only/disable` — パスワード再認証で解除
- `GET/POST /recovery` — リカバリコードでログイン。5/分レートリミット、列挙対策

- リカバリログイン成功時は `consume_recovery_code()` + `login_user(remember=False)` + `session["pending_recovery_action"]=True`
- `before_request` フック `pending_recovery_gate`: pending 中は許可エンドポイント以外を `/settings/passkeys` へ 302
- `maybe_clear_pending_recovery()` ヘルパ: パスキー >=1 + 有効リカバリ生成済みで自動クリア

### 削除ガード

body: ## Why Today's pipeline emits visibility through `progress()` calls coupled directly to console output. That makes UI iteration expensive — every dashboard tweak requires a fresh `$3–8`, 3–6 minute run — and forces a single output format on all consumers (TTY users, CI logs, post-hoc inspection). The spec at `specs/feat-tui-event-decoupling.md` proposes an event bus as the single source of truth, with thin TUI renderers and a developer replay tool that makes UI iteration cheap. ## What - An in-process event bus replaces direct `progress()` calls across every stage (discovery, coordinator, working groups, cross-pollination, forum, synthesizer, API queue). - Three TUIs attach to the bus: `log` (line-oriented, default for non-TTY), `debug` (raw JSON envelopes per line), and `silent` (no-attach). - An always-on event recorder appends each envelope to `~/.msv/ideas//events.jsonl` for later replay. Opt-out via `MSV_NO_RECORD=1`. - An ink-based dashboard becomes the auto-default for TTY users, with stage rows, working-group cells (pair members + per-substage progress), budget header, recent-events tail, and a cross-pollination panel. - `node tools/replay.js ` reads the recorded `events.jsonl` and replays through a fresh bus into the same TUIs. Realtime playback by default; `--follow` tails an in-progress file for co-watch in a second terminal; replay mode adds an interactive scrubber footer with two progress bars (time + event-index) and arrow-key bindings (±1s, ±10s, ±1 event); backward seeks reset and refold the reducer state. ## Testing ### Live run, dashboard TUI - [x] `msv run ` on a TTY shows the dashboard with stage rows, working-group cells, and budget header - [x] Working-group cells advance through substages (ideation → adversarial → alignment → researcher → observation → debate) - [ ] Cross-pollination panel shows pair members and reactions as they happen - [x] Pressing `q` exits cleanly; the terminal prompt returns - [x] On completion, the dashboard renders the final state for ~2s then unmounts ### Live run, non-TTY - [ ] `msv run > run.log 2>&1` produces line-oriented output with `[level] [stage]` prefixes - [ ] `grep '\[t_001\]' run.log` returns a per-territory log ### Live run, debug TUI - [ ] `msv run --tui=debug 2>&1 | jq 'select(.name | startswith(\"wg.researcher\"))'` shows researcher events with full payloads - [ ] Every emitted line is valid JSON ### Replay, dashboard mode - [x] `node tools/replay.js ` mounts the dashboard and begins realtime playback - [x] The two-bar progress region updates as events emit - [x] At the very last event both bars are visually full and both labels show `(100%)` - [x] At the first event both bars are empty and both labels show `( 0%)` - [x] `space` pauses; pressing it again resumes from the current cursor - [x] `→` advances 1 second of event-time; `Shift+→` advances 10 seconds; `Alt+→` advances one event - [ ] `←` / `Shift+←` / `Alt+←` scrub backward; the dashboard state refolds correctly to the new position - [x] `q` exits ### Replay, log mode with scrubber - [ ] `node tools/replay.js --tui=log` shows formatted log lines as scrollback with a pinned scrubber footer - [ ] Forward seeks (`→`, `Shift+→`, `Alt+→`) emit subsequent lines faster - [ ] `space` pauses and resumes - [ ] Pressing `←` is a no-op (footer hint shows the forward variants only) - [ ] `q` exits ### Replay, follow mode (co-watch) - [ ] Terminal A: `msv run ` is in flight - [ ] Terminal B: `node tools/replay.js --follow` shows the dashboard reflecting terminal A's progress - [ ] When terminal A's run completes, terminal B exits cleanly after ~2 seconds ### Missing idea - [ ] `node tools/replay.js bogus-id` exits with status 1 and stderr mentions `events.jsonl` and the id ### Replay from archive - [ ] After `msv archive `, `node tools/replay.js ` still resolves the events file from `~/.msv/archive//` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: rew1l
body:
## Summary

- Adds the context-engineered story file for **Story 5.7 — Discard a Battle**, the final story of Epic 5 (Battle Management) and the terminal-*abandon* twin of 5.6's terminal-*success* conclude.
- Flips `5-7-discard-a-battle` from `backlog` → `ready-for-dev` in `sprint-status.yaml` (epic-5 already `in-progress`).

## What's in the story

`DELETE /battles/:id` **soft-delete** (`status → 'discarded'`), a `discard` mutation on `useBattleActions`, and a destructive Discard button gated by the **pre-existing cross-platform `ConfirmDialog`** (UX-DR13). AC4's realtime banner-removal is free via 5.4's already-allowlisted `battle_discarded` seam — one `publisher.publish` call.

## Reviewer notes

The story is deliberately exhaustive (it's the only artifact the dev agent gets). Key guardrails baked in:

- **⛔ Hard prerequisite:** 5.1/5.3/5.4 (and 5.6) are documented but **not yet implemented in code** — verified on this branch. HALT-if-blocked instruction included.
- **Soft delete, not hard delete** — Epic 6 history needs the record; `$set status` only, no `deleteOne`.
- **No `discardedAt` / no `result` write** — schema has neither; explicit anti-pattern callout.
- **ConfirmDialog, not `Alert.alert`** — the iOS/Android-only trap that breaks the web release-parity gate.
- **Discard is NOT dirty-gated** (unlike 5.6's Conclude) — locked with rationale.
- 5.6↔5.7 merge-touch coordination on `useBattleActions.ts` + `(battle)/index.tsx` documented for either merge order.

All three open decisions (response shape, ConfirmDialog copy, no dirty-gate) were **confirmed by Ivan (2026-05-17)** — the saved-questions section is now a confirmed decision log with zero remaining ambiguity.

This PR is **docs/process only** — no application code changes.

## Summary
- add a diagnostic-only selected K JSON precision frontier under the f64 probability-history effect
- extract the raw reference sidecar decimal for the selected post-RoPE K value and compare parsed f32 bits against the captured value and F16 midpoint
- keep the next action pointed at reference tensor capture/storage precision when JSON decimal text preserves the midpoint capture

Regenerated `target/a770-diagnostic/bitnet-reference-layer-trace-compare-f64-selected-k-json-precision-frontier.json` reports:

```text
classification = f64_selected_k_json_decimal_preserves_midpoint_capture
record_name = kcur_history_kv_head1_ref_layout-0
first_value_index = 722

author: paul-hammant
body:
## Summary

Two surprises noticed while porting `mquickjs_build.c` — neither needed a new language feature, but one was a real latent codegen bug worth fixing on its own.

- **`switch` fallthrough (the real bug):** parser had `switch`/`case`/`default` wired up since the language's first weeks, but codegen emitted the C `switch` with NO `break;` at the end of each case. Any switch whose arms didn't all `return` fell through to `default` for every input. Fix: `codegen_stmt.c` auto-inserts `break;` at the tail of each case unless the last statement is itself a control-flow exit (`return`/`break`/`continue`). No existing `.ae` test or stdlib file used `switch` — there were no callers to update.
- **C-style `for` loops (just a tested form):** the parser already accepted `for (init; cond; step) body` (`parse_for_loop`) but it was untested end-to-end. `test_for_loop_c_style.ae` now pins: typed init, inferred init, pointer-stride step. The empty-step form `for (init; cond;) { body }` is known-bad (parser pulls the next body statement into the step slot); explicitly noted in the test's preamble as out-of-scope, tracked separately.

Background: I was about to ask for `switch` and C-style `for` as new Aether features for the mquickjs port. Audit revealed both already existed at the parser level — `for` worked end-to-end (just untested), `switch` had a footgun. This PR fixes the footgun and pins the working form.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/regression/test_switch_no_fallthrough.ae` — covers assignment-style multi-arm switch (the form that was silently broken) and the early-return form (which already worked).
- [x] `tests/regression/test_for_loop_c_style.ae` — typed init, inferred init, pointer-stride step.
- [x] `make ci` — 531 of 534 `.ae` tests pass; the 3 failures are pre-existing HTTP shell-test flakes (`http_h2_concurrent_dispatch`, `http_reverse_proxy_pool_extra`, `http_server_h2` — all `grep READY + sleep 0.3` port-readiness races).
- [x] `make -C mquickjs test` — all 6 mquickjs tests still pass.
- [x] No `.ae` file in `std/` or `tests/regression/` uses `switch`, so the codegen change has no risk of regressing existing callers.

author: chloe463
body:
## Summary

- Add `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, and `XDG_STATE_HOME` to `zsh/.zshenv`
- Use `${VAR:-default}` form so existing values are respected
- `ZDOTDIR` is intentionally **not** set in this PR — zsh continues reading from `$HOME`

## Why

Part of the XDG Base Directory migration (#138). Establishing these variables first is a safe, non-breaking prerequisite that makes them available to subsequent phases without changing any shell startup behavior.

## Changes

- `zsh/.zshenv`: prepend XDG variable exports before the existing Prezto runcom source

## Test Plan

- [x] `zsh -i -c 'echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME'` → `/Users/tsuyoshi/.config`

## §1 Scope

Doc-only doctrine truth-up. CLAUDE.md auto-loads to every agent every session; it had drifted from code reality in ways that would cause a future agent to **break working production behavior**. Zero runtime logic changed.

- **CLAUDE.md** — kids/music audio doctrine (6 stale locations), false "ONLY createClient()" claim, 3 stale facts, Mission #2 minimal annotation
