`git diff --stat`: 2 `.md` content + 2 `.md` renames (100%) + 1 `.ts` JSDoc comment. `5 files changed, 73 insertions(+), 76 deletions(-)`.

## §2 Root cause

Doctrine drift from two events:
1. **`d2951ddd` (2026-04-21, "migrate kids + music to Supabase — Google Play 200 MB fix")** reversed the "kids/music stays local" invariant. CLAUDE.md still asserted the *opposite* in 6 places (incl. a "P0" and a "Hard invariant"), and `useAudioUrl.test.ts` already asserts the new behavior (`describe('useAudioUrl — kids and music go through Supabase')`). **Risk averted:** an agent reading "kids/* never reaches Supabase P0", seeing kids audio resolve via Supabase, treating it as a P0 regression, and re-localizing → re-bloating the bundle past Google Play's 200 MB base-module limit → broken ship.
2. **Post-#533 line drift.** `renderer-schema-contract.md` shipped in #533 with code basis `29bc2b75`; #533's own D1–D4 fix (squash `97623db8`) plus #530/#532/#534/#535/#536 shifted every per-field line ref by +7..+11. §9 still presented D1–D4 as an open "Phase 2 fix" though they shipped in the *same* PR.

**CLAUDE.md** (10 line edits): pipeline steps 2–3, "Hard invariant", Mercy Speak kids path, "Kids audio stays local P0", "Bundled adult-room audio removed", `.env.local`, `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`, the createClient bullet, and a **minimal** Mission #2 annotation (principle verbatim + Architecture pointer — the non-negotiable stands; only the delivery mechanism changed).

**supabaseClient.ts**: `ONLY ONE createClient()` → `ONLY browser/client createClient()` + the intentional SSR service-role exception (`src/server/host/renderer.ts:39`, server-only, never bundled). Comment-only.

**renderer-schema-contract.md**: header basis `29bc2b75`→`b3e7d590`, 878/183→889/184 lines; every §2 per-field line ref remapped (verified against HEAD); §4/§5/§6/§7/Appendix inline refs corrected; §9 rewritten from "recommended Phase 2 fix" → **CLOSED, applied in #533 (squash `97623db8`)**, retained as the historical drift record. **Reports archived**: `cc7-ci-diagnosis.md`, `cc7-validate-rooms-errors.md` → `reports/archive/`. The brief also listed `a9-route-recovery-diagnosis.md`, `RECON-korean-audit.md`, `french-example-en-audit-2026-05-16.md` — these **never existed in tracked git history** (untracked scratch in the recon worktree only), so nothing to move; not invented. `sw-stale-html-diagnosis-2026-05-14.md` kept (CLAUDE.md still references it, current).

## §6 Risk surface

**Zero runtime impact.** The only `.ts` change is inside a `/* */` JSDoc block — byte-identical compiled output, no AST/lint effect, not an eslint-disable directive (diff confirmed). All other changes are markdown; recon confirmed **no `.yml`/`.ts`/`.js`/`.json`/`.sh` references any changed doc path** (the string "CLAUDE.md" appears only in unrelated prose comments about non-negotiables #1/#5). author: sethdford
body:
## Summary

Four atomic commits, each independently verifiable, building from test-pinning toward real user-facing capability:

1. [`413ab58b`](https://github.com/sethdford/h-uman/commit/413ab58b) **refactor(channels,daemon)** — Extract `hu_imessage_build_inline_reply_hint_for_batch` from `src/daemon.c:8817`. The daemon's inbound-iMessage inline-reply context-builder was 28 lines of inline logic untestable without driving the full epoll loop. Now a pure helper callable from tests via `hu_imessage_test_set_guid_lookup`. Also adds a 2026-05-17 status section to the Tier-B private-API feasibility deferral doc.
2. [`1429a073`](https://github.com/sethdford/h-uman/commit/1429a073) **refactor(context,daemon)** — Extract `hu_leave_on_read_decide(is_group, already_in_period, helper_says)` pure predicate from the daemon's `#ifndef HU_IS_TEST` state machine. Three booleans in, `hu_leave_on_read_decision_t` enum out (RESPOND / ALREADY_IN_PERIOD / TRIGGER_NEW). Daemon retains stateful ring-buffer work; the decision policy is now unit-testable.
3. [`6de91e2c`](https://github.com/sethdford/h-uman/commit/6de91e2c) **fix(persona)** — `hu_contact_profile_t.affect_mirror_ceiling` was declared on the struct and used by `hu_affect_mirror_ceiling()` but never parsed from JSON. Tests passed because they set the field directly in C, bypassing the disk-to-runtime path. Disk-loaded personas saw `0` regardless of config. Adds the parser + a JSON roundtrip test + a clamp test.
4. [`3e1f5c33`](https://github.com/sethdford/h-uman/commit/3e1f5c33) **feat(persona,daemon)** — Per-contact `leave_on_read_pct` override. Mirrors the layered-lookup shape of `hu_affect_mirror_ceiling`: contact override > overlay > 0 default. Adds field to `hu_contact_profile_t`, the `hu_leave_on_read_pct_effective(contact, overlay)` helper, JSON parsing in both nested+top-level shapes, and daemon wire-up so e.g. "30% leave-on-read with friends, 5% with family" is now expressible. Unblocks future per-axis overrides (formality, emoji_usage, avg_length) using the same recipe.

**Net: +21 tests, ~460 LOC, four atomic commits.** Each verified with the project's quality gate (full `human_tests` suite under ASan dev preset). No regressions; last commit ran `10,454/10,454 passed`, exit 0, no ASan trips.

## Pattern notes

- Commits 1 + 2 follow the [security-predicate-extraction.md](.claude/rules/security-predicate-extraction.md) rule: pure inputs, small-enum output, callable from tests.
- Commit 3 is the kind of latent bug warned about in [tests-that-pin-bugs.md](.claude/rules/tests-that-pin-bugs.md) — tests that pin in-memory behavior but never exercise the JSON path. Worth a separate audit pass to find other contact-profile fields that may have the same shape (struct-declared, runtime-used, JSON-unparsed).
- Commit 4 establishes the reusable per-contact-override recipe: (a) struct field with 0/NULL sentinel, (b) `hu_<axis>_effective(contact, overlay)` helper, (c) JSON parse in nested + top-level shapes, (d) daemon looks up contact then calls effective helper.

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake --build --preset dev` clean
- [x] `./build/human_tests` — 10,454 / 10,454 PASS, exit 0
- [x] No ASan trips (`grep -E "==[0-9]+==ERROR|SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer:"` empty)
- [x] Each commit independently builds and passes the suite (verified between commits)
- [ ] CI green on Linux + macOS
- [ ] CodeQL clean
- [ ] No benchmark regression

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)

- **Outbound iMessage threading via IMCore** — still gated by [docs/plans/2026-05-10-imessage-private-api-feasibility.md](docs/plans/2026-05-10-imessage-private-api-feasibility.md). The four re-open conditions have not advanced; commit 1 updates the deferral status without overriding the decision.
- **Other per-contact overlay axes** (formality, emoji_usage, avg_length, etc.) — the recipe from commit 4 makes these mechanical to add. Best done one PR per axis to keep diffs reviewable.
- **JSON-parse audit for the rest of `hu_contact_profile_t`** — commit 3 fixed one field. A targeted audit pass would find any other "declared + used + unparsed" fields.

body:
## Summary

`:command_palette` is a member of `@layer_callout_kinds` (and therefore of `@component_kinds`), so the generic component-fallback render clause at the top of `live_ui/renderer.ex` was shadowing the specific `:command_palette` clause that lived ~500 lines later. Elements with kind `:command_palette` never reached the native `LiveUi.Widgets.CommandPalette` renderer; they fell through to the fallback that emits `data-live-ui-unsupported-native-component="fallback"` with no items.

This PR moves the specific `:command_palette` clause to immediately follow `:unread_badge`, right before the `@component_kinds` fallback. This matches the pattern already used for the other `@layer_callout_kinds` (`:top_strip`, `:sidebar_shell`, `:sidebar_section`, `:sidebar_item`) and for `:mode_nav` from `@form_control_kinds` — all of which had their specific clauses placed before the fallback.

A `NOTE` comment is added so future additions to `@layer_callout_kinds` (or any `@component_kinds` member) get their specific clauses in the right spot.

## Discovery

Found while wiring the canonical `:command_palette` IUR on ariston-ui's `/operator` shell (ariston-ui PR #368, Wave AshUI-3.7-A CP-1). The downstream PR initially carried a local renderer-bypass workaround; Codex deep-review flagged the bypass as a P2 ("new UI must traverse the canonical `LiveUi.Renderer`"), and the right fix was to correct the ordering upstream rather than work around it downstream.

## Summary

Investigation of "exported 3MF imported into Bambu Studio with many more colors than I actually painted." The functional fix I tried (drop the default color from `<m:colorgroup>`) silently disabled Bambu Studio's "Standard 3MF Import Color" dialog — painted colors didn't make it across at all. Reverted that change in the follow-up commit; the export is back to the prior baseline.

What's still in the PR after the revert:
- **`tests/threemf-color-export.spec.ts`** — new Playwright regression coverage that exports through `partwright.export3MFData()`, unzips the 3MF, and asserts the colorgroup shape. Pins down today's format (default + N painted, `<object pid="2" pindex="0">`, every triangle tagged) so the next iteration has something concrete to push against.

Parked per user — the root cause needs a sample 3MF + Bambu screenshot to diagnose properly (whether the "many more" report was the +1 default we can see in the file, or something Bambu does on top during import).

- [x] `npx playwright test tests/smoke.spec.ts tests/paint-render-color.spec.ts` — 12/12 still pass

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- Bambu Studio's color-import trigger is in `bbs_3mf.cpp` — `m_group_id_to_color` map populated from `m:colorgroup` parsing. From the source it looks like the colorgroup alone should be enough, but in practice removing the object's `pid="2" pindex="0"` (or removing per-triangle `pid` on unpainted faces) skipped the dialog entirely. Worth digging into Plater.cpp / ObjColorDialog invocation to find the exact gate.
- Promising alternative not yet tested: emit both `<basematerials id="1">` (default, ignored by Bambu) and `<m:colorgroup id="2">` (painted colors). Object points at basematerial via `pid="1" pindex="0"`; painted triangles override with `pid="2" p1="N"`; unpainted inherit the basematerial. Bambu should see N painted colors only — but needs a Bambu round-trip to confirm.

author: dennys246
body:
## Summary

Replaces the static "Accepting submissions" banner on `/hrf_upload` with a live status pill that polls `https://api.hrfunc.org/healthz` from the browser.

- **Green pill + "Accepting HRF Submissions"** on HTTP 200
- **Red pill + "Submission system down"** on HTTP 503 or any fetch/network error
- **Neutral gray "Checking submission status…"** while the first response is in flight
- Polls on page load and every 60s thereafter. `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers announce state changes without interrupting.

## Design notes

- **Direct browser → HRServ, no Flask proxy.** HRServ's `feat/cors-healthz` already CORS-allows `https://hrfunc.org`, `https://www.hrfunc.org`, and `http://localhost:5000` for GET/HEAD. No custom headers means it's a CORS simple request — no preflight, cheap to poll. A Flask `/api/health` proxy would just stack an extra cache that can go stale on its own.
- **503 is rendered red, not treated as a fetch error.** `fetch()` only rejects on network failure, so `resp.ok ? "ok" : "down"` correctly maps both 200 and 503 to the right pill state — the pill never vanishes on degraded responses.
- **Submit stays enabled when red.** Per the chosen design: warning-only, since the existing upload flash already handles a real failure gracefully and a flaky healthz could otherwise wrongly block a user.

## Test plan

- [ ] Local: `flask run` on port 5000, load `/hrf_upload`, confirm pill turns green (live `api.hrfunc.org/healthz` is in the CORS allowlist for `localhost:5000`)
- [ ] Force-degraded path: temporarily change `HEALTHZ_URL` to a bogus host (e.g. `https://api.notarealhost.invalid/healthz`), confirm pill renders red on fetch error
- [ ] Devtools Network tab: confirm a clean GET fires on load + every 60s, no preflight OPTIONS
- [ ] Light + dark mode visual check on the pill colors
- [ ] After Render deploy: open `hrfunc.org/hrf_upload`, verify green pill renders from the live origin

## Out of scope

- No automated test coverage — there's no JS test harness in this repo and adding one for ~60 lines of inline DOM code isn't worth it. Manual browser verification per the test plan above.

author: alejandroeml-su
body:
## Problema

Toda la UI de Sync estaba en español hardcodeado. El sistema de i18n
nativo (Ola P4 · P4-4) ya existía con `useTranslation`/`getServerT` y
diccionarios `es.json` / `en.json`, pero:

1. Usaba códigos cortos (`es`/`en`) en lugar de BCP-47 (`es-MX`/`en-US`)
   — al integrar con sistemas corporativos (Vercel headers, OAuth IdP)
   esperaban el formato canónico.
2. No detectaba `Accept-Language` del navegador en la primera visita
   (el usuario aterrizaba siempre en español hasta que abría el
   switcher del sidebar).
3. Faltaba un selector con etiqueta completa en `/settings/profile`
   (sólo había el toggle compacto del Sidebar).
4. Login, recuperar contraseña, headers de las rutas más usadas
   (`/list`, `/kanban`, `/timeline`, `/calendar`, `/dashboards`,
   `/portfolio`, `/brain`, `/gantt`) seguían con texto hardcodeado.

## Fix

Wave R5E (18 SP) — Cobertura **útil** del UI core en bilingüe es-MX
(default) + en-US, manteniendo el framework habilitado para expansión
incremental:

- **`src/lib/i18n/translate.ts`** · SUPPORTED_LOCALES migrado a
  `['es-MX','en-US']` con tabla de aliases backward-compat para cookies
  ya persistidas (`es` → `es-MX`, `en-GB` → `en-US`, `es-419` → `es-MX`,
  etc.). Nueva función pura `resolveAcceptLanguage(header)` que parsea
  RFC 7231 con `q=` weights y devuelve el match BCP-47.
- **`src/proxy.ts`** · En la primera visita (sin cookie `x-locale`)
  resuelve `Accept-Language` y setea la cookie. **No** sobrescribe la
  preferencia manual.
- **`src/lib/i18n/messages/{es-MX,en-US}.json`** · renombrados +
  ampliados con namespaces nuevos:
  - `auth`: login, recuperar contraseña, reset password, prompt de
    auth en perfil, errores OAuth.
  - `kanban`: header + nombres de columnas (TODO/IN_PROGRESS/REVIEW/DONE).
  - `pages.list|kanban|timeline|calendar|portfolio|brain|dashboards`:
    title + subtitle.
  - `pages.gantt.headerTitle|headerHint`: cronograma + hint de
    teclado/drag.
  - `pages.profile.locale*` + `pages.profile.futureBody`: selector
    completo.
- **`src/components/profile/ProfileLocaleSection.tsx`** (nuevo) ·
  dropdown `<select>` con etiquetas completas ("Español (México)" /
  "English (United States)"). Persiste vía `setLocaleAction` y recarga.
- **`src/components/auth/LanguageSwitcher.tsx`** · sigue siendo el toggle
  compacto del sidebar (ES/EN), ahora con códigos BCP-47.
- **Login / forgot / reset password** · pages + forms traducidos
  completos vía `getServerT`/`useTranslation`.
- **Headers de /list, /gantt, /kanban, /timeline, /calendar, /dashboards,
  /portfolio, /brain** · leen `pages.<route>.title|subtitle`.
- **`/settings/profile`** · monta `<ProfileLocaleSection>` entre Identidad
  y Push.
- **Brain pm-actions / insights-actions** · `getServerLocale()` ahora
  devuelve BCP-47; helper local `localeShort()` colapsa a `'es'|'en'`
  para los prompts del LLM (idioma del modelo no varía por región).
- **AuditLogClient** · helpers `formatAbsolute`/`formatRelative` aceptan
  cualquier BCP-47 (`startsWith('en')`).
- **Tests** · `tests/unit/translate.test.ts` ampliado a 13 casos (incl.
  aliases backward-compat + `resolveAcceptLanguage` con q-weights);
  `tests/component/Sidebar.test.tsx` migrado a códigos BCP-47.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` silent.
- [x] `npm run lint` — sin errores nuevos (las 2 errores preexistentes
  de `WhiteboardEditor.tsx` no son de este PR; las 39 warnings tampoco).
- [x] `npm run build` exitoso (compila + genera 22 páginas estáticas).
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/unit/translate.test.ts` → **13/13 passed**.
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/component/Sidebar.test.tsx` → **11/11 passed**.
- [ ] Validar en navegador: `/settings/profile` → cambiar a "English
  (United States)" → recargar → sidebar/botones aparecen en en-US.
- [ ] Login con `Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9` desde una sesión
  privada → la página de login aparece en inglés desde el primer render.

## Deuda registrada

Cobertura intencionalmente parcial — la meta era el framework + UI
core. Quedan pendientes para waves futuras:

- Strings dentro de plantillas PDF (Reporting PDF #275).
- UI dinámica de Brain AI (Knowledge / Project Manager / Insights /
  Strategist / Writer): los tab labels y la respuesta del LLM se quedan
  en es-MX por defecto. El locale ya se propaga al prompt del LLM
  (vía `localeShort()` en pm/insights-actions), pero los _labels_ de
  pestañas y mensajes UI estáticos del Brain no están en el catálogo.
- Mensajes generados por Brain Insights AI en runtime (los emite el
  LLM según el locale del usuario, pero el reporte previamente
  persistido en BD queda en el idioma original — no se traduce on
  demand).
- Audit log labels de acciones (`ACTION_LABELS` en `AuditLogClient`)
  siguen hardcoded en es-MX. El header de la página y columnas sí
  están traducidos.
- TaskForm completo (labels, placeholders, validation messages): este
  PR no toca `src/components/interactions/task-form/TaskForm.tsx`. Los
  campos compartidos (`task.form.*`) ya estaban traducidos desde Ola
  P4; los strings específicos del flujo de creación quedan en es-MX.
- Páginas administrativas (`/settings/roles`, `/settings/teams`,
  `/settings/users`, `/audit-log`): muchas ya usan `t()` parcialmente;
  cobertura 100% queda fuera de scope R5E.

author: ss-sonic
body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

Closes #2522.

### The bug

`createChatSdkBridge` accepts a `transformOutboundText` config function — the adapter-specific outbound sanitizer (Telegram uses `sanitizeTelegramLegacyMarkdown`). It's wired into the bridge at `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts:124` and called on the normal text branch at `L474`, but the two card branches above it built `Card` / `CardText` components from raw, unsanitized text:

- `ask_question` (L399) — `CardText(question)` and the `Card({ title })` wrapper
- `send_card` (L429–468) — `CardText(cardSpec.description)`, `CardText(child)`, `CardText(child.text)`, `Card({ title })`, and `fallbackText`

The transform stayed plumbed but unused on exactly the paths that emit approval cards and `send_card` payloads — i.e. the messages most likely to embed markdown special chars from agent-controlled metadata. Telegram rejected with `Bad Request: can't parse entities` and the admin's DM never received the card, leaving the agent in a stuck "waiting for approval" state with no visible card to act on.

Reproducible with any agent group whose name contains an `_` — e.g. `repo_pilot` triggering `install_packages`. The question body `Agent "repo_pilot" is attempting to install...` has its single unbalanced `_` at byte offset 38, exactly where Telegram's legacy Markdown parser fails.

### The fix

Apply `transformText` to every user-visible string before constructing `Card` / `CardText` nodes, mirroring the existing text-branch pattern at `L474`:

- `ask_question`: sanitize `title`, `question`, and `fallbackText`
- `send_card`: sanitize `title`, `description`, string and `{text}` children, and `fallbackText`

Button labels are left raw — they come from `NormalizedOption.label`, which the SDK escapes appropriately, and they're echoed into `fallbackText` after sanitization just like the raw text would have been.

### Tests

`src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` gains a new `transformOutboundText wiring` describe block that supplies a tagging transform (`(t) => '«' + t + '»'`), captures the rendered `Card` via the existing `makePostCapture` helper, walks the Card tree with a small `collectCardText` traversal, and asserts that:

- ask_question's `title`, `question` (via CardText), and `fallbackText` are all tagged.
- send_card's `title`, `description`, string children, and `{text}`-object children are all tagged, plus `fallbackText`.
- plain markdown messages still apply the transform (regression guard for the path that wasn't broken).

Full suite: 31 files, 331 tests passing (15 of those in `chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts`).

body:
This PR introduces a more resilient local infrastructure for the Devops God Mode. 

Key changes:
1. **Armored Launcher**: A new `launcher.py` (and corresponding `launcher.exe` in build) acts as a watchdog. It monitors the backend via the `/health` endpoint and automatically restarts it if it crashes or fails health checks.
2. **Professional Installer**: An Inno Setup script `installer.iss` has been created to package the application into a professional Windows installer (`GodModeSetup.exe`), handling folders, shortcuts, and initial configuration.
3. **CI/CD Integration**: The `.github/workflows/windows-exe-real-build.yml` has been updated to build these new artifacts and upload them as part of the release process.
4. **Resilient Connectivity**: Added documentation and recommendations for using Tailscale IPs to ensure stable PC-Mobile communication.
5. **Stability Fixes**: Corrected test path issues in the autonomous pipeline to ensure verification steps pass reliably in different directory structures.

author: lacatoire
body:
Paths containing a dot (e.g. `test.1`) were treated as a single file and never expanded to `/path/**/*`, so phpDocumentor reported an empty documentation set when run with `-d test.1`.

## Summary

- `slotFormat` (`formatSlotDate`, `formatSlotDateTime`) and `ZonedDateUtils#format` previously pinned dayjs to French at module-import / construction time, so dates stayed French even after the user switched language via the LanguageSwitcher.
- Read `currentLocale.value` from `\$lib/states/locale.svelte` at call time instead. Eagerly import both `dayjs/locale/en` and `dayjs/locale/fr` so dayjs can switch synchronously.
- `ZonedDateUtils`'s explicit `formatLocale` constructor argument still wins; the previous browser-locale fallback is replaced by the widget's active locale. `WidgetPage.svelte` drops the hard-coded `'fr'` and lets the new default take over.

Pure code wiring — no translation keys, no message file changes.

- [x] \`pnpm build\` — clean build

  - \`formatSlotDate('2026-05-17', 'dddd DD MMMM')\` → \`dimanche 17 mai\` (fr) / \`Sunday 17 May\` (en)
  - \`formatSlotDateTime('2026-05-17', '19:30', 'ddd DD MMM HH:mm')\` → \`dim. 17 mai 19:30\` (fr) / \`Sun 17 May 19:30\` (en)

## Summary

First half of TASKS.md Step 5c. Adds a daily Playwright smoke test that exercises the admin sign-in flow against the deployed Vercel site. Doubles as Supabase keepalive — the dashboard load fires a `SELECT` against the `quotes` table on every run, replacing the dummy `keepalive` table approach.

This PR only **adds** the new workflow. Once it has run green on schedule at least once, a **follow-up PR** will remove the old `supabase-keepalive.yml` and drop the `public.keepalive` table via migration.

## What's in this PR

- **`e2e/admin-smoke.spec.ts`** — visits `/`, asserts `/admin` redirects to `/admin/login`, signs in with `E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, asserts the dashboard mounts, clicks the Quotes tab and asserts no "failed to load" banner, signs out. Skips cleanly when env vars are absent so it doesn't break local `npm run e2e` for other developers.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-smoke.yml`** — `schedule: "0 0 * * *"` + `workflow_dispatch`. Installs chromium, runs only the smoke spec, uploads the Playwright report on failure (7 day retention).
- **`playwright.config.ts`** — `webServer` now skipped when `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL` is set externally (CI hits the deployed URL, doesn't need a local dev server). Local `npm run e2e` is unchanged.

## Prereqs (one-time, manual — must be done before the cron is useful)

- [ ] Create a dedicated `e2e@…` user in Supabase Auth (any password — store it as a secret).
- [ ] Add GitHub Actions secrets:
  - `E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL` — the e2e user's email
  - `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — the e2e user's password
- [ ] After merge: trigger the workflow manually via Actions tab → "Daily smoke" → "Run workflow" to confirm it passes before relying on the cron.

If the secrets aren't set, the test calls `test.skip(...)` and the run shows green-but-skipped. That's intentional — the workflow won't false-fail before you're ready.

## Related Issue

## Description of changes
- `_handleAction`'s `BURN_6909` branch forwarded a caller-supplied `from` to `PoolManager.burn` without checking it against `msgSender()`. Because `withdrawClaim` documents `PoolManager.setOperator(permPosm, true)` as the supported approval pattern, any caller of `modifyLiquidities` could pair `BURN_6909(currency, victim, amount)` with `TAKE(currency, attacker, amount)` and burn a victim's 6909 claim once the operator approval is active.
- Adds `from != msgSender()` revert in the `BURN_6909` branch. `withdrawClaim` already encodes `from = msg.sender = msgSender()` inside the unlock callback, so the legitimate path is unaffected.
- Adds a unit test asserting an unrelated caller cannot drain an admin-held 6909 claim via raw `modifyLiquidities`.

body:
`FLUXFLAGS` currently applies to every Flux invocation, including dependencies. This change introduces `FLUXLOCALFLAGS`, parsed like `FLUXFLAGS` but applied only to the local target crates selected by `cargo flux` (default members, `--workspace`/`--exclude`, and `-p` selection).

- **cargo-flux: local-only env flags**
  - Added parsing for `FLUXLOCALFLAGS` in `cargo-flux`.
  - Kept `FLUXFLAGS` behavior unchanged.
  - Applied `FLUXLOCALFLAGS` only when generating rustflags for packages identified as local check targets.

- **Target crate selection logic**
  - Added local package ID computation in `cargo_flux_opts` based on existing CLI selection semantics:
    - explicit `-p` packages
    - workspace/default-member behavior
    - `--exclude` filtering

- **Docs**
  - Updated install guide with `FLUXLOCALFLAGS` behavior and usage.

Example:

```console
FLUXLOCALFLAGS="-Finclude=src/**" cargo flux -p my-crate
```

This applies `-Finclude=src/**` to `my-crate` (local target) but not to dependency crates.

author: agentydragon
body:
## Summary

The `partial_swap` vendor stage already rewrites caller imports to
bare specifiers (`import { observer } from "mobx-react-lite"`) and
writes `vendor_partial_swap_manifest.json` alongside the regular
vendor manifest. But until now nothing on the runtime side consumed
that manifest — the live proxy didn't read it, no importmap was
injected, and loading a page with a partial-swap'd vendor would
silently fail before the app boots (browsers reject unresolved bare
specifiers at module-parse time).

This wires up the missing live-proxy half:

- **`live_proxy/vendor_runtime.mjs`** learns
  `loadPartialSwapRuntimeIndex`, `buildPartialSwapImportMap`, and
  `resolvePartialSwapRuntimeRequest`. The index reads the partial-
  swap manifest, resolves each package's filesystem mount root via
  the existing `package_roots`/`packages_root` machinery, and
  exposes a URL prefix
  `<appAssetPrefix>/_partial_swap/<package>/<subpath>` where the
  package directory is served verbatim (so relative imports inside
  the package resolve against the same mount).
- **`live_proxy/proxy.mjs`** loads the index (defaulting to
  `<vendor_manifest_dir>/vendor_partial_swap_manifest.json`),
  injects a `<script type="importmap">` block with one entry per
  partial-swap'd package into the served HTML, and routes
  `_partial_swap/...` asset requests through the new resolver.
  `rewriteHtmlForLiveProxy` gains an `importMap` parameter; callers
  pass `null` when no partial-swap is in scope, preserving existing
  HTML output.
- **Auto-extension resolution** for partial-swap requests: when the
  exact path doesn't exist on disk, fall back to `.js` / `.mjs` /
  `.cjs` suffixes, then `index.{js,mjs,cjs}`. npm packages
  routinely use extension-less ESM imports (`import "./utils"`),
  and the browser sends the literal URL — without the fallback the
  importmap-driven fetches 404. Every candidate is built with
  `resolve` from the mount root, so the existing
  `assertPathWithinRoot`/`assertRealPathWithinRoot` checks still
  apply.

## Test plan

- [x] `bazelisk test //devinfra/js/debundle/live_proxy:proxy_test --config=rbe` — existing proxy tests stay green
- [x] Consumer-side smoke from gaffer-private (mobx `dist/mobx.esm.production.min.js` served via importmap, fetched and parsed by the browser, mobx.esm.js loads with no `process` reference error). The mobx partial-swap experiment surfaced a separate two-mobx-instances issue at the gaffer-spec layer and that experiment was reverted there, but the runtime serving path proven out here is the prerequisite for any future partial-swap to actually boot in a browser.

author: sol-duara
body:
### Expression identity model (breaking schema change)
Expressions are no longer identified by `name + semver`. They now use a `(group, author, expression)` tuple. References in workflow YAML change from `expression: build:^0.1.0` to path-style `expression: build` (or `author/build` / `group/author/build` for disambiguation). The `cdrus` block replaces the top-level `version` field in workflow YAML.

### `run` accepts multiple workflows
`iron-monkey run a.yaml b.yaml c.yaml` pitches all three simultaneously. Each gets its own bus connection, chain ID, and timing — one failure does not abort the others.

### `pitch` command + repertoire YAML
`iron-monkey pitch --from repertoire.yaml` is the per-workflow control surface. A repertoire expresses a dictionary of pitches in YAML, with a `shared` defaults block and per-pitch overrides for `interval`, `bus`, `seed`, `inject`, `synth`, and `manifest_out`. Merge priority: CLI flags → `shared` → per-pitch.

### Test coverage improvements
- `src/types.ts` and `src/workflow/types.ts` type guards (`isEventItem`, `isExpressionItem`) now have dedicated unit tests
- `src/schema/loader.ts` was untested (the existing test only covered the duplicate in `src/loaders/`); added `tests/schema/loader.test.ts`
- Pure type-declaration files excluded from coverage reporting so the report only shows executable code
- 6 new tests for `runWorkflows`, 15 for the repertoire loader

### README
Updated to reflect all of the above: new commands, repertoire YAML format and field reference, corrected expression syntax throughout, new "Pitching multiple workflows" section.

author: adhithyan15
body:
## Summary

Two coordinated bug fixes that align mini-sqlite's `ORDER BY` NULL placement with real SQLite.

- **sql-codegen 1.27.0 → 1.28.0**: default `nulls_first` resolution now depends on direction (FIRST for ASC, LAST for DESC). Explicit `NULLS FIRST`/`NULLS LAST` still honoured.
- **sql-vm 1.25.0 → 1.26.0**: removed a `-rank` negation bug in `_do_sort` that inadvertently coupled NULL placement to sort direction. NULL position now obeys `k.nulls` regardless of ASC/DESC.
- **mini-sqlite 1.36.0 → 1.37.0**: new oracle test file with 10 byte-for-byte comparisons against the real `sqlite3` module.

## Truth table (after fix)

| `ORDER BY x` | NULL position |
|--------------|---------------|
| ASC (default) | first |
| DESC | last |
| ASC NULLS LAST | last (explicit) |
| DESC NULLS FIRST | first (explicit) |

## Summary
Adds the chapter book picker to the review and active phases of the planner, allowing returning users to change their read-aloud book without redoing the entire plan. Also introduces loading and error states to gracefully handle Firestore collection fetch failures.

## Changes

- **Renamed `ChapterBookPicker` variant**: `'card'` → `'compact'` (slim single-row picker with `maxWidth: 480px`, no internal header)
- **Added loading state**: New `loading` prop shows a disabled placeholder with spinner while `chapterBooks` collection loads

## Implementation Details

- Loading state uses `CircularProgress` + disabled `FormControl` to signal that the picker is coming
- Error state wraps the fallback `TextField` in a `Tooltip` explaining the degradation
- Empty library still renders the full `Select` (not a text input) so users can reach "Add a new book"
- `PlannerSetupWizard` now accepts optional `chapterBooksLoading` and `chapterBooksLoadError` props and passes them through to `ChapterBookPicker`

author: vitormrodovalho
body:
## Summary

Cycle 6 W3 Wave 1 — frontend defensive coding hotfix following operator's production triage report (2026-05-17 12:04 UTC). User declared W2 GATE met honestly and handed over the bug file at `/home/vitormrodovalho/meridianiq-issues-2026-05-17.md` for next-step prioritization. Backend diagnostic ran in-session — the 502s in the file were transient (captured during PR #142 deploy window); current state is healthy. Real remaining bugs after filtering: silent fetch hangs + SVG NaN errors.

## Honest delivered value (<50 words per L6.8 candidate)

Fix production fetch hangs (12s per-attempt + 60s total budget) in api.ts wrapper + 3 raw-fetch pages. Fix Pareto SVG NaN errors via `Number.isFinite` filter in ScatterChart + ParetoChart derivations. Add typed `TimeoutError` class + 3 i18n keys for localized timeout UX in 4 affected pages.

## Diff stat

```
 web/src/lib/api.ts                                | 44 ++++++++++++++++++++++-
 web/src/lib/components/charts/ParetoChart.svelte  | 35 +++++++++++++-----
 web/src/lib/components/charts/ScatterChart.svelte | 18 ++++++----
 web/src/lib/i18n/en.ts                            |  1 +
 web/src/lib/i18n/es.ts                            |  1 +
 web/src/lib/i18n/pt-BR.ts                         |  1 +
 web/src/routes/benchmarks/+page.svelte            | 25 ++++++++++---
 web/src/routes/duration-prediction/+page.svelte   | 11 ++++--
 web/src/routes/pareto/+page.svelte                |  7 +++-
 web/src/routes/whatif/+page.svelte                |  6 +++-
 10 files changed, 124 insertions(+), 25 deletions(-)
```

## What this PR DOES

1. **`api.ts request<T>()` wrapper:**
   - Adds `AbortSignal.timeout(12_000)` **inside** the retry loop (fresh signal per attempt — a reused signal would abort every retry after the first one fires, caught by frontend-reviewer entry-council pre-edit).
   - Adds 60s total wall-clock budget across the 5-retry loop.
   - Treats per-attempt timeout as cold-start-like for retry purposes.
   - On final-attempt timeout, throws typed `TimeoutError extends ApiError` (`name = 'TimeoutError'`, `errorCode = 'request_timeout'`).
2. **4 pages** (pareto, duration-prediction, benchmarks, whatif) — catch blocks detect `e.name === 'TimeoutError'` and surface localized `$t('error.request_timeout')` instead of untranslated browser message.
3. **3 raw-fetch pages** (pareto, duration-prediction, benchmarks) — add inline `AbortSignal.timeout(12_000)` to their fetch options (they bypass the `request()` wrapper).
4. **2 charts** (ParetoChart, ScatterChart) — derive `finitePoints` / `finiteData` filtered to `Number.isFinite(x) && Number.isFinite(y)` entries. All `Math.min/max(...)` derivations + SVG `{#each}` loops use the filtered array. Belt-and-suspenders: `xScale` / `yScale` also `Number.isFinite()` check their output.
5. **3 i18n locales** — `error.request_timeout` key (en / pt-BR / es).

## What this PR EXPLICITLY DOES NOT do

- **Does NOT** harden BarChart / GanttChart / ResourceChart / MultiRevisionSCurveChart / TimelineChart — these are empty-safe via existing `Math.max(..., 1)` or gated-derived patterns. No production evidence of NaN bugs in these charts. Frontend-reviewer pushed for "all 7 charts" but speculative defensive hardening without production evidence is the exact L6.8 displacement-activity pattern Cycle 6 H-shape was structured to avoid. Filing follow-up issue for explicit Wave 2 if production evidence accumulates.
- **Does NOT** migrate the 3 raw-fetch pages to use `request()` — refactor work, not hotfix. Inline timeout achieves the same defensive surface.
- **Does NOT** pinpoint the specific source of `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'error')` in `CseCgBWy.js` from the bug file — bug file's own diagnosis attributes this to backend 502 cascading; backend is now healthy post-PR-#142 deploy. Symptom resolution validated empirically (see "CI status" below).
- **Does NOT** add a cancel button for in-flight requests (UX gap noted for future wave).

## Local verification

```
$ cd web && npm run check
   COMPLETED 671 FILES 0 ERRORS 0 WARNINGS 0 FILES_WITH_PROBLEMS

$ npm test -- --run
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
   Tests       58 passed (58)
   Duration    1.36s

$ npm run build
   ✓ built in 2.51s
```

## Pre-merge council trail

### Frontend-reviewer entry-council (pre-edit, this session)

Returned 3 P0 blockers + scope expansion pressure:

1. **SHIP-STOPPER: `AbortSignal` reused across retries.** Original draft created signal once at top of `request()` and passed via `mergedInit`. Every retry would have aborted immediately. **Fixed:** signal created inside the for-loop per attempt.
2. **`|| 1` guard insufficient for Infinity values.** In JavaScript, `NaN || 1 = 1` (NaN is falsy) but `Infinity || 1 = Infinity` (Infinity is truthy). When `points = []`, `Math.min(...[]) = Infinity`, and the fallback `xMax - xMin || 1` doesn't save you. **Fixed:** filter to finite values upstream, plus belt-and-suspenders `Number.isFinite()` check in `xScale`/`yScale` output.
3. **Scope expansion to all 7 charts.** Frontend-reviewer pushed: "ParetoChart and ScatterChart fixes alone are cherry-picking." **Pushed back:** speculative hardening without production evidence is the L6.8 displacement pattern Cycle 6 is structured to break. Filing follow-up issue if production evidence accumulates.

Also caught one factual error in proposed plan: claimed MultiRevisionSCurveChart needed patching — on inspection, its derivations are already gated by `$derived.by(() => { if (curves.length === 0) return null; ... if (ms.some(Number.isNaN)) return null; ... })`. Already safe. Removed from scope.

### DA exit-council
Pending on this PR. Will run after CI green.

## Cycle 6 context

- **W2 HARD GATE: MET HONESTLY** per operator self-report (2026-05-17). Per ADR-0025, artifact does NOT enforce; Cycle 7 council judges based on self-report. Issue #134 not visibly logged with 5 CDs but operator may track CDs elsewhere — noted in `memory/project_resume_next_session.md` for Cycle 7 council reference.
- This PR unlocks Cycle 6 W3 execution (Frontend DA cluster originally planned as #105/#106/#107/#108 + #110 + #46 — production hotfix takes precedence and overlaps the W3 frontend-focused window).
- Diverges from original ADR-0025 W3 wave plan (a11y intrinsic merit cluster) — production stability supersedes planned hygiene. Diversion captured here; not a Cycle 6.5 amendment trigger.

- [x] Local Vitest 58/58 pass
- [x] Local Vite build green
- [ ] CI green on PR (backend / frontend / e2e / CodeQL / gitleaks)
- [ ] DA exit-council clean

body:
## What

Adds two new collections to `azure.subscription.cloudDefenderService`, surfacing Microsoft Defender for Cloud **posture findings** — not just the pricing-tier configuration the service modeled before.

### `assessments` — `Microsoft.Security/assessments`
Security recommendations and their health status. Fields: `id`, `name`, `displayName`, `status` (Healthy/Unhealthy/NotApplicable), `statusCause`, `statusDescription`, `severity`, `resourceId` (ARM ID of the assessed resource), `additionalData`.

- `resourceId` is derived from the assessment ID (the segment before `/providers/Microsoft.Security/assessments/`).
- `severity` is joined in from the assessment **metadata catalog** — both the built-in (`NewListPager`) and subscription-scoped (`NewListBySubscriptionPager`) lists — because the assessment list response itself does not carry severity. Container-vulnerability sub-findings have no catalog metadata, so their severity is legitimately empty.

### `alerts` — `Microsoft.Security/alerts`
Active security alerts. Fields: `id`, `name`, `displayName`, `severity`, `status`, `description`, `alertType`, `intent` (kill-chain), `vendorName`, `compromisedEntity`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `timeGenerated`, `remediationSteps`, `resourceIdentifiers`.

## Why

`cloudDefenderService` previously exposed only Defender pricing tiers, secure scores, regulatory compliance standards, and security contacts. The actual recommendations and alerts — the data auditors query to assess posture — were not modeled. Both new collections are lazy (fetched only when queried) and degrade to an empty result on access-denied.

## Notes

- No new dependency — `armsecurity` v0.14.0 was already imported.
- New `.lr.versions` entries land at `13.11.3` (next patch after the provider's current `13.11.2`); `config.go` is intentionally not bumped.
- `azure.permissions.json` is unchanged — the new `Microsoft.Security` read calls are already covered.

## Testing

Verified against a live Azure subscription:
- `assessments` returns rich data — 1256 rows with populated `severity`, plus correct `status`/`displayName`/`resourceId`.
- `alerts` resolves cleanly and returns `[]` (no active alerts in the test subscription).

## Summary

Mild deepening of the Activity detail page. Pulls three concerns out of `ActivityDetail.vue` (~30 LOC removed) into a dedicated composable + module-level pure helpers:

- `parseSyncLogEntries(json)` — tolerant JSON parse of the session's `entries` column. Empty string / malformed JSON / non-array payloads all collapse to `[]` so the page renders the empty state rather than crashing on a bad row.
- `formatSyncLogEntryTime(ts)` — locale-aware time-of-day formatter (`HH:MM:SS`) for log-entry timestamps. Invalid input passes through verbatim.
- `iconForSyncLogLevel(level)` — `error`/`warn`/`info` → Directus icon name.
- `useSyncLogEntries(session)` — view-model that bundles `entries` (reactive parse of the supplied session ref) + the two formatters, so the template binds one composable instead of three named imports plus an inline `computed`.

## Context

This is the one architectural item left in the Activity surface — most of the original "session-view module" deepening shipped across PRs 35–47 (`use-activity-log.ts`, `use-sync-log-user-names.ts`, the `SessionsTable` + `SessionMetadata` + `StatusLabel` components). Surveying today, the only remaining inline ad-hoc parsers were in `ActivityDetail.vue`. This PR closes that gap.

`ActivityDetail.vue` drops from 210 → 184 LOC.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive modpack import support, a Modrinth mod browser UI, and extensive test coverage to validate launcher compatibility with Prism Launcher and upstream APIs.

## Key Changes

### Modpack Import Services
- **FtbImporter**: Import modpacks from the FTB (Feed the Beast) API via pack ID and version lookup
- **CurseForgeImporter**: Parse and import CurseForge modpack ZIPs (manifest.json format)
- **ModrinthImporter**: Import Modrinth .mrpack files with full dependency resolution
- **PackwizImporter**: Import Packwiz packs from pack.toml URLs with mod resolution

### Mod Management
- **ModrinthClient**: Full Modrinth API v2 client for searching projects and versions
- **ModManager**: High-level service for browsing, installing, enabling/disabling, and removing mods
- **ModBrowserViewModel & ModBrowserWindow**: New UI for searching and installing mods from Modrinth with real-time search and version selection

### Mod Loader Installers
- **ForgeInstaller**: Download and process Forge installer JARs (legacy and modern formats)
- **NeoForgeInstaller**: Handle NeoForge mod loader (Forge successor for 1.20.1+)
- **QuiltInstaller**: Fetch Quilt loader profiles from QuiltMC meta server
- **ForgeInstallProfile**: Model for parsing install_profile.json from Forge installers

### Testing & Validation
- **PrismParityTests**: Comprehensive tests validating our launcher produces identical output to Prism Launcher for Minecraft versions, Fabric, and asset indices
- **LiveApiTests**: Integration tests against real upstream APIs (Mojang, Fabric, Modrinth)
- **CurseForgeManifestParsingTests**: Validate manifest.json parsing matches Prism behavior
- **ModrinthIndexParsingTests**: Validate modrinth.index.json deserialization
- **ForgeInstallerFormatTests**: Validate old vs. new Forge format detection
- **FtbComponentBuildingTests**: Validate FTB target → component mapping
- **MavenPathTests**: Validate Maven coordinate resolution
- **VersionComparisonTests**: Validate semantic version comparison for updates

### UI & UX Enhancements
- **CreateInstanceWindow**: Added mod loader selection (Forge, Fabric, Quilt, NeoForge) with version loading
- **MainWindow**: New import menu with CurseForge, Modrinth, and FTB options; mod browser button
- **VersionSelectorViewModel**: Refactored to fetch real version data from Mojang manifest API with filtering
- **MainWindowViewModel**: Integrated new import services, mod manager, and update checker

### Supporting Services
- **UpdateChecker**: Check GitHub Releases for newer launcher versions
- **ModLoaderService**: Enhanced to support multiple mod loader installers
- **JavaManager**: Fixed TAR.GZ extraction permissions on Unix systems
- **LibraryManager**: Added Maven repository URL support for library downloads

### Models
- **Modrinth models**: ModrinthProject, ModrinthVersion, ModrinthIndex, ModrinthSearchResult
- **Forge models**: ForgeInstallProfile with support for both old and new formats
- **FTB models**: FtbPackSummary, FtbPackInfo for API responses
- **MinecraftVersionEntry**: New model for version selector with real API data

## Notable Implementation Details
- All importers follow a consistent async pattern with progress reporting
- Parity tests use known-good values from Prism Launcher's meta server (updated 2025-05-17)
- Mod browser supports filtering by project type (mod, modpack, resourcepack, shader)
- Forge installer handles both legacy (≤1.12.2) and modern (≥1.13) formats
- Maven coordinate resolution matches Prism Launcher's library path logic
- Version comparison strips pre-release suffixes for semantic versioning

## Summary

Block 31 of 12-hour physics-loop campaign. **POSITIVE narrow closure** on `poisson_self_gravity_loop_note` (audited_conditional, desc=697, load-bearing 13.195).

Carves out a Class-A code-level identity on `scripts/poisson_self_gravity_loop.py` that does NOT transit the conditional upstream `minimal_source_driven_field_probe_note`.

## Theorem (one sentence)

For every `(source_strength, epsilon)` with `epsilon * source_strength = 0`, the loop's screened-Poisson field is bit-exactly zero on every lattice cell, the outer self-consistency loop converges in <= 2 iterations with final `field_delta = 0.0`, and `_propagate_from_sources` reduces bit-exactly to the bare lattice propagator.

The proof rests on the IEEE-754 identity `0.0 * y = 0.0` for finite `y` — purely algebraic on the loop runner's own code, not a numerical coincidence.

## V1-V5 angles

V1: ε=0 closed-form kernel identity → **chosen** (★★★★★, strongest)
V2: iteration-1 loop/inst identity (trivial post-iteration)
V3: frozen-field Born I3 structural vanishing (★★★★)
V4: convex-weight invariant (not load-bearing)
V5: V3 restated

V1 wins because it gives a bit-exact identity AND structurally explains the cached zero-epsilon exact-zero digits, without transiting the conditional upstream.

## What is NOT claimed

- Does **not** promote `poisson_self_gravity_loop_note` from `audited_conditional`. The conditional verdict still applies to nonzero-coupling rows and the inherited bounded admissions (BA-1)-(BA-3).
- Does **not** ratify `minimal_source_driven_field_probe_note`.
- Does **not** claim a self-gravity mechanism, weak-field saturation, or backreaction phase.
- Does **not** depend on V3 sibling note's machinery (different runner, different short-circuit).

## Artifacts

author: kim-em
body:
This PR records the per-turn progress entry for `/work` session
`7ef5ff71`. The session claimed #4779
(`quadraticIntegerRootFactors?_pairwise_not_associated`) and
discovered the planned theorem statement is provably false.

Concrete counterexample: take `core = (X-1)^2 = X^2 - 2X + 1`.

* `Primitive core` holds (`content = gcd(1, 2, 1) = 1`).
* `0 < leadingCoeff core` holds (`leadingCoeff = 1`).
* `core.degree?.getD 0 = 2`.
* `integerRootCandidates core = [1, -1]`.
* `splitIntegerRootFactorsAux` extracts `(X-1)`, then the recursive
  call with tail `[-1]` and quotient `(X-1)` finds that `(X+1)` does
  not divide `(X-1)`, leaving the residual as `(X-1)`.
* So `split.1 = #[X-1]`, `split.2 = X-1`, and the residual branch
  pushes the residual into the output:
  `quadraticIntegerRootFactors? core = some #[X-1, X-1]`.

The output pair `(X-1), (X-1)` is `ZPoly.Associated` via the unit
`DensePoly.C 1`, so `Pairwise (¬ Associated · ·)` is false. The
issue body's claim "core is squarefree by primitive-quadratic
structure" is incorrect — primitivity plus degree-2 does not imply
squarefree.

The fix is to add `Hex.ZPoly.SquareFreeRat core` to the hypothesis
list. The downstream caller in #4747 has
`core = (normalizeForFactor f).squareFreeCore` and can discharge
this via `ZPoly.primitiveSquareFreeDecomposition_squareFreeCore`
(`HexPolyZ/Basic.lean:3017`). Sibling #4604 deliverable 2 cites the
same lemma and needs the same correction.

#4779 was skipped (`replan`) with the full counterexample posted as
an issue comment.

The session also skipped #4334 (HexLLL inconclusive scientific
benchmarks) — host load average 11.55 / 11.02 / 11.86 on the shared
pod host, well above the contention threshold the issue body
documents for prior skips. Re-dispatch needs the scheduled
release-candidate benchmarking workflow on dedicated hardware per
`SPEC/benchmarking.md`.

author: scylladbbot
body:
The `test_max_cells` test was flaky due to `std::bad_alloc` caused by Seastar buddy allocator fragmentation. The root causes are:
1. The doubling loop with 24 iterations of CREATE/INSERT/DROP fragmented the allocator
2. The test built the whole batch as a single string that takes contiguous memory

Also, some iterations inserted zero rows, but still did CREATE/DROP table which also contributed to the fragmentation.

This patch series:
- Skips iterations that insert zero rows
- Creates the table once, truncates it after each test iteration
- Switches to prepared statements

Investigation results are presented in detail in https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/SCYLLADB-1645

Fixes SCYLLADB-1645

CI stability improvement. Backport to versions that have this test.

## Summary

Sweep verification: both findings in this artifact are **already addressed** by PR #161 (commit `5d62c3d`). No code changes are required.

## Findings vs current code

**Finding 1 — Auto-compute `content_hash` on artifact store and update**
- `store_artifact` (`src/tools/artifacts.ts:287-290`): hashes when content is provided, and because the assignment happens after the metadata spread, the server-computed value always overrides any caller-supplied `content_hash`.
- `update_artifact` (`src/tools/artifacts.ts:650-657`): the `contentUpdated` branch recomputes only when content is in the update payload; server-computed value overrides caller-supplied.

**Finding 2 — `content_hash` not recomputed on re-promotion to locked status**
- Handled by the branch at `src/tools/artifacts.ts:665-682` (added in PR #161). Fires when promoting from a non-locked status to a locked status with row content present but `content_hash` missing from metadata.

## Goal conditions

All five hold against current `main`:
- ✅ Auto-computed on `store_artifact` when content is provided.
- ✅ Auto-computed on `update_artifact` when content changes.

## Summary

- Shifts `pages.yml` cron from `0 10 * * *` to `0 14 * * *` so the daily dashboard re-render sits well after `update-linpeas` (09:00), `stale-pin-check` (10:30), and `verify-latest-release` (12:00).
- Adds a new `## Cron schedule` section to `docs/architecture/ci.md` documenting all seven cron workflows and the by-design Pages staleness window.

Implements approved spec `.claude/specs/2026-05-17-ciw-2-cron-collision-design.md`. Addresses audit findings CIW-2 (`ci-workflows.md`) and NX-PD-3 (`nix-build.md`) from the 2026-05-16 post-Docker-Hub security review.

## Rationale

The previous 10:00 UTC cron only left 1h of slack after `update-linpeas` (09:00). On slow bump days the dashboard could publish `drift.days = 1` while the bump PR was still merging. The push-trigger + release-trigger on `pages.yml` already refresh the site within minutes of any bump merge; the daily cron is the no-bump-today floor.

The dashboard remains documentation, not a trust anchor — per `.claude/CLAUDE.md` GitHub Pages binding invariants and `docs/security/trust-model.md`.

### What does this PR do?

When options are reordered (e.g., when a model's position in the list moves to do favouriting/unfavouriting it in the model list), the highlighted selection was staying at the same row index and pointing to a different item. Now we use on(() => flat(), ...) with the previous flat array to find the previously selected value in the new options list and restore the selection to the correct index.

This means that when the `ctrl+f` key is used to favourite or unfavourite their model in the `model_list`, the selection will remain on the same model instead of remaining on the same index (which will now contain a different model).

author: baseballyama
body:
## Summary

Phase A nibble (per the refreshed PERF_ROADMAP.md): replace the
text-based dev-mode \`===\` / \`!==\` → \`\$.strict_equals(...)\` pass for
\`.svelte.js\` / \`.svelte.ts\` modules with an OXC-AST-based visitor.

The text version (\`rune_transforms::transform_strict_equals\`) walked
the script character-by-character and tried to skip string literals
by counting unescaped quotes — fragile under:

- escaped quotes inside strings (\`\"a \\\" === b\"\`)
- regex literals (\`/===/\\.test(s)\`)
- line and block comments
- template literal interpolation (\`\\\`\${a === b}\\\`\` vs static \`\\\`===\\\`\`)

OXC's parser knows about all of those, so the AST visitor's
correctness is structural, not heuristic.

## Implementation

\`src/compiler/phases/3_transform/client/strict_equals_ast.rs\` (new, ~210 LOC):

1. Parse the script (\`SourceType::ts()\` or \`SourceType::mjs()\`,
   chosen from the \`.ts\` filename suffix).
2. Walk every \`BinaryExpression\`; rewrite \`StrictEquality\` /
   \`StrictInequality\`.
3. Collect \`(start, end, replacement_string)\` triples, apply
   right-to-left so earlier offsets stay valid.

Nested cases like \`(a === b) === c\` work via fixed-point
iteration: each pass only rewrites *leaf* strict-equals binaries
(those whose operand source doesn't itself contain \`===\` / \`!==\`),
then re-parses and repeats. Terminates in O(max nesting depth)
passes — typically 1.

Thread-local \`Allocator\` matches the pattern used by
\`ast_state_transform\` — reset between calls, no arena re-creation
cost per compile.

Component instance scripts already get this rewrite via
\`ast_state_transform::try_rewrite_strict_equals_binary\` (which has
to drain inner state-var replacements into the operand text — much
heavier machinery). Module scripts have no state vars to interleave,
so the standalone helper here is much smaller.

## Test plan

- [x] 11 new unit tests in \`strict_equals_ast\` cover: basic
  \`===\`/\`!==\`, string-literal safety, template-literal expression
  interpolation, regex literals, nesting, TypeScript syntax,
  parse-error fallback, no-op when operators absent
- [x] Full lib suite: 535/535 (was 524 + 11 new)
- [x] \`cargo fmt --check\` clean
- [x] \`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings\` clean
- [x] Falls back gracefully (returns \`None\`, source untouched) on parse error

## Migration plan

The legacy \`rune_transforms::transform_strict_equals\` and its helpers
stay in place (already \`#[allow(dead_code)]\`); they'll be deleted in
a follow-up once the rolling Phase A migration confirms the AST path
is stable across the full 3341 fixture suite.

author: firatcand
body:
## Summary

Refactor `forge orchestrate` from the v0.2.x flat 6-verb surface into the v2 verb-table dispatcher with a strict read-only / user-approved-mutating split (per `spec/ORCHESTRATOR.md` §CLI surface, rewritten 2026-05-17). Absorbs FORGE-79 (file-glob overlap library) per plan fork F10.

- **17 verbs** registered across two bands plus a nested `run` sub-tree.
  - Read-only (no lease, no tracker mutation): `phases`, `status`, `questions`, `doctor`, `attach`, `spec-diff`, `run list`.
  - User-approved mutating: `claim`, `dispatch`, `heartbeat`, `question`, `answer`, `event`, `complete`, `cancel`, `reconcile`, `gc`, `run start`.
- **Stable JSON envelope** on every `--json` invocation: `{ ok, data? | error: { code, message, retriable, details? } }`.
- **Verb-table dispatcher** (`src/cli/orchestrate/index.ts`) — `Map<string, VerbHandler | Map<string, VerbHandler>>`. `--help` walks the registry so the read/mutate classification table cannot drift from the implementation (guarded by a unit test).
- **Centralized arg validation** in `src/schemas/cli-args.ts` — one zod schema per verb plus shared primitives (`TaskIdSchema`, UUIDv7 schemas for run/claim/attempt/question, `DecisionKeySchema`, `PhaseSchema`, `RoutingHintSchema`).
- **`src/orchestrator/overlap.ts`** (absorbed FORGE-79) — pure file-glob classifier consumed by `phases --ready` to tag candidates `no-overlap | soft-overlap | hard-overlap`. Tasks without declared `write_globs` default to worst-case-assume-overlap-on-hard-lock-only.
- **`TaskSchema.status` + `TaskSchema.write_globs`** — optional fields on phases.yaml task entries; the loader was previously silently dropping these.
- **3-task e2e integration test** spawns `dist/bin/forge.cjs` and drives the full lifecycle (run start → phases → claim → dispatch → heartbeat → question → cancel | complete) against a fixture. `FORGE_NOOP_TRACKER=1` keeps it hermetic.
- **Dropped without alias**: `next`, `suggest-next`, `session-check`, `intent-detect`. Replacements: `phases --ready` for listing, `status` for re-grounding, `/amend-roadmap` for intent.

## Why

P2.5-T05 ships the simplified CLI surface that the rest of Phase 2.5 sits on top of:
- Dispatch skill rewrite (FORGE-98) builds on the read/mutate split.
- Doctor scopes (FORGE-99) extend the `--scope` flag.
- Reconcile (FORGE-100, just merged) now flows through the same dispatcher.

The dropped verbs were redundant in the simplified design — sole-user decision, no compat shim per plan F4.

## Forks asked & answered (in plan)

| Fork | Answer |
|---|---|
| F1 doctor scope | A — SPEC↔code only; ADR scopes return `SCOPE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| F2 file layout | A — migrate all 6 existing verb files into `src/cli/orchestrate/` (via `git mv` so blame follows) |
| F4 `run` depth | A — 3-level `run start | list` (nested Map in dispatcher) |
| F10 overlap | B — absorb FORGE-79 into this PR |
| F6 zod schemas | A — centralized `src/schemas/cli-args.ts` |
| F7 e2e test | A — `node --test` spawns `dist/bin/forge.cjs` subprocess |

## Known limitations (documented in code)

1. **Tracker wiring deferred to FORGE-98**: claim/dispatch/heartbeat use a `ClaimableTracker` interface. Production wiring reads `.forge/settings.yaml` but currently returns `NO_TRACKER_CONFIGURED` for real configs; `FORGE_NOOP_TRACKER=1` or missing settings yields a `NoopTracker`. This keeps FORGE-96 scope tight and unblocks the dispatch-skill PR that will provide the real factory.
2. **Heartbeat fencing**: spec line 181 has no `--claim` flag, so the verb reads identity from `lease.json` to renew. The lower-level `leases.heartbeat()` still has the proper LEASE_STOLEN fence; CLI-level detection of stale workers is a follow-up.
3. **`verdict.verified.json`**: CLI self-attest only in v0.4; full re-verification (re-running tests + lint via spawnSync) is a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — green
- [x] `npm test` — 1034 / 0 / 11 (skipped) — includes 83 new tests across overlap (18), envelope (8), cli-args schemas (16), phases/doctor/run-list/run-start (15), claim/dispatch/heartbeat (12), question/event/complete/cancel (10), help-drift (4), 3-task e2e (3)
- [x] `npm run build` — green
- [x] `npm run test:pack` — 0 forbidden paths in tarball
- [x] `node dist/bin/forge.cjs --version` — 0.2.2
- [x] `node dist/bin/forge.cjs orchestrate` — classification table renders
- [x] `gitleaks detect` — no leaks
- [x] Merged `origin/main` (FORGE-100 reconcile + FORGE-115 worktree std) and rewired reconcile through the new verb table

## Linked

### Motivation
- Fornecer um backend em Django para servir as páginas estáticas e expor uma API JSON para persistência dos itens cadastrados pelo frontend.
- Substituir chamadas locais diretas entre arquivos HTML por rotas e recursos gerenciados pela aplicação web para facilitar deploy e evolução.

### Description
- Adiciona um projeto Django mínimo (`producao/`) com `manage.py`, `settings.py`, `urls.py` e `wsgi.py`, e configura `STATICFILES_DIRS` para servir `style.css` a partir de `/static/`.
- Cria o app `core` com o modelo `Item` em `core/models.py` e views em `core/views.py` que renderizam as páginas (`/`, `/dashboard/`, `/itens/`, `/usuarios/`) e implementam a API `GET/POST /api/itens/` para listar e cadastrar itens em JSON (endpoint CSRF-exempt para uso simples via fetch).
- Atualiza os templates estáticos (`index.html`, `dashboard.html`, `itens.html`, `usuarios.html`) para usar rotas Django e `/static/style.css`, e adiciona JavaScript em `itens.html` que consome a API com `fetch` para carregar e cadastrar itens dinamicamente.
- Adiciona `requirements.txt` com `Django>=5.0,<6.0` e cria diretório de migrações (`core/migrations/__init__.py`).

### Testing
- Executei a tentativa de checagem e migrações com `python manage.py check && python manage.py makemigrations core && python manage.py migrate`, que falhou com `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'django'` porque o pacote Django não estava instalado no ambiente.
- Tentei instalar dependências com `pip install django -q`, que falhou por limitação de rede/índice de pacotes no ambiente (erro de conexão/403), impedindo a execução de comandos de gerenciamento do Django.
- Os arquivos e alterações foram validados localmente no repositório (estrutura e alterações de templates e views), e a aplicação pode ser totalmente testada seguindo: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `python manage.py makemigrations core`, `python manage.py migrate`, `python manage.py runserver` e abrindo `http://127.0.0.1:8000/itens/` para testar listagem e cadastro.

## Summary

This PR codifies the Scarab SSOT-only pull-loop invariant as ADR-0042 and blocks active Railway push-path control for the scarab fleet.

Invariant:
- scarabs stay live on Railway after one deploy
- scarabs poll `ssot.scarab_strategy` for optimizer/format/hidden/lr/seed/steps/status

author: bootjp
body:
## Summary

Stage 6C-2d per the [PR #762 plan](https://github.com/bootjp/elastickv/pull/762) and the 6C sub-decomposition landed in PR #781 / #782 / #783.

Ties the encryption-side guard primitive ([PR #782 `GuardSidecarBehindRaftLog`](https://github.com/bootjp/elastickv/pull/782)) to the raftengine-side scanner ([PR #783 `Engine.EncryptionScanner()`](https://github.com/bootjp/elastickv/pull/783)) in `main.go`'s startup phase. **Completes the §9.1 `ErrSidecarBehindRaftLog` work end-to-end.**

## What this PR ships

### `main_encryption_startup_guard.go` (new)

| Function | Role |
|---|---|
| `checkSidecarBehindRaftLog(runtimes, defaultGroup, sidecarPath, encryptionEnabled)` | Locates the default-group runtime, type-asserts its engine to local `encryptionGapEngine` interface, reads the §5.1 sidecar, delegates to the inner helper |
| `runSidecarBehindRaftLogGuard(gapEngine, sidecarPath, defaultGroup)` | Per-engine inner half. Split out so tests use a stub instead of constructing a full `raftengine.Engine` |
| `chainEncryptionStartupGuard(prevErr, ...)` | Composes the guard with the existing `buildShardGroups` error path. Keeps `run()`'s cyclop budget intact |

### Lifecycle phase ordering

```
1. loadKEKAndRunStartupGuards   ← 6B-2 RPC gate + 6C-1/6C-2 flag/sidecar/exhaustion
2. buildShardGroups             ← opens every shard's engine
3. chainEncryptionStartupGuard  ← 6C-2d gap-coverage guard (NEW)
4. gRPC servers / accept loop
```

Step 3 runs in a **different lifecycle phase** from steps 1 — the guard requires the engine to be open and its applied index populated from WAL+snapshot replay.

### Skip conditions (`checkSidecarBehindRaftLog` returns nil)

- `encryptionEnabled` is false — no encryption opt-in, no gap to refuse on
- `sidecarPath` is empty — operator hasn't configured a sidecar location
- On-disk sidecar file absent — bootstrap hasn't committed yet
- Default-group runtime missing — no engine to query
- Engine not open — earlier startup-guard layer would have caught this

### Why scope is restricted to the default group

The §5.1 sidecar tracks a **single** `raft_applied_index`, advanced only by `WriteSidecar` calls in `ApplyBootstrap` / `ApplyRotation` on the default group's FSM. Other shards' Raft logs don't carry encryption FSM entries — running the guard against them would always report caught-up (gap == 0). `findDefaultGroupRuntime` silently skips non-matching runtimes.

## Test coverage (11 new tests)

| Test | Path |
|---|---|
| `_DisabledNoop` | `encryptionEnabled=false` → skip |
| `_NoSidecarPathNoop` | empty path → skip |
| `_SidecarAbsentNoop` | on-disk file missing → skip |
| `_SidecarStatError` | I/O error (NUL path) → wrapped, NOT `not-exist` |
| `_NoRuntimes` | no default-group runtime → skip |
| `_CaughtUp` | sidecar idx >= engine idx → pass, scanner never consulted |
| `_GapNotCovered` | gap exists, scanner says no → pass |
| `_GapCovered` | gap covers relevant entry → `ErrSidecarBehindRaftLog` |
| `_ScannerError` | scanner error → propagated wrapped, NOT `ErrSidecarBehindRaftLog` |
| `_PropagatesPrevError` | chain with non-nil prev → returns prev verbatim |
| `_NilPrevRunsGuard` | chain with nil prev → forwards to guard |

Tests use `stubGapEngine` + `stubScanner` to exercise the per-engine inner function directly, avoiding the full `raftengine.Engine` interface (which would require panic-stubs for ~30 unrelated methods).

## Posture matrix (before/after this PR)

| Scenario | pre-this-PR | post-this-PR |
|---|---|---|
| Sidecar caught up to engine | boot, encrypted | boot, encrypted |
| Sidecar behind, gap harmless (no §5.5 opcodes) | boot, encrypted | boot, encrypted |
| Sidecar behind, gap covers `OpBootstrap` / `OpRotation` | **boot, HaltApply on first post-cutover read with `unknown_key_id`** | refuse: `ErrSidecarBehindRaftLog` |
| Sidecar behind, gap covers only `OpRegistration` | boot, registry replays cleanly | boot (PR #782 narrowed predicate excludes 0x03) |

## Caller audit (per cron directive)

No public function signatures changed. The new functions in `main_encryption_startup_guard.go` are package-internal. `main.go run()` is the sole production caller; tests call the inner helpers directly.

The semantic effect of the wiring: nodes whose sidecar is behind by an encryption-relevant interval now refuse at startup instead of silently booting into a HaltApply later. This is a tighter failure boundary — operators see the §9.1 typed refusal pointing at `encryption resync-sidecar` rather than triaging downstream `unknown_key_id` errors.

## Stage 6B-2 / 6C-1 / 6C-2 / 6C-2b / 6C-2c invariants preserved

All earlier guards and their lifecycle phases unchanged. This PR composes existing primitives — no new sentinel, no new opcode, no new wire format.

## Five-lens self-review

1. **Data loss** — net-positive. Catches the partial-write-crash failure mode between an encryption-relevant Raft commit and the sidecar update. The guard primitive existed since PR #782 but was operator-inert until this wiring.
2. **Concurrency / distributed failures** — runs at startup before any goroutine fan-out / gRPC accept. No shared state introduced.
3. **Performance** — single sidecar read + single scanner call per process start on the happy path.
4. **Data consistency** — the only §9.1 mechanism that catches "Raft committed but sidecar missed it" partial writes. Without it the first post-cutover read would HaltApply.
5. **Test coverage** — 11 new tests cover every branch. Full main package test suite passes with no regressions.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race -timeout=180s .` — PASS (all main package tests + 11 new)
- [x] `go test -race -timeout=120s ./internal/raftengine/etcd/... ./internal/encryption/...` — PASS (no regressions)
- [x] `go build ./...` — PASS
- [x] `golangci-lint run .` — 0 issues (cyclop holds at 10 via the composition helper)
- [ ] Full Jepsen suite — not run; the guard is purely a startup refusal that runs before any Raft entry can be served

## Plan

**Stage 6C is now complete** (6C-1 ✅ + 6C-2 ✅ + 6C-2b ✅ + 6C-2c ✅ + 6C-2d this PR).

Next stages per PR #762:
- **6C-3** — `ErrNodeIDCollision` + `ErrLocalEpochRollback` (bundles with Stage 6D's capability fan-out)
- **6D** — `enable-storage-envelope` admin RPC + §7.1 Phase-1 cutover (**now UNBLOCKED** — all `ErrSidecarBehindRaftLog` work has shipped)
- **6E** — `enable-raft-envelope` admin RPC + §7.1 Phase-2 cutover (bundles 6C-4)
- **6F** — `--encryption-rotate-on-startup` ergonomics

author: tas50
body:
## What

Adds the `aws.appsync` resource family so audits can query AWS AppSync managed GraphQL APIs.

- **`aws.appsync.graphqlApi`** — primary `authenticationType` and `additionalAuthenticationProviders`, CloudWatch field-logging level (`logFieldLogLevel`, `logExcludeVerboseContent`, `logCloudWatchLogsRole`), `xrayEnabled`, the `webAcl` guarding the endpoint, `queryDepthLimit`/`resolverCountLimit`, `introspectionConfig`, `visibility`, `apiType`, `uris`, `tags`, `ownerContact`, and the response-cache state via `cache*` fields (lazily fetched via `GetApiCache`; null when no cache is provisioned).
- **`aws.appsync.apiKey`** — API keys issued for an API (`id`, `description`, `expires`, `deletes`).

## Why

Closes the [AWS Foundational Security Best Practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/appsync-controls.html) AppSync control gap — AppSync was the only FSBP-relevant service entirely unmodeled in the provider:

| FSBP control | mql field |
|---|---|
| AppSync.2 — field-level logging enabled | `logFieldLogLevel` |
| AppSync.4 — GraphQL APIs should be tagged | `tags` |
| AppSync.5 — should not use API-key auth | `authenticationType` + `additionalAuthenticationProviders` |
| AppSync.6 — API caches encrypted at rest | `cacheAtRestEncryptionEnabled` |
| AppSync.7 — API caches encrypted in transit | `cacheTransitEncryptionEnabled` |

## Notes

- Cache config is flattened onto `graphqlApi` with a `cache` prefix rather than a sub-resource — the API cache has no natural ID and holds no typed references.
- Resolvers, data sources, types, functions, and the newer Event APIs are intentionally out of scope; none are needed for FSBP.
- The permissions extractor is taught the `Appsync` client method so `appsync:ListGraphqlApis`, `appsync:GetApiCache`, and `appsync:ListApiKeys` land in `aws.permissions.json`.
- New `.lr.versions` entries are at `13.25.1` (provider is `13.25.0`); `config.go` is untouched.

## Verification

Built and installed the provider, then verified against a live AppSync API (created and torn down): all fields — including `cache*`, `apiKeys` time conversion, `uris`, the `apiId` selection key, and a null `webAcl` — resolved correctly. Region iteration confirmed across an account with no APIs (clean empty results).

author: copilot
body:
## Fix `regenerate-articles.yml` failure

[Run 25999650147 / job 76420346217](https://github.com/Hack23/euparliamentmonitor/actions/runs/25999650147/job/76420346217) failed in the **Commit regenerated articles** step with:
```
fatal: pathspec 'analysis/daily/**/article.meta.json' did not match any files
```

### Root cause
The aggregator writes the run sidecar as `article-meta.json` (hyphen), not `article.meta.json` (dot) — confirmed by `scripts/aggregator/article-generator.js` and the existing on-disk layout under `analysis/daily/<date>/<slug>/article-meta.json`. Because the workflow step runs under default `bash -e`, the unmatched git pathspec aborted the whole step before any commit could happen, so no regenerated `article.md` / news HTML changes were ever committed even though step 7 (`npm run generate-article:all`) succeeded.

The neighbouring comment also misdescribed the news output: in reality the aggregator writes a single English Markdown source `news/<date>-<slug>.en.md` plus 14 language HTML variants `news/<date>-<slug>-<lang>.html` — not 14 markdown files.

### Change
`.github/workflows/regenerate-articles.yml`:
- `analysis/daily/**/article.meta.json` → `analysis/daily/**/article-meta.json`
- Comment block aligned with the real aggregator output.

### Verification
Locally, all four corrected pathspecs resolve to tracked files:
- `git ls-files 'analysis/daily/**/article.md'` ✓
- `git ls-files 'analysis/daily/**/article-meta.json'` ✓
- `git ls-files 'news/*.md'` ✓
- `git ls-files 'news/*.html'` ✓

Once merged, re-running the **Regenerate Articles** workflow (`workflow_dispatch`) will execute `npm run generate-article:all`, then successfully stage and commit every regenerated `article.md`, `article-meta.json`, English `.en.md`, and 14-language HTML file.

## Summary

Implements PR 6 of the chat UI feature: messages render when a conversation tab is active, with per-conversation scroll, own vs other alignment, and timestamps. Also adds a small client-side account cache so sender labels can show usernames instead of UUIDs.

### Account cache (new `client/src/account/`)

- `AccountState { own_account_id: RwLock<Option<Uuid>>, cache: DashMap<Uuid, AccountPublicSerial>, in_flight: DashMap<Uuid, ()> }` wired onto `STATE`.
- `RwLock<Option<Uuid>>` rather than `OnceLock` so a future logout/login or reconnect-as-different-account can re-set it.
- Catch-up: `GET /account` first (sets `own_account_id`, caches own public account); after fetching members per conversation, fills any uncached usernames via `GET /account/{id}` per missing id.
- WS chat / member-joined events trigger a deduped lazy fetch (`spawn_fetch_if_missing`) for unknown senders so future renders resolve the username.
- `AccountPublicSerial` (in `shared`) gains `Deserialize`.

### Message view

- New `draw_conversation_view` for the `ChatTab::Conversation(id)` arm.
- Header via `draw_panel_header` (`<name>  (<n> members)`); long names truncate with ellipsis.
- Body in the per-conversation `VerticalScrollRegion` (already on `ConversationViewState`).
- Each message: sender header line `<username> | <Mon D HH:MM:SS local> (<rel>)` (UUID fallback when username isn't cached yet) + body wrapped via `text_wrap::wrap_text`.
- Own messages right-aligned; other messages left-aligned. Wrap width is `0.88 *` inner width.
- Sender label color is `WINDOW_INTERIOR_BORDER_COLOR` placeholder; per-account hashing is PR 8.

### Auto-scroll-to-bottom (encapsulated in `VerticalScrollRegion`)

- Internal `pending_snap_to_bottom` flag; `scroll_to_bottom()` flips it; `update()` consumes it (snap to new `max_scroll`) or otherwise clamps `scroll_offset` to `[0, max_scroll]`.
- `scroll_clamped()` (user wheel) clears the flag, so a pending snap is cancelled if the user scrolls.
- `is_at_bottom()` reports either current-at-max or pending-snap.
- `ConversationViewState::new()` initializes with `scroll_to_bottom()` so opening a tab lands on the latest messages.
- `handle_message` queries `is_at_bottom()` once and calls `scroll_to_bottom()` if true; no per-frame check, no draw-side conditional.

### Misc

- `ScrollHandler` now routes scroll wheel to the active tab's region (list vs conversation).
- Debug seed: moved into `ws::hook::after_connect` so it runs after `catch_up`, lets it use the live `own_account_id`. Adds a `me` account, several `me` messages across conversations, and a long-wrapping own message for visual verification.

### Plan / spec updates

- `plans/2026-05-08-chat-ui-design.md`: added "Account cache" to the data layer, dropped the "you" special-case for own messages.
- `plans/2026-05-09-chat-ui-plan.md`: replaced the stale PR 6 stub with an up-to-date contract.

## Summary
Older EM tables (Abra Ca Dabra, 4 Roses, 4X4 Atari, ...) store high scores in VPReg.ini using a different shape than the modern HighScoreN one:
- `hiscore=N` for the single high score
- `hsa1`/`hsa2`/`hsa3` as 1-indexed positions into a fixed 38-char alphabet (`"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_<"`) for the initials

The alphabet is fully consistent across the 100+ extracted scripts I surveyed; encoding test: `hsa1=4 hsa2=15 hsa3=7` -> `D`,`O`,`G`.

## What's new
- `scores::vpreg::extract_sections` falls back to `try_legacy_em` when the modern HighScoreN scan misses; decode using the canonical alphabet.
- `indexer::extract_vpreg_section_keys` regex extended to surface the section name from `LoadValue(<arg>, "hiscore")` / `"hsa<N>"` calls too, so the dispatcher can find the section in scripts that don't use HighScoreN at all.

## Coverage
- Abra Ca Dabra (real played file): now reports `DOG 10000`.
- Bulk rescan: OK 400 -> 409 (+9); no-high-scores bucket 479 -> 470.
- Regressions clean on Matrix (modern VPReg), 2 in 1 (single-hisc EM), Carnaval (Black's 5+5), Aerosmith (multi-key VPReg).

## Tests
- 6 new vpreg.rs tests: Abra Ca Dabra shape, missing-hsa, zero hiscore fall-through, extended-alphabet decode (`0_<`), out-of-range index drop.
- 1 new indexer.rs test: legacy LoadValue keys surface the section name.
- 152/152 total tests pass; clippy + fmt clean.

## Dependency
Stacked on #788 (multi-section-key VPReg) - the legacy parser needs the section-key extractor to find sections in tables that use hardcoded literal section names like `"Abra_Ca_Dabra"`. Should land after #788.
