body: Addresses #13068, only the part about the Plots action bar (not the Viewer action bar, which can come in a separate PR) This PR reworks the plots pane action bar to consolidate the three "Open somewhere else" affordances we had (popout for HTML plots, the editor target dropdown for regular plots, and "Open plots gallery in new window") into a single split button dropdown on the right side, with the same Positron custom icon that we use on the editor. The dropdown's contents adapt to the current plot type, and "Open Plots Gallery in New Window" is always present as the last entry below a separator (hopefully to indicate that it's a different kind of action): Other action bar changes here: - Dark filter moved from the right side to the left, because I think we should not prioritize it so much compared to the "Open somewhere else" actions and it makes the more-used behavior persist more at smaller widths: - Separator added between "Copy plot to clipboard" and the Zoom dropdown, to highlight that these all work similarly to each other (same kind of buttons with similar UX): - The new split button's primary (icon) click repeats the user's most recent choice. The choice is persisted to the storage service via the plots service, so it survives closing the gallery, switching plots, or reloading the window. - When no prior choice applies to the current plot type, the menu visually checks the fallback action so the user can see what the primary click will do. - I updated the user-facing strings to be consistent with the project style (title case). I'll highlight that _before_ this change, an HTML plot open in the auxiliary window plots gallery WOULD have a button to open it in a new window (i.e. a browser) but now it does not. Static plots never had that ability in the auxiliary window. I think the consistency here is good. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Consolidate the plots pane's "Open in..." actions into a single dropdown with consistent placement and iconography (#13068) ### Validation Steps @:plots @:web @:win 1. Generate a regular plot (matplotlib / ggplot). Confirm the action bar shows a single "Open in..." split-button on the right, plus Clear all. 2. Open the dropdown. Confirm it lists "Open in New Window", "Open in Editor Tab", "Open in Editor Tab to the Side", a separator, then "Open Plots Gallery in New Window". 3. Click one of the editor-target options. Reopen the dropdown and confirm that option is checked. 4. Click the split-button's icon area (not the caret). Confirm it repeats the most recent choice. 5. Click "Open Plots Gallery in New Window". Close the gallery. Reopen the dropdown and confirm gallery is checked; primary click reopens the gallery. 6. Reload the window with the gallery preference set. Confirm the gallery remains the checked / default-click option. 7. Generate an HTML plot (e.g. plotly, htmlwidgets, shiny). Open the dropdown. Confirm it lists "Open Plot in New Window", a separator, then "Open Plots Gallery in New Window". 8. Click "Open Plot in New Window". Reopen the dropdown and confirm popout is checked. 9. With no plots in the pane, confirm the "Open in..." button is still visible and the dropdown shows just "Open Plots Gallery in New Window" (checked). 10. Confirm the Dark filter dropdown is now on the left side (after the sizing dropdown). 11. Confirm there is a visual separator between "Copy plot to clipboard" and the Zoom dropdown.

author: bmsull560
body:
## **User description** ## Summary Closes six P0 security gaps identified in the production assurance audit. The platform's tenant isolation score was 65% against a 95% GA target; this PR addresses the highest-severity items blocking release. **What changed and why:** - **RLS NULL bypass (3 migrations):** Migrations 014, 029, and 030 created RLS policies with `tenant_id IS NULL OR ...`, making rows without a `tenant_id` visible to every tenant. New migrations 032 (L4 billing + CRM) and 013 (L1 crawl_decisions) replace those policies with strict `tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)` matching. Migration 029 is patched in-place. All fix migrations drop and recreate both `tenant_isolation_policy` and `admin_bypass_policy` to ensure a consistent policy set. - **Permission wildcard bypass:** `has_permission` accepted `"*"` and `"all"` as wildcards granting all access. `extract_context_from_jwt` stored raw JWT permission strings verbatim, so a JWT with `permissions: ["*"]` produced a context that passed every permission check. Both are now fixed: `extract_context_from_jwt` filters to known `Permission` enum values only; `has_permission` uses a single-pass enum-only lookup and fails closed on unknown strings. - **Tenant lifecycle enforcement:** `GovernanceMiddleware.dispatch()` did not enforce `pending` or `deleted` tenant status — only `suspended` had an exception class (never raised). The dispatch path now rejects suspended (403), pending (403), and deleted (404) tenants before `call_next`, reading `tenant_status` from `ctx.raw`. `PendingTenantError` and `DeletedTenantError` exception classes added. - **P0 test coverage:** Six test files added or expanded to cover the above gaps and prevent regression. ## Governance Impact (Required for backend/frontend/API changes) - **Contract shape impact:** None — no API response shapes changed. - **Tenant isolation impact:** Behavior changed and covered — RLS policies tightened, permission checks hardened, lifecycle enforcement added. - **Compatibility shim impact:** None. - [x] I verified tenant scoping and authenticated context handling for affected backend data paths. ## Change Type - [x] Bug fix ## API Evolution (Required for Phase 3 Feature Tickets) N/A — no route changes. ## Release & Policy Checklist (Required) - [x] No API contract changes — `contracts/openapi/` not affected. - [x] No deprecations introduced. ## Validation - **101 passed, 76 skipped, 0 failed, 0 xfailed** across the full security test suite. - Skips are pre-existing (require live FastAPI TestClient / infrastructure not available in unit test environment). - All new and modified test files compile and collect cleanly. ``` pytest tests/security/test_permission_bypass.py \ tests/security/test_rls_enforcement.py \ tests/security/test_jwt_config_validation.py \ tests/security/test_rbac.py \ tests/security/test_tenant_lifecycle.py \ tests/security/test_neo4j_rls_write.py \ tests/security/test_tenant_mismatch.py \ tests/security/test_jwt_validation.py \ tests/security/test_cross_tenant_write.py \ tests/security/test_auth_boundaries.py \ tests/security/test_auth_source_validation.py # 101 passed, 76 skipped in 2.70s ``` ## Risks / Rollback - **Known risks:** Tenant lifecycle enforcement reads `tenant_status` from `ctx.raw` (decoded JWT claims). If issued tokens do not include `tenant_status`, the check is a no-op — a separate DB lookup would be needed for out-of-band status changes. This is documented in the code. - **RLS migration rollback:** `downgrade()` functions restore the original NULL-permissive policies. Migration 032 `downgrade()` recreates `admin_bypass_policy` without `WITH CHECK` to match the original definitions from migrations 014/030. - **Permission change rollback:** `has_permission` and `extract_context_from_jwt` changes are backward-compatible — valid `Permission` enum values continue to work identically. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Close tenant isolation and permission bypass gaps** ### What Changed - Tenant-scoped data now uses strict tenant matching in affected tables, so rows without a tenant ID are no longer visible across tenants - Permission checks now reject wildcard and unknown permission claims, so `*` and `all` no longer grant access - Requests from suspended, pending, or deleted tenants are blocked before business logic runs, with suspended and pending returning 403 and deleted returning 404 - Added regression coverage for tenant isolation, permission bypasses, JWT validation, Neo4j write scoping, and tenant lifecycle enforcement ### Impact `✅ Fewer cross-tenant data leaks` `✅ No wildcard permission bypass` `✅ Clearer blocked-tenant responses`

author: manisharadwad
body:
The isGpuAccelerationSupported() method previously gated premium model tiers (Qwen3-1.7B Q8_0, Gemma4 E2B Q8_0) to only Qualcomm Adreno GPU devices, excluding Mali (Exynos, Tensor, Dimensity) and PowerVR GPUs entirely.

This was wrong because:
- llama.cpp Vulkan/OpenCL is 10-15x slower than CPU on ALL Android GPUs
- The app builds llama.cpp CPU-only (all GPU backends OFF)
- GPU vendor has no correlation with CPU inference capability
- It created artificial device bias that excluded high-end phones like Pixel 9 Pro (Tensor/Mali) from the best model tier

Fix: use CPU feature detection (ARM i8mm + dotprod instructions) as the heuristic instead. These are ARM v8.2-A/v8.6-A matrix multiplication instructions that genuinely accelerate LLM inference on CPU, making them the correct performance predictor regardless of GPU vendor.

Also fixed assessDevice() to call isGpuAccelerationSupported() instead of duplicating the same logic inline.

💡 **What:** Added a new method `log_metrics_many` to `DatabaseManager` that uses `executemany` for batch inserting metrics. Updated `ingest_data.py` to accumulate metrics in a list and call the new method instead of calling `log_metrics` sequentially inside a loop.

- Improvement: ~99.5% faster execution time for metric logging

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #135. Adds `triangle_descriptor_database.hpp` so the STD-style
triangle primitives can drive actual place recognition:

- **Hashing** (`quantizeEdges` + `packHash`): sorted edges → uint64 bucket key. Edges within `edge_bin_m` share a bucket so noisy descriptors still match.
- **TriangleDatabase**: hash → list of `(submap_id, vertex positions)` so geometric verification works without re-reading keypoints.
- **`accumulateVotes`**: per-query hash lookup with `max_votes_per_query` cap (avoid dominance from one degenerate bucket) and `exclude_submap_id` for adjacent-frame suppression.
- **`findLoopCandidate`**: top-voted submap → RANSAC over matching triangle pairs using `estimateRigidFromTriangle`. Accepts when `min_inliers` proposals agree on SE(3) within `inlier_translation_m` / `inlier_rotation_deg`.

All under BSD-2 so the default workflow keeps it (vs GPLv2 STD).

## Wave 1 / B2 — axios chain bump (15 Dependabot HIGH alerts)

### Problem
`axios@0.21.4` was pulled in via a 4-level transitive chain:
```
angular-audio@1.7.3
  └── browser-sync@2.29.3 (vendored, legacy)
        └── localtunnel@2.0.2
              └── axios@0.21.4
```

This chain triggered **15 Dependabot HIGH alerts** (CVE-2023-45857,
CVE-2024-39338, CVE-2024-57965, CVE-2025-27152, CVE-2025-54371,
CVE-2025-58754…) covering SSRF, ReDoS, prototype pollution, and
credentials leakage.

### Why `npm overrides`
The parent chain is unmaintainable from our side: `angular-audio` is an
abandoned AngularJS 1.x plugin pinning `browser-sync 2.x`. `npm update`
cannot reach `axios` (depth-4 transitive). `overrides` is the standard
npm mechanism for forcing a secure version of a transitive dep.

Override target: `^0.31.1` — last patch of the `0.x` line, the only
line `browser-sync 2.x` is compatible with.

### Validation
- Post-override lockfile: `node_modules/axios = 0.31.1` (was 0.21.4) ✅
- `npm audit`: **axios no longer appears in advisories** ✅
- Aggregated count: 40 → 38 (npm audit group-by; Dependabot will close
  the 15 axios alerts on next scan)

- `client/package.json`: +3 / 0 (new `overrides` block)
- `client/package-lock.json`: regenerated (+70 / -14)

- npm Dependabot remaining: -15 axios alerts

author: sebastienrousseau
body:
## Problem

Visitors with French-language browsers were getting 302'd to \`/fr/\` on every visit to the apex, even when they explicitly clicked an EN link from a search result or shared message. Many of those readers are bilingual, prefer the canonical EN copy, and don't realise a redirect just happened. Multiple complaints rolled in.

## Fix

The Worker still honours the two explicit opt-ins:

- **\`pref-lang=<lang>\` cookie** — set by clicking the in-page locale switcher (30-day TTL)
- **\`?lang=<lang>\` deep-link** — sets the cookie and 302s

Everything else now lands on the canonical EN homepage. Accept-Language is no longer sniffed. \`parseAcceptLanguage\` and \`pickSiteLang\` plus the BCP-47 \`TAG_TO_LANG\` table go away — they had no other callers. Net: -235 +36 lines.

## Test coverage

43 tests, 100 % line / branch / function coverage on \`workers/lang-router.js\`. The handler tests that previously asserted Accept-Language redirects now assert pass-through. A new regression test pins the behavior so any future re-introduction of A-L sniffing fails CI:

\`\`\`
handler: Accept-Language fr-FR no longer triggers a redirect
\`\`\`

All 14 in-repo gates pass locally.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (build + diff + accessibility + lighthouse + Worker 100 % coverage)
- [ ] After merge + \`npx wrangler deploy\`: \`curl -sI -H \"Accept-Language: fr-FR,fr;q=0.9\" https://sebastienrousseau.com/\` returns 200, not 302
- [ ] \`curl -sI -H \"Cookie: pref-lang=fr\" https://sebastienrousseau.com/\` still returns 302 to \`/fr/\` (explicit cookie still honoured)
- [ ] \`curl -sI \"https://sebastienrousseau.com/?lang=de\"\` still 302s to \`/de/\` and sets the cookie

## Deployment note

This PR changes Worker behavior, so the rollout is **merge → \`cd workers && npx --yes wrangler@latest deploy\`** to push the new code to the edge. Until that second step runs, the live Worker keeps the old Accept-Language behavior.

body:
Fixes #1254.

Master CI Playwright fail-fast on every push since #1252:

```
❌ Mobile viewport (375px): observer IATA badge stays visible — not clipped:
   .badge-iata right edge 376.25 exceeds 375px viewport
```

## Root cause

After #1252 unhid `.col-observer` at narrow widths so the IATA pill from
#1188 renders on mobile, at 375px the cell padding + truncated observer
name (10 chars in grouped rows) + `.badge-iata` pill (`padding: 1px 5px`
+ `margin-left: 4px`) sums to ~376.25px — overflowing the viewport by
1.25px.

Same class of failure as #1250/#1251 (VCR LCD-clip).

## Fix

`public/style.css` — inside the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)`
block, shrink `.badge-iata` `padding: 1px 5px → 1px 3px` and
`margin-left: 4px → 2px`. Reclaims ~6px horizontally, well clear of the
1.25px overflow. Desktop (≥641px) styling untouched.

The failing E2E sub-test in `test-observer-iata-1188-e2e.js` (added in
#1189 R1) IS the red. Mutation verified locally:

| Variant            | Result |
|--------------------|--------|
| WITHOUT this fix   | ❌ `.badge-iata right edge 376.25 exceeds 375px viewport` |
| WITH this fix      | ✅ all 3 sub-tests pass |

```

All observer-IATA E2E tests passed.
```

- All colors via existing CSS variables (no theming illusions; only

author: lukeevanstech
body:
## Summary

Profilarr v2.0.0 ([release post](https://old.reddit.com/r/radarr/comments/1tg27tq/profilarr_v2_is_out/)) — new upstream registry, new parser sidecar, new auth/env model.

- **Image registry change**: `docker.io/santiagosayshey/profilarr:v1.1.4` → `ghcr.io/dictionarry-hub/profilarr:2.0.0` (`sha256:f66cfde5…`).
- **Parser sidecar** added: `ghcr.io/dictionarry-hub/profilarr-parser:2.0.0` (`sha256:2d3094fe…`) on `localhost:5000`. Required for the v2 custom-format / quality-profile test UI; linking, syncing, upgrades all work without it but the testing UX is degraded if it's absent.
- **LSIO-style env**: `PUID=1000`, `PGID=1000`, `UMASK=022`, `AUTH=on` (first-user signup), `ORIGIN=https://profilarr.\${SECRET_DOMAIN}`, `PARSER_HOST=localhost`, `PARSER_PORT=5000`.
- **Mounts**: `/config` and `/home` are now scoped to the `app` container via `advancedMounts`. The parser is stateless and shares only `/tmp`.

## ⚠️ v1 → v2 is a destructive migration

Per the release notes: *"v2 is not compatible with v1. The underlying database and customisation systems changed significantly, so existing v1 databases/configs/appdata won't work directly in v2."*

The existing `profilarr` PVC (5Gi, `ceph-block`) must be wiped before the new pod starts. Merging this PR alone is **not** enough — the wipe must be done by hand.

## Rollout runbook

```bash
# 1. Pause Flux so it doesn't fight the wipe
flux -n media suspend hr profilarr
flux -n media suspend ks profilarr

# 2. Tear down the running pod, then the PVC (must be in this order)
kubectl -n media delete deploy profilarr --wait=true
kubectl -n media delete pvc   profilarr --wait=true

# 3. Merge this PR.

# 4. Bring it back — Flux recreates an empty PVC, then rolls v2 + parser
flux -n media resume ks profilarr
flux -n media resume hr profilarr
flux -n media reconcile ks profilarr --with-source

# 5. Watch it come up
kubectl -n media get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=profilarr -w
kubectl -n media logs -f deploy/profilarr -c app
kubectl -n media logs -f deploy/profilarr -c parser
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Local `flux-local build hr` renders cleanly (verified: two containers, /config scoped to `app`, parser TCP probes on 5000).
- [ ] CI `Flux Local - Diff` posts the expected manifest delta.
- [ ] After rollout: pod is `2/2 Running`, app container shows v2 startup, parser container listens on 5000.
- [ ] First-visit signup flow works at `https://profilarr.\${SECRET_DOMAIN}`.
- [ ] Connect Dictionarry database (default) and confirm sync to Radarr/Sonarr instances.
- [ ] Spot-check CF testing UI to confirm the parser sidecar is reachable.

author: vibecoderst
body:
## Summary Removed the `FALLBACK_NEAT_AI_VERSION` constant from `src/utils/Version.ts`. The constant duplicated `deno.json` `version` and required a dedicated sync test in `test/creature/VersionStartupLog.ts` to police drift — a classic two-sources-of-truth footgun. Per KISS, the `file://` (local dev/test) load path now reads `deno.json` once at module load and treats it as the single source of truth. JSR consumers still derive the version from `import.meta.url` and see no behaviour change. The local-dev startup log line now carries a `(local)` suffix so it cannot be confused with the JSR-derived line. Closes #2720. ## Evidence This is a backend-only change with no UI; the evidence is the test suite for `src/utils/Version.ts`, which exercises the real `getNeatAiVersion()` and `logNeatAiVersionOnce()` functions and asserts on their outputs. ``` $ deno test --allow-all test/creature/VersionStartupLog.ts running 5 tests from ./test/creature/VersionStartupLog.ts Version: getNeatAiVersion returns a valid semver string ... ok (0ms) Version: local load path resolves the version from deno.json ... ok (0ms) Version: logNeatAiVersionOnce emits exactly once per process ... ok (0ms) Version: local file:// startup log carries the (local) suffix ... ok (0ms) Version: first Creature construction logs version, subsequent do not ... ok (3ms) ok | 5 passed | 0 failed (13ms) ``` Other quality output observed during the full test run confirms the new log format on the local path (e.g. `[neat-ai] running version 5.0.27 (local)` emitted by worker tests). ### Version-resolution flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Mod["src/utils/Version.ts loads"] --> Check{"import.meta.url
matches JSR pattern?"} Check -- "yes (https://jsr.io/...)" --> Parse["parse version from URL
(no file I/O)"] Check -- "no (file://)" --> Read["read deno.json once
(single source of truth)"] Parse --> Cache[("VERSION_INFO cached
at module load")] Read --> Cache Cache --> Get["getNeatAiVersion()"] Cache --> Log["logNeatAiVersionOnce()
appends ' (local)' on file:// path"] ``` ## Test Plan Modified `test/creature/VersionStartupLog.ts`: - **Removed** the sync test `Version: FALLBACK_NEAT_AI_VERSION matches deno.json version` — the constant it policed no longer exists, so there is nothing to sync. - **Replaced** with `Version: local load path resolves the version from deno.json`, which asserts that `getNeatAiVersion()` on the local (`file://`) load path agrees with `deno.json` `version`. author: josephsystems
body:
## Summary
Implements the foundational layer that every other feature in Lobby depends on. A user who clones the repo can now run `npm run setup`, answer a few questions, and end up with a `lobby.config.json` and a generated SQL migration ready to apply.
 
---
 
## What Changed
 
### New folders
- `types/` — TypeScript contracts. No logic, just shape definitions.
- `database/` — Framework-agnostic database utilities.
- `scripts/` — package manager scripts

### New files
 
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `types/config.ts` | Type definitions for `lobby.config.json` (`LobbyConfig`, `FieldDefinition`, `FieldType`) |
| `database/migration-generator.ts` | Generates SQL from config. Three exports: `generateInitialMigration`, `generateAddColumnsMigration`, `generateEditColumnsMigration` |
| `database/migration-runner.ts` | Applies pending `.sql` files from `migrations/`. Uses Kysely for tracking, raw `pg` for SQL execution |
| `scripts/setup.ts` | Interactive CLI wizard. Collects waitlist config, writes `lobby.config.json`, generates initial migration |
| `scripts/migration-run.ts` | Applies pending migrations. Reads `DATABASE_URL` from `.env` |
 
### Modified files
 
| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| `tsconfig.json` | Added `include`, `exclude`, `paths` for `types/*` and `database/*`, added `esModuleInterop` |
| `package.json` | Added `kysely`, `pg` to dependencies. Added `tsx`, `@types/pg` to devDependencies. Added `setup`, and `migration:run` scripts |
| `.gitignore` | Added `lobby.config.json`, `migrations/`, `.env` |
 
---
 
## Scripts Introduced
 
```bash
npm run setup          # Run once — collects config, writes lobby.config.json, generates initial migration
npm run migration:run  # Applies all pending migrations to the database
```
 
---
 
## Migration Architecture
 
Migrations are **per-instance** and **git-ignored**. Every deployment generates its own based on the fields chosen during setup. The `_lobby_migrations` table in Postgres tracks which files have been applied so they never run twice.
 
```
npm run setup
  └── writes lobby.config.json
  └── generates migrations/{timestamp}_initial_setup.sql
 
npm run migration:run
  └── creates _lobby_migrations table if not exists
  └── reads migrations/ directory
  └── skips already-applied files
  └── applies pending files in timestamp order (each in a transaction)
  └── records applied files in _lobby_migrations
```
 
Field-change script (PR 6) generates its own migration file and tells the user to run `migration:run` to apply it.
 
---
 
## How to Test
 
**Prerequisites:** A running PostgreSQL instance with a database created and `DATABASE_URL` set in `.env`.
 
**1. Run setup**
```bash
npm run setup
```
- Answer the prompts
- Confirm `lobby.config.json` was created at project root
- Confirm `migrations/{timestamp}_initial_setup.sql` was created
- Open the SQL file and verify the columns match what you selected
**2. Run migrations**
```bash
npm run migration:run
```
- Confirm the output shows `✓ {filename}`
- Connect to your database and verify:
  - `waitlist_entries` table exists with the correct columns
  - `_lobby_migrations` table exists with one row recording the applied file
  - Position trigger (`trg_waitlist_position`) exists
  - Updated-at trigger (`trg_waitlist_updated_at`) exists
**3. Re-running migration:run**
```bash
npm run migration:run
```
- Should output `All migrations already applied` — nothing runs twice
**4. Guard: re-running setup**
```bash
npm run setup
```
- Should immediately exit with:
  `lobby.config.json already exists. To edit or add fields, run: npm run fields`
---
 
## Notes
- `generateEditColumnsMigration` returns `null` when no fields actually changed. PR 6 field scripts use this to skip writing an empty migration file.
- Risky `ALTER TABLE` operations (type changes, `SET NOT NULL`) include warning comments in the generated SQL prompting the user to back up data first.

### Motivation

- Provide a Windows tray application to bridge custom status text into Steam Rich Presence (development using SpaceWar AppID `480`).
- Offer a lightweight UI for controlling status, sync interval, auto-start, dark mode, and current-playback integration. 
- Make the app resilient to missing Steam DLLs, Steam not running, and avoid duplicate instances while persisting user settings.

### Description

- Add core application entry and lifecycle: `Program.cs`, single-instance guard `SingleInstanceService.cs`, and main tray context `TrayApp.cs` which implements periodic callbacks, Steam init/retry, menu actions, status syncing and music polling. 
- Implement UI form `StatusForm.cs` with settings, presets, dark mode theming, window-size persistence and event hooks for user actions. 
- Add services: `SteamPresenceService.cs` (Steamworks init, robust Set/Clear Rich Presence, UTF-8 truncation), `MusicPresenceService.cs` (Windows system media session polling), `ConfigService.cs` (load/save JSON config at `%AppData%`), and `AutoStartService.cs` (user-level Run registry enable/disable).

Follow-up to #51 (merged at 246f3ec, before these commits landed). The 5 DiffTabs commits got orphaned on the branch after merge; reopening as a separate PR. The 4 already-merged triage commits will show as no-ops vs current dev.

Replaces the bottom-of-turn stack of \`▸ <preview> +N/-M\` collapsible chips with one CodeBlock-style frame whose header is a wrapping ribbon of file tabs (basenames). Active tab swaps the DiffBlock body.

- Gateway wraps \`inline_diff\` with \`┊ review diff\`, \`+N/-M\` summary, and \`…\` truncation lines. \`sanitizeDiff()\` strips them before \`DiffBlock\`.

author: czlonkowski
body:
## Summary

- Every route is now loaded via `React.lazy`. The Vite default chunker emits one chunk per dynamic `import()` boundary; the entry chunk shipped to a cold operator carries only React runtime + i18n bootstrap + Chrome shell + Skeleton/RouteSkeleton primitives. Route bodies stream in when needed.
- New `RouteSkeleton` composer maps each `Tab` → one of three shapes (table / cards / editor) and feeds it to the per-tab `<Suspense fallback=…>`. Built on B1's `Skeleton` primitives, so design-system invariants (no animation loop, no drop-shadow, `role="status"` announcement) carry through unchanged.
- Sidebar buttons fire a prefetch handler on `onMouseEnter` + `onFocus` (mouse and keyboard parity). The handler calls the matching dynamic `import()` — Vite's module-record cache dedupes against the post-click resolution, so a pre-warmed chunk resolves synchronously when the click lands.
- New `ROUTE_PREFETCH: Readonly<Record<Tab, () => Promise<unknown>>>` exported from `App.tsx` for exhaustiveness pinning: adding a new tab without wiring its prefetch is a TS compile error.

## Observed metrics (post-build, this branch)

- **Entry chunk: 95.53 KB gzipped** (47.7% of 200 KB budget).
- **22 JS chunks** in `dist/ui/assets/` (well above the 7 route-chunk floor).
- All 11 named routes surface as distinct chunks: Activity, Agents, Audit, Cost, Domains, LlmPolicy, Outputs, Prompts, Reports, Review, Sources.

## Tests (TDD)

`packages/ui/tests/unit/route-lazy.test.tsx` (6 tests):

author: whitphx
body:
## Summary

Closes the last deferral from #2450: applies the **loop / relay injection** pattern from #2447 (which originally decoupled `WebRtcWorker`) to `MediaStreamMixTrack`, then adds the **layer-2 mix tests** that were deferred because the class couldn't be constructed without a Streamlit `Runtime`.

## Refactor

`MediaStreamMixTrack.__init__` gains two optional keyword-only kwargs:

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    kind: str,
    mixer_callback: MixerCallback[FrameT],
    mixer_output_interval: float = 1 / 30,
    *,
    loop: Optional[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop] = None,
    relay: Optional[MediaRelay] = None,
) -> None:
```

When omitted, the resolver falls back to `get_global_event_loop()` and `get_global_relay()` — byte-for-byte the same behavior as before. Tests (and any non-Streamlit caller) can inject their own.

**Placement subtlety:** aiortc's `MediaStreamTrack.__init__` sets its own `self._loop` from the current event loop, so this class's `self._loop` assignment has to land *after* `super().__init__()` to avoid being clobbered. The original code already worked around this; the new version preserves the order with an explanatory comment.

## Tests

`tests/mix_test.py` adds three layer-2 cases against the test's running event loop:

| Test | What it asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_mixer_callback_receives_a_single_input` | One input track → each mixer-callback invocation gets a 1-element list |
| `test_mixer_callback_receives_multiple_inputs` | Two input tracks → at least one mixer-callback invocation gets a 2-element list (inputs warm up independently, so not every call) |
| `test_mixer_output_cadence_tracks_configured_interval` | `recv()` calls are spaced by ≈ `mixer_output_interval` (generous bounds for scheduler jitter) |

Local soak: **5× consecutive green runs**.

`refactoring/05-add-pytest-layers.md` (the deferred mix-test rows), and the precedent from `refactoring/04-decouple-worker-from-streamlit-runtime.md`.

body:
## Summary

A wide ``mean ± std`` error bar can hide a single iter that breached a ceiling. Concrete case: orak's Stage Q n=5 sweep produced `[71.43, 57.14, 28.57, 28.57, 28.57]` — iter 1 was the first M5 breach across all stages but the bar shows mean=42.86 ± 20.20 → error-bar top sits at 63.06, *below* the breach. The chart visually misrepresented the result.

Fix: add an opt-in ``metric_scores: dict[str, list[float]]`` field to ``Milestone``. When populated, ``plot_milestone_progression`` overlays the raw per-iter scores as scatter dots — the breach now sits visibly on the ceiling line.

- ``Milestone`` dataclass: new ``metric_scores`` field, default empty dict (backwards-compatible).
- yaml schema: ``score: { mean: 42.86, std: 20.2, scores: [71.43, 57.14, ...] }`` parses into all three fields.
- ``_draw_metric_lines``: scatter loop after the errorbar render, same color as the line, white-edged for contrast, ``zorder=4`` so dots sit above the errorbar caps.

author: jamierowe1994
body:
Three improvements to the studio's editor surface.

1. Searchable Google Fonts picker (~150 families).
   - Catalogue baked into editor.astro frontmatter (top-150 popular Google fonts: sans/serif/display/script/mono) and injected as JSON. Picking a font lazy-loads its CSS from fonts.googleapis.com on first use — no startup cost, no per-font network call until needed.
   - Replaces the native <select> in both the top context bar (when text is selected) and the right properties panel. Same widget in both places: trigger button shows current font, click opens popover with search input + scrollable list, click outside / Escape closes.
   - On template load, any text element's font CSS is pre-loaded so the canvas paints in the right typeface immediately.

2. Download dropdown.
   - Replaces the old standalone "Export JPG" + "Download (PNG)" buttons with a single Download ▾ menu (top right). Options: PNG (transparent), PNG (with background), JPG, PDF.
   - "PNG transparent" skips the background fill so cut-outs from the BG remover export cleanly.
   - PDF export wires up jsPDF via dynamic CDN import — only fetched when a user picks PDF. Page size matches the canvas dimensions (no surprise margins) and embeds the rendered JPG.

3. Six more sizing presets in the Resize panel: TikTok (1080x1920), LinkedIn Post (1200x627), X/Twitter (1200x675), Pinterest (1000x1500), YouTube Thumbnail (1280x720), FB Cover (820x312). Existing presets (IG, Story/Reel, Landscape, FB Link, A4) untouched.

Small follow-up to the recent Unified Water LOD ownership change.

On my setup, LOD water no longer disappeared, but after going into an interior and back out some water surfaces could flicker heavily until the area was reloaded. This keeps the current vanilla LOD ownership path, but cleans up some stale water state around terrain block transitions.

Changes:
- clear detached water children through `TESWaterSystem` instead of only detaching the scene children
- run the duplicate water cleanup after the `AddLODWater` / `RemoveLODWater` handoff
- refresh `BSWaterShaderProperty::plane` during water setup so stale transition data does not survive on one of the overlapping surfaces

Testing:
- built `ALL-VS2022` locally
- shader tests passed, 166 assertions
- tested an equivalent v1.5.2 build in game by repeating exterior -> interior -> exterior transitions; the water stayed visible and the transition flicker stopped

* **Bug Fixes**

author: aulait92
body:
## 1. Reject → Replace

Der Reject-Button machte vorher nichts Sinnvolles (nur DB-Status). Jetzt umgenutzt:

- Klick markiert Variante als rejected
- Triggert sofort eine Ersatz-Generation (1 neue Variante im selben Request)
- Brainstorm bekommt die Headlines aller Geschwister-Varianten als Avoid-Liste — Claude soll explizit eine andere Mechanic + anderen Hook-Angle wählen
- Neue Variante kommt als frische Telegram-Message mit vollem Button-Set → weiter iterierbar

Button heißt jetzt **🔁 Ersetzen** statt **❌ Ablehnen**.

## 2. Count-Mismatch (10 angefordert, 7 geliefert)

Zwei Ursachen:

**a) Brainstorm-max_tokens zu klein.** 2000 reichte nicht für 10 detaillierte Konzepte → Output truncated. Hoch auf 4000.

**b) Promise.all killt den ganzen Batch bei einem Failure.** Wenn 1 von 10 parallelen Execution-Calls failed (Claude-Rate-Limit, Parse-Error, Playwright-Timeout), verlor `Promise.all` alle 10. Umgestellt auf `Promise.allSettled` in:
- `generateCreativeVariants` (Phase-2-Calls)
- `generateCreatives` (Render + R2-Upload)

Jeder Failure wird einzeln geloggt, erfolgreiche Varianten kommen durch. Plus Warning wenn Brainstorm weniger Konzepte als gefordert liefert.

author: axhoover
body:
## Summary

Wires the `microcrypt-sync` deterministic orchestrator lane, which pulls the quantum-cryptography dependency graph from [`sattath/microcrypt-zoo`](https://github.com/sattath/microcrypt-zoo) into the wiki without duplicating existing content.

- **`scripts/microcrypt-sync.mjs`** — pure-JS planner: parses the upstream DOT graph, diffs against committed state, and emits a structured JSON plan of only new things to add. The bot prompt consumes the plan; the model never parses the `.gv` file directly.
- **`scripts/microcrypt-graph.mjs`** — regenerates `content/Microcrypt Zoo.md` with an SVG embed, injecting wiki links on mapped nodes and dimming unmapped ones.
- **`.orchestrator/prompts/microcrypt-sync.md`** — thin bot lane prompt; follows the same lane discipline as the other four bots.
- **`.orchestrator/microcrypt-map.json`** — human-curated dedup boundary. All 57 upstream nodes start `"unmapped"` — nothing enters the wiki until a human curates this file.
- **`vendor/microcrypt-zoo`** — git submodule (Apache-2.0, upstream LICENSE retained).
- **`.orchestrator/decide.mjs`** — gates the lane on a sha256 comparison of `vendor/microcrypt-zoo/microcrypt.gv` against the hash stored in `microcrypt-sync.json`; first run always fires (stored hash is null).
- **`.github/workflows/weekly-orchestrator.yml`** — new `microcrypt_sync` job with GraphViz install, submodule update, plan, model, embed-page regen, and state recording (in that order).

## ⚠️ Separation-direction hazard

`microcrypt.gv` encodes separation edges (oracle/black-box impossibility results) with a `dir="back"` rendering hack: an edge `A -> B` in the dashed-red block means *"B cannot be constructed from A"* — the opposite of the arrow's literal direction.

`microcrypt-sync.mjs` classifies every such edge as `kind: "separation"` and emits it as **DIRECTION-UNRESOLVED** — it reports both endpoints and the paper URL but **never asserts a direction**. The bot prompt requires reading the cited paper and routes any resulting claim through the **skeptical-checker** lane for human sign-off. No directional separation statement can enter the wiki from this lane alone.

Do not "fix" this in the script — it is intentional.

## Local verification output

Run against the test fixture (all 57 nodes unmapped):

```
node scripts/microcrypt-sync.mjs \
  --gv test/microcrypt.gv \
  --map .orchestrator/microcrypt-map.json \
  --state .orchestrator/state/microcrypt-sync.json \
  --content content \
  --plan-out /tmp/plan.json
```

```
microcrypt-sync: 30 actionable item(s); 57 unmapped node(s), 0 unmapped citation(s).
```

30 reference stubs proposed; zero primitive/implication writes — confirming the dedup boundary: nothing about the graph's structure enters the wiki until `microcrypt-map.json` is curated.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm local verification output matches above
- [ ] Review `decide.mjs` hash-gating logic (`microcryptSyncShouldRun`)
- [ ] Review workflow step ordering — `--write-state` must run after the model step
- [ ] Curate a handful of nodes in `.orchestrator/microcrypt-map.json` (map known primitives like OWF, PRG, PRF to existing slugs) before the first live run
- [ ] On first live run, verify no existing pages are modified — only new `content/References/` files and `content/Microcrypt Zoo.md`

author: davidban77
body:
Closes #363.

## Summary

The `§Gap window` section explains the syntax correctly but offers no guidance on how to **verify** that gaps are firing in a live pipeline. Two pitfalls hide them by default:

1. **Prometheus instant queries** use a 5-minute `lookback_delta`, so a series that stopped emitting 10 seconds ago still looks "live" — a 20-second gap is invisible at the expression-bar default.
2. **Grafana auto step-size** evaluates a 5-minute range at ~30-second steps, collapsing a 240k-sample run to ~7 dots that read as missing data even when they aren't.

The fix is a specific query (`count_over_time(<metric>[1s])`) and a 1-second min step. Obvious once you see it; confusing until you do.

## What this PR adds

A `!!! tip` admonition placed immediately after the existing _"This emits events for 1m40s, then goes silent for 20s, then repeats."_ line, before §Burst window. The admonition covers:

- The two pitfalls (lookback + step-size), each with the actual symptom you see.
- The recommended PromQL: `count_over_time(interface_oper_state[1s])`.
- Grafana Explore settings: **Min step `1s`**, **Time range Last 5 minutes**, time-series view.
- A self-contained chart showing the resulting duty cycle for `examples/basic-metrics.yaml` (`every: 2m for: 20s, rate: 1000` → ~100s of ~1000/s, then 20s of zero, repeating).
- A closing line that the same trick generalizes to `bursts:` and other rate-shaping fields.

## On the image choice — SVG mockup, not a screenshot

The issue suggested a PNG screenshot. I shipped an **SVG mockup** instead, at `docs/site/docs/configuration/img/gap-duty-cycle.svg`. Trade-off explained:

| | Screenshot (PNG) | SVG mockup (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Private labels | Risk of leaking hostnames / clusters | None — synthetic data |
| Stale when Grafana UI changes | Yes — re-shoot each time | No — text-editable |
| Renders at any zoom | Pixellates | Crisp |
| File size | ~50–150 KB typical | 3.1 KB |
| Matches Sonda palette | Whatever Grafana theme | Yes (lime + midnight) |
| Re-render to tweak | Requires repro setup | Edit numbers, build |

The mockup is a faithful **structural** representation — Grafana panel header, axis labels, dashed grid, lime stroke with gradient fill under the curve, two annotated `20s gap` callouts — and conveys the same teaching point (rectangular duty cycle = gaps firing correctly) without the screenshot baggage.

If you'd rather have a real screenshot too, happy to add one as a follow-up — but my recommendation is to keep just the mockup so the docs don't bit-rot the next time Grafana ships a UI refresh.

## Numbers match the actual example

The issue's starter text mentioned `every: 30s for: 20s` in one spot and the `basic-metrics.yaml` example (`every: 2m for: 20s`) in another. I went with the **actual file** so the docs stay coherent — the existing §Gap window example block right above already uses `every: 2m for: 20s`. Time range bumped from `Last 2 minutes` (which shows only one cycle for `every: 2m`) to `Last 5 minutes` (shows two-plus cycles, the rectangular pattern is unmistakable).

## Test plan

- [x] `mkdocs build --strict` clean
- [x] SVG parses as valid XML
- [x] Admonition renders in the page at the right anchor (between gap example and §Burst window)
- [x] Numbers cross-checked against `examples/basic-metrics.yaml` (rate=1000, gaps every 2m for 20s) and the existing prose ("emits events for 1m40s, then goes silent for 20s")

## Scope

- Single file edit + one new image. No code, no other docs, no CHANGELOG (release-please owns it).
- Follow-up issue welcome if we want a parallel `§Burst window` verification tip — same pattern, different query (`rate(metric[1s])` to show the multiplier kicking in). Out of scope here per the issue.
